articleTitle: Construction and Application of Intelligent Heat Supply Real-time Alarm System
abstract: Aiming at the current intelligent heating system during the operation of many parameters need to be accurately controlled but the monitoring data is huge resulting in many operational anomalies and dangers cannot be found in a timely manner, this study is based on the B/S architecture to build a set of real-time alarm system for intelligent heating and apply it in the intelligent heating system. Firstly, the data collection of PLC and other bottom equipments are carried out through SCADA and the collected data is stored in the database through ODBC. Secondly, useing the software to write the alarm module, the module uses multi-threaded simultaneous detection of merchants, heat exchange stations, power plants, the first station and a network of parameters, to reach a fast, real-time detection of the intelligent heating system and alarm records into the database. For the alarm process due to the alarm module is too sensitive to repeat the alarm, through the data filtering of the alarm limit of the most optimal design of the alarm module to optimise the alarm records. The alarm records are finally displayed through the Web client. Finally, this alarm system is applied in the dispatching center of Dalian Clean Energy Group, and in the process of application, this alarm system effectively reduces the time and difficulty of investigating abnormalities and dangers in the intelligent heating system, and provides security for the intelligent heating system, and it has good effects in specific applications.

articleTitle: Valid RBFNN Adaptive Control for Pure-Feedback Nonlinear Systems With Matched Uncertainties
abstract: This article studies neural network (NN) adaptive control for pure-feedback nonlinear systems with matched uncertainties. Radial basis function NNs (RBFNNs) are used in the backstepping design approaches to compensate for nonlinear uncertain functions. The valid compact sets for RBFNN adaptive controllers is presented, on which local RBFNN approximators are defined and the closed-loop state should always remain. Regarding the use of one property of the weight vectors in RBFNNs, the computation of the valid compact set is given explicitly as well as the configuration requirements of RBFNNs. Furthermore, within this compact set, the rigorous proof is given on RBFNN adaptive controllers for solving a tracking problem to a given smooth enough reference signal. Finally, several simulation results are provided to illustrate the feasibility and efficiency of the obtained results.

articleTitle: Positive Filtering of Positive Complex Networks Using Linear Programming
abstract: This paper investigates the filtering design of positive complex networks in both discrete- and continuous-time contexts. A positive filtering is proposed for discrete-time complex networks. The filtering gain matrices are designed based on a matrix decomposition approach. All positivity and stability conditions are described in terms of linear programming. A novel positivity analysis framework is constructed for complex networks and the corresponding error systems and a gain filtering design is solved using copositive Lyapunov function. The presented filtering design approach is developed for continuous-time complex networks. Finally, an example is provided to verify the validity of the proposed filtering.

articleTitle: An Attention Ant Colony Algorithm for Solving SDVRP
abstract: The Split Delivery Vehicle Routing Problem (SDVRP) is a hot topic in the field of logistics research. Recently, popular solution methods include heuristic algorithms and deep reinforcement learning algorithms. Heuristic algorithms can achieve high solution quality but require longer solution times, while deep reinforcement learning algorithms offer faster solution times but may compromise solution quality. To better balance solution quality and computation time, an Attention Ant Colony Optimization (AACO) algorithm is proposed, which combines heuristic algorithm with deep reinforcement learning algorithm. By utilizing the probability values output by the attention model as heuristic information for the ant colony algorithm, the guidance capability of heuristic information on ants is enhanced, thereby improving solution speed. The effectiveness of AACO is verified through testing on different datasets.

articleTitle: A quantitative mitigation model for supply chain disruptions considering reconfiguration
abstract: In recent years, global supply chains have faced great challenges due to emergencies. A manufacturer is the core of a supply chain and its disruption will cause more damage to the supply chain. This work investigates the problem of reduced production capacity in some of a manufacturer’s factories affected by disruptions, and reconfigures the supply chain by introducing production lines and expanding capacity in factories not affected by the disruptions. A supply chain disruption mitigation model is developed with the objectives of minimizing cost and maximizing system resilience. To characterize the supply chain system resilience, a resilience metric is constructed. To efficiently solve the developed model, an improved NSGA-II algorithm is developed. The algorithm ensures the feasibility of the solution and improves the solution efficiency through improved heuristic rules and specific restoration strategies. The effectiveness of the proposed model and solution algorithm is verified through numerical experiments. This work can offer a potentially useful tool to help the manufacturers reduce losses whenever the supply chain system experiences production disruptions.

articleTitle: Lightweight VGG Rolling Sound Classification Model Based on Combinatorial Features
abstract: In response to the intelligent transformation of the steel manufacturing industry, many teams are exploring the application of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms to optimize the steel rolling process. Intelligence brings advantages to the steel industry in terms of labor reduction, high-quality development, and data-driven decision-making compared to traditional models. The basic direction of the development of intelligence in the steel industry is to use acoustic and visual features for real-time monitoring of steel rolling engineering applications and to provide a visual representation of the field state, but due to the objective nature of the production methods in the steel industry, the quality of the visual features is more inconsistent. Therefore, this study analyzed the available sounds of critical processes generated in the rolling shear zone. It was observed that these sounds exhibit few samples and a high degree of similarity, complexity, and partial synchronization. To address this issue, feature fusion methods were proposed, furthermore, there were challenges in generalization and accuracy improvement when training with limited datasets, therefore data augmentation techniques were applied to improve the performance. To address the problem that Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with high computational complexity cannot be efficiently applied in the field, the model is optimized accordingly. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated on the proposed rolling line shear zone sound dataset. The experimental results show that the study can efficiently classify the sound in the steel production site, providing a research basis for the development of real-time sound monitoring applications in the steel production site.

articleTitle: Semantic Object-Level Modeling for Robust Visual Camera Relocalization
abstract: Visual relocalization is crucial for autonomous visual localization and navigation of mobile robotics. Due to the improvement of CNN-based object detection algorithm, the robustness of visual relocalization is greatly enhanced especially in viewpoints where classical methods fail. However, ellipsoids (quadrics) generated by axis-aligned object detection may limit the accuracy of the object-level representation and degenerate the performance of visual relocalization system. In this paper, we propose a novel method of automatic object-level voxel modeling for accurate ellipsoidal representations of objects. As for visual relocalization, we design a better pose optimization strategy for camera pose recovery, to fully utilize the projection characteristics of 2D fitted ellipses and the 3D accurate ellipsoids. All of these modules are entirely intergrated into visual SLAM system. Experimental results show that our semantic object-level mapping and object-based visual relocalization methods significantly enhance the performance of visual relocalization in terms of robustness to new viewpoints.

articleTitle: Distributed Fixed-time Secondary Control for Heterogeneous Battery Energy Storage Systems
abstract: Based on the consensus theory of multi-agent systems (MAS), this article proposes a distributed fixed-time control strategy for heterogeneous battery energy storage systems (BESSs) in droop-controlled microgrids. The droop control of microgrids creates frequency deviations from the target value, leading to decreased accuracy of power sharing and frequency. A fixed time secondary control method is proposed to address the deviations arising from the primary control as well as to achieve the objectives of frequency regulation, active power sharing, and energy level balancing within a fixed timeframe. Additionally, the fixed-time control approach can provide an explicit estimate of the settling time without any dependence on the initial conditions. With the foundation of theoretical analyses, the consistency and convergence of the control algorithms are clearly revealed. Eventually, the suggested control strategy is validated by conducting case studies using a modified IEEE 34-bus testing system implemented in MATLAB.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fixed-time Observer-based Formation Robust Control of Fixed-wing UAV with Multiple Leaders
abstract: In this paper, the fixed-wing UAV formation control problems with multiple leaders is studied. For this UAV system, an adaptive fixed-time observer is proposed to observe the convex combination of multiple leaders. Adaptive parameters eliminate the need for followers to know both the input information of leaders and its upper bound, reducing the need for information acquisition. The proof of observer stability based on Lyapunov stability theory shows that the observation errors converge to the neighborhood of the origin within fixed-time. At the same time, the adaptive robust controller is designed for the followers considering external disturbances, so that the system has strong anti-disturbance ability. The proof of controller stability based on Lyapunov stability theory shows that the state errors converge to the neighborhood of the origin exponentially. Finally, the effectiveness of the method is proved through simulation.

articleTitle: Bearing Cooperative Fault Diagnosis Based on Multi-adversarial Multi-domain Adaptive Network
abstract: The existing methods for diagnosing faults in bearings require a considerable number of labeled signals. However, practical engineering scenarios often involve a significant amount of unlabeled signals. To address this issue, this study introduces a novel approach called the Multi-Adversarial Multi-Domain Adaptive Network (MMAN). To capture the temporal correlation present in vibration signals, a shared feature extractor is devised using multi-head self-attention encoder. An adversarial module is devised to calculate the adversarial loss of multi-source domain. Additionally, a source-target domain adaptive subnet is formulated, utilizing the local maximum mean discrepancy (LMMD) loss function, to aid in class alignment between the source and target domains.. The paper concludes by presenting a collaborative decision-making strategy involving multiple subnets. This approach employs the LMMD loss to calculate confidence scores, aiding the multi-subnet classifiers in making well-informed fusion decisions. This contributes to the improved accuracy of collaborative fault diagnosis. The introduced method is assessed using bearing fault data gathered under variable speed conditions, and the outcomes from comparative experiments emphasize the excellence of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Sliding Mode Fault Tolerance-Based Buffer Control of Aircraft Magnetorheological Landing Gear
abstract: The buffer control method of magnetorheological aircraft landing gear is a hot topic in the research of aircraft landing gear. In order to ensure that the magnetorheological buffer system can still work effectively when the damper fails, This paper presents an adaptive sliding mode fault-tolerant control algorithm to improve the buffering efficiency of aircraft landing gear buffering system. Firstly, the relevant parameters of magnetorheological are identified and the model of magnetorheological buffer system is established. Then, based on the fault information estimated online by adaptive law, a sliding mode fault-tolerant control law is designed to compensate the influence of damper fault on magnetorheological buffer system. Finally, the simulation results show that compared with passive control and PID control, the landing gear buffer system based on adaptive sliding mode fault-tolerant control can not only compensate the influence of damper fault, but also effectively improve the buffer efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on Ramp Merging Strategies Based on Different Traffic Conditions in a Fully Connected Environment
abstract: The development of autonomous driving technology faces a significant challenge in effectively addressing the ramp merging task. Current research encounters difficulties in handling the dynamic coupling between the longitudinal speed adjustment of ego vehicles and merging gap selection, as well as ensuring intelligent interaction with mainline vehicles. To tackle this issue, this paper proposes a baseline merging strategy using a virtual fleet in an interconnected environment. Subsequently, dynamic arrival time-based merging strategies are introduced for three cooperative merging scenarios. These strategies aim to synchronize the speed of ego vehicles on the ramp with the fleet on the right side of the mainline while ensuring minimal disruption to the efficiency of upstream vehicles. Simulation results demonstrate that the three cooperative merging strategies outperform the baseline strategy in terms of efficiency and comfort, significantly reducing merging completion time. Notably, Scenario 1 exhibits the shortest merging time, achieving an approximate 8% reduction in overall merging time for the three on-ramp vehicles compared to the baseline strategy. These findings provide valuable insights for researchers to develop ramp merging technologies in a fully connected environment.

articleTitle: Image Enhancement Method for Smart Grid Visual Monitoring System
abstract: In the field of video surveillance in the smart grid, monitoring room staff are faced with the problem of being unable to see low or excessive illumination areas clearly due to diverse lighting conditions in the monitoring scene. To allow them to observe more image details, it is necessary to increase the contrast of these areas and improve the visibility of the images. This paper proposes a method to enhance uncertain illumination images. Our solution is to decompose the image by filtering to enhance the details, and adjust the brightness with an adaptive scheme. First, the Guide Filter (GF) is used to decompose the input image into a base layer and a detail layer. After filtering, the detail layer is stretched by the arctan function and adjusted by the light intensity of the base layer, and then the adjustment result is linearly combined with the base layer. Finally, the brightness is adjusted by using the adaptive curve guided by "maximum entropy" to improve the contrast in low illumination areas and excessive illumination areas. Experimental results show that this algorithm can significantly improve the quality of images with uneven illumination, more details in low illumination areas and excessive illumination areas can be observed, and it has the advantage of lower running time consumption over some popular algorithms.

articleTitle: Large constellation TT&C resources scheduling method based on improved differential evolution
abstract: The scheduling task of TT&C resources is a high complexity dynamic constrained combinatorial optimization problem. Aiming at the issues of large number of satellites, complex types, and high conflict probability of TT&C time windows, this paper proposes an improved adaptive differential evolutionary algorithm to solve the problem of scheduling TT&C resources for large constellation. Firstly, the problem model is constructed, the gain of each TT&C task is a decreasing function over time, and the algorithm needs to maximize the total income; secondly, the adaptive differential evolution algorithm is improved, and a conflict value penalty function algorithm based on the greedy principle is proposed for the conflict cancellation of the time window, which is capable of judging the degree of superiority and inferiority of solution vectors with the same standard. It adopts the sum of the gain minus the sum of the penalty function value as the optimization index to retain the better solution vectors for the optimization process. Thus, the better solution vectors are controlled for iterative evolution. In this paper, three existing algorithms that use different ways to deal with time window conflicts are selected for comparison, and the experimental results show that the algorithm in this paper converges faster, the convergence results are better, and it performs better.

articleTitle: Stackelberg Game-based Secure Tracking Control for an Unmanned Surface Vehicle under Actuator Attacks
abstract: During the navigation of an unmanned surface vehicle (USV), the control input is often vulnerable to intelligently malicious behavior, leading to deviations from the intended trajectory. To this end, a Stackelberg game-based secure tracking control (STC) of the USV is investigated, while considering the unknown dynamics, actuator attacks, and external disturbances. The velocity error dynamics, involving control input and actuator attack, are established to mitigate the burden of controller design in the Stackelberg game framework. To address the challenges posed by unknown dynamics and external disturbances, an integral reinforcement learning (IRL) algorithm with the additional neural network (NN) is deployed to directly derive approximate optimal solutions for the Stackelberg game, effectively mitigating instability of the STC decision-making process, and enhancing the robustness and adaptability of the USV. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the Stackelberg game-based STC scheme for the USV under actuator attacks.

articleTitle: An Ensemble-Based Informational Fast Resampling Method for Multiclass Imbalanced Data Stream Classification
abstract: Data stream is a common and infinite form of data in the era of big data. Ensemble learning can adapt to the dynamic update characteristics of data stream, thus having significant advantages in data stream classification. In addition, the most commonly used method for class imbalance is resampling, which can change the underlying distribution of data and reduce the imbalance ratio. Therefore, this paper proposes an ensemble-based Informational Fast Resampling Method (IFRM) for multiclass imbalanced data stream classification. Firstly, the issue of multiclass imbalanced data stream is analyzed. Secondly, the framework of the proposed method is introduced, which includes four parts: class imbalance judgment, samples selection, samples synthesis, and weighted ensemble. Finally, the performance of the proposed method is verified through various experiments. Theoretical analysis has shown that this method has low time complexity compared to other multiclass data stream classification algorithms. Furthermore, experimental results confirm the effectiveness of the informational fast resampling technique proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Stabilization of Sampled-Data Systems with Noisy Sampling Intervals and False Data Injection Attacks
abstract: In the presence of noisy sampling intervals, the modeling and stabilization problem for a class of sampled-data systems subject to false data injection is investigated. First, the false data injection attack is modeled as discrete sampling format and the continuous-time system under consideration is converted into a discrete-time system with stochastic parameters. Then, in order to deal with computational difficulties, mathematical expectations of both matrix exponential and integral of matrix exponential function are calculated by Kronecker product operation and the law of total expectation. Based on this, the sampled-data stabilization controller is designed such that the closed-loop system is mean-square exponential stable with a prescribed H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performance under noisy sampling interval. Finally, two illustrative examples are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed design algorithm.

articleTitle: State and Input Network Reconstruction for Heterogeneous Networked Dynamical Systems
abstract: In this paper, we address the reconstruction problem of both state network and input network for heterogeneous networked dynamical systems (NDSs). Different from most existing works, we aim to identify networks of heterogeneous NDSs without assuming any prior knowledge of external input matrices. We first establish a sufficient condition for network reconstruction in noise-free scenarios leveraging an appropriately constructed matrix equation of which parameter matrices are constructed using external inputs and external outputs of heterogeneous NDSs. We develop an identification approach that allows us to accurately reconstruct the state and input networks simultaneously once the matrix equation permits a unique solution, which can be ensured by proper rank conditions. The proposed approach demonstrates its effectiveness in network reconstruction even in the presence of process noise. Finally, we numerically verify the efficacy of the proposed method under both noiseless and noisy conditions.

articleTitle: Weakly supervised infrared and visible image fusion based on attention mechanism
abstract: In response to the issues of high model complexity, poor generalization, and loss of detail information in the current infrared and visible image fusion algorithms, this paper proposes a weakly supervised infrared and visible image fusion network based on attention mechanism. Firstly, infrared and visible images undergo feature extraction using convolutional neural networks. Subsequently, the deep convolutional features are reversely transmitted and the proposed channel attention interaction module and spatial attention interaction module are successively used to fuse and filter features of different layers to improve the fluidity of network features and effectively retain the details of the source image. Finally, a residual structure is employed for feature reconstruction to mitigate information degradation post-fusion. Additionally, leveraging threshold segmentation to generate uncertain labels, the network undergoes weak supervision, thereby augmenting its focus on prominent infrared targets. Comparative evaluations against nine advanced fusion algorithms are conducted on the TNO and MSRS datasets. Experimental results show that the proposed network exhibits strong competitiveness in infrared and visible image fusion tasks.

articleTitle: Transform Nonlinear Programming Problem to Initial-Value Problem to Solve, Part 1: Within the Feasible Region
abstract: A dynamic method to solve the general Nonlinear Programming (NLP) problem, inspired by the Lyapunov continuous-time dynamics stability theory in the control field, is proposed. The optimal solution is regarded as the stable equilibrium point of a finite-dimensional dynamic system and solved in an asymptotic manner. Under the premise that the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) optimality condition exists, the Dynamic Optimization Equation (DOE), which has the same dimension to that of the optimization parameter vector, is established within the feasible region and its solution will converge to the optimal solution of the NLP globally. The expressions of the Lagrange multipliers and the KKT multipliers during the entire optimization process are also derived. Using the matrix pseudo-inverse, the DOE is valid even without the linearly independent regularity requirement on the nonlinear constraints. Via the control based method, it is shown that the NLP may be transformed to the Initial-value Problem (IVP) to be solved efficiently, with mature ordinary differential equation integration methods.

articleTitle: Real-Data-Driven Offline Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Vehicle Speed Decision Making
abstract: In recent years, reinforcement learning has demonstrated its powerful learning ability and application potential in the autonomous driving decision module, in comparison to traditional methods. However, due to the interaction with the environment, it is mostly limited to the simulation environment. Offline RL, on the other hand, can learn through fixed data sets and is considered a feasible means to push reinforcement learning to practical applications. To verify whether offline RL can exhibit excellent performance under real-world datasets, we provide a benchmark for offline RL using the Argo dataset. This paper first introduces a variety of offline RL algorithms, followed by the processing of scenes such as starting, following, and parking in the dataset, as well as the generation of the dataset and simulation environment. Different datasets were obtained through data enhancement and other methods, and several state-of-the-art(SOTA) offline RL algorithms were tested and compared with imitation learning BC. Finally, the conclusion and analysis are presented. Our code is available at https://github.com/hjcwuhuqifei/offline_rl_benchmark_by_argo.

articleTitle: An Indirect Prescribed Performance Design Framework for Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems under Switching Graphs
abstract: This paper presents an indirect yet new prescribed performance design framework for unknown nonlinear multi-agent systems under switching undirected connected communication topology. By means of the neighboring information, a fully distributed and purely robust control scheme is established via a backstepping-like design procedure, which is capable of steering the output tracking errors to an arbitrarily prescribed residual set at a user-predesignated convergence rate. The developed design possesses several salient merits: (i) Contrary to the existing work, a new yet indirect prescribed performance design mechanism is introduced to avoid the potential jumps outside the boundaries of traditional performance functions without prior topology knowledge at switching time; and (ii) Unlike approximation- or adaptive-based results, the design is in a low complexity (model-, approximation- and adaptation-free) fashion. Furthermore, it is shown that all the closed-loop signals are semi-globally uniformly ultimately bounded (SGUUB). Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed theoretical results is illustrated via numerical simulations.

articleTitle: A Mobile Charging Scheduling Scheme with Obstacle Avoidance in Wireless Rechargeable Sensor Networks
abstract: Wireless rechargeable sensor networks have attracted wide attention in recent years due to the energy supply for sensor nodes. However, most of the previous works study wireless charging schemes take no account of practical conditions such as obstacles in the network area, which will increase the node failure rate. Therefore, a mobile charging scheduling scheme with obstacle avoidance is proposed in this paper. First, a task node selection algorithm is designed to fully utilize the energy budget for wireless charging. Then, a globally optimal charging path with obstacle avoidance is planned. Simulation results show that the obstacle avoidance function is realized and the proposed charging scheme effectively reduces the node failure rate by comparison.

articleTitle: An Efficient Obstacle Avoidance Approach For USV Considering The Heading Angle Constraint
abstract: The application of Unmanned Surface Vessel (USV) is gaining a lot of attraction in military, commercial, and scientific researches. However, due to various potential obstacles in the actual ocean, USV must be able to detect these obstacles in real-time, and take measures to avoid them safely. In this paper, we propose a novel method: Gradient and Node Optimal Rapidly-exploring Random Trees (GO-RRT) algorithm, which leverages the principles of APF (Artificial Potential Field) algorithm and RRT(Rapidly-exploring Random Tree) algorithm, incorporating gradient vectors within the framework of RRT algorithm while optimizing node placements. This work includes: (i) thoroughly considering the constraints in USV path planning based on the advantages of RRT; (ii) adopting an improved RRT based on APF potential function, significantly improving the efficiency of path search, and optimizing the generated path to make the actual distance of the path shorter; (iii) a dynamic obstacle detection algorithm that enables USV to prevent the initiation of obstacle avoidance algorithms in unobstructed sea conditions, thereby saving computational resources. In this work, GO-RRT can improve the quality of generated paths, and effectively reduce the consumption of computational resources. Our algorithm obtains superior performance, and achieves efficient results in simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Combustion Status Recognition of MSWI process Based on Flame Image by Using YOLOv5
abstract: The combustion status is one of the key controlled variables in the municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) process. At present, the actual industrial process mainly relies on domain experts to observe the flame image. By using such manual mode, it is easy to cause the instability of the MSWI process and lead to the increase of pollution emission concentration. The complexity of the MSW composition can lead to the characteristics of the flame in the furnace, such as large brightness difference and motion blur. To solve these problems, this article proposes a method for combustion status recognition of the MSWI process based on flame image by using YOLOv5. The method uses backbone for feature extraction and uses the head layer for status recognition. The experimental result shows that the proposed method has higher accuracy than Alexnet, Vggnet, Googlenet and other algorithms.

articleTitle: Evolutionary game theory combined with reinforcement learning synthesis - A comprehensive survey
abstract: Within the realm of modern intelligent science, the fields of evolutionary game theory (EGT) and reinforcement learning (RL) have exhibited an inherently intertwined relationship since their inception. This symbiotic association has been further accentuated, especially in light of the significant advances in artificial intelligence technologies witnessed in recent years. As a result, their synergistic interactions have grown increasingly profound, catalyzing an explosive surge in interdisciplinary research endeavors. To align with this prevailing trend, the objective of this survey is to provide a comprehensive assessment of the interconnections, distinctions, and recent advances in the combination of EGT with RL. We approach this from three perspectives: Q-learning, the Bush-Mosteller (BM) model, and deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Subsequently, the most recent advances in research within these three dimensions are categorized based on distinct subject areas. Ultimately, this nascent cross-disciplinary research domain is comprehensively summarized, and its future prospects are outlined.

articleTitle: Distinguish ionospheric scintillation and multipath in GNSS signals based on machine learning
abstract: A significant component influencing GNSS positioning accuracy is ionospheric scintillation. Scintillation is commonly described in terms of its amplitude and phase using the scintillation parameters S4 and σφ, respectively. In certain situations, multipath effects could have an impact on S4 and σφ. In this work, we present a machine learning approach to discriminate between multipath and ionospheric scintillation effects using GNSS simulation data. The covariance between the in-phase and orthogonal phase outputs, the signal strength variance, and the average signal strength of the GNSS receiver’s tracking loop are the inputs used in this model. The data can be categorized using this approach as flashing, multipath, or mixed GNSS signals. The scintillation signals are further classified into three categories according to the scintillation grades. The model’s overall accuracy in experiments was 96%.

articleTitle: BSTNet for Content-Fixed Image Harmonization
abstract: Image harmonization aims to enhance the visual coherence of composite images, where composite images refer to placing an object from an image onto another one. Most traditional deep learning-based image harmonization methods utilize encoder-decoders to extract semantic features to achieve foreground-background harmony. With the proposal of RainNet, an increasing number of researchers focus on the foreground-background style feature transfer for image harmonization. While these approaches have demonstrated visually commend-able performance, they neglect that the semantic features learned by convolutional neural networks contain two factors: content and style, which cause the foreground texture features to change. For the above problem, we propose the Content-Fixed Background Style Transfer(CF-BST) module to preserve the content of the foreground while altering its stylistic features to achieve harmony with the background. The CF-BST module includes three steps: first, foreground features are normalized to obtain foreground content features; second, the VGG encoder extracts background style features. Finally, the foreground content and background style features are fused. In addition, we introduce the Enhanced Contextual Fusion (ECF) module to address the limitations of the U-Net in feature extraction and contextual perception. The ECF module consists of three branches that enhance feature representation by aggregating local and global information through multi-scale receptive fields. We conducted experiments on the iHarmony4 dataset and the results show that our proposed network achieves the state-of-the-art performance in image harmonization tasks.

articleTitle: Critical Scenario Generation for Realistic Testing of Autonomous Driving System via Multi-vehicle Cooperative Control
abstract: Among the three major safety assessment processes (i.e. simulation, closed-course test, and public road test) for highly automated driving systems (ADS), closed-course tests offer a high level of fidelity and provide a secure and controllable testing environment. However, due to the lack of realistic background traffic, scenarios in closed-course tests are usually static and limited. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a new safety assessment framework, which integrates cooperative speed optimization of multiple traffic participants and active conflict generation along the reference path. Through the speed planning for background vehicles and background dummies, the conflict between the background participants and the tested autonomous vehicle is generated to test the performance of the autonomous vehicle in corner cases. The effectiveness of the proposed conflict generation algorithm is validated through MATLAB simulations and implemented at Tongji University’s intelligent connected vehicle evaluation base. Test results demonstrate the capability of the proposed framework to assess the safety performance of highly ADS in a cost-effective manner.

articleTitle: Control of Flexible Launch Vehicle Based on Singular Perturbation and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: In this paper, a data-driven algorithm based on singular perturbation (SP) and reinforcement learning (RL) for the elastic launch vehicle attitude control and elastic suppression has been proposed. Considering that the rigid body state and elastic mode exhibit different time-scale properties, the model is initially decomposed into a stiff body slowly changing subsystem and an elastic fast changing subsystem by employing the SP theory. In addition, a data-driven off-policy learning algorithm is proposed to address the problem of the inability to obtain a precise mathematical model due to aerodynamic parameter perturbation during flight. Without using the precise mathematical model of the system, the algebraic Riccati equation (ARE) of the subsystem can be solved iteratively to obtain its control law, then the control law of the original system is obtained through composite control strategy. Finally, the elastic suppression performance of the proposed method and using a notch filter is compared, which demonstrates the proposed method has a better performance and the rigid body attitudes converge more quickly and steadily.

articleTitle: Accelerating genetic algorithm based on optimization of feasible search space and its application in cascade reservoir optimal operation analysis
abstract: The cascade waterpower development is an important component of the world energy development, as an typical non-engineering measure of cascade waterpower development, combined optimal operation of cascade hydropower stations, involving widely discipline categories and department interests, is essentially an decision-making problem of large complex system, which has a profound theoretical and practical guiding significance for realizing the coordinated and sustainable development of regional water resources, social economy and ecological environment. As the researching difficulties of large complex constraints and curse of dimensionality when applying the swarm intelligent optimization algorithm in optimal operation of cascade hydropower stations, the accelerating genetic algorithm (AGA), in which the optimizing space of the variables are shrinking gradually with the increase of the iteration times, was introduced in the research of optimal operation of cascade hydropower stations, and the feasible decision space for the optimization variables of different station and period were formed based on the principles of classification and reverse iteration, and then the accelerating genetic algorithm based on feasible search space optimization and its application in the cascade waterpower development were discussed in this paper. Finally, applying the method in the combined optimal operation example of Wujiang cascade hydropower stations, which has a good representative of hydraulic and power characteristics in China, and the result shows that, the accelerating genetic algorithm based on feasible search space optimization has strong self-adaptability and global optimization ability for solving the complex constraints and improving the optimization efficiency, and the average annual energy output is 289.67×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>kW•h, with the increasing extent of 2.60% when comparing with the designing values of the Wujiang cascade stations. So, it is obvious that applying the accelerating genetic algorithm based on feasible search space optimization in the optimal operation research of cascade hydropower stations is feasible and reasonable, and the research results would provide scientific and effective decision basis for the centralized dispatching and operation of cascade hydropower stations, and also enrich and develop the theoretical and practical research system of regional waterpower development and utilization.

articleTitle: Input-output finite-time stability and stabilization of stochastic Markovian switching systems under finite-time boundedness
abstract: This paper investigates finite-time mean square boundedness (FTMSB) and input-output finite-time mean square stability (IO-FTMSS) of stochastic Markovian switching systems (SMSSs). Simultaneous consideration is given to the state and output stability to prevent the occurrence of huge and unacceptable values throughout certain transient periods. Utilizing a collection of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs), a sufficient condition for the system satisfying both FTMSB and IO-FTMSS is developed for a class of bounded input signals. Furthermore, via state feedback and output feedback, two controllers are developed to achieve the closed-loop system both FTMSB and IO-FTMSS. The proposed criteria ensure that the state and output of SMSSs remain within a designated threshold over the specified time interval. Finally, to illustrate the feasibility of the suggested technique, two examples are shown.

articleTitle: Event-triggered Model-free Adaptive Sliding-mode Control for CPSs under DoS Attacks
abstract: This article investigates an event-triggered model-free adaptive sliding mode control issue of cyber-physical systems with dual channels denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. First, a model-free adaptive sliding mode control scheme is established with merely the input and output data of the controlled plant, and the dual channels DoS attacks are modeled. Second, an event-triggering mechanism is introduced in the model-free adaptive sliding mode control scheme, which can effectively reduce the number of data transfers to reduce the communication burden. Moreover, on the controller side, the input and output compensation algorithms are designed to reduce the effect of DoS attacks under forward and feedback channels. Finally, the convergence of the control error is roughly proved, and the results of simulation studies demonstrate the proposed approach’s effectiveness.

articleTitle: Prescribed-Time Tracking Control of Electro-Hydraulic Servo Systems with Non-Vanishing Uncertainties
abstract: Most of the existing nonlinear control methods for electro-hydraulic servo systems can only ensure the output tracking error to asymptotically converge to zero or an adjustable compact set around zero, which will result in not good enough transient tracking performance. In this paper, a prescribed-time tracking control strategy is proposed for electro-hydraulic servo systems subjected to non-vanishing uncertainties. The nonlinear mathematical model of electrohydraulic servo system with both matched and mismatched uncertainties is firstly established. Then, a prescribed-time controller is designed by introducing a novel finite-time function based on backstepping framework. The closed-loop system stability analysis reveals that the proposed controller guarantees the output tracking error to converge to zero in finite time. Furthermore, the convergence time can be explicitly pre-determined and is independent of initial condition. Comparative simulation results are obtained to verify the high-performance nature of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Detour Estimation for Vehicle Routing Problems
abstract: For the vehicle routing problem, this paper introduces a baseline function computation approach with “Detour Estimation” in deep reinforcement learning. During the training process, if a truck still has feasible customers to serve every time it prepares to return to the depot, it is considered that the truck has taken a detour, and at this moment, the detour estimation for this partial solution is calculated, referred to as “partial detour estimation.” After completing the service of all customers and returning to the depot, the overall detour estimation of the entire delivery path is calculated based on a rule that gives less weight to earlier detour estimations, known as “overall detour estimation.” This paper computes the REINFORCE algorithm’s baseline by subtracting the “overall detour estimation” from the “true path length” to expedite algorithm’s convergence and enhance solution quality. Experimental results show that the method proposed in this paper, when applied to problems of size 20, 50, and 100, reduces the deviation from the optimal solution compared to the baseline calculation method in the original paper by 0.5 at most, respectively, demonstrating the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning based parameter optimization of cascade control loop in the Coke Dry Quenching System
abstract: Waste heat boiler is an important part of dry quenching power generation, and its steam drum level cascade three impulse system is characterized by strong perturbation, non-linearity, strong coupling and multiple working conditions. In this paper, a reinforcement learning based parameter optimization of cascade control loop in the coke dry quenching system is proposed for such series control problems. Based on the uncertainty of the state combination between the control parameters of the cascade loop and the liquid level of the steam, this paper uses a BP neural network to model the controller parameters and optimization indexes, uses the NSGA-II algorithm to select the design factors of the system, transforms the PID parameter optimization problem into a combination optimization problem, and finally using the reinforcement learning mechanism gives the optimal control strategy under multiple operating conditions. The simulation experiments are carried out through the data of a 180t/h dry quench coke waste heat boiler steam drum level system, and the results show that compared with similar controllers, the control strategy proposed in this paper can significantly reduce the maximum overshooting amount with a small increment in the rise time.

articleTitle: The impact of nodes of information dissemination on epidemic spreading in multiplex networks
abstract: This paper conducts research on the relationship between information transmission and disease transmission by establishing a UAU-SEIR model. In contrast to previous studies, we take into account the variations in individual awareness of prevention and control. By modeling the two-layer network and combining the microscopic Markov chain method, we mathematically deduce the epidemic threshold in our model. Additionally, we conduct a detailed study on the impact of nodes that do not change their own consciousness in the model. We find that in the consciousness layer, fixed nodes with high degrees play a crucial role in the spread of diseases. Fixed nodes that are disconnected from other nodes in the consciousness layer may lead to the appearance of outbreak points and steady-state points of diseases in advance. These findings are of significant importance for formulating effective prevention and control strategies and raising public health awareness.

articleTitle: Association Rule-based Soft Labeled Human Activity Recognition Using Wearable Sensors
abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) with wearable sensors has been widely used in many human-centric applications, due to the prevalent of various IoT devices and low-cost wearable sensors nowadays. Typically, training a reliable HAR system requires activity labels to be both completely and precisely annotated. While, high-quality annotations are always quite difficult to acquire for users, even it is possible to collect a large number of activity data in practice. In this paper, an accurate and interpretable HAR model is constructed for achieving favorable recognition performance under the circumstance of limited activity labels. The essence of our proposal is to assign soft labels for those available unlabeled data by using the association discovery and hierarchical clustering techniques, which to some degree reduces the accuracy loss caused by the lack of activity labels in training set. Moreover, a soft label-based evidential association rule learning procedure is conducted for learning the relations between instance features and activity classes. Finally, all the generated association rules from available labeled or unlabeled data are fused for the belief classification of unknown input instances. Experiments on the public UCI smartphone and self-collected activity datasets demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposal, in which the classification accuracy of the proposal improves at most 5% and 11% if compared with the classical (association) rule-based models CBA and BRBCS.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Intelligent Optimization Algorithm for Hot-Dip Galvanizing Batch Scheduling
abstract: In response to the challenges in batch production, customization of user demands, and the complexities of the hot-dip galvanizing process in practical steel production, a two-stage intelligent optimization algorithm (TIOA) is proposed. TIOA aims to enhance production efficiency and resource utilization by reducing internal variety and specification switches in the plans while smoothing the transition between plans. In hot-dip galvanizing production, the imperative is to minimize indirect continuity costs between materials while considering factors such as material priority, rolling schedule quantities, and critical process specifications. However, there exists a contradiction in the requirements for inter-batch continuity and intra-batch continuity in bulk production planning. To address this contradiction, in the first stage of TIOA, a variable neighborhood search algorithm is proposed to identify transition materials based on the characteristics of inter-batch transitions. Subsequently, a heuristic algorithm is employed to obtain the initial solution to the problem. In the second stage of TIOA, an adaptive neighborhood genetic algorithm is introduced. Mutation operations from genetic algorithms are embedded into an adaptive neighborhood search algorithm, taking advantage of the genetic algorithm’s strong exploration capability and the rapid local convergence of the adaptive neighborhood. Finally, the algorithm is validated using actual data from hot-dip galvanization production. The obtained results are compared with those derived from an expert-based heuristic approach, confirming the effectiveness of TIOA.

articleTitle: Using Feature Alignment Learning To Improve The Output Repeatability Of Classification Neural Network
abstract: Deep learning is extensively applied in industrial defect detection, with deep neural networks classifying product images for quality assessment. However, disturbances in captured images due to factors such as assembly tolerances and vibrations can compromise the consistency of network outputs, affecting Attribute Reproducibility and Repeatability (AR&R) evaluations. This paper proposes a feature alignment method for neural networks to improve output repeatability, which has shown significant enhancements in classification consistency and accuracy on an inductance defect dataset.

articleTitle: An Iterative Algorithm for Unrolled Unsupervised PET Image Reconstruction
abstract: In recent years, the potential of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for PET image reconstruction has been widely acknowledged. However, the effectiveness of CNNs relies on the availability of a substantial data set containing paired low-quality and high-quality reference PET images. Acquiring such a data set is often not feasible in clinical practice. The deep image prior (DIP) based on unsupervised learning can effectively address this problem by utilizing only prior information and measurement data of patients. In this paper, we propose an accelerated restart algorithm that integrates the DIP framework into the maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) PET image reconstruction. Our framework combines a CNN with the expectation maximization (EM) update step to ensure data consistency. The experimental results on both computer-simulated and clinical PET data sets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Adaptive RBF Network-Based Sliding-Mode Fault-Tolerant Control for Hypersonic Vehicles With Model Uncertainties
abstract: This paper introduces a fault-tolerant control methodology for hypersonic vehicles encountering actuator faults and model uncertainties. The initial step involves the construction of a nonlinear dynamic model for Hypersonic Vehicles (HSV), founded on published data regarding the Winged-Cone aircraft. Subsequently, a finite-time nonsingular terminal sliding mode controller is devised to mitigate the adverse effects of lumped interference, encompassing actuator faults, model uncertainties, and external disturbances. Then, a finite-time adaptive Radial Basis Function (RBF) neural network is developed to estimate the lumped interference, bolstering system robustness while ensuring control quantity continuity. Furthermore, a finite-time disturbance observer is integrated into the approach to gauge the estimation error of the RBF neural network and acquire the essential parameters for controller adjustments. Finally, the efficacy and robustness of the proposed control strategy are substantiated through a combination of theoretical analysis and simulation results.

articleTitle: Telecom Fraud Identification based on Vertical Federated Secure Boosting Tree Algorithm
abstract: With the continuous development of the Internet industry, the means of fraud have become more and more deceptive, and telecom fraud has gradually become a common means, telecom fraudsters are able to take advantages of new technological means to carry out criminal activities. Therefore, the model being able to accurately identify fraud phone numbers is demanded as it can fundamentally avoid the risk of fraud. However, the data of customers are always privacy sensitive. In order to prevent the privacy of each telecom operator’s customers from being leaked in the process of modeling whether an unknown phone number is a telecom fraud number using vertical federated learning. Secure Boosting Tree (SBT) algorithm was introduced to handle the phone number data, and the optimal model was obtained through a large number of comparative experiments. Compared with the results obtained by the traditional centralized learning method, the effectiveness of federated learning is verified.

articleTitle: Information-Weighted Consensus Optimal Kalman Filter for Linear Systems with Fading Channels
abstract: This paper is concerned with the optimal Kalman consensus filter (KCF) for discrete-time systems with fading channels, where each channel is suffered from different transmission delays and packet losses. Firstly, the reorganisation observation technology is adopted to transform the observation sequence with time delay into a delay-free observation sequence. Secondly, an KCF is presented by the mean squared method, and the closed-form expressions for the Kalman gains and consensus gains are derived. The novelty of this paper is that a novel matrix-weighted consensus algorithm is applied to deal with the distributed state filter of the fading channel systems, which is with the optimality property and recursion form.

articleTitle: Adaptive Memory Event-triggered H∞ Filtering for T-S Fuzzy Systems under DoS Attacks
abstract: This paper investigates the event-triggered H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> filtering problem of Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy systems under periodic denial-of-service (DoS) jamming attacks. A novel adaptive memory event-triggered mechanism (AMETM) is introduced to determine whether current sampled data of the sensor should be transmitted to reduce the communication burden for filter design. By using time-varying Lyapunov-krasovskii functional method, sufficient conditions are derived such that the filtering error system is exponential stability and satisfies the prescribed H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performance. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated by a numerical example.

articleTitle: Smooth Switched Flight Control Design of Fixed-wing Aircraft for Heavy Payload Airdrop
abstract: This paper investigates the issue of flight control of fixed-wing aircraft (FwA) in heavy payload airdrop tasks, where smooth control commands are considered for actuators. The case that heavy payloads are mounted out of the symmetry plane is taken into account for dynamic modeling of the FwA, where the dynamic model is split into different modes corresponding to various situations of mounted payloads. Considering the dramatic variations of mass and center of gravity, a multi-equilibria switched system (MESS) is formulated for flight control, where the stable (unstable) modes correspond to the cases of symmetry (unsymmetry) mounting to ensure that the airdrop is with small rolling/yawing angles. By inserting the smooth portion, a smooth switched controller and the corresponding dwell time condition is obtained for MESS to tackle the flight control problem in heavy payload airdrop of FwA, which has not been considered before. The effectiveness and advantages of the proposed controller are demonstrated via simulations.

articleTitle: Robust and Real-Time Road Edge Detection with Flexible LiDAR Configuration
abstract: Road edge detection is an important component in autonomous driving for along-side scenarios. The road edge is defined as a boundary line where there is a height change from the road surface. However, the traditional LiDAR-based methods are not sensitive enough for small height difference. In addition, the point cloud needs to be provided in a channel-based organization, which means that at most one LiDAR’s data can be used for edge detection. In this paper, a novel road edge detection method is proposed to utilize flexible LiDAR configuration, e.g., multiple LiDARs. Specifically, the raw point cloud is first sorted in polar coordinates, and coarse edge points are generated according to height gradient for accurate ground segmentation. The non-ground points are further used to determine the road types based on occupancy map and beam models. The final edge points in the region of interest are extracted by dynamic slide window. Our method is evaluated on unmanned ground vehicle equipped with two Robosense LiDARs, and extensive experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: A Log Anomaly Detection Based on Incremental Contrastive Learning
abstract: To address issues such as the dynamic variations of large-scale log data, the difficulty in obtaining anomaly labels, and time-series dependencies, a log data anomaly detection method based on incremental contrastive learning is proposed. This method employs incremental contrastive learning to train data to adapt to continuously changing data distributions and the problem of lacking labeled data. It utilizes a distillation approach to design the loss function, transferring knowledge from the original model to the new model to mitigate catastrophic forgetting issues. In the sequence data processing stage, an attention shift mechanism is introduced to automatically learn the importance of each feature for the detection model, shifting the model’s focus to the most informative features to enhance the accuracy of detection. Experiments conducted on open-source datasets validate that this method effectively improves the accuracy of anomaly detection.

articleTitle: Research on Pedestrian Gender Detection Based on A Lightweight Model
abstract: In recent years, a variety of emergency events have been occurring in buildings in countries. For there are some differences between male and female in movement ability and evacuation behavior, gender has a non-negligible impact on evacuation and decision-making of emergency events. Thus, it is of great practical significance to detect the gender of pedestrians at entrances or exits of buildings in real time to grasp the proportion of different gender people in buildings and to formulate emergency warning or evacuation strategies scientifically. In response to the requirement of rapid emergency response, this paper proposes a pedestrian gender detection method based on a lightweight object detection model YOLOX-Tiny. In addition, considering the inaccurate pedestrian gender detection caused by the change of pedestrian posture and camera angle, the attention mechanism CBAM is introduced to enhance the ability of filtering a large amount of redundant information, obtaining key information and acquiring pedestrian gender characteristic information. Through the experiments of self-made pedestrian gender datasets, the results show that the detection accuracy of the improved model is increased by 1.8%, and the detection speed reaches 251FPS, which can meet both speed and accuracy of pedestrian gender detection in emergencies.

articleTitle: LTGGNet:Concrete Crack Detection Network Based on Local Topology and Global Grouping
abstract: Crack detection is an important part of building structural health monitoring. However, the traditional convolution is difficult to capture the characteristics of tiny concrete cracks and the complex topology, which ultimately leads to the misclassification of crack segmentation. To address the above problems, a concrete crack detection network based on local topology and global group attention (LTGGNet) is proposed. In the encoding part, a deformable local attention module (DLA) is designed to improve the ability of the network to extract tiny crack features and complex topologies. It uses deformable convolution to extract the crack regional features and topology information, and strengthens the network’s discriminability of the tiny crack pixel features. In the decoding part, a global grouping context aggregation (GGC) module is proposed to enhance the global modeling ability of the network to capture images of crack structures. It uses the self-attention mechanism to establish the correlation representation of the global information and enhance the long-range dependency of the topology, thereby achieving the accurate localization of cracks and the recovery of details. The experimental results show that the proposed network achieves 75.84%, 86.26%, 59.20%, and 74.37% in the metrics IoU and F1-Score, respectively, on the public crack datasets Deepcrack and Crack500. Compared to the comparison network, the proposed network has a better concrete crack segmentation effect. The ablation experiments further verify the effectiveness of the network.

articleTitle: Optimization Method for Launch Vehicle Attitude Control Parameters Based on Bayesian Optimization
abstract: The paper presents a Bayesian Optimization-based method for designing attitude control parameters of Launch Vehicles. It proposes an algorithm for optimizing control parameters using small sample simulation data to construct a Gaussian process regression model. This approach significantly reduces simulation time and costs compared to traditional methods. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the method through experiments, showing its ability to quickly find appropriate control parameters, meet margin design criteria, and offer significant advantages in simulation costs over Particle Swarm Optimization algorithms.

articleTitle: Security Tracking Control for Discrete-Time Stochastic Delayed Networked Systems With Cyber-Attacks by Dynamic Event-Triggered Approach
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to develop a security tracking controller for discrete-time delayed stochastic network control systems (SNCSs) that are vulnerable to stochastic cyber attacks. The presented strategy, called the Dynamic Event-Triggered Communication Approach (DETCA), adapts the volume of data transmitted across the network based on fluctuations in tracking error system, while concurrently maintaining the desired level of the tracking performance. These stochastic cyber attacks encompass deception attacks and denial-of-service (DoS), which may occur during signal transmission over the network. Based on Lyapunov stability theory, a sufficient condition is provided for guaranteeing the asymptotic stability of the tracking error system. The linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) are employed to solve the event-triggering parameters and the tracking controller gain. The efficacy of the proposed theoretical results is lastly demonstrated by a simulation example provided.

articleTitle: Multi-UAV Trajectory Planning Based on Improved Multi-population Grey Wolf Optimizer Algorithm
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are gradually and frequently applied in a wide range of fields, and how to reasonably control the trajectory of UAVs to better accomplish the tasks is an important challenge for people. Based on the MP-GWO algorithm that combines the Gray Wolf optimization algorithm and multiple swarm ideas, this paper introduces nonlinear decreasing control parameters for the Multi-population Grey Wolf Optimization (MP-GWO) algorithm, and proposes a position updating strategy combining the dynamic weighted averaging method and the static averaging method, in order to improve the algorithm’s convergence accuracy and convergence speed. We construct a model for UAV trajectory planning in complex environments, describe the cooperative trajectory planning problem, and analyze the constraints affecting the cooperative operation of multiple UAVs. In this paper, we design a scenario to run multiple group intelligence algorithms, and comparatively analyze the performance of GWO, MP-GWO, cuckoo search GWO (CS-GWO), and improved MP-GWO algorithms. The experimental results show that our method outperforms the other methods in the paper in terms of the convergence value of the objective function.

articleTitle: Small Invasion Obstacle Detection on the Railway Track Based on BD-YOLOv5
abstract: With the increase of railway operation kilometers and the increase of operation speed, ensuring the safety of train operation has become the focus of attention. Among them, the consequences of the collision event between the train and the obstacles invading the railway gauge are particularly serious. Therefore, the detection of railway obstacles is an important guarantee for the safe operation of trains. This paper proposes a BD-YOLOv5 model, which introduces the BiFormer attention mechanism to better integrate the context information around the target, so that the model can capture the characteristics of small targets more accurately. At the same time, the ODConv is used to replace the original Conv layer, which has a new multidimensional attention mechanism with a parallel strategy, learning the complementary attention of the convolution kernel along all four dimensions of the kernel space in any convolution layer. It reduces the number of parameters and also enhances the feature extraction ability of CNN basic convolution operation. The experimental results show that the Precision can reach as high as 97.5%, the Recall value achieves 98.4%, and the frame per second (FPS) is 100. BD-YOLOv5 can meet the practical application requirements of railway obstacle detection.

articleTitle: Real-time Multi-object Tracking Research Based on Image and Point Cloud Fusion
abstract: Negotiating an optimal balance between accuracy and real-time in object detection and tracking technologies remains a key challenge within the autonomous driving realm. This study presents IAFusionMOT, a real-time multi-object tracking algorithm that fuses image and point cloud data, resolving the limitations of unimodal tracking and the complexities of multi-object tracking. IAFusionMOT incorporates a novel four-level associated structure that synergistically integrates the combined detection outputs with the trajectory library, enabling adaptability to various environments. It employs geometric data from the 3D detection frames to formulate an efficient cost function that optimizes the association between sequential frames using Hungarian matching. This study benchmarks IAFusionMOT on the KITTI tracking dataset, where it significantly outperforms existing trackers. Particularly in pedestrian tracking, the Higher Order Tracking Accuracy(HOTA) metrics reaches 51.12%, an improvement of 12.5% and the single-frame inference speed increased to 164 FPS, demonstrating the algorithm’s superior performance in both accuracy and speed. Further field-testing in real vehicles confirms the algorithm’s robust ability to track objects in diverse scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhancing Axial Compressor Stall Warning with Time-Frequency Generative Adversarial Networks: A Novel Approach in Advanced Signal Processing
abstract: In the domain of axial compressor stall warnings, existing methods largely focus on time or frequency domain analyses, leading to excessive dependence on signal quality, increased rates of false alarms, and merely partial extraction of characteristics signaling an imminent stall. To overcome these challenges, it is imperative to develop a model that can swiftly and effectively identify early anomalies that signal an impending stall within a complex time series. Such a model ideally enables a thorough extraction of early stall indicators. This paper introduces the Time-Frequency Generative Adversarial Networks (TFGAN), representing the inaugural innovative fusion of adversarial training with time-frequency analysis. Utilizing the Wigner-Ville distribution function, the TFGAN achieves enhanced fidelity in information exchange between the time and frequency domains. Through adversarial training, the TFGAN discerns the characteristic states of various sequences following time-frequency analysis, precisely identifying conditions that suggest pre-stall precursors, thus fulfilling the goal of accurate stall warnings. Empirical results show that the TFGAN model effectively captures the complex time-frequency relationships present in signal data, facilitating the identification of subtle temporal changes across different features. This enables the swift extraction of stall characteristics, anomaly detection, and stall prediction within complex time series data. When compared with a range of generative models, the proposed method markedly outperforms experimental benchmarks in generative accuracy and predictive capability, as demonstrated by both qualitative and quantitative analyses.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Class Incremental Learning for Packaging Defects with Double Class Feature Interaction
abstract: It is crucial to conduct defect detection and classification for cigarette packages, as it helps enterprises identify problems and improve product quality. However, in real production environment, new categories of defects continue to arrive, causing huge difficulties for defect classification. Directly fine-tuning the existing model to learn new defect categories can cause catastrophic forgetting problems, especially when only few samples per class are available, this will leading to serious over-fitting problem. In this paper, we fully utilize various features in our model to construct an inter class relationship network, thus solving the problem of few-shot class incremental learning (FSCIL). We initially train a powerful encoder using the concept of supervised contrastive learning to achieve better classification performance on the base classes, and frozen its parameters to prevent catastrophic forgetting and prepare for subsequent incremental learning. Then, we propose an classifier incremental learning method based on dual feature interaction combined with the aforementioned encoder to facilitate the learning of new defect categories. Our method achieved best accuracy compared with other methods in our Cigarette Incremental Learning dataset.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral Image Classification Using Spatial and Spectral Features Based on Deep Learning
abstract: In recent years, deep learning has been widely applied to the classification of hyperspectral images and has achieved good results. Most of the hyperspectral image classification experiments use spatial features, and it is easy to ignore the spectral features of the image. In order to make full use of the advantages of convolutional neural network (CNN), We use the MNF(Minimum Noise Fraction) and GABS(Gray value with adaptive band selection) methods to obtain the bands required for classification, and then use 3DCNN to extract the spatial features and spectral features of hyperspectral images. The combination of spatial spectral features not only adds useful information, but also effectively eliminates some of the noise. In this paper, a three-dimensional convolutional neural network is used to simultaneously extract the features of the fused spatial spectral information and classify the hyperspectral image. The proposed method is tested on three publicly available data sets: University of Pavia, Salinas and Indian Pine. The results of the competition show that our method can achieve the state-of-the- art classification accuracy in the three data sets.

articleTitle: Multi-microgrid Multi-energy Optimal Scheduling Strategy Based on Hybrid Energy Storage System and Sharing Technology
abstract: To effectively enhance the utilization of renewable energy in multi-microgrid systems while ensuring fair distribution of benefits among microgrids, this paper proposes a multi-microgrid multi-energy optimal scheduling strategy based on hybrid energy storage system (HESS) and sharing technology. Firstly, a novel multi-microgrid multi-energy shared energy storage system framework is designed, considering that a HESS is equipped with hydrogen storage system, electric boiler, heat storage tank, P2G devices and gas storage tank as well as coordinates the multi-energy sharing among microgrids. All microgrids and HESS are composed into a microgrid alliance for cooperative game. Secondly, the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is used to solve the optimal energy transaction volume and transaction price between each microgrid and HESS. Then, the asymmetric Nash negotiation (ANN) method is used to fairly distribute the benefits obtained by each subject. Finally, the simulation experiment shows that the proposed multi-microgrid multi-energy optimal scheduling strategy can not only meet the needs of various energy sources of microgrid, but also improve the utilization rate of renewable energy and the economic benefits of each subject.

articleTitle: Robust fusion filter for multisensor descriptor control system with uncertain variances, random one-step delays and colored measurement noises
abstract: For the linear stochastic multisensor networked descriptor control system with random one-step measurement delays, colored measurement noises and uncertain variances, the robust local and fusion time-varying filters are presented and the global robustness is proved. First, a new standard state space model is obtained based on the singular value decomposition (SVD) method and augmented state approach. And the actual and conservative correlation variances of fictitious process and measurement noises are obtained. Applying the minimax robust estimation principle and Kalman filtering theory, the robust local time-varying Kalman filter of new reduced-order state and white noise deconvolution filter of fictitious process noises are presented. Then, the local and distributed fusion robust filters for original descriptor system, and the actual filtering error variances are obtained. Further, the global robustness of the local and fusion filters is proved. A simulation example about two-loop circuits system verifies the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm and results.

articleTitle: An Image Denoising Algorithm Based on Improved Median Filter and Threshold Function
abstract: Mixed noise is commonly present in images, posing challenges for traditional denoising algorithms such as median filtering, mean filtering, and wavelet threshold filtering. In this paper, a novel approach is proposed for denoising mixed noise. The proposed method combines an improved median filtering technique with a wavelet thresholding function. By incorporating the strengths of both methods, our algorithm aims to effectively remove mixed noise from images. Firstly, we enhance the performance of the median filtering algorithm to provide initial denoising. Subsequently, a two-level wavelet transform is applied to the pre-filtered image, enabling the extraction of high-frequency components. These components are then filtered using an improved thresholding function and median algorithm. Finally, an inverse wavelet transform is performed to reconstruct the denoised image. The experimental results show that our algorithm improves the peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of the denoised image by 2.17%~10.56%, and reduces the root-mean-square error (RMSE) by 6.24%~25.19% compared to the algorithms such as the median filter, wavelet soft-threshold filter, wavelet hard-threshold filter, and wavelet semi-soft threshold filter, etc. Hence, the proposed algorithm in this paper exhibits superior preservation of image details and more efficient removal of mixed noise.

articleTitle: Soft Sensor Model for Cobalt Oxalate Synthesis Process Based on Probabilistic Slow Feature Analysis and Least Squares Support Vector Regression
abstract: In view of the nonlinear and time-varying characteristics existing in industrial processes, this paper proposes an integrated soft sensor model based on probabilistic slow feature analysis (PSFA) and least squares support vector regression (LSSVR) to achieve real-time measurement of quality variables. First, the PSFA method was used to effectively capture the slow feature vector of the process and solve the slow time-varying problem; then, the LSSVR method is utilized to establish the relationship between slow features and quality variables, thereby achieving online prediction of quality indicators. Finally, a numerical case and cobalt oxalate synthesis process data were applied to demonstrated the effectiveness of this propose approach.

articleTitle: Soft Open Point and Mobile Energy Storage System Coordination Planning for Improving the Resilience of Distribution Systems
abstract: With the deep integration of power grid and transportation network, in order to improve the resilience of distribution network, a three-layer coordinated planning model of SOP and MESS is proposed. In the pre-disaster prevention stage, the upper layer establishes a timing series loss sensitivity model to determine the optimal access position of SOP. The middle layer establishes a two-stage robust optimization model considering the uncertainty of wind power output and network reconstruction to solve the number and location of MESS access. In the post-disaster recovery stage, a hybrid integer second-order cone programming model for multi-source collaborative recovery of SOP, MESS and diesel generators is established in the lower layer to solve the optimal load recovery scheme. Finally, through the improved IEEE33 node example, it is proved that the proposed model is effective for improving the resilience and economy of the distribution network.
