articleTitle: Application of Additive Decomposition Based Composite Control in Image Rotation Compensation Mechanism
abstract: This paper focuses on the aerial imaging system image rotation compensation servo mechanism, the influence of disturbance on its tracking accuracy, using additive decomposition theory to decompose the system into two subsystems, the main system is responsible for accurate tracking, the nominal model of which is designed based on acceleration control proportional-derivative (PD) controller to ensure the accurate tracking of the servo mechanism on the moving target; the auxiliary system is responsible for disturbance rejection, the design of generalized The auxiliary system is responsible for the disturbance suppression, and the generalized nonlinear expansion state observer (G-NESO) is designed to observe and compensate for the equivalent disturbance; combined with the new high-order sliding mode compensator, the system disturbance is further refined and compensated. The stability of the control system is proved using Lyapunov theory. Finally, MATLAB simulation is used to verify the effectiveness and feasibility of this method.

articleTitle: A Method for Detecting Gradient Coil Cooling Faults for Magnetic Resonance Imaging
abstract: This paper proposes a method for monitoring and diagnosing cooling system faults in the gradient coils of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). In fact, cooling system fault can potentially lead to significant imaging deviations. Hence, a Hash Cerebellar Model Articulation Controller (LCMAC) is devised to learn the normal characteristics of gradient coils. When cooling failure affects the gradient coils' performance, the LCMAC response deviates from the norm. Additionally, two characteristic variables, degradation index, and waveform index, are introduced for residual error analysis. Notably, this approach offers the advantage of not requiring the dismantling of the MRI equipment's outer casing or the addition of extra sensors. Moreover, an alternative strategy is formulated to identify degradation types and estimate their severity. Testing a typical gradient coil under five fault conditions in the air conditioning unit validates the effectiveness and robustness of this strategy.

articleTitle: Human Gait Detection Method Based on Binocular Vision for Virtual Reality Omnidirectional Treadmill
abstract: Authentic walking experience is a key issue for immersive virtual worlds. The omnidirectional treadmill (ODT) is an effective solution to realize the virtual reality free walking experience in a limited indoor space, and real-time human positioning is a crucial component of this solution. However, existing strategies often do not combine ODT and human positioning systems well, there are problems in cost, anti-interference, accuracy and so on. In this paper, we propose a lightweight method for human gait detection on a virtual reality ODT. Our method combines the characteristics of the ODT by using infrared markers, image processing, improved Kalman filter and other algorithms to obtain real-time posture of a mobile binocular camera and gait information. The experimental results show that this method can effectively track the corresponding gait information of users’ feet and waist when walking freely on ODT. The detection accuracy can reach millimeter level, and this information can be used for subsequent control of ODT, thus effectively solving the movement problem in indoor virtual reality. Compared with other methods, our approach has several advantages, including low cost, no need for additional calibration, anti-interference, no additional space occupation and convenient use. And it avoids the defect of recalibration required for positioning base station movement in other methods.

articleTitle: Soft Sensor Development for Industrial Thickener using Neural Ordinary Differential Equation
abstract: The on-line measurement of underflow concentration,which is a crucial indicator for the thickening process, presents a significant challenge in mineral industry. This paper proposes a modeling approach employing a neural ordinary differential equation network with deep learning. The approach is designed to address the prediction challenges associated with underflow concentration in a thickener. Initially, we create a historical dataset using real data generated by a thickener operating under normal conditions at an industrial site. Subsequently, we train the neural ordinary differential equation network model for underflow concentration prediction. Finally, a subset of the dataset is selected to validate the accuracy of the predictions. The proposed approach achieves higher prediction accuracy compared to traditional deep learning methods.

articleTitle: Semantic Map Construction of UAV Autonomous Landing in Unknown Environment
abstract: Aiming at the problems of environment identification and dynamic target information detection in the process of autonomous landing map construction of quadrotor UAVs in unknown environments, a method of autonomous landing semantic map construction of UAVs in unknown environments is proposed. Firstly, an improved Deeplabv3+ model is proposed. The image collected by UAV is restored based on the Lucy Richardson algorithm. On this basis, the information after fusion processing of the collected original image features and restored image features is input into the semantic segmentation model. Shufflenetv2 is used as the backbone network of Deeplabv3+ and the CBAM attention mechanism is introduced to improve the accuracy of the semantic segmentation model. Secondly, to improve the accuracy of dynamic target detection, a dynamic target detection method based on optical flow and semantics is designed. The environmental semantic information is introduced into the Lucas Kanade algorithm to estimate the motion displacement of the airborne camera to determine the optical flow threshold of the dynamic target. Then, a semantic grid map is established to model the environment, define the measurement index of the safe landing sites, and design the selection strategy of the safe landing sites. The ICG Drone Dataset is used for experiments, and the results show that the image segmentation accuracy of the designed method is improved by 4.3% on average compared with the traditional DeeplabV3+ model, and the detection rate of the dynamic targets reaches 93.8% correctly. The measured results show that the drone can accurately detect the dynamic targets in an unknown environment and autonomously select the safe area as the landing site.

articleTitle: Bayesian CNN-GRU with Attention Mechanism for Lithium-ion Battery State of Health Estimation
abstract: Accurate estimation of the state of health (SOH) is crucial for ensuring the safe and stable operation of lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries. This paper presents an approach called Bayesian CNN-GRU with Attention Mechanism (AM-BCG) to estimate the entire lifecycle health state of the battery. Effective feature extraction is performed during the SOH estimation to ensure accurate prediction. Specifically, domain knowledge- related temporal features of Li-ion battery degradation processes are extracted, while capacity difference curves are utilized as spatially relevant features for model inputs. The AM-BCG approach comprises parallel CNN-GRU networks with attention mechanism and bayesian neural networks (BNN). The parallel CNN-GRU networks extract generalized information from prior data, the attention mechanism increases the weight of essential features and reduces overfitting, and BNN provides uncertainty estimates. Experimental validation on the A123 67Ah LFP battery dataset confirms that the proposed method exhibits high robustness and accuracy in estimating battery SOH.

articleTitle: Research on inter-process communication based on multi-core MCUs
abstract: In the field of embedded systems, the challenges associated with the application of multi-core MCUs are primarily manifested in the process of inter-process communication. Although communication methods between cores based on operating systems have matured to a considerable extent, achieving a satisfactory balance between communication efficiency and capacity remains a difficult endeavor. Some inter-process communication algorithms based on operating systems still largely reside in the theoretical domain, with practical implementation being some distance away. In embedded systems without an operating system, shared memory serves as a module capable of direct interaction with the MCU, offering significant advantages in terms of communication efficiency and capacity. This article is grounded in shared memory and presents a design for distributed shared memory inter-process communication, using the iterative computation model of an induction motor. Experimental comparisons are conducted between this approach and the RPMessage inter-process communication method, with respect to communication speed compared to single-core computation. The experiments demonstrate that the distributed shared memory approach can significantly reduce computation time during data processing, as opposed to single-core computation. This research holds valuable implications for the application of inter-process communication in multi-core MCUs.

articleTitle: Reduced-Order Observer-Based Event-Triggered Consensus Control of Linear MASs With Directed Topologies
abstract: This paper addresses the event-triggered leaderless and leader-follower consensus problems of general linear multiagent systems (MASs) under directed topologies. By utilizing the relative outputs of neighboring agents, two novel distributed reduced-order observer-based event-triggered control (ETC) laws are proposed. Based on the Lyapunov function method, it is proved that the leaderless consensus and the leader-following consensus can be achieved under the proposed control laws, respectively. Additionally, the Zeno behavior is proven to be excluded. Finally, two simulation examples are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the obtained results.

articleTitle: Motion Planning for Autonomous Vehicles in Uncertain Environments Using Hierarchical Distributional Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Safe and effective motion planning is essential for autonomous vehicles to successfully drive in complex and dynamic urban environments. However, most current methods lack considering the collision risk caused by obstacle occlusion and only consider longitudinal speed planning, which leads to overly conservative motion. The motion planning model proposed in this paper can consider the lateral motion of the vehicle while considering the risk of collision, improving safety and motion flexibility. It integrates distributional reinforcement learning with the path-speed decoupling scheme, yielding a hierarchical distributional reinforcement learning iterative optimization motion planning model. The high-level layer for path planning uses distributional reinforcement learning to choose local path points based on scattered point sampling. The low-level layer uses distributional reinforcement learning to adjust speed for each time step. These two layers achieve optimal performance through an iterative optimization method. The proposed model is trained and tested using the CARLA simulation platform in the scene where a pedestrian suddenly appear from the blind spot. The results reveal that, in comparison to the method that just employs speed planning, the suggested model’s success rate is increased to 99.75% and the travel speed is increased by 14.88%. The model is also verified based on actual driving data. It is proven that the model can avoid risks brought on by limited perception and has a flexible response capability to achieve efficient traffic.

articleTitle: Security Assessment of Intelligent Cabin Controller Using AHP-Fuzzy Evaluation
abstract: The development of new energy vehicles brings new requirements for vehicle information security. According to the WP29.R155 regulations and ISO 21434 standards, it is required to conduct relevant information security assessments of systems before the development of vehicle information security. However, the current assessment of vehicle information security primarily remains qualitative, leading to a rather passive approach in security protection. Therefore, the quantification assessment of network security risks becomes particularly important. In response to the above issues, this paper proposes an Analytic Hierarchy Process-fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method for information security risk assessment to achieve quantitative analysis of information security risks. The method mainly includes the construction of a fuzzy comprehensive evaluation factor set, the calculation of evaluation sets and fuzzy comprehensive judgment matrices, the calculation of weight sets and judgment matrices, and multi-level fuzzy comprehensive judgments. To validate the usability and rationality of this method, an intelligent cabin controller is selected as a case for a thorough analysis and assessment of information security risks. By thoroughly exploring the system architecture of the controller, the direction of data flow, and its interaction with the external environment, we extract the data/communication security assets that require protection. We comprehensively assess the potential threats and risks it faces. This provides strong support for the later development of vehicle information security and, at the same time, establishes a scientifically feasible foundation for formulating protection strategies for vehicle information security.

articleTitle: Parameter identification and vibration suppression for Flexible Aircraft Wings based on Support Vector Machine
abstract: This study investigates the control challenges of flexible aircraft wings through parameter identification. The Disturbances affecting flexible aircraft wings are commonly assumed to be random, making it difficult to satisfy the necessary statistical assumptions. Thus, we propose a parameter identification approach against specific parameters of aircraft wings based on a support vector machine (SVM) to rddress this situation. To suppress the elastic deformation of the flexible aircraft wings, a boundary control scheme based on a radial basis function (RBF) neural network is proposed based on the identification results. Finally, two simulation examples are provided to validate the effectiveness of the parameter identification method and the boundary controller respectively.

articleTitle: A radial projection assisted two-stage evolutionary algorithm for many-objective optimization
abstract: In recent years, lots of many-objective evolutionary algorithms have been proposed. However, as the number of objectives increases, most of them still cannot maintain a good balance between convergence and diversity of the population. To address the problem, this paper proposes a radial projection assisted two-stage evolutionary algorithm for many-objective optimization(RP-TSEA). In this paper, the environmental selection process is divided into two stages, which cooperate to make the population converge to the Pareto front from various directions and further balance convergence and diversity of the population. To be specific, the first stage selects two individuals with the most similar search direction, and then the second stage selects the best individual from these two individuals to enter the nest generation. The above process is repeated until a new population is formed for the next generation. In addition, an effective mating selection assisted by radial projection is designed to pick out promising individuals for variation, and further improve the search ability of the algorithm.. The experimental results on the WFG test suit have shown that the proposed algorithm can achieves better performance than six comparative algorithms.

articleTitle: Design of low power consumption portable ECG monitoring system
abstract: At present, China's population is aging seriously, and the younger group often works overtime and stays up late, so the incidence of cardiovascular disease in China is increasing. Currently, the diagnosis and prevention of cardiovascular diseases can only be addressed by specialized hospitals, and most patients miss out treatment because of its time-consuming and laborious nature. In this paper, we have designed an Electrocardiogram monitoring system that is portable and easy to operate. The system uses the ESP32WROOM32E, which integrates a Bluetooth RF front-end, as the main control chip, and uses AD8232 as the front-end acquisition chip, around which targeted filter circuits are designed, as well as a digital filter for the main control chip. The collected signals are pre-processed and then the data is sent to the upper computer WeChat applet via low-power Bluetooth. Through verification, the system designed in this paper is characterized by portability, low cost, low power consumption and easy operation.

articleTitle: M2CNet: An Infrared and Visible Image Fusion Method Based on Dual Marginal Contrastive Learning
abstract: Since there is no ground truth for infrared and visible image fusion, where there are huge differences in appearance and content between the source images, most fusion methods are based on unsupervised learning. However, current used losses in unsupervised learning, i.e., pixel losses and structural losses, do not accurately characterize the modal differences between source images. And the complex losses, which combines multiple losses, show poor robustness on various datasets and lead to difficulty in model convergence. In addition, most methods struggle to achieve a satisfactory information balance between source images. To solve these challenges, we proposed a fusion method based on dual marginal contrastive learning, namely M2CNet. First, we propose a novel contrastive loss with dual margin penalties to enhance the ability of building cross-modal connections between fusion image and source image. It is important to note that our approach exclusively utilizes this succinct loss to address the fusion task without currently used losses. Second, we propose a three-branch network to fuse extensive complementary information from source images and make an excellent trade-off between them. Qualitative and quantitative experiments demonstrate the superiority of our method over the state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: A Siamese tracker based on precise fusion of prior information and multi-layer features
abstract: With the rapid advancements in deep learning, Siamese trackers have made significant strides in terms of both performance and speed. Nonetheless, when confronted with the task of effectively managing dramatic object deformations, particularly when the aspect ratio of the target is presented in an extreme proportion, most trackers are prone to losing the target, resulting in tracking failure. To tackle this challenge, we created an anchor-free conjoined network predicated on a priori information and proportion fusion (SiamPIP). We discerned that the genuine target frame, provided by the initial frame, exhibits high purity, free from any noise interference. This represents the sole prior information in the entire tracking task, enabling us to effectively utilize the initial frame information to filter the template features extracted from the backbone network. Additionally, traditional Siamese models often overlook the differences between classification and regression tasks when amalgamating deep and shallow features. Classification tasks typically require more profound semantic information, while the features of shallow networks are better suited for regression tasks, necessitating precise fusion of features. Therefore, when faced with the challenge of severely deformed objects, our model can accurately distinguish the foreground from the background while preserving the accuracy of the regression boundary box. Notably, our model also performs well in the face of challenges such as motion blur. We have achieved exemplary performance metrics of 0.707 (AUC) on OTB100, 0.340 (EAO) on VOT2019, and 0.643 (AUC) on UAV123.

articleTitle: A Stochastic Configuration Network with Attenuation Regularization and Multi-kernel Learning and Its Application
abstract: To improve the generalization and robustness of the stochastic configuration network (SCN) model, an improved SCN algorithm is proposed. Attenuated L2 regularization is added to the iterative solution process of the output weight, which not only reduces the output weight of the hidden layer nodes in the early iteration, but also ensures that the new nodes after multiple iterations are not affected by the larger regularization coefficient, forming the constraint effect of first tight and then loose. In addition, the multi-kernel learning method is introduced to obtain the characteristics of the sample data, and the penalty weight matrix of the training samples is determined, so as to re-evaluate the output weight of the SCN model to enhance the robustness of the model. The performance of the proposed method was tested on four standard datasets and historical data from municipal solid waste incineration processes. The experimental results show that the modeling method proposed in this paper has certain advantages in improving the model’s generalization and robustness.

articleTitle: Optimization design of PMECC based on improved OBL and analytical decision-making multi-objective grey wolf optimization algorithm
abstract: In order to increase output torque while reducing eddy current loss as much as possible, this paper proposes a multi-objective grey wolf algorithm based on improved opposition-based learning (OBL) and analytical decisionmaking (IOAD-MOGWO), and applies this algorithm to the multi-objective optimal design of permanent magnet eddy current coupler (PMECC). Firstly, the Box-Behnken design method (BBD) is used to obtain the sample data required to construct the PMECC model, based on which the response surface methodology (RSM) is used to establish an approximate mathematical model about the structural parameters and performance indicators. Secondly, the IOAD-MOGWO algorithm is proposed, which solves the problems of local convergence and low search efficiency of the original multiobjective grey wolf algorithm by introducing the improved OBL strategy and the individual search strategy based on analysis and decision-making. Finally, a comparison of the optimization results with those obtained by the other two algorithms demonstrates the superior performance of the IOAD-MOGWO algorithm. In addition, the optimization results before and after the improvement are compared by means of COMSOL finite element simulation experiments. The simulation results show that compared with the original PMECC, the output torque of the optimized PMECC is greatly improved and the eddy current loss is significantly reduced, which proves the reliability of the optimization method.

Author Keywords: Multiobjective grey wolf optimization algorithm based on improved OBL and analytical decision-making

articleTitle: Multi-scale perceptual image super-resolution reconstruction based on coordinate attention mechanism
abstract: In this paper, we propose a multi-scale perceptual image super-resolution reconstruction network based on coordinate attention mechanism by modifying the SRGAN algorithm. Firstly, we introduce a multi-scale perceptual block to extract feature information at different scales. It can enable our model to focus on the important feature area and improve the visual perception of the generated image. Secondly, we add spectral norm normalization layer to the discriminator network to constrain the weight of the discriminator during the training, to enhance the stability of the network during training. Finally, we replace the original MSE loss function with the Charbonnier loss, which is more robust to outliers, to optimize and train the proposed algorithm. Furthermore, the regularization loss is added to suppress image noise and artifacts. Experimental results show that the generated images using our proposed algorithm have better visual perception and richer high-frequency details.

articleTitle: Distributed Adaptive Leaderless Consensus of Uncertain Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems under Event-Triggered Communication with Positive MIETs
abstract: In this paper, leaderless consensus control is investigated for uncertain nonlinear systems with event-triggered communication. Different from the existing results, exponential leaderless consensus is achieved under directed graphs with a positive minimum inter-event time (MIET) guaranteed for each agent. The main challenge lies in the cross-coupling term associated with asymmetric Laplacian matrix and the unknown parameters of all the agents in the derivative of Lyapunov function. To address this issue, a novel distributed event-triggered control scheme is presented to eliminate this term by applying adaptive invariance and immersion control. Besides, concurrent learning control is incorporated in the design of the controllers to ensure a positive MIET for each agent by achieving exponentially convergent rate for the parameter estimation errors. It is proved that all the closed-loop signals are globally uniformly bounded and exponential leaderless consensus can be reached. Moreover, a positive MIET can be guaranteed for each agent. Finally, an illustrative simulation is provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the presented control scheme.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Based Self-Driven Model Predictive State Constraint Control for Spacecraft Deorbit
abstract: In addressing the multi-constraint optimization control problem of active orbital decay for spacecraft, this study proposes a Model Predictive Control (MPC) approach that incorporates reinforcement learning, employing a self-triggered and adaptive prediction horizon. To tackle coupled orbital state constraints, this paper introduces a method based on reinforcement learning utility reward functions. Furthermore, this method incorporates the driving force into the prediction step and control mechanism of Model Predictive Control, forming a self-driven and adaptive step-length Model Predictive Control approach. At each triggering moment, the controller solves the spacecraft’s optimal orbital decay control problem (OCP), providing an optimal control sequence and determining the next triggering time and prediction horizon. This approach enhances the efficiency of solving Model Predictive Control, simultaneously improving its capabilities in handling multi-constraint predictive control problems. Simulation results ultimately confirm the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: EEG classification based on improved Genetic Algorithm channel selection
abstract: The control of intelligent peripheral devices such as robot arm and mouse movement through brain-computer interface needs to be based on accurate feature extraction and analysis of EEG signals. The signal-to-noise ratio of EEG signals is low and the signal dimension is high. The feature extraction of multi-channel EEG signals will introduce interference signals, so it is necessary to eliminate noise and redundant information signals by channel selection algorithm. Aiming at the problem that the traditional channel selection method needs to pre-define the number of selected channels and cannot meet individual differences, this paper proposes an EEG signal classification method based on improved Genetic Algorithm for channel selection. Then, Discrete Wavelet Transformation, and Common Spatial Pattern are used to extract the features of motor imagery EEG signal data after channel selection, and the EEG signal features are classified by Support Vector Machines. The experimental results show that the average classification accuracy of EEG signals after channel selection is 5% higher than that of all channels, and the problem of individual differences in the number of channels and channels is solved.

articleTitle: ESN-ATCN: A Solar Irradiance Prediction Model by ESN-TCN with Attention Mechanism
abstract: Accurate prediction of solar irradiance is crucial to fully utilize solar energy. Solar irradiance is often not accurately predicted due to temperature, humidity, seasonal conditions, and other factors. In order to improve the accuracy of solar irradiance prediction, we propose a solar irradiance prediction model that combines Echo State Network(ESN), Temporal Convolutional Networks(TCN) and the attention mechanism. ESN has strong nonlinear feature extraction and modeling capabilities by virtue of its unique reserve pool. TCN performs well in time series forecasting due to its parallel structure and larger acceptance domain. However, for the prediction process of long time series, Echo state networks and TCNs lack consideration of attention to critical information, and some non-critical information may affect the final prediction results. Therefore, in this paper, we propose to combine ESN, attention mechanism, and TCN network and present a new solar irradiance prediction model ESN-ATCN. The introduction of the attention mechanism allows the model to pay more attention to key information, improving the accuracy of the predictions.Experiments are conducted on real solar irradiance data, and the results demonstrate the accuracy of the prediction of the proposed model, which outperforms the ESN, TCN, DeepESN and LSTM.

articleTitle: Resilient Privacy-Preserving Consensus of Cooperative-Competitive Multi-Agent Systems under Byzantine Agents
abstract: This paper investigates secure and privacy-preserving consensus control for cooperative-competitive multi-agent systems (MASs) under Byzantine attacks. Considering that agents simultaneously interact cooperatively and competitively, we introduce a novel differential private (DP) resilient bipartite consensus protocol based on the Mean-Subsequence-Reduced (MSR) algorithm to defend against Byzantine agents. First, a resilient bipartite consensus controller incorporating Laplace noise is developed, which only works on competitive pairs of agents in the presence of potential eavesdroppers. Then, the convergence and privacy analyses demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can effectively preserve the privacy of initial states while simultaneously achieving resilient bipartite consensus. Furthermore, the privacy level is shown to be correlated with the minimum network degree. Finally, numerical simulations verify the effectiveness of the proposed results.

articleTitle: Optimal Scenario Reduction Method for Stochastic Programming via Probabilistic Similarity Function
abstract: In the scenario-based stochastic programming problems, the computational burden increase as the number of scenarios increases, which involves necessary scenario reduction operations. For the scenario reduction problem with high-dimensional random vector, an optimal reduction framework is presented to eliminate redundant scenarios. In this framework, the concept of probabilistic similarity function is firstly proposed to solve the problem that scenarios cannot be clearly distinguished by traditional distance-based reduction methods in the high-dimensional scenario clustering process. The relative distance under each dimension of scenarios is considered in the computation of probabilistic similarity function, which depends not only on the values of two scenario vectors but also on the overall scenario set. The proposed recursive-type reduction method aims at maximizing the probabilistic similarity between the original scenario set and reduced scenario set. The numerical results demonstrate that our method can exhibit better performance than distance-based methods and have good universality for different stochastic programming problems.

articleTitle: Online Finite-Horizon ADP Algorithm for Solving Non-Cooperative Differential Games
abstract: In this paper, online reinforcement learning solution to finite-horizon non-cooperative differential games is investigated. The main challenges are that, the Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs equation is time-varying, and in terms of parameter convergence, conventional learning approaches, with persistence of excitation condition satisfied, may cause undesired oscillations in the system states and deteriorate system performance, especially in finite-horizon situations. Regarding these, we develop a finite-horizon adaptive dynamic programming algorithm for continuous-time systems, where the idea of simulation of experience in concurrent learning technique is adopted to guarantee fast online parameter convergence. Boundedness of the system states and weight estimation errors is proved. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the presented method.

articleTitle: UAV-Assisted Adaptive Relay Nodes Placement for Network Connectivity Recovery in WSNs
abstract: Connectivity is a fundamental requirement for Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). Failures in multiple nodes can disrupt network connectivity, leading to the formation of disjointed subnetworks. To restore network connectivity, a UAV-assisted Adaptive Relay nodes Placement algorithm (UARP). is proposed in this paper. To concentrate relay nodes placement and reduce the travel distance of UAVs, a concept of UAV Areas is introduced to identify the areas between interrupted network partitions. Based on the number of network partitions within UAV Areas, two different strategies are employed to place relay nodes and reconnect the partitions for the scenarios with more and fewer partitions, respectively. With the proposed algorithm, relay nodes are strategically placed within UAV Areas, which can reduce the required number of relay nodes and shorten the UAV travel distance. Simulation results indicate that the UARP algorithm reduces relay usage by 10% to 20% and decreases UAV travel distance by 5% to 10% compared to other algorithms. The algorithm also demonstrates satisfactory performance in terms of packet delivery rate, convergence time, and transmission delay.

articleTitle: Adaptive control for a class of nonlinear systems with unknown control gains and input saturation
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive neural network (NN) asymptotic tracking control strategy is proposed for a class of nonlinear systems with unknown control gains and external disturbances under asymmetric input saturation constraint. Based on backstepping technique and command filter, a new controller containing the Nussbaum-type function is designed. Then the NN with minimal learning parameter is adopted to online approximate the unknown nonlinear function, where the unknown ideal weight vector and the approximation error are estimated by adaptive laws. Additionally, a new inequality is utilized to guarantee the desired output can be tracked asymptotically. The results show that all signals are bounded in the closed-loop system. Finally, the simulation result demonstrates the effectiveness of our proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Finite-time fractional-order nonsingular terminal sliding mode attitude controller for unpowered reentry vehicle
abstract: For the convergence time of fractional order sliding mode attitude control for unpowered reentry vehicle is difficult to estimate, a fractional order nonsingular terminal sliding mode attitude controller is proposed in this paper. Combining the advantages of fractional calculus and non-singular terminal sliding mode, the controller has the characteristics of higher control precision, faster convergence rate and convergence in a finite time. The chattering problem is solved by introducing a saturation function into the control signal. The stability of the system is proved by Lyapunov's second method. A new method is adopted to obtain the analytical expression of the state error by solving the fractional differential equation, and then the finite time convergence of the system is proved. The simulation results show that the controller has good robustness and better convergence than the existing fractional order and integer order sliding mode attitude controller.

articleTitle: A Multi-objective Evolutionary Algorithm Based on Q-learning for Adaptive Reference Vectors and Partition Deletion Strategy
abstract: The performance of decomposition algorithms is highly sensitive to the shape of the Pareto front, as the predefined reference vectors may not always be adapted to various problem characteristics without prior knowledge. Moreover, as the number of optimization objectives increases, the objective space will be filled with a large number of non-dominated solutions, making it difficult to compare their quality. To address these issues, this paper proposes a decomposition algorithm based on an adaptive reference vector Q-learning with partition deletion strategy (RVQP) approach. The proposed method consists of three main operations: a reinforcement Q-learning (RQ) operation, a reference point sampling operation, and a partition deletion operation. The RQ operation considers the adaptive process of reference vectors as a reinforcement learning task, assisting the reference vectors in learning from the environment and selecting action plans based on optimal features. The reference point sampling operation generates new reference vectors using a distributed model. The partition deletion strategy is employed in environmental selection to eliminate inferior individuals, thereby increasing selection pressure. Experimental results comparing the proposed algorithm with typical problems and classical algorithms have validated its competitiveness and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Q-learning-based space target selection for CNS/INS integrated navigation
abstract: To solve the problem that intermittent celestial observation will hamper the navigation accuracy of celestial and inertial integrated navigation system (CNS/INS), a Q-learning-based space target selection method is proposed. The visibility situation of space targets is analyzed under given flight mission, which lays the foundation for subsequent pointing optimization. Q-learning algorithm is employed to optimize the sequence of visible space target. The reward function is designed based on the trace of Fisher information matrix and the rotation angle of optical axis which could make a synthetic balance between navigation accuracy and rotation cost. By setting the optimized pointing sequence to CNS/INS integrated navigation system, unintermittent celestial observation can be achieved to guarantee filtering performance with relatively low rotation cost, which has a certain value of practical engineering application. Comparative simulation experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of navigation accuracy and rotation cost.

articleTitle: A Distributed Energy Sharing Framework for Communities with PV Prosumers and Aggregate EV Prosumers
abstract: Under the energy policy that encourages local consumption of renewable energy, energy sharing between neighboring prosumers is more effective compared with the case of independent operation of each prosumer. This paper proposes a new energy sharing framework of community prosumers, considering that the energy sharing operator (ESO) is equipped with two types of energy storage devices (batteries and powerto-gas devices) and the two types of prosumers (photovoltaic prosumers and aggregate electric vehicle prosumers) have both electricity and hydrogen loads. The Stackelberg game framework is designed with the ESO as leader and the two types of prosumers as followers. The ESO aims to maximize its revenue and coordinate the energy sharing between community prosumers by setting dynamic electricity prices. Each prosumer maximizes its payoff through optimal response. A distributed bi-level iterative algorithm is designed to solve the Stackelberg game equilibrium strategy, which can protect the privacy information of prosumers effectively. Simulation results are provided to show that the proposed community prosumer energy sharing framework can not only increase the benefits of the ESO and all prosumers, but also reduce the load pressure of the main grid.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation and Optimization of Cold Tandem Rolling Thickness and Tension Control Based on Subspace LQG Benchmark
abstract: In the cold tandem rolling production process, thickness and tension control systems are essential. However, factors such as changes in production conditions and lack of maintenance can degrade the performance of these systems. To monitor the operation of controllers in real time, this paper introduces a performance monitoring algorithm based on the subspace Linear Quadratic Gaussian (LQG) benchmark. First, we use subspace identification algorithms to process historical rolling mill data to obtain subspace matrices and design a subspace-based LQG thickness-tension predictive controller performance evaluation benchmark. Next, the controller parameters of cold tandem rolling are optimized using particle swarm optimization, enhancing the overall system level. Finally, we evaluate the frame predictive controller online by solving real-time performance indicators of cold tandem rolling and comparing them with the established performance benchmark. Experiments prove that the subspace performance evaluation algorithm can accurately represent the performance level of the control system and effectively monitor controller performance changes.

articleTitle: Knowledge graph embedding model based on multi-hop adaptive graph attention network
abstract: Knowledge graphs use graphs to represent multi-relational data. Graph attention networks have recently demonstrated remarkable efficacy in predicting connections within knowledge graphs. The focus of graph attention networks is restricted to the embedded information from nodes that are first-order neighbors. To obtain multi-order neighbor information, existing works usually use superimposed multi-layer graph attention networks to achieve the purpose of aggregating multi-order neighbor information. However, this methodology could lead to a homogenization of node features in the knowledge graph, thereby posing challenges to the differentiation of features among nodes. We introduce an approach that employs a multi-hop graph attention network to integrate relationships between nodes across multiple hops and entity details, viewing the combined features of nodes from different orders as temporal sequences. The gating mechanism inherent in Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks is utilized to selectively distill and refine the feature information of nodes. The effectiveness of our model is substantiated through evaluations on popular benchmark datasets, with the experimental findings revealing its superior predictive accuracy in knowledge graph link prediction compared to extant models.

articleTitle: Detection of Faults and Attacks in Power Monitoring System via Semi-Supervised Learning with Pseudo Label Refinery
abstract: With the expansion of power grids and incorporation of new energy sources, fault and attack detection in power monitoring systems has become increasingly vital for maintaining grid stability and safety. A significant challenge for data-driven detection methods is the scarcity of labeled measurement data, which critically hampers their detection performance. This paper proposes a novel data-driven framework, SuPer, for detecting faults and attacks in power monitoring systems. SuPer employs a novel combination of self-adaptive thresholding-based pseudolabeling and prototype-based data purification strategies, which have superior detection performance under conditions of scarcity labeled data. SuPer generates reliable pseudo-labels for massive unlabeled measurements and selects the high-confidence ones to participate in the training process, which enhances the machine learning model’s ability to identify anomalies accurately. Extensive experiments are conducted in a power system framework to demonstrate SuPer’s effectiveness, particularly highlighting its improved performance in scenarios with limited labeled data.

articleTitle: Ground Mirror Simulation System Based on Digital Twins: Concept, Development and Prospects
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, big data, internet of things, cloud computing and other technologies, digital twin, parallel system and other new generation simulation technologies have became a research hotspot in the field of intelligent manufacturing, complex system management and control. It has been widely concerned by researchers in many industries such as aerospace, shipping, power, medical, and smart cities. This report will discuss the ground image simulation technology based on digital twin. Firstly, the development of digital twin technology and parallel simulation technology are introduced. Then, the concepts and key technologies of digital twin technology and ground image simulation technology are introduced respectively. Finally, according to the previous research work, this paper describes the idea of promoting the research of digital twin in the control system simulation test system. This report can provide support and reference for broadening the vision of simulation profession and doing well in the preliminary research and engineering application of simulation profession.

articleTitle: Robust Multimodal Place Recognition through Intensity Information from LiDAR
abstract: Place recognition tasks are essential for robot perception and navigation as they help eliminate cumulative errors in long-term robot pose estimation. Typically, when using LiDAR for position recognition tasks, the focus has primarily been on its three-dimensional features, often overlooking the embedded image features. To fully leverage the multimodal data of LiDAR, this paper proposes a unified place recognition method specifically designed to extract both image and three-dimensional features from LiDAR. The approach combines bag-of-words vectors with intensity scan context to accurately calculate similarity scores for candidate frames. Subsequently, this paper employs a particle filter method for fusion estimation, amalgamating candidate frames from multimodal features to determine the ultimate closed-loop candidate frame. In comparison to other methods, the approach increases the number of closed-loop candidate detections while maintaining a higher level of accuracy. Furthermore, the precision-recall curve consistently maintains the highest average precision compared to single-feature methods.

articleTitle: FGD Process Identification: An Information-theoretic Convolution Network Learning Approach
abstract: Nowadays flue gas desulphurization (FGD) technologies have been extensively applied in the coal-fired electricity-generating plants. As emission standards for sulfur dioxide (SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) have become more stringent in recent years, there is a real need to develop more advanced modeling techniques such that the FGD process can be identified accurately, which in turn provides a reliable foundation for FGD process control and optimization. However, FGD process has characteristics of large time delay, strongly nonlinear dynamics, making traditional identification models become ineffectual. To address this issue, this paper proposes a hybrid model consisting of information-theoretic technique and convolution neural network (CNN). To verify the proposed identification approach, a real FGD system of a 600MW coal-fired power station is selected as case analysis. Experimental results indicate that our model achieves satisfactory identification result and performs better than other popular FGD models appeared in previous studies, demonstrating the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed MI-CNN model.

articleTitle: Research on real-time performance of 5G AGV remote control network
abstract: To improve the real-time performance of automated guided vehicle (AGV) remote control, a 5G end-to-end real-time network performance study was conducted. This paper designs a communication architecture between AGV and the 5G network, builds a 5G network communication environment for remote control of AGV, creates a 5G end-to-end simulation model, and analyzes the composition and causes of 5G link delay. The 5G network performance indicators were verified through 5G link simulation experiments based on MATLAB, and the uplink pre-scheduling method was used to reduce latency. Finally, the AGV remote control was used to physically verify the feasibility of the uplink pre-scheduling approach. The experimental results show that the real-time performance of the 5G network can be improved by turning on the uplink pre-scheduling process and provide a valuable technical research direction for remote control of AGVs in industrial 5G logistics scenarios.

articleTitle: Focus on Complex Background and Multi-Scale Remote Sensing Images Objects Detection
abstract: Remote Sensing images are characterized by multi-scale objects and complex background compared with ordinary natural images. Due to the existence of large size objects and small size objects of remote sensing images, and the problem of imbalance between foreground and background information, it has always been a bottleneck to improve the accuracy of object detection in visible remote sensing images. This paper proposes a detection DA-DET, it contains ResNet-DCN module and Augment-FPN module. Compared with other detectors, DA-DET can extract object features better. ResNet-DCN can extract the features of the object and neglect background information, in addition, Augment-FPN can fusion of low-level spatial feature information with high-level semantic feature information. Specifically, the images is fed into the detection, ResNet-DCN can extract more information on object features and Augment-FPN can fully fuse feature information. Verify the validity of the method in the experiments.

articleTitle: Fully Actuated System Approach to Attitude Stabilization Control of Robot Manipulator
abstract: In this paper, a high-order fully actuated (HOFA) system approach is proposed for the attitude stabilization problem of robotic manipulators. Different from most existing results, the proposed method guarantees a linear time-invariant closed-loop system with arbitrarily assignable eigenvalues. Firstly, the HOFA model for the attitude system is derived from the original dynamic equations. Then, by using the fully actuated characteristics of the obtained HOFA system, the nonlinearity in the system is completely canceled and a linear time-invariant system with arbitrarily assignable eigenvalues is derived. Finally, the control law is designed for the problem of attitude stabilization, and simulations are carried out based on practical engineering parameters, which demonstrate the effects of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Trajectory Tracking Control For Quadrotors Based On The Feedback Of Wind-Vortex Parameters Control Model
abstract: The downwash airflow generated by the rotor of a quadcopter will create "wind-vortex" on the canopy of plants, and the wind-vortex parameters to some extent represent the deposition effect of pesticides. These wind-vortex parameters correspond to the flight parameters, and to achieve real-time and fast-tracking of the flight velocity and altitude of the unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) during pesticide spraying, and thus to achieve good spraying effects, a sliding mode trajectory tracking control scheme based on the feedback of wind-vortex parameters control model is proposed. First, a set of wind-vortex images is identified using the YOLOV3-tiny model to obtain the corresponding wind-vortex parameters. Then, the wind-vortex parameters are converted into UAV flight parameters through the wind-vortex parameter control model. Finally, adaptive sliding mode control is used in the position loop and sliding mode controller with extended state observer (ESO) is used in the attitude loop for fast-tracking of flight parameters. Simulation results show that the designed controller has high tracking accuracy and good anti-disturbance capability, and can effectively control the altitude and velocity of the agricultural UAVs.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal dynamics optimization of a Gierer-Meinhardt system based on PD control strategy
abstract: The dynamic control of ordinary differential systems has yielded fruitful results, but the spatiotemporal control of partial differential systems is still a problem to be solved. The Gierer-Meinhardt system is a partial differential system that has been extensively studied in reaction-diffusion theory. It can plausibly explain many phenomena in biology and chemistry. In this paper we investigate the effect of PD controller on the dynamics of spatiotemporal evolution of the Gierer-Meinhardt system. The conditions under which Turing instability occurs before and after the Gierer-Meinhardt system is controlled are obtained by linear stability analysis. Numerical simulations show that PD controller promotes the occurrence of Turing instability in the Gierer-Meinhardt system. Furthermore, it can change the spatial structure and speed up the formation of Turing pattrens.

articleTitle: Research on the optimization and configuration of integrated photovoltaic and energy storage systems in smart buildings considering the lifecycle costs
abstract: With the increasing global demand for sustainable development and energy efficiency, the optimization and intelligent configuration of building energy systems have become key to achieving sustainable development goals. This paper establishes a solid theoretical foundation for integrated photovoltaic and energy storage system configuration based on analysis. Firstly, a photovoltaic power station in a northern region is selected for load data analysis to determine the photovoltaic capacity and energy storage capacity. Secondly, considering the photovoltaic consumption rate and system operating costs, optimization objectives, constraints, and battery parameters are established. Based on this, an improved algorithm is used to optimize the capacity allocation of mixed energy sources throughout the lifecycle of the integrated photovoltaic and energy storage system in buildings. The effectiveness and rationality of the model are verified through case studies.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis for a Delayed Lotka-Volterra System with Harvesting and Stocking Rates in Parameter Space
abstract: In this paper, we focus on the stability of a delayed Lotka-Volterra type predator-prey system with harvesting rate K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and stocking rate K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. All the system parameters (K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) and the delay τ are treated as free parameters. Our objective is to study the stability in the entire (K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, τ)-space. First, we consider the case when (K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) is fixed and analyze the stability along the whole τ axis. Such a problem, which is called the complete stability problem w.r.t. delay, can be solved by addressing the corresponding auxiliary characteristic roots. The stability analysis is then extended to the scenario with additional free system parameters (K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). We can study the complete real root classification for the auxiliary characteristic equation. As a result, we are able to characterize the stability property over the entire (K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, τ)-space. The approach presented in this paper provides a new way to design (K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) such that the system is in a stable state. Finally, some representative examples are given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach.

articleTitle: Design of Electric Power Supply and Distribution System for Smart Park
abstract: With the rapid development of smart parks, higher requirements have been put forward for the electric power supply of smart parks. Adequate and high-quality electricity is the guarantee for the stable operation of smart parks. In order to improve the rationality and reliability of the electric power supply and distribution system configuration, this article takes a certain technology industry park project as an example to elaborate on the design concept, ideas, and schemes of the electric power supply and distribution system, providing some reference for similar projects.

articleTitle: Linear Quadratic Optimal Control of Itô Stochastic Systems with Wiener and Poisson Noises
abstract: This paper investigates the infinite horizon optimal control problem for a class of continuous-time Itô stochasticˆ systems subject to continuous Wiener and discontinuous Poisson noises. Firstly, a stochastic algebraic Riccati equation (SARE) with Poisson jump intensity is provided for the concerned systems. Secondly, a numerical iterative algorithm is developed to converge the solution of the proposed SARE, and a new policy iterative algorithm, which depends only on the partial system dynamics, is designed by using the integral reinforcement learning method. In addition, a new algorithm is proposed to compute the maximum Poisson jump intensity under different the convergence accuracy of the proposed numerical and policy iterative algorithms. Finally, an actual example is given to illustrate the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed algorithms.

articleTitle: Fish Length Estimation Based on Stereo Vision and Keypoint Detection
abstract: Fish length information is of great significance in aquaculture. However, traditional fish length measurement methods are not only time-consuming and labor-intensive but can also impact fish growth. Therefore, this paper proposes an automatic non-contact fish length measurement system based on stereo vision and keypoint detection. The process begins with the calibration of the stereo images. The rectified left image is input into the YOLOv7 network to detect fish suitable for length measurement. The detected fish are then passed through an improved HRNet (FPN-HRNet) to identify key points on the fish in the image. Using the coordinates of these key points and corresponding disparity values, 3D spatial coordinates are calculated. To reduce the occurrence of significant errors in fish length measurements due to inaccuracies in the 3D coordinates of keypoints, a curve fitting is applied to these spatial coordinate points. After fitting, the spatial distances between these points are calculated to obtain the fish length. The experimental results show that the average relative error of length measurement is 3.01%, which indicates that the proposed fish length measurement system can accurately and reliably measure the length of fish.

articleTitle: Security Control for Cyber-Physical Systems Under Event-Triggered Mechanism
abstract: This paper studies the effective and secure control of cyber-physical systems under False-data-injection attacks. In order to mitigate the attacks against the actuators of the cyber-physical systems, we propose a security control algorithm that combines event-triggered mechanism and active mobile target defense. Firstly, the system is modeled as a switching system composed of multiple controllable subsystems, and then the system structure is changed using random switching to enhance the unpredictability of the system, making it difficult for attackers to invade. In addition, the proposed event-triggered mechanism reduces communication costs while ensuring system stability. Finally, the effectiveness of the security control algorithm was verified through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Distributed Model Predictive Control for Vehicle Platooning with Intermittent Communication
abstract: The problem of distributed cooperative control of vehicle platoon is addressed, subject to irregular time-varying delays and possible information losses in the communication links among the vehicles. Our control objective is to drive the vehicles to reach a line formation with the desired spacing while moving forward according to the platoon leader’s velocity. Firstly, we propose an intermittent communication algorithm to obtain a reference velocity for vehicle tracking. Secondly, we use a DMPC strategy to track the reference velocity for achieving the control objective of the vehicle formation. Finally, the paper concludes by illustrating the applicability and effectiveness of our proposal through simulated experiments over PF communication topology.

articleTitle: An optimized fusion algorithm for an inertial-based integrated navigation system under fault
abstract: In inertial-based integrated navigation systems, the outputs of auxiliary systems are often affected by faults. However, the traditional fault diagnosis algorithms that isolated faulty subsystems or measurements were weak for small-amplitude or slow-changing faults which were caused by disturbed environments, which essentially introduced faults into the navigation results. To improve the accuracy of the inertial-based integrated navigation system under disturbance faults, an optimized algorithm for multi-sensor fusion is proposed. The fault statistic of the aided navigation information is calculated using the state chi-square test. Then, a fault-threshold ratio is constructed by combining the detection threshold and the lower bound. The fault-threshold ratios are normalized by integrating the fault analysis of all subsystems. The results are utilized as the coefficients for sub-filters, weighting the variance of state estimation after a measurement update. Finally, the algorithm is tested offline in a street scenario. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can reduce the positioning error mean by 75.7% compared with the none-detection mode.

articleTitle: Interless: Interference-Aware Deep Resource Prediction for Serverless Computing
abstract: Serverless is an emerging cloud computing paradigm that allows functions to share resources. However, function resource sharing introduces interference, which results in performance degradation. Existing resource prediction approaches ignore the function instance placement and interference between functions. Thus, they cannot predict the resource finely. This paper proposes Interless, an interference-aware resource prediction system for serverless computing with a sequence-to-sequence neural network. The Interless’s encoder directly learns function instance interference by the TPA-LSTM module. TPA-LSTM can also capture historical request queuing for better prediction. Interless’s decoder contains a GRU module for long-time series prediction. Long-time prediction is essential for time reservation in function scheduling and warm-up. Moreover, long-time series prediction helps Interless identify system anomalies and cyber threats by comparing monitored and predicted resource consumption. We implement Interless on top of Docker Swarm as a serverless system for resource prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that Interless reduces the MAPE, RSE, and SMAPE of prediction by 64%, 58%, and 65%, respectively, compared to the state-of-the-arts.

articleTitle: Multi-agent Consensus Research Based on Differential Privacy Gaussian Mechanism
abstract: This paper investigates a class of first-order discrete-time multi-agent systems (MASs) that maintain (ϵ, δ)- differentially private. Firstly, we introduce function-generated noise to agents to obscure information, safeguarding the privacy of agents against adversaries’ attacks. Secondly, Conditions for achieving mean-square consensus of the MASs in the presence of added noise are explored, ensuring convergence of agents’ states to the mean of initial states. Thirdly, (ϵ, δ)-differential privacy for the MASs is achieved by optimizing or adjusting parameters of the Gaussian mechanism. Finally, the validation of the proposed methods is demonstrated through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Research and Simulation Analysis on Path Planning of Sampling Robot Based on Mineral Sampling
abstract: The sampling of mineral samples in the field is an important basic work. Due to the large amount of related sampling work, the manual sampling has the problems of low efficiency and high labor cost. The research of mineral sampling robot has important basic research value. Taking mineral sampling as the research object, this paper studies and analyzes the path planning of sampling robot by using MATLAB to simulate the environmental map of field sampling. Through simulation experiments and data analysis, using the path planning of ant colony algorithm, the sampling robot based on mineral sampling in this paper can realize the sampling of single point mineral samples and multi-point mineral samples, and shows good rapidity and efficiency, which ensures that the sampling path of the robot is relatively optimal, and provides better application basic research for the research of mineral sampling robot.

articleTitle: Early Fault Detection in Distribution Networks Based on Wavelet Packets and Anomaly Transformer
abstract: Given the escalating complexity of operations in distribution networks, the formidable challenge of early fault detection persists. This study proposes an anomaly detection algorithm that integrates wavelet packet data processing and an Anomaly Transformer structure. Initially, the wavelet packet algorithm is applied to remove large amplitudes, high-frequency harmonics, and easily reconfigurable components from the raw data, emphasizing fault characteristics. Subsequently, the Anomaly Attention algorithm model, based on the Transformer architecture, is used to assign weights to the most critical features through matrix calculations. The prior-association and series-association of each time point in the voltage and current time series signals are calculated. The association discrepancy values between prior-association and series-association are utilized to assess abnormal conditions within the distribution network. Finally, an IEEE-33 node microgrid model is developed using the MATLAB/Simulink simulation platform for experimental validation. The results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves high accuracy in early fault detection within distribution networks.

articleTitle: Adaptive Robust Anti-disturbance Synchronization for Leader-follower Ships under Cyber-attacks
abstract: This paper investigates the synchronization control problem of follower ship during underway replenishment. Solving the problem of the time-varying gain caused by cyber-attacks and disturbance compensation is the key to ensure safe synchronization of follower ship. Firstly, the disturbance observer is designed to provide time-varying disturbance estimates in the ocean, and the adaptive law is constructed to update the unknown control parameters in real time. Secondly, the anti-disturbance tracking controller for synchronization is designed by combining the disturbance observer with the vector backstepping technique. Finally, simulations are conducted on a 1:70 scale model ship. The results show that the anti-disturbance tracking controller can realize the synchronization navigation between the follower ship and the leader ship, and all signals in the closed-loop synchronization tracking control system are global uniform ultimate boundedness.

articleTitle: RTPR-DETR : A Real Time Small Object Detection Network Based on Partial-Convolution with structural re-parameterization
abstract: To address the issue of high parameter and computational requirements in current drone target detection, a lightweight small object detection network for drone aerial images is proposed. Firstly, through simple experiments, the differences in parameter and computational requirements of various convolution operations are analyzed. The PConv (Partial Convolution) is then introduced to replace the convolution operations in RT-DETR. This replacement reduces the computational and parameter requirements of the model while maintaining its accuracy. Secondly, structural re-parameterization and multi-scale attention are incorporated into the backbone network to enhance feature extraction, thereby improving the model’s accuracy in detecting small objects. Lastly, considering the dominance of small objects in drone images, the IoU loss function is modified to Inner-MPDIoU loss, which increases the contribution of loss for small objects and further improves small object detection performance. According to the experimental results on the VisDrone dataset, there is a significant improvement in comparison to the original RT-DETR-r18 model, the proposed model achieves a reduction of 29.4% in model parameters, a decrease of 28.5% in model size, a decrease of 24.6% in GFLOPs, an increase of 3.1% in mAP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf>, an increase of 2.5% in mAP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50:95</inf>, and an FPS (Frames Per Second) of up to 65.7.

articleTitle: Structure Design and Kinematics Analysis and Experiment of Rope-driven Continuum Robot
abstract: In this paper, aiming at the charging scenario of new energy vehicles, a rope-driven continuous robot structure is designed. Combining the modeling methods of flexible robot and winding rigid robot, a kinematic model of rod-driven continuum robot is established, and a method to solve its inverse kinematics is designed according to the pose of the target point given by the continuum robot in the actual scene. A numerical analysis method based on Newton-Raphson method is designed to solve the complex inverse kinematics evaluation problem. The calculated Angle is substituted into the forward kinematics of the continuum robot and the transformation relationship between the driving rope length, and the change of the driving rope length is obtained, so as to achieve the target pose of the robot driven by the driving rope. Through experiments and modeling, the actual results of experimental calculation on a rope-driven continuum robot with a total length of 990mm were compared with the results of kinematics modeling to prove the feasibility of the method. The driving rope can control the continuum robot to achieve the target pose.

articleTitle: Optimization of Hydrogen Containing Integrated Energy System Operation Considering Demand Response and Ladder-type Carbon Trading
abstract: The coastal refining and chemical industrial park possesses ample resources for renewable energy power generation, exhibits a consistent need for concentrated hydrogen, and demonstrates a high level of energy coupling. Consequently, it exhibits significant potential for demand response. This paper presents a novel optimization approach for managing the operation of a integrated energy system that incorporates hydrogen, taking into account complete demand response and ladder-type carbon trading. The proposed method aims to address the hydrogen demand and carbon reduction requirements of a comprehensive industrial park. To begin, it is important to develop a prototypical energy system model for coastal refining and chemical industrial parks. Furthermore, it is important to examine the methods by which the parks engage in carbon trading and implement a hierarchical model for carbon trading mechanisms. Thirdly, considering the price elasticity factor and the incentive effect of subsidies, a integrated demand response model for the park is established. Subsequently, the economic operation objective incorporates the carbon quota transaction cost and park demand response cost. The CPLEX solver is employed to solve the model and derive the economic operation outcomes of the system. In this study, a numerical analysis was performed to validate the economic and low-carbon characteristics of the optimization outcomes, using a coastal chemical park located in eastern China as a case study.

articleTitle: Abnormal object detection model of transmission line corridors based on improved YOLOv5
abstract: Power transmission lines are highly susceptible to environmental factors. In order to ensure the reliability and stability of the power system, it is necessary to detect the risks present in the lines in a timely manner. Due to the complex background of transmission line corridors and the large number of small objects to be detected, existing object detection methods suffer from problems such as low detection accuracy and high false-negative and false-positive rates. In order to solve the above problems, this paper proposes an improved You Only Look Once (YOLO) v5s: Firstly, by adding Efficient Channel Attention Neural Networks (ECA-Net) and combining it with the C3 module, the network’s feature extraction ability is improved, and the object prediction is avoided to be interfered by the complex environment; Secondly, to reduce the rate of false negatives and false positives of small targets, the SPD-Conv module has been added. Thirdly, replacing the detection header with the reparameterisation align decoupled head. It resolves the conflict between classification and regression tasks and addresses the issue of misalignment between two branching tasks that arises due to the lack of a connection between them. The results of the experiment demonstrate that the model proposed in this paper effectively enhances the recall rate and average precision mean. On the anomalous object dataset of external damage to transmission line corridors, mAP@0.5 improved by 1.0%, recall by 2.8% and mAP@0.5:0.95 by 1.8%. For early warning systems, the importance of recall is obvious, so the improved model has a better application.

articleTitle: Robust Hybrid Intelligent Control Using Probabilistic Feature for Active Power Filter
abstract: The escalating harmonic issues in the power grid pose a significant threat to the stability and security of the power system. While active power filter (APF) is a dependable solution for harmonic suppression, they grapple with challenges related to uncertainties in control design. Addressing this concern, an enhanced terminal sliding mode control (TSMC) scheme is proposed for APF, leveraging a probabilistic wavelet fuzzy neural network (PWFNN). Initially, the dynamic model of APF, accounting for external disturbances and component parameter perturbations, is derived based on its internal structure. Subsequently, TSMC is applied to APF, and its stability and finite-time convergence are demonstrated through Lyapunov theory. Additionally, a PWFNN, integrating probabilistic features to augment wavelet neural networks, is constructed to approximate uncertain functions, with adaptive laws governing network parameters. Simulation results validate that PWFNN outperforms in harmonic suppression.

articleTitle: Three-phase Inverter Open Circuit Cross-Domain Fault Detection Based on Inception-DANN
abstract: The inverter is one of the most important components in photovoltaic and wind power generation systems, and its stability is crucial to the smooth operation of the system. Power devices are the most fragile components in the inverter. Fault diagnosis and timely processing can greatly improve the reliability of the power generation system. Existing data-driven fault diagnosis methods are designed based on fixed working conditions. Once the system parameters change, the diagnosis accuracy will significantly decrease. To solve these problems, this study proposes a three-phase inverter open circuit fault diagnosis method based on domain adversarial neural network. This method selects the three-phase inverter phase voltage as the input signal, improves the convolutional neural network through the Inception structure, and then uses the domain adversarial neural network to learn domain invariant features. Finally, the diagnosis results are obtained based on the output of the fault classifier. Experimental results show that in transfer diagnosis tasks across different systems, the method achieves an average diagnosis accuracy of 95.01% and exhibits robustness in various noisy environments.

articleTitle: Architecture Design and Implementation of Digital Twin System of Hot Rolling Process
abstract: Hot rolling process is the key process of steel production. Due to the characteristics of high temperature, continuity, high real-time and uncertainty of the process, it is very difficult to schedule the production process of hot rolling. The traditional methods based on mathematical models and algorithm can not meet the actual production needs. Digital twin technology provides a new technology for the transformation and upgrading of traditional industries to intelligent manufacturing. In this paper, the architecture, digital twin models, numerical simulation analysis and data interface of digital twin system are proposed for hot rolling process of steel products. The digital twin system was implemented by using augmented reality (AR) technology and Unity 3D to improve the immersion and information perception. Based on the background of a Chinese hot rolling production line, the function of digital twin system is verified. The experimental results show that the visual modeling technology based on augmented reality is feasible and the digital twin system is correct and reliable. The architecture scheme and implementation technology of the digital twin system have good research significance and application value.

articleTitle: Lightweight Neural Network for Highway Toll Vehicle Classification
abstract: With the continuous development of computer vision technology, transportation systems are gradually approaching intelligence. This article proposes a lightweight neural network for highway toll vehicle classification, which can replace manual judgment of toll vehicle types. It is compared and validated with other object detection algorithms on the Beijing Hong Kong Macao Expressway dataset. The results show that the method proposed in this article has higher real-time performance and accuracy.

articleTitle: Data-driven Modeling of Comprehensive Academic Level and Physical/Moral Education for Students in Control Discipline
