However, in complicated real-world scenarios, the feature information based on intra-epipolar line alone is too weak to facilitate stereo matching. In this paper, we present a simple but highly effective network called Alternated Attention U-shaped Transformer (AAUformer) to balance the impact of epipolar line in dual and single view respectively for excellent generalization performance. Compared to other models, our model has several main designs: 1) to better liberate the local semantic features of the single-view at pixel level, we introduce window self-attention to break the limits of intra-row self-attention and completely replace the convolutional network for denser features before cross-matching; 2) the multi-scale alternated attention backbone network was designed to extract invariant features in order to achieves the coarse-to-fine matching process for hard-to-discriminate regions. We performed a series of both comparative studies and ablation studies on several mainstream stereo matching datasets. The results demonstrate that our model achieves state-of-the-art on the Scene Flow dataset, and the fine-tuning performance is competitive on the KITTI 2015 dataset. In addition, for cross generalization experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, our model outperforms several state-of-the-art works.

articleTitle: Pricing and coordination in a supply chain with risk aversion under cost uncertainty
abstract: This paper investigates the effects of risk aversion on the optimal prices and supply chain (SC) coordination under cost uncertainty. In the SC, the manufacturer and the retailer are the Stackelberg leader and the follower, respectively. The risk-neutral and risk-averse scenarios are studied and then the equilibrium solutions are derived and compared. Finally, a revenue sharing (RS) contract is proposed to coordinate the SC. It is shown that risk aversion has a negative effect on the wholesale price and the retail price; Risk aversion makes all the utilities of the manufacturer, the retailer, and the SC decrease; The SC can be coordinated to the centralized level if the retailer shares its revenues with the manufacturer and the fixed compensation satisfies a certain condition.

articleTitle: Surface Defect Detection on Steel Plates Based on Improved Unet Network
abstract: In the steel manufacturing process, various defects may arise in steel plates due to inadequate manufacturing processes. To address issues such as low accuracy and missed detections during the inspection process, this paper proposes an enhanced Unet model for surface defect detection. Firstly, the model incorporates the Global Context (GC) module, replacing traditional skip connections, thereby enhancing the model's perception of features at different scales and levels to improve segmentation performance. Secondly, to tackle the challenges of sample imbalance and uneven defect areas, a composite loss function is designed for training, comprising Focal loss, Tversky loss, and BCEWithLogitsLoss. This addresses sample imbalance and the difficulty in segmenting small regions. The results demonstrate that our model outperforms traditional Segnet, Fcn, and Unet models in terms of accuracy and segmentation metrics, including IOU and Dice coefficients.

articleTitle: Image Deblurring Method Based On Simplified Gated Activation Network
abstract: The camera will produce a large number of low-quality images under extreme or improper operation conditions, image deblurring is an effective solution, but the existing SOTA methods seek to restore spatial details, ignoring the increasing computational cost. In this paper, we propose a Simplified Gated Activation Network (SGANet), which adopts the U-Net-shaped deep auto-encoder structure as a whole, and uses skip connection between encoders and decoders to transmit and fuse the feature information of different scales. In the detail part, Gated Linear Unit (GLU) is simplified by using channel split technology and depthwise separable convolution, the nonlinear expression ability of the model is enhanced at the same time, so as to achieve a high level in balancing complexity and image deblurring performance. We use two methods to verify the effectiveness of SGANet, one is to evaluate the PSNR index of the model on the baseline dataset (GoPro), and the other is to compare the performance difference between original image and deblurred image in object detection task. Therefore, we also make a blurred images dataset in semi-structured road scene for experiment. Experimental results show that the deblurring performance of our model surpasses many excellent methods, and the computational cost is greatly reduced.

articleTitle: Deep Bayesian Forest Fusion Ensembled Algorithm
abstract: Currently, the conventional deep-ensemble modeling approach faces several challenges, including intricate computations, diminished accuracy, and inadequate generalization performance. In response, this study introduces the Deep Bayesian Forest Fusion Ensembled (DBFE) modeling method. Firstly, a comprehensive model comprising layered forests is devised, utilizing binary trees renowned for their strong interpretability. Concurrently, Bayesian inference is employed as a performance screening criterion to evaluate the fitness of the individual-layer forest models, yielding the layered forest model. Subsequently, the Mahalanobis distance between the single-layer predictions and the ground truth is computed to ascertain adherence to predefined disparity thresholds. Should these thresholds be satisfied, the reconstituted dataset is forwarded to the subsequent layer; conversely, construction ceases and output is generated. Finally, leveraging the weights of the sub-models, the impact of each sub-model's predictions on the ensemble model prediction is assessed, thereby effectuating the ensemble model's prediction. The efficacy of the proposed method is corroborated through validation against benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: NFC controller-based hybrid structural vibration control in offshore wind power systems
abstract: The simulation-based research approach is used to simulate, analyze, and experimentally verify the vibration suppression and load shedding performance of the active-passive hybrid control device using a 5 MW barge-type wind power system as the research object. The findings demonstrate that, in comparison to passive control, the active-passive hybrid structure control system based on the NFC algorithm achieves good stability control and large-scale sway suppression, making it more suitable for the offshore wind power technology engineering application.

articleTitle: Research on DC Bus Voltage Regulation in Islanded and Grid-Connected Modes of Hybrid Microgrid
abstract: As environmental and energy issues become increasingly prominent, the penetration rate of new energy distributed power generation is also increasing. In the operation process of new energy AC-DC hybrid microgrid, improving the stability of DC bus voltage is of great research significance. This paper takes the AC-DC hybrid microgrid composed of photovoltaic power generation units, battery energy storage units, loads and DC/DC converters as the research object. In the off-grid operation mode, the entire system is divided into two operating modes according to the DC bus voltage; in the grid-connected operation mode, the entire system is divided into two operating modes according to the battery SoC (State of Charge). Study different control strategies in different working modes. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy was verified through simulation.

articleTitle: Design of UAV manipulator system based on active disturbance rejection control
abstract: This paper elaborates the design of a control system for a flying manipulator, consisting of an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) with a 3-link arm. We introduce a cascaded active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) methodology, where both position and attitude of UAV are governed through the active disturbance rejection control strategy. In order to enable the UAV to perform aerial object grasping, we employ a recurrent neural network approach for inverse kinematics calculations of the manipulator. The movement of the manipulator generates disturbance forces and torques that impact the position and attitude of the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV), therefore, it becomes imperative to conceive and implement a cascaded Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC) system to effectively mitigate these disturbances. In this paper, comprehensive simulation experiments have been conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology. The experiments serve to demonstrate the ability of the cascaded Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC) in proficiently attenuating disturbances stemming from manipulator motion. Additionally, the recurrent neural network approach efficiently and accurately computes the manipulator’s inverse kinematics. The results show the method’s remarkable robustness and control accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on Earth Observation Satellite Scheduling based on Deep Reinforcement Learning and Rule Method
abstract: Scheduling Earth observation satellites is a challenging multiple constraint combinatorial optimization issue. Target sequencing and establishing the observation time are the two components of Earth observation satellite scheduling. In this paper, a Markov Decision Process is used to model the satellite observation process, and the scheduling goal is to maximize the total profit rate. To implement target selection and sequencing, a scheduling decision model is built and trained by the deep reinforcement learning algorithm, and the observation time is determined using the earliest possible observation time rule approach. Experiments are conducted on randomly generated data, and the results show that the scheduling decision model is feasible and has the same effectiveness with unknown data.

articleTitle: Improved Fall-down Detection Algorithm: FE-YOLO
abstract: To address the concerns regarding dataset completeness and detection speed for common fall injuries in the elderly, a comprehensive dataset has been established. Additionally, a lightweight fall detection model named FE-YOLO, which is based on YOLOv8, has been developed. This model replaces the network’s internal feature extraction module with a more efficient Fasternet Block module and introduces an enhanced detection head that utilizes data sharing and grouped convolution techniques. When compared to the YOLOv8n model, the FE-YOLO model demonstrates a reduction in parameters by 43.1%, a decrease in GFLOPs by 51.9%, an improvement in model inference speed by 9.70%, and an increase in FPS by 10.5%. Notably, these enhancements do not significantly impact the average accuracy of the model. The efficiency of the FE-YOLO model renders it suitable for deployment on devices with limited computing power.

articleTitle: Output Ripple Suppression for LLC Resonant Converter
abstract: The nonlinear characteristics and pulse frequency modulation operation of the LLC converter give rise to diverse operating modes and characteristics across different frequencies. This intricacy heightens the challenges associated with modeling, analysis, and the design of control strategies for LLC converters. Concerning control strategies, conventional PI controllers exhibit inadequate responses to input voltage ripple disturbances and sudden changes in input voltage. Additionally, significant input voltage ripple leads to substantial twice-line-frequency ripple in the LLC converter’s output. The presence of excessive ripple current can result in elevated battery charging temperatures, diminishing charging efficiency, and shortening battery lifespan. In pursuit of enhancing battery charging quality, this study proposes a control strategy that amalgamates input voltage ripple feedforward compensation with Proportional-Integral-Resonant (PIR) control to mitigate the twice-line-frequency ripple. This paper firstly establishes the input-output characteristic function of the LLC converter, followed by designing corresponding control strategies to address the issues inherent in the LLC converter. Simulation and experimental results affirm that the devised feedforward compensation and PIR control strategy are more effective in suppressing twice-line-frequency ripple compared to conventional PI controllers.

articleTitle: Tube-Based Model Predictive Control for Linear Discrete Time Systems with State Delay and Bounded Disturbances
abstract: This paper proposes a tube-based model predictive control algorithm for linear discrete time systems with state delay and bounded disturbances to ensure input-to-state stability. Firstly, we solve an optimization problem with delayed parameters to obtain a nominal control law. Then, we design a discrete time Lyapunov-Krasovskii function to derive an ancillary control law. Combining the two control laws, we obtain a control law that can ensure the system is input-to-state stable. Next, input-to-state stability is proved by a Lyapunov method. Moreover, the feasibility of the control algorithm is ensured by introducing constraints about the control laws in delayed time interval into the system. Finally, the effectiveness of the developed control strategy is verified by simulations.

articleTitle: Weak magnetic detection signal detection based on digital lock-in amplifier
abstract: Optical pump magnetometer is a high-sensitivity and high-precision weak magnetic detection equipment commonly used in marine magnetic survey, which has a wide range of applications in marine geological research, resource exploration, magnetic target detection and so on. The lock-in amplifier is the key to determine the detection accuracy of weak magnetic signals in optical pump magnetometer. A fully digital lock-in amplifier based on the orthogonal phase-sensitive detection algorithm is proposed, which integrates the signal generator and phase-sensitive detector into a single field programmable gate array (FPGA) chip, and uses software programming instead of hardware circuit design. The system has the advantages of simple debugging, high integration. The direct digital synthesis(DDS) technology is used to generate the driving radio frequency coil signal and quadrature reference signal in the digital domain, which can reduce the phase-sensitive detection error. The frequency control word is used to generate the driving frequency, which can eliminate the frequency measurement error. The narrowband low-pass filter is implemented through multi-rate decimation technology, and the coordinate rotation digital computer(CORDIC) algorithm is used to implement the arctangent operation. The results show that the fully digital lock-in amplifier can accurately measure the phase of the signal to be measured in the full phase range of -180°~180°,and the absolute error is less than 0.0925°.

articleTitle: Adaptive Resilient Event-Triggered Control for Networked Switched Systems Under DoS Attacks
abstract: This paper is concerned with the adaptive resilient event-triggered control problem for networked switched systems with nonperiodic denial of service (DoS) attacks. In order to save limited network bandwidth and reduce the negative impact on system performance caused by DoS attacks, a novel adaptive resilient event-triggered scheme (ARETS) is developed, which can save the communication cost and improve the flexibility of the system. With considering the ARETS, dwell time switching and transmission delays, the criterion of asymptotic stability and ${\mathcal{L}_2}$-gain performance is derived such that the system under DoS attacks owns security performance. On this basis, the co-design conditions of the ARETS and the controller are proposed. Finally, a simulation example is given to verify the effectiveness and merits of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Exponential stability of the Euler-Bernoulli beam with free ends by the Lyapunov function method
abstract: In this paper we consider the exponential stability of the Euler Bernoulli beam with free ends. Firstly, we prove the exponential stability of the Euler Bernoulli beam under boundary feedback control by the Lyapunov function method. Secondly, we design the Luenberger observer system by the observation signal. Then we construct the control based on the observer and obtain a closed-loop system. Finally, we prove that the closed-loop system is exponentially stable by constructing the appropriate Lyapunov function.

articleTitle: Two-stage guidance for autonomous transfer on asteroid surface
abstract: As a probe landing on the surface of the asteroid, the autonomous transfer needs to be performed due to the change of the target landing point. In this paper, a two-stage guidance method is proposed for the autonomous transfer problem on the asteroid surface, which contains an autonomous obstacle avoidance stage and a re-landing stage. Firstly, the trajectory optimization problem of the optimal fuel consumption is established, and the reference control profile is solved by Gauss pseudo-spectral method. On this basis, for the autonomous obstacle avoidance stage, an obstacle avoidance compensation term for the reference control thrust is designed, which has a collision threat warning function. For the re-landing stage, the ZEM/ZEV guidance method is designed with the time-to-gogo parameter satisfying the thrust constraint solved. Finally, the proposed guidance method is simulated using the 433 Eros asteroid model. The results show that the guidance method can realize the autonomous obstacle avoidance and the re-landing for the asteroid autonomous transfer mission.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Cervical Cell Images Instance Segmentation Based on Adversarial Training
abstract: The limited size of the accurately annotated cervical cell image datasets brings great challenges to the research of deep learning segmentation algorithms. This paper proposes an efficient instance segmentation method for fewshot cervical cell images. Firstly, find the ROI (region of interest) centered the nucleus for each cell. Then, the cells at the center of the ROIs are segmented by center cell segmentation network (CCSN) which is trained by adversarial mechanism, this net can learn cell morphology probability distribution from limited number of samples. In addition, we designed a dual-scale discriminator and applied it to adversarial training to improve the integrity of segmentation by strengthening the judgment of the center cell segmentation results. This paper conducts ablation and comparative experiments on the CCEDD dataset, when only 10 cervical cell TCT images participated in the training, the Dice of the proposed method reaches 92%, and the FNR<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf> is improved by 32% compared with U-Net. Experimental results show that compared with existing methods, our method has better indicators under training with limited number of samples and can achieve accurate segmentation of cervical cell instances.

articleTitle: Hybrid impulsive flocking control for multi-agent systems with fault tolerance
abstract: The problem of leader-following flocking control in multi-agent systems with complex dynamical networks using hybrid impulsive and pinning control techniques, along with fault tolerance, has been investigated. Specifically, these mechanisms efficiently reduce control resource consumption and transmission redundancy. Additionally, they address parametric uncertainties, actuator failure, and deception attacks to enhance overall network stability. Moreover, gyroscopic and braking forces are utilized for obstacle avoidance. By leveraging transmission topology structure and impulsive control theory, sufficient criteria are derived to allocate admissible error bounds for maintaining flocking stability. Finally, numerical simulations are conducted to validate the theoretical analysis.; more precisely, it results in a 19.46% decrease in control cost compared to mainstream continuous control structures, and the alternative collision avoidance component leads to a 20.88% reduction in average control distortion.

articleTitle: Multi-sensor based graph convolution fault diagnosis method
abstract: In recent years, research based on Graph Neural Network (GNN) has made significant progress in the field of rotating machinery fault diagnosis. Current methods usually only rely on data from a single sensor for diagnosis. This method is easily affected by problems such as noise interference and missing data from the sensor itself, resulting in inaccurate diagnostic results. Multi-sensor systems can reflect the operating status of machinery more comprehensively and reliably, and also put forward higher requirements for data algorithms. Different from previous deep learning models, graph neural networks have significant performance in mining graph structures and can effectively integrate multiple node relationships and features. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-sensor based graph convolution fault diagnosis method. This method first converts data collected by multiple sensors into a graph data structure, and then uses a graph convolutional neural network to process these graph data and extract feature information. Finally, the feature information is input into the classifier for fault diagnosis. Compared with the single-sensor fault diagnosis method, this method has higher accuracy and reliability.

articleTitle: A Compensation Method for Group Target State and Structure Estimation based on GLMB
abstract: To overcome the coupling problem of structure and state estimation in cluster target tracking, this paper introduces a compensation algorithm for group target estimation founded on Generalized Labeled Multi-Bernoull filter. Firstly, based on the dynamic model of the cluster target, the collaborative noise model of the cluster target is described and established. Secondly, the structure of the cluster is estimated to obtain the cooperative noise compensation term and compensate the group target prediction state under the cooperative condition. Finally, under the framework of GLMB filter, the update status and estimated structure of the cluster are obtained, and the prediction structure of the cluster is further compensated.

articleTitle: Fault Tolerant Extended Kalman Filter for Power Grid Synchronization Estimation Against Partial Missing Measurements
abstract: Aiming at the problem of partial measurement loss of power grid synchronous estimation, a resilient fault-tolerant extended Kalman filter (RFTEKF) is proposed to dynamically track voltage amplitude, voltage phase angle and frequency. First, the positive sequence fast estimation model of three-phase unbalanced network is established. Secondly, the loss phenomenon of measurements occurs in a random way and the randomness of data loss is defined by the discrete distribution of the interval [0,1]. Subsequently, a resilient fault- tolerant extended Kalman filter based on the real-time estimation framework is designed by using time-stamp technique to acquire partial data loss information. Finally, extensive simulation results manifest that the proposed RFTEKF can synchronize the power grid significantly more effectively than the traditional extended Kalman filter (EKF).

articleTitle: Distribution cable arc-earth fault identification based on ensemble empirical mode decomposition and one-dimensional convolutional neural network
abstract: Distribution cables are an important part of the power grid, and arcing ground faults in cables can pose a major safety hazard to the grid. Due to fault signals' complex and non-smooth characteristics, extracting features and identifying them accurately remains a challenge. In this paper, a distribution cable arc-earth identification method based on ensemble empirical mode decomposition (EEMD) and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) is proposed. Based on the relevant principles of EEMD, a more detailed decomposition of the signal is realized to extract its effective features; then a one-dimensional convolutional neural network is constructed to realize fault feature extraction and classification; finally, the PSCAD/EMTDC simulation software is used to generate a cable fault signal dataset to verify the effectiveness of the algorithm in this paper. The simulation results show that EEMD-CNN achieves higher accuracy in cable fault diagnosis compared with EMD decomposition and traditional classification models (99.4%), and is an effective cable fault diagnosis method that can improve the reliability and efficiency of grid operation.

articleTitle: Pedestrain Navigation Using an INS/EKF Framework Aided by UWB Ranging
abstract: Inertial Measuring Units (IMU) can be used to estimate the movement of a person with a methodology that is called Pedestrian Dead-Reckoning (PDR). PDR positioning error will accumulate over time, and other measurement information is needed to eliminate the error gradually increasing. The distance information between pedestrian and fixed points can be obtained by UWB ranging, which is a good means of correcting IMU positioning errors. In order to utilize ranging information, the position of the UWB fixed point (be called beacon) in the navigation frame is required. In some cases, the position of the beacon needs to be estimated online. Meanwhile, IMU output and UWB ranging information all contain time-varying biases. Estimating the biases in real time can improve positioning accuracy. In this paper, we present a navigation framework which positioning pedestrian no accumulating error over time, using MEMS IMU and UWB chips. At the same time, unknown UWB beacon position will be estimated at pedestrian initial stage, and biases of IMU and UWB ranging will be estimated in real time.

articleTitle: Fast Lane Detection Method Based on Improved Multi-branch Residual Network
abstract: Lane line detection emerges as a pivotal technology within the autonomous driving perception suite, demanding exceptionally rapid processing speeds. Traditional approaches typically treat lane detection as a semantic segmentation issue, posing challenges for swift and efficient detection. This paper considers lane line detection as a classification problem, employing a residual network augmented with multiple branches to extract image features. At the end of the feature network, a spatial and channel-wise attention network is fused to enhance the model's ability to extract features. The extracted image features are classified by the classification network composed of full-connection layer, and the final lane detection results are obtained. Experimental results show that the accuracy and F1-measure of this algorithm on TuSimple dataset and CULane dataset have reached 95.83 and 70.4 respectively. Compared with the original method, it is improved by 2.96% and 2% respectively. Moreover, the model exhibits an impressive inference speed of 155 frames per second (FPS) on an RTX 3070 GPU for images at a resolution of 288×800. These results affirm the model's dual strengths in rapid inference and superior detection precision.

articleTitle: Distributed finite-time state observer-based formation control for multiple underactuated AUVs under directed topology
abstract: In this paper, a distributed finite-time state observer-based formation control scheme under directed topology is proposed for multiple underactuated autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) in the presence of uncertain dynamics and unknown time-varying external disturbances. Firstly, a distributed finite-time state observer is proposed for each follower AUV to estimate the position and velocity of the leader within a finite time. Then, a finite-time disturbance observer is constructed to estimate the compound disturbances lumped by the uncertain dynamics and unknown time-varying external disturbances. Further, a distributed finite-time formation control law is proposed by incorporating the above two observers into the dynamic surface control method, which ensures that the AUVs achieve the desired formation pattern within a finite time. Theoretical analysis and simulation results indicate that the proposed formation control law can make the multiple AUVs achieve the desired formation within a finite time.

articleTitle: Cement fineness prediction model based on fuzzy cognitive map
abstract: To achieve fine-grained control of cement fineness in the final grinding process of cement roller press, a method of establishing a cement fineness prediction model based on fuzzy cognitive maps is proposed. Firstly, based on the process and expert experience, the network topology of the fuzzy cognitive map is determined. Secondly, three commonly used activation functions are analyzed. According to the inference mechanism of the fuzzy cognitive map and the physical process of the final grinding of the cement roller press, the optimal activation function is determined. Finally, the fuzzy cognitive map model is established using a combination of the least squares method and Hebbian learning rules. By comparing with the simulation results of genetic algorithms, it is proven that the fuzzy cognitive map model established in this combined manner balances prediction accuracy and the speed of online updates.

articleTitle: Dynamical Analysis and Optimal Control of Stochastic Infectious Disease System with Virus Concentration Perturbation
abstract: A stochastic infectious disease system with virus concentration perturbation is established, and complex dynamical analysis and stochastic boundedness of solution of dynamical system are investigated. The uniqueness and existence of global positive solution and the asymptotic behavior around the interior equilibrium point are analyzed Furthermore, the optimal control of the proposed system is also discussed. Numerical simulations are carried out to show consistency with theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Dc Motor Control: A Global Prescribed Performance Control Strategy Based on Extended State Observer
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the high-precision motion control problem of DC motors. By designing an extended state observer, system uncertainties and external disturbances can be estimated and compensated in the control law. By introducing a shifting function and a fixed-time prescribed performance, a global prescribed performance control scheme is constructed to achieve desirable transient and steady-state tracking performance. The proposed control strategy ensures that the tracking error can converge to a prescribed region within the user-specified time under any bounded initial tracking error, thereby eliminating the longstanding dependence on accurate initial conditions. Using Lyapunov stability theory, it is proved that all the closed-loop system signals are uniformly bounded. Finally, numerical simulations confirm the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Power Allocation Strategy Based on Optimal Temperature Tracking for the Contactless Urban Rail Hybrid Energy Storage System
abstract: In this paper, a power allocation strategy based on optimal temperature tracking is proposed for the contactless urban rail hybrid energy storage system. First, the maximum power is limited by the charge and discharge capacity factors to prevent overcharging and discharging of system. Second, a power allocation method based on optimal temperature tracking under minimum power loss is employed, which extends the battery lifetime. Third, the current control method based on FCS-MPC is adopted to control the DC-DC converters. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Improved Model Predictive Speed Control of PMSMs Based on Delay Compensation and Fuzzy Tuning
abstract: MPSC of PMSMs can give the optimal reference current signal but fails to get enough attention in the industry, because the application of MPSC depends on the accurate speed loop model and the control parameters in the controller are usually selected by trial-and-error method. The issues above are solved by following steps. Firstly, a fuzzy weight factor tuning method is proposed to adjust the coefficients online in both reference trajectory and cost function. This method remarkably improves the transient response and reduce the steady speed fluctuations. Secondly, a two-step predictive strategy is adopted to reduce the overshoot brought by the above method and time delay of the control system. Lastly, a new MPSC with shorter rise time, smaller overshoot and steady errors is proposed. Experimental results validate the superior performance of the improved MPSC than the conventional MPSC.

articleTitle: Research on Electricity Load Forecasting Based on EEMD-GA-LSTM
abstract: Accurate short-term load forecasting is crucial for the economic operation of power grids. In order to improve the prediction accuracy of power system load, this paper proposes a genetic algorithm (GA) optimized long-short-term memory neural network (LSTM) prediction method. The method firstly decomposes the raw numbers into several modes by integrating the empirical modal decomposition (EEMD) method, and then the LSTM network is used to make predictions respectively, and at the same time, the GA optimization algorithm is used to optimize the predict network parameters, so as to obtain the combined prediction model of EEMD-GA-LSTM. Finally, the prediction effect of the model is verified by experimental data, and the results show that the model has a good prediction effect.

articleTitle: An Augmented Extended Kalman Filter-based Algorithm for Magnetic Tracking
abstract: This study assesses the impact of magnetic interference from instruments on the performance of a permanent magnet positioning system within surgical settings. The evaluation covers the movement and rotation of key components such as the operating table and ultrasound device. A novel approach utilizing an augmented extended Kalman filter is proposed to enhance the accuracy of magnetic tracking amidst interference and mitigate its effects on the surgical scene. This method identifies and reduces the influence of ultrasonic probes, surgical instruments, and the operating table. Experimental results demonstrate that the tracking accuracy achieved by this approach in the specified application scenarios is comparable to scenarios without interference, showcasing robust performance and real-time.

articleTitle: Adaptive Load Relief Control Method of Launch Vehicle Based on Improved PSO
abstract: Aiming at the load relief method of the new generation launch vehicle during its boost phase when flying through windy areas. The multi-loop load relief method based on overload feedback loop and extended state observer(ESO) is studied theoretically. The control parameters are tuned by particle swarm optimization algorithm(PSO), and an improved algorithm with particle reset strategy is proposed to improve the population diversity and avoid the population falling into local optimum. The simulation evaluation results show that the active load relief method based on the improved particle swarm optimization algorithm has better adaptability to high-altitude wind disturbance and can further improve the load relief capability of the launch vehicle.

articleTitle: An Anti-disturbance Control Strategy for Underwater Peg-in-Hole Operation
abstract: In the proximity stage in the peg-in-hole operation, the control effects of underwater manipulator is strongly affected by external disturbance and model uncertainty, including ocean currents, friction, and imprecise model of underwater environments, all of which make it difficult to realize precise control in the task of the peg-in-hole. To this end, disturbance observer and radial basis function neural network are introduced to underwater manipulator control framework to solve the issue. Disturbance observer introduces equal compensation based on the observation results of model error from external disturbance estimation. Radial basis function neural network reduces imprecise parameters through online training, which achieves model uncertainty approximation. The peg-in-hole proximity experiment is carried out in an actual pool environment to verify the effectiveness of the motion control strategy proposed. Compared with other control strategies, the proposed control scheme reduces the root mean square error of the underwater manipulator’s motion by 52.91%.

articleTitle: Recognition of Small Foreign Fiber Targets in Recycled Cotton Based on Coarse-to-Fine Detection Method
abstract: In the context of small target detection within recycled cotton, detection precision is significantly compromised by the uneven distribution of foreign fibers. To augment both the efficiency and accuracy of detection, this study introduces a nuanced coarse-to-fine detection paradigm. In the initial phase of the proposed methodology, a coarse-grained technique is utilized for preliminary detection across the entire image, effectively and rapidly identifying the majority of foreign fiber targets. This is followed by the application of a fine-grained technique to these initially detected targets, aiming to significantly enhance the precision of recognition. Results from comparative experiments demonstrate that this innovative coarse-to-fine approach substantially improves the identification and categorization of small foreign fiber targets within cotton, outperforming traditional single-grain detection methods. On the testing dataset, the model achieves a mean Average Precision (mAP@0.5) of 90.33%, which signifies a 3.7% enhancement compared to previous methodologies. This strategic transition from a broad to a more detailed detection approach markedly increases detection accuracy and operational efficiency, thus confirming its effectiveness and superiority in overcoming the challenges inherent in detecting small foreign fiber targets in cotton.

articleTitle: On Linear Convergence of Adaptive Sign-based Gradient Descent
abstract: This paper investigates a sign-based algorithm for unconstrained optimization problems, which leverages the sign of gradients rather than full gradients to reduce the communication cost in distributed optimization, and addresses the convergence failure of sign-based methods with nonadaptive step sizes. Specifically, the algorithm, called AS-GD, is demonstrated to be linearly convergent to a neighbourhood of the optimal value when the objective function is strongly convex, smooth or nonconvex, smooth but satisfies the Polyak-Łojasiewicz condition. Notably, AS-GD can further reduce or potentially eliminate the neighbourhood through appropriate adjustments to its hyperparameters. Synthetic and real-world numerical experiments are conducted respectively to validate the theoretical result.

articleTitle: Research on the Mixed H2/H∞ State Feedback Control Parameter Problem Based on Teaching-Learning-Based Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Due to the complex principles and design rules of robust controllers, their design has always been a rather difficult problem. To address the difficulty in selecting weight matrix parameters for the reference output in the design of a hybrid H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> state feedback controller in robust control problems, a parameter optimization scheme based on teaching-learning-based optimization algorithm (TLBO) is raised in this paper. Firstly, the convex optimization solution problem equivalent to the mixed H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> state feedback controller with closed-loop pole region constraint is described, which leads to the research problem of this paper, that is, the selection of weight matrix parameters. Then, the weight matrix is parameterized, and the parameters are optimized and solved based on TLBO to optimize the performance of the controller. Finally, simulation experiments are designed, and the results show that compared with the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> state feedback control and the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> state feedback control, the hybrid H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> state feedback controller designed in this paper behaves better in terms of suppressing external interference and initial disturbance. Moreover, the controller raised in this paper has good robustness to the perturbation of system parameters.

articleTitle: Hybrid Intelligent Closed-loop Control of Oxygen Content in Flue Gas for MSWI
abstract: The municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) process is subject to factors such as strong nonlinearity, changes in working conditions, and difficulty using precise mathematical models to describe complex characteristics, resulting in the fact that traditional PID control cannot effectively control the amount of oxygen content of the flue gas. The oxygen content of the flue gas is one of the key factors in the effect of municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI), and either too high or too low oxygen content will affect whether the incineration and safety production can be effectively carried out. This paper proposes a hybrid intelligent closed-loop control method consisting of four parts: the pre-set module, the oxygen content of the flue gas forecasting model, the forecasting compensator, and the feedback compensator. Finally, the experiments are conducted to us the field operating data from a large MSWI plant. The results showed that, compared with the traditional method, the control accuracy of the oxygen content of the flue gas improved.

Author Keywords: oxygen content of the flue gas

articleTitle: Visionless Terrain Sensing and Stiffness Adaptive Attitude Control for Quadruped
abstract: Aiming at quadruped robots’ difficulty stabilizing motion in unstructured terrain, the paper proposes a vision-independent terrain sensing and stiffness adaptive control scheme. The robot state is utilized to predict the external environment and suppress the high-frequency jittering of the body in undulating environments to improve the anti-interference ability. In addition, a stiffness adaptive controller is designed by combining impedance theory, which improves the convergence speed of control deviation and enhances the dynamic stability of the robot by solving the optimal stiffness variation law. The final simulation results show that the method proposed in this paper significantly improves the robot’s adaptation to the terrain and motion smoothness.

articleTitle: Research on The Calculation Method of Artillery Elements Based on The Future Point Correction
abstract: In order to improve the firing accuracy of the closerange anti-missile anti-aircraft artillery weapon system, the main factors affecting the firing accuracy are analyzed, and for the problem that the target motion assumption error generated by the mismatch between the target motion model assumption and the target’s actual motion in the fire-control solving of the weapon system leads to a large error in the anti-aircraft artillery firing elements, the method of calculating anti-aircraft artillery elements based on the correction of the future point is researched. By establishing a prediction model based on the deviation of target filter data andfuture point data, the future point is corrected while predicting, and the corrected future point data is used to solve the plurality of anti-aircraft gun firing elements to improve the firing accuracy of the system. A simulation system based on the future point correction method of artillery plurality calculation is constructed, and the effectiveness of the method in improving the firing accuracy of the artillery weapon system is verified by live- fire test.

articleTitle: Event-triggered-based sequential fusion filters for CPSs with deception attacks and correlated noises
abstract: In order to reduce the computational burden of fusion center and ease off the communication pressure, for the CPSs with deception attacks and correlated noises under the SoD event-triggered mechanism, a sequential covariance intersection fusion Kalman filter and a sequential inverse covariance intersection fusion Kalman filter are presented, where the SoD event-triggered mechanism is considered in the data transmission process of the CPSs, and random deception attacks occures in the triggered observations, which are sent to the estimator and then to the fusion center. Both algorithms have good tracking results and good accuracies, a little lower than the centralized fusion algorithm. Simulation example of the tracking system verifies the effectiveness of two above sequential fusion algorithms.

articleTitle: An ontology-based approach for constructing data model of BIPM
abstract: Building Information Physical Model (BIPM) is a new type of special information model that integrates static information, dynamic interaction mechanism and physical mechanism information. However, BIPM lacks a data model with a statute description and structured storage of computable entities, which will not guarantee the interoperability of BIPM. Therefore, this study proposes a method of statutorily describing BIPM entities based on the ontology technology proposed to establish a unified description model for BIPM. Subsequently, the application of BIPM data model in the intelligent control of chiller is taken as an example to illustrate that BIPM data model supports open access on the computer.

articleTitle: Design and Research of a New Intelligent Handshake Robot based on the Perspective of the Science Popularization
abstract: The research of robot science popularization equipment plays the most important role of foundation and guidance in improving the scientific literacy of the whole people, and is the research focus of related science popularization fields. Taking the multifunctional robot arm as the research object, this paper designs a new handshake robot popular science equipment from the perspective of popular science. Its structure mainly includes robot arm, robot bionic finger, control system, sensor detection module and so on. It can simulate the whole process of human automatic handshake, and can also realize other functions such as greeting and object handling. Through the production of the robot arm, the feasibility and stability of the handshake robot arm designed in this paper are verified, which provides relevant basic equipment and platform for the research and development of robot science popularization equipment.

articleTitle: Detent Force Reduction in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Linear Motor Based on Arc-teeth
abstract: Permanent Magnet Synchronous Linear Motors (PMSLM) has the advantages of high thrust force density, high acceleration, high speed, high precision, high efficiency etc. However, the detent force of PMSLM is an inevitable problem, caused by their inherent end-disconnection structure. Excessive detent force will cause thrust fluctuations and reduce the system’s stability. To resolve the above problems, an improved PMSLM structure based on arc-teeth is proposed to reduce detent force. Firstly, the motor permeability distribution is analyzed at different moments based on the flux-tube method, and the expression of detent force is derived. Second, the finite element model of PMSLM is established to optimize the height of arc-teeth, and the optimal structural parameters of the motor is obtained. Finally, the performance advantages of the proposed PMSLM are verified by comparing with traditional linear motor.

articleTitle: Time Series Slow Feature Extraction for Dow Data Problem
abstract: Handling process data characterized by strong nonlinearity, high dimensionality, cross-correlations, and auto-correlations presents a considerable hurdle for data-driven soft sensor modeling. While traditional slow feature analysis (SFA) adeptly captures slow and static features from linear data, it may falter in capturing the nonlinear, high-dimensional, and dynamic features inherent in time series data. Conversely, although Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks are designed to address long-term dependencies within sequences, they encounter challenges, particularly with very lengthy data sequences, in effectively capturing these dependencies. Consequently, relying solely on SFA or LSTM may prove inadequate for addressing the complexities of time series data in industrial processes. To confront these challenges, this study proposes an innovative approach termed Slow LSTM (SLSTM), which amalgamates the hidden layers of LSTM and SFA to enhance feature extraction. These extracted features are subsequently fed into a fully connected layer for prediction. The efficacy of this proposed method is validated through comparisons with various methods, including SFA-FC, LSTM, and RNN.

articleTitle: Rural end logistics site-route planning based on two-layer programming
abstract: Solving the "last mile" problem of rural logistics distribution is an important strategy to prosper rural e- commerce, promote the upgrading of farmers' consumption, improve farmers' quality of life, and serve the country's rural revitalization. This work proposes to adopt the "joint distribution-collection" model without establishing a joint distribution center in the rural end logistics distribution and establishes a two-stage site-path planning model, which is used to solve the rural end logistics distribution problem. A town in the southern Plain is taken as an example to obtain all the points of interest (POI) and the path information between them. Then we select the delivery point of interest set from all the points of interest, and use the distribution of buildings to simulate the actual distribution of express volume. The calculation results show that this method is effective.

articleTitle: Consensus of second-order nolinear multi-agent systems with a smart leader via impulsive control
abstract: This essay studies the leader-following consensus problem of second-order nolinear multi-agent systems with a smart leader. Taking advantage of impulsive control, a distributed impulsive consensus control protocol is showcased to reduce the communication consumption. In contrast to a conventional leader which is not impacted by other followers, a kind of novel smart leader with an external control input to regulate its own states is deployed by exploiting the information of its neighbors in an impulsive manner. This modified control framework allows the error between the followers and the leader to reduce, thus elevating the tracking control performance of the system. The designed protocol is theoretically analyzed from stability utilizing the Lyapunov function and the impulsive control theory, and several sufficient conditions of achieving leader-following consensus are derived. Finally, several numerical simulation results are provided to corroborate the validity of the theoretical result.

articleTitle: A Robust Tracking Method Based on Dynamic Template Updating
abstract: The classical Siamese network tracking algorithm only uses the initial frame image as template, which brings the problem of degradation of tracking accuracy for long-time tracking or for targets that have obvious deformation. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a robust tracking method based on dynamic template updating(short as DTU). Firstly, the original Siamese network is improved by adding new network branches and feedback links so that the current tracking results can participate in the template updating. Secondly, the average peak energy is used to determine the updating, fusing the current tracking results with the original template to obtain a dynamic target template that can reflect the current state of the target in real-time. Finally, an attention mechanism is added in the region proposal network(RPN) to enhance target features and improve tracking robustness. Experiments on two open benchmarks datasets, VOT2018 and OTB100, show that the proposed method achieves advanced performance compared with existing tracking algorithms.

articleTitle: Reduced-Reference Quality Assessment for Single Image Super-Resolution using Attention Mechanism
abstract: Single image super-resolution (SISR) technology has greatly improved visual quality of images by enhancing their resolutions. SISR has been widely investigated in recent years. However, it is challenging to fairly estimate the performances of various SISR methods, as the lack of reliable and accurate criteria for perceptual quality. In this paper, we introduce the attention mechanism into the quality assessment of SISR images, and propose a novel reduced-reference quality assessment metric for SISR with the low-resolution image information. Experimental results on three public SR-IQA databases demonstrate the effectiveness and generalization ability of our proposed method compared with other quality assessment algorithms.

articleTitle: A System for Detecting the Effectiveness of Cathodic Protection in Buried Pipelines
abstract: The effectiveness testing of cathodic protection for buried pipelines is an important means of pipeline corrosion prevention. Some pipeline laying environments are accompanied by strong electromagnetic interference, which will seriously affect the effectiveness of pipeline cathodic protection. Conventional testing methods for such pipelines will not be able to detect effective cathodic protection data. A pipeline cathodic protection detection system was designed to address this phenomenon, and the main performance and indicators of the system were verified through laboratory and field testing. The test results indicate that the detection system has strong detection capabilities, consistent with the detection results of imported equipment, and has strong practicality, which will play a certain role in the future localization and promotion of the system.

articleTitle: Classification of Alzheimer’s Disease via Spatial-Temporal Graph Convolutional Networks
abstract: In recent years, functional brain networks have been widely used for brain disease classification tasks. Graph convolutional networks (GCN), as one of the existing methods, focuses on inter-subject relationships and subjects’ brain region connectivity relationships. Though spatial features can be extracted by GCN-based methods from functional brain network, temporal relationships between brain regions are frequently ignored. In this paper, we propose a spatial-temporal graph convolutional network (STGCN) model to solve this problem. A temporal convolution module (TCM) is designed to learn information about the alteration of brain regions with time, and a spatial convolution module (SCM) is employed to extracted features of brain regions. TCM contains two parts, single-brain-region convolution and multi-brain-region convolution, to fully capture the alteration of brain regions with time from two perspectives. We finally evaluate our model on the ADNI dataset and obtain good results.

articleTitle: Occlusion face recognition method based on Multi-Gate Attention Mechanism and Gate Recurrent Unit
abstract: With the continuous research of deep convolutional neural networks, face recognition technology has made tremendous progress, but there are still many challenges and difficulties in complex environments. Especially when global infectious diseases are raging, everyone must wear masks, thus leading to the masking of key facial features, which makes traditional facial recognition technology unable to recognize faces in many cases. In this paper, we propose an occlusive face recognition method based on Multi-Gate Attention Mechanism combined with Gate Recurrent Unit (MGAM-GRU). The network structure is based on GRU, introduces multi-gate attention mechanism, improves on the existing MGAM-LSTM method, and replaces LSTM with GRU. Compared with LSTM networks, GRU networks have simpler structure, fewer parameters and easier convergence. Experimental results show that the proposed MGAM-GRU method has high recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: Input-to-state Stability Analysis for Servo Drive Systems with Time-varying Delays and Disturbances
abstract: This paper is devoted to studying input-to-state stability analysis for servo drive systems with time-varying delays and disturbances. With the help of the Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional method and the free-weighting matrices approach, a new input-to-state stability criterion on servo drive systems with time-varying delays and disturbances is proposed. Based on the criterion, the relationship between the PID controller gains and the input-to-state stability of the system can be obtained. Finally, a numerical example and a case study are given to show that the proposed criterion is effective.

articleTitle: Adaptive Nonsingular Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Tracking Control for Second-order Nonlinear Systems with External Disturbances
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode (NFTSM) tracking controller for second-order nonlinear systems with external disturbances. Firstly, a novel NFTSM mainfold is constructed to directly address the singularity issue from the perspective of sliding mode surface design and enhance the convergence speed of the tracking error. Then, in order to achieve more accurate dynamic response on the uncertain nonlinear system, a robust adaptive control strategy is introduced into the sliding mode control strategy to estimate the unknown external disturbance. The system states can converge to an arbitrarily small set around the origin within a finite time. Finally, a simulation example is included to further testify the validity of the proposed control approach.

articleTitle: An Improved N-step Phase Shift Method for High-temperature Objects
abstract: N-step phase shift method is widely used because of its high accuracy and efficiency. However, when the detected object is at high temperature, the infrared radiation generated by the detected object would cause great interference to the projected image, which seriously affect the accuracy of unwrapped phase. To solve this problem, we establish a physical model of high temperature thermal radiation. By analyzing the model, an improved N-step phase shift method for high-temperature objects is obtained. We first mix the phase shift fringe images into color images with weak infrared radiation, and then obtain a high precision phase information by analyzing and calculating color phase shift fringe images modulated by the object surface. To verify the method in this paper, we compare this method with N-step phase shift method in different phase shift steps. The experimental results show that this method in this paper could get high-precision of the unwrapped phase. The detection accuracy is improved by about 20.83%.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral Image Classification Based on the Fusion of Superpixels and Deformable Features
abstract: Convolutional neural network is widely used in hyperspectral image classification for its excellent spatial-spectral feature extraction ability. However, the distribution of objects in hyperspectral images is highly complex, and it makes it difficult for conventional convolutional kernels to extract deep spatial features, which limit the classification performance. Therefore, a novel deformation feature fusion convolution network (DFFCN) is proposed in this work. Firstly, deformable convolution based on superpixels is used to extract the features of complex ground objects. At the same time, traditional convolution is used to extract neighborhood features of ground objects. Then, the above features are fused based on a channel attention mechanism. Finally, deep feature extraction and classification are performed on the fused features. The features based on the distribution of ground objects are fused while the neighborhood features of ground objects are retained. Experimental results on three real HSI data sets demonstrate that DFFCN can obtain better classification performances than several well-known classification methods.

articleTitle: Improvement scheme of vehicle routing for community group purchase based on adjustable orders
abstract: Firstly, this paper puts forward vehicle routing problem for community group purchase. Based on the order quantity and distance principle, screening some self-pickup points and assigns orders from these points to the other self-pickup points. Then taking the data of VRP(vehicle routing problem) benchmark as an example and the genetic algorithm is designed to solve VRP after adjusting the orders of self-pickup points. In addition, by sensitivity analysis of order quantity and distance, this paper studies the impact of changes in order quantity and distance standard on total distribution costs.

articleTitle: Distributed Cooperative Guidance Law for UAV Swarm Based on Reinforcement Learning
abstract: We propose a distributed cooperative guidance law for UAV swarms based on the multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) algorithm. Specifically, we propose a cooperative guidance law based on sliding surface and use an improved MADDPG algorithm to intelligently design the parameters of the proposed guidance law. The improved MADDPG algorithm includes a communication module based on multi-head attention network and a mixer network. Simulation experiments show that the cooperative guidance law can effectively achieve the cooperative guidance and collaboration of UAV swarms.

articleTitle: A prediction model for the width of medium thick plate based on the fusion of point prediction and interval prediction
abstract: The prediction of the width of medium thick plate is very important to increase the product yield. Most of the current research focuses on improving the prediction accuracy of the high point, but seldom considers the ability of the model to resist the risk, which is urgently needed in the existing hot rolling production system. In this paper, a fusion method based on point prediction and interval prediction is proposed, which can balance the accuracy and risk of the medium thick plate width prediction models. The main work is to screen out the original industrial process variables that have a great influence on the width of medium thick plate through hierarchical clustering, and to construct the point prediction and interval prediction models by combining the upper and lower bounds detection method of Deep Neural Network Model and Quantile Regression Neural Network. The experiments show that the proposed fusion of point prediction and interval prediction can take into account the accuracy and risk of medium thick plate width prediction model. The experiments show that the interval coverage ratio is 0.95, and the normalized average width of predicted intervals is 0.10, which indicates that the model has a very good prediction performance and risk resistance ability.

articleTitle: Estimation for Linear Repetitive Processes based on Event-triggering Mechanism under DoS Attack
abstract: This paper addresses the state estimation of linear repetitive processes affected by DoS attacks. An estimator with H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performance is designed based on an event-triggering mechanism. Firstly, the linear repetition process is two-dimensional (2-D) system, and a 2-D DoS attack and event triggering mechanism model is established. Then designed an estimator, on which we built the augmentation error system and specified the desired performance metrics to ensure that the system would remain robustness in the face of DoS attacks and event triggering mechanisms. By using Lyapunov theory, the sufficient criterion to ensure the robust stability of augmented error system is provided. The explicit expressions of the estimator’s parameters are obtained by solving a matrix inequality. Finally, a simulation example is presented to validate the feasibility of the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Study on Verification of Slope Angle Recognition Algorithm based on Vehicle Speed
abstract: In this paper, a verification algorithm for the vehicle slope angle recognition is studied. The actual slope signal is extracted from the longitudinal acceleration and the actual vehicle speed of the three-coordinate acceleration sensor. The problem that the longitudinal acceleration signal of the three-coordinate acceleration sensor includes both the actual slope and the vehicle acceleration information is solved. The longitudinal acceleration of the sensor is subtracted from the acceleration calculated from the actual vehicle speed to obtain the actual slope angle. In order to engineering the algorithm, two Kalman filters are added to optimize the algorithm, and filter the longitudinal comprehensive value and the calculated slope angle measured by the three-coordinate acceleration sensor. The method is suitable for different vehicle load, speed, actual acceleration, wind resistance and braking torque. Based on Simulink simulation environment, four kinds of working conditions were simulated respectively. The vehicle load variation condition based on dynamics algorithm; The vehicle speed variation condition based on dynamic algorithm; The condition that the acceleration signal is increased step by step, and then reduced step by step, based on the optimization algorithm; Based on the optimization algorithm, the vehicle speed is increased from a standstill and then reduced in the uphill condition. The simulation results show that the effectiveness of the proposed verification algorithm based on the longitudinal acceleration and vehicle speed signals of the three-coordinate acceleration sensor. And it is obviously better than that of the slope angle calculated by the dynamic algorithm.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Different Prediction Models of Inorganic Fertilizers N, P, and K Under Different Soil Fertility Conditions
abstract: Nutrient management is a key measure to achieve the target crop yield. Choosing appropriate predictive models and adjusting nutrient supply according to actual conditions can effectively reduce nutrient loss, improve crop yield and product quality. Therefore, we conducted research on the prediction models of inorganic fertilizers N, P, and K in greenhouse tomatoes based on the target yield. In this paper, we analyzed four different neural network prediction models: the neural network prediction model based on ant colony optimization algorithm, the neural network prediction model based on sparrow search algorithm, neural network prediction model based on genetic algorithm and neural network prediction model based on particle swarm optimization algorithm, and compared and analyzed the prediction results of inorganic fertilizer N, P and K under different soil fertility conditions to understand which neural network prediction model will produce the best prediction effect. The simulation results showed that under medium soil fertility, the neural network prediction model based on genetic algorithm had the best prediction effect of inorganic fertilizer N, P, and K. The verification results showed that its mean square error (MSE) and coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) were the best, which were 0.0031 and 0.8200 respectively. However, under low soil fertility and high soil fertility, the neural network prediction model based on the sparrow search algorithm had the best prediction performance, and its MSE and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> were the best.

articleTitle: Polygonal constrained adaptive MPC dynamic obstacle avoidance based on safety trigger mechanism
abstract: In order to improve the adaptability of autonomous vehicles in dynamic obstacle environments, this paper designs a novel constrained obstacle avoidance strategy based on adaptive model predictive control˄MPC˅ algorithm. Firstly, an adaptive MPC prediction model is established based on the vehicle kinematics model. Secondly, a safety trigger mechanism is defined to update the polygonal constraints established in this paper, which is introduced into the MPC optimization problem and solved by a quadratic programming algorithm. Finally, the results of the integrated obstacle avoidance framework established in this paper are tested in several scenarios. The results show that the algorithm can effectively avoid collisions in both static and dynamic obstacle environments, which lays the foundation for the subsequent development of real scenarios.

articleTitle: Stabilization of the Markovian jump system with a mode-separation controller
abstract: This paper studies the stabilization of continuous-time linear Markovian jump systems based on mode-separation controllers. Unlike traditional mode-dependent controllers, the mode-separation controller in this paper is selected based on event triggering, which is more in line with the actual issue and does not require knowledge of the real-time modes of the system. In addition, a sufficient condition for the stability of the system is obtained through the LMIs. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the method in this paper is verified by a simulation example.

articleTitle: Heuristic Based Online Information Path Planning
abstract: Autonomous exploration is the basic research of UAV in many fields, which requires UAV to automatically explore unknown space and obtain complete environmental information. Sampling based method is one of the classical methods of independent exploration. However, although the existing sampling-based methods can complete the task, there are still problems of low detection efficiency caused by UAV maneuvering and low path quality. Current research is focused on improving the efficiency of independent exploration. Therefore, in order to overcome the above problems, this paper proposes a heuristic online information planning method based on sampling. In this method, a heuristic path decision method based on RRT* is proposed, which can better consider the overall environmental information and generate high-quality exploration paths compared with traditional sampling-based methods. Secondly, considering the acquisition of the whole environment information, the heuristic evaluation function is designed, and high-quality viewpoint is continuously selected as the next local navigation target to optimize the path and generate a smooth path. We conducted several simulation experiments to test our approach, and the experimental results show that the algorithm outperforms the benchmark algorithm in terms of both flight time and total path length.

articleTitle: Threat level assessment method for reconnaissance satellites based on improved TOPSIS
abstract: Aiming at the problems of subjectivity and uncertainty in the assessment method of reconnaissance satellite threat level, an expert entropy weight TOPSIS method based on improved TOPSIS (Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution) is proposed. Considering the coverage performance, reconnaissance performance, and defense performance of the reconnaissance satellite, establish an evaluation index system, use the principle of combined weighting, combine the expert experience weight and the entropy weight to calculate the evaluation index weight, and then use the TOPSIS method to calculate the threat level. Compared with the traditional TOPSIS method, the simulation results show that this algorithm introduces more reasonable index weights and can obtain threat assessment results that align with objective laws.

articleTitle: Improving Jamming Efficiency: A Dynamic Route Planning Approach for Ground Radar Suppression
abstract: Radar has become a crucial apparatus for providing electromagnetic situational information in the battlefield. Specifically, about radar suppression, the issue is of great significance. And long-range support jammer has the problem of low jamming efficiency when performing the mission of suppressing ground radar. Thus, we devise a dynamic optimal route planning algorithm, significantly improving the interference effectiveness against ground radar. Preliminarily, through an analysis of typical radar suppression scenarios with the jammer’s inherent attributes, the study designed the aircraft route planning constraints. Then, leveraging the effective configuration area within the mission scenario, we integrate attributes of both the radar and jammer, the cross-constraint conditions have been established to facilitate a reasonable deployment of route points. To evaluate interference effectiveness, the study combines operational route points of the interference aircraft with the effective suppression area and builds up an efficiency assessment criterion for the ground radar suppression route planning algorithm. Simulation experiments shows that our dynamic optimal route planning algorithm increases interference efficiency by an average of 15.794% compared to traditional routes in the setting missions. Our research provides theoretical support and practical guidance for tactical decisions in the long-range support jammer suppression of ground radar.

articleTitle: Extremum Seeking Based on Sliding Mode Control for Precision Motion Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the implementation of ultraprecision control in industrial settings, with a particular emphasis on overcoming the waterbed effect in linear controllers, mitigating the chattering phenomenon in sliding mode control, and optimizing feedback controller parameters. A hybrid control strategy is developed, combining linear and nonlinear control techniques, effectively resolving the waterbed effect and chattering issues. The strategy includes the innovative use of Second-Order Integral Sliding Mode Control (ISMC) within a nonlinear feedback channel. Additionally, a self-tuning method employing discrete extremum seeking is introduced to dynamically optimize the controller’s gain, enhancing system responsiveness and stability under various operational conditions. The paper details model development, outlines the control methodology, and presents simulation results, demonstrating the efficacy of the approach in tackling these challenges.

articleTitle: MIDNet: A Weakly Supervised Multipath Interaction Network for Image Defogging*
abstract: To overcome the overfitting problem caused by supervised defogging methods trained on synthetic datasets, some weakly supervised defogging methods trained by feeding unpaired synthetic images have been proposed. However, these methods usually express the cycle of defogging and reconstructed fog through adversarial training, without considering that this manner may be unsatisfactory for achieving the texture and detail restoration. To tackle this issue, a weakly supervised multipath interaction defogging network (MIDNet), which is trained by feeding unpaired images, is proposed. Specifically, we consider the information interaction of different generative networks. To gradually improve the quality of defogged images, MIDNet utilizes progressive paths to obtain the model parameter feature maps from different networks. The interaction of information is achieved through vertical path interaction function. Moreover, a SAMRiR module is proposed to fuse and extract features from different paths. Experiments are conducted to show that the proposed MIDNet achieves favorable performance in both qualitative and quantitative comparisons. Furthermore, we also utilize YOLOv5s to detect objects on foggy and defogged images, and experimental results demonstrate that image defogging indeed facilitates performance improvements of object detection tasks.

articleTitle: PET Image Reconstruction Based on Graph Learning
abstract: Positron emission tomography (PET) is a powerful functional imaging modality, but it has low resolution at low dose tracers. In order to improve the quality of reconstructed images, this paper proposes a novel PET image reconstruction method based on graph learning. Firstly, the graph Laplacian matrix is obtained from the low-quality PET images through graph learning. Then, the PET image is iterative reconstructed using the weight matrix. Our method utilizes graph learning to better leverage the structural information of PET images. The results from simulations and in-vivo data experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves better performance over traditional methods and KEM method.

articleTitle: Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Neural Network Control for Furnace Temperature in Municipal Solid Waste Incineration Processes
abstract: Furnace temperature plays a pivotal role in ensuring the stability of municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI), influenced by variable factors such as material composition, feeding patterns, and equipment operation. We introduce an interval type-2 fuzzy neural network (IT2FNN) control method. Initially, we analyze furnace temperature control characteristics to identity crucial operating variables. Subsequently, we construct a multiple-input single-output (MISO) model for furnace temperature using the linear regression decision tree (LRDT) algorithm. Finally, we develop an IT2FNN-based controller for furnace temperature. The effectiveness of our proposed method is confirmed through control experiments using actual MSWI process data.

Author Keywords: interval type-2 fuzzy neural network (IT2FNN) control

articleTitle: Two-Layer Defense Architecture for False Data Injection Attack in Grid CPS
abstract: The destructive problem, which is in grid cyber-physical system, is generated by false data injection attack. A two-layer defense architecture based on random forest and long short-term memory is proposed. Firstly, random forest algorithm is utilized to implement multi-label localization layer for false data injection attack, and outputs the location label of attacked node. Then, the grey wolf algorithm is adopted to optimize the long short-term memory network, achieving the state data prediction layer. After eliminating state data corresponding to the attacked node, historical state data is utilized to predict. Finally, through the simulation analysis, the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method are demonstrated by experiments: For the attack location layer, the detection accuracy of the proposed is about 4% higher than that of the comparison in IEEE14 system. For the state prediction layer, the root-mean-square error of the proposed is decreased by 2.43% and 1.08% in node 2, and by 3.03% and 1.66% in node 5, which is compared to the BP and LSTM, respectively.

articleTitle: Low-complexity tracking control for high-order uncertain nonlinear systems with hard and soft constraints
