Furthermore, we incorporate the information entropy of nearby grids surrounding each agent as the guiding rules.Finally, the simulations verify that proposed method can achieve the full coverage of the mission area efficiently and the searching efficiency of the proposed flocking search method outperform the traditional searching algorithms.

articleTitle: End-to-end Knowledge Graph-enabled Multi-round Dialogue Model Based on Transformer
abstract: As an important branch of artificial intelligence, natural language processing can complete many complex tasks for humans. Among them, intelligent dialogue is to allow users to communicate with a dialogue model and let it complete specific tasks. In order to better propose an end-to-end dialogue model, this work adopts a structural model based on Transformer and a pointer generation network, which seeks an appropriate alternative through the pointer generation network. Moreover, the end-to-end model has the ability to directly copy unknown words from the knowledge base. It makes innovations in many aspects such as the input part of the encoder, the encoding of position information, the ONE-HOT matrix, and the task layering of the decoding layer. The study compares the proposed model with benchmark models including Seq2Seq, Seq2Seq+Attn, and Mem2Seq through experiments under two datasets, i.e.,bAbI and In-Car. On the bAbI dataset, the proposed model significantly outperforms Seq2Seq and Seq2Seq+Attn models in terms of word accuracy, dialogue accuracy, and BLUE score indicators. On the In-Car dataset, it is found that the proposed model is better than the Mem2Seq model in handling long corpus.

articleTitle: Adaptive control of strict-feedback nonlinear systems with output constraints and input delays
abstract: In this paper, the adaptive control problem of strict-feedback nonlinear systems with output constraints and input delay is studied. By using the auxiliary system to eliminate the effect of input delay. At the same time, the unknown nonlinear functions are effectively approximated by using neural network. It is explained by the theoretical analysis that the tracking error is asymptotically converging to zero and the constructed Barrier Lyapunov function (BLF) can ensure that the requirement of system output is not violated. Finally, simulation results are given to illustrate the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Robust convergence of uncertain fuzzy BAM neural networks with time-varying delays
abstract: This paper focuses on the robust exponential convergence of uncertain Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy bidirectional associative memory (BAM) neural networks with time-varying delays. Using Lyapunov method and delay inequality technique, several sufficiently easily verifiable criteria are derived to guarantee that the T-S fuzzy BAM neural networks with time-varying delays to converge robustly exponentially to a ball in the state space with a pre-specified rate. Finally, a numerical example with simulations is given to illustrate the effectiveness of our theoretical results.

articleTitle: Design of Fire Emergency Escape Guide System Based on Zigbee
abstract: The increase in flammable decorative materials, the frequent use of various types of electrical appliances, and people’s weak awareness of fire prevention has led to frequent fire accidents. Therefore, a fire emergency escape guide system based on Zigbee is designed and implemented, which guides people to quickly evacuate when a fire occurs. The system constructs a Zigbee wireless sensor network. Firstly, a variety of sensors in the Zigbee network, such as smoke sensor, CO sensor, temperature sensor, are used to collect on-site data in real time. Secondly, the system comprehensively analyzes the characteristic parameters collected by all the sensors, and determines whether a fire has broken out. And then, according to the fire situation, the optimal escape path is calculated using A-star algorithm. Finally, the planned escape path is sent to the system terminal through the Zigbee network, so that the trapped people can escape quickly.

articleTitle: Path planning of underwater vehicle based on improved particle swarm algorithm
abstract: Particle swarm algorithm can overcome the shortcomings of insufficient optimization ability, large calculation amount and difficulty in planning the optimal path of traditional algorithms in the path planning of underwater vehicles with complex processing environment and many constraints. However,traditional particle swarm algorithms have drawbacks such as low accuracy and easy falling into local optima. In order to solve this problem, This paper sets an inertia weight that decreases with the number of iterations and an asynchronous shrinkage learning factor for the particle swarm algorithm under the condition of converting from a spatial coordinate system to a spherical coordinate system and then applies it to the path planning of underwater vehicle.Simulation experiments show that the improved particle swarm algorithm (LINW-SPSO) proposed in this paper is superior to the traditional particle swarm algorithm in terms of algorithm stability and path planning effect.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Tracking Control for Three-wheeled Mobile Robots Combined with Gaussian Process Regression
abstract: This paper studies the tracking control problem of the three-wheeled omnidirectional mobile robot (TOMR) subject to the coupled input constraint and unknown disturbances. First, a new type of coupled input constraint of three-wheeled omnidirectional mobile robots at kinematic level is derived. Second, we apply Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) on experimental data to compensate for the disturbances. Third, the trajectory tracking control algorithm is proposed based on nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) method and Gaussian Process Regression. To reduce the computational burden of the control law, three efficient improved approaches are proposed. Finally, we generalize the designed control strategy to solve the popular collision avoidance problem. Numerous simulations are carried out to validate the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Global Prescribed Performance Control for Pure-Feedback Systems with Sensors and Actuator Faults
abstract: This paper presents a low-complexity global fault-tolerant control method, capable of guaranteeing prescribed transient behavior and irrespective of initial condition for the un-certain pure-feedback systems with sensors and actuator faults. First, the golbal control for pure-feedback system is first achieved without using the mean value theorem, the proposed method is derived from a novel semi-bounded modeling approach, which transforms the pure-feedback nonlinear systems into strict feedback nonlinear systems. Then, novel transformation functions related to performance functions are introduced to the control design such that no compensators or approximation structures are needed, which results in the global tracking controller for pure-feedback nonlinear systems with sensors and actuator faults. Moreover, the virtual control laws and actual control law are only related to the tracking errors, which implies that the proposed method has much more relaxed conditions than all the existing methods. Finally, the simulation results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Positioning Algorithm based on Vehicle-vehicle Collaborative Location for Auxiliary Transport Vehicles in Underground Mines
abstract: Aiming at the problem of narrow space and serious multipath effect in the underground tunnel of mines, the automatic driving vehicle will receive signals propagated by multiple paths, which leads to the large positioning error of the automatic driving vehicle, the Channel-slam algorithm based on the vehicle-vehicle collaborative positioning is proposed. The algorithm uses the vehicle-vehicle sending position information to each other and the multipath signal received by the vehicle to improve the positioning accuracy of the target vehicle. Firstly, the propagation of multipath signals and vehicle-vehicle communication scenarios are modelled, and then the Bayesian model of the positioning system is established by taking advantage of the characteristics of information exchange and multipath effect of downhole vehicles. The factor graph is used to estimate the position of the two target vehicles, to achieve the precise positioning of downhole vehicles. Through simulation experiments, compared with the traditional single-vehicle localisation algorithm, the vehicle-vehicle collaborative localisation algorithm proposed in this paper has faster particle convergence, smoother and more stable target tracking trajectories, and improved positioning accuracy by 48.6%.

articleTitle: Improvements of underwater visual image enhancement method based on the fusion of optical-model methods and model-free methods
abstract: The ability of underwater robots to perceive specific targets autonomously is an important guarantee for underwater robots to complete underwater tasks. However, the quality of underwater images decays with increasing underwater depth, resulting in low-contrast and high color distortion. In this paper, we improve the existing enhancement methods based on the fusion of optical-model methods and model-free methods to give a new set of learning-based underwater image enhancement method. The depth map features of a specific scene are first acquired, and the depth map is used as input to measure decay patterns and transmission maps. For background light estimation, we propose an estimation algorithm based on global background illumination, which successfully solves the problem of uneven illumination caused by the traditional processing. For white balance, we propose a method of white balance based on chromatic adaptation transform, which successfully solves the problem of local distortion caused by the inability of traditional white balance methods to adapt to the underwater environment. The traditional image weighted fusion method has fixed weights and cannot guarantee the optimal quality of the fused image. This paper propose a method for statistically optimal fusion weights, which significantly improves the quality of the fused image. In this paper, the UIQM and UCIQE are used as underwater image quality evaluation metrics. Experimental results show that the proposed method improves 2.24 and 2.1427 in two metrics compared to the FUnlE-GAN algorithm, 0.45 and 2.1627 compared to the Deep WaveNet algorithm, 0.57 and 2.0727 compared to the Retinex-based algorithm, 0.9 and 0.8317 compared to the Automatic red channel algorithm, 0.33 and 2.4307 compared to the WCID algorithm, respectively.

articleTitle: Mode Transition Modeling and Coordinated Control of a Parallel TBCC
abstract: This paper investigates the modeling and coordinated control of a certain parallel turbine based combined cycle (TBCC) during mode transition. In view of the strong time-varying nonlinearity of the TBCC mode transition and the large range of changes in the state variables and splitter plate opening, a TBCC mode transition coordinated control method based on the polynomial nonlinear parameter-varying (PPV) model is proposed. Based on the component-level models of Turbine and Ramjet engine, PPV models are established using system identification method, which can simultaneously reflect the time-varying and nonlinear characteristics of the engine. State feedback controllers are designed based on gain scheduling and PPV stabilization control theory, and verified on the PPV model. The simulation results show that the proposed method can achieve good control effect, and the actual thrust can quickly track the target thrust, thereby realizing coordinated control of mode transition and smooth transition of total thrust. Moreover, compared to the gain scheduling controller, the proposed method can achieve thrust tracking more quickly and smoothly.

articleTitle: Iterative Learning Observer-based Fault Diagnosis with actuator and sensor fault in linear system
abstract: For a class of continuous linear systems containing external perturbations and internal faults (actuator and sensor faults), this paper recommends a fault diagnosis method using an iterative learning observer. An iterative learning observer that simultaneously estimates and reconstructs the state and faults of the system is developed in this paper. It is only at the same time that the conditions for the stability of the observer are assigned through linear matrix inequalities (LMIs).Also to inhibit the instability of the system caused by external perturbations, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performance metrics are employed in this paper. A simulation is carried out at last to verify the reliability and validity of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Contour Error Pre-compensation Control for X-Y Motion System Driven by Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors
abstract: In order to improve the control accuracy of the X- Y motion system driven by permanent magnet synchronous motors and to reduce the contour error of the motion system. A contour error pre-compensation control strategy is proposed in this paper. First, the contour error of linear trajectory and circular trajectory is analyzed, then the contour error model of the dual-axis system is analyzed by combining the cross-coupled control. The comparison of the contour error relationship of the system is performed when the cross-coupled is added and no cross-coupled. At the same time, the position signal of the single axis is predicted and the contour error of the dual-axis system is calculated. To further improve the level of cross-coupling, an active pre-compensation control strategy is proposed to compensate the contour error to the position and velocity loops. Finally, the modeling simulation is performed in Matlab/Simulink and the contour errors are compared in the three methods without cross-coupled control, with cross-coupled control, and active pre-compensation control. The results show that the proposed control strategy is able to predict the position signal before the contour error occurs, and then pre-compensate the contour error in order to further improve the dynamic response speed and contour accuracy of the system.

articleTitle: Coverage-Based Multi-Target Dynamic Allocation and Cooperative Encirclement Strategy
abstract: Swarm maneuverable target allocation stands as one of the most pivotal techniques in group cooperative confrontations. This article, grounded in the coverage function, employs an enhanced particle swarm algorithm to investigate the allocation and encirclement strategy for multiple aerial vehicles in cooperative counteraction against a group of mobile targets. Initially, based on the design of the encircling zone, a coverage function for multiple aerial vehicles targeting mobile objectives is crafted. Subsequently, a comprehensive objective function, incorporating threat indices and damage effectiveness, is formulated to address the collective mobile targets. Leveraging the improved particle swarm optimization algorithm, this approach allocates the group of mobile targets, effectively transforming group cooperative confrontations into a multitude of group-to-one and one-to-one challenges. Simultaneously, real-time dynamic allocation is triggered based on the coverage function, ensuring continuous target coverage by multiple aerial vehicles up to the terminal moment. Ultimately, through numerical simulations, the efficacy of this allocation and encirclement strategy is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Application of GIS-aided INS/GNSS/GPRS navigation technology in logistics
abstract: Aiming at the problem of effective transportation in high-precision logistics, this paper adopts global navigation satellite system, general packet radio service and inertial navigation technology to construct an integrated navigation system within GIS-aided, and designs a federal filter structure with adjustable information allocation coefficients to get navigation solving. To eliminate the observation anomaly, the DBSCAN clustering algorithm is used to evaluate the performance of the measurement information and serve as the basis for setting the adjustment information allocation coefficient, which can effectively improve the contribution of the local optimal estimation of the integrated navigation system and optimize the global evaluation. The geographical information can be used to avoid congested road sections in real time to improve the efficiency of logistics transport and distribution. Finally, simulation results shown that the integrated navigation system proposed and the designed federal filter structure can effectively improve the navigation and positioning accuracy of the vehicle, and improve the stability of the system in the case of limited satellite signal reception. The horizontal position accuracy of the logistics vehicle is controlled within plus or minus 3m.

articleTitle: Integrated Guidance and Motion Control for USV Collision Avoidance
abstract: In coastal waters, the navigable domain of unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) is restricted due to irregular static obstacles and encountered vessels, which increases the collision risk (CR) of a USV with encountered vessels and hence collision avoidance (COLAV) maneuvers of the USV will increase its sailing distance. This paper proposes a new integrated guidance and motion control scheme for the COLAV of USVs with encountered vessels based on the idea of nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC). An integral-type objective function of NMPC is designed as a function with respect to the heading deviation, surge speed, and distance from the USV position at instant t to its next waypoint position in the planned path over a prediction time horizon. The navigable domain of the USV, CR indexes of the USV with encountered vessels, USV dynamics, etc., are taken as the constraints of the objective function. Using a nonlinear programming technique, we obtain optimal solutions minimizing the objective function subject to the constraints, i.e., the optimal thrust and yaw moment for the integrated guidance and motion control for the COLAV of the USV with encountered vessels. Simulations and simulation comparison results on the USV and four other vessels demonstrate that, under the proposed integrated guidance and motion control scheme, the USV avoids collisions with encountered vessels along a shorter route with a lower CR.

articleTitle: RAM-SFE : A Novel Unsupervised Anomaly Detection Method Based on Random Anomaly Multi-Scale Feature Extraction
abstract: Anomaly detection is an important application in large-scale industrial manufacturing. However, most of the current surface defect detection methods based on image reconstruction use normal samples to train autoencoder (AE), which is easy to mistakenly identify normal pixels as abnormal pixels. Aiming at the shortcomings of surface defect detection methods based on image reconstruction, an anomaly detection method based on random anomaly multi-scale feature extraction (RAM-SFE) is proposed in this paper. Firstly, a data enhancement method (CNP) with cutting and noise paste is proposed, which enables the model to be trained with false abnormal data and enhances the robustness of the model. Secondly, a new image quality assessment scheme is proposed by combining gradient intensity Similarity deviation (GMSD), Structure Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) and Smooth L1, which solves the problem that the key information and texture details are not sufficiently concerned. At the same time, this method adopts multi-scale feature extraction technology, and introduces attention mechanism to make the model pay more attention to the sensitive region. Experiments show that compared with other anomaly detection methods, the proposed method achieves the best anomaly detection performance in many categories.

articleTitle: Collaborative Path Planning for Multiple Autonomous Underwater Vehicles Based on Improved Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
abstract: To solve the collaborative path planning problem of multiple autonomous underwater vehicles in complex environments, an improved particle swarm optimization algorithm is proposed to address the problems of traditional particle swarm optimization algorithms being prone to falling into local optima and having slow convergence speed, resulting in unreasonable search results. Firstly, a dynamic optimization formation transformation obstacle avoidance strategy was adopted for the multi AUV formation problem, and a formation obstacle avoidance strategy was designed that includes multiple modes of formation zero transformation, isomorphic transformation, and heterogeneous transformation. At the same time, this algorithm nonlinearly functionalizes the invariant inertia weights and acceleration constants in traditional particle swarm optimization algorithms, thereby optimizing the optimization ability and solving the problem of traditional particle swarm algorithms being prone to falling into local optima.

articleTitle: Adaptive trajectory tracking for an indoor blimp based on MPC and NDO
abstract: Indoor blimp has been widely studied because of its excellent safety and endurance capabilities. This paper focuses on the analysis of a helium-filled blimp operating in an indoor environment. The three degrees of freedom dynamic model is decoupled into planar motion and vertical motion, which are organized in the form of state space. To improve the anti-disturbance performance of the blimp, a model predictive control strategy based on a nonlinear disturbance observer is designed, and the mathematical derivation of the design is given in detail here. Finally, this paper builds a simulation platform and verifies the effectiveness of the control algorithm through the simulation results.

articleTitle: Discrete Adaptive Control of Hypersonic Vehicles Based on Characteristic Models with Fuzzy Neural Network Observer
abstract: A novel discrete adaptive control scheme is developed based on the characteristic modeling theory, for the attitude control of a hypersonic vehicle with strong nonlinearities and uncertainties. A new structure of the characteristic model is proposed firstly, in which an extended state is added to describe the unmolded dynamics and disturbance. Then a fuzzy neural network observer is constructed to approximate the extended state, and the updated law of the characteristic parameters and the net parameters are designed simultaneously based on the structure of the characteristic model. Further, to reject the undesired influence of the time-variation of characteristic parameters and the approximation error of the neural network, a nonlinear term containing a saturation function is added to the parameter adaption law. Then an error-surface based control law is proposed on the basis of the characteristic model. Using the Lyapunov stability theory, the closed-loop system is proved stable and convergence properties of the system are assured. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed adaptive control scheme is illustrated by several representative simulations.

articleTitle: Efficient Attentional Underwater Image Enhancement Generative Adversarial Network
abstract: In the domain of underwater imaging, the attenuation of light, varying light conditions, and suspended particles often degrade image clarity, resulting in a loss of visual information and color distortion. The proposed Efficient Attentional Underwater Image Enhancement Generative Adversarial Network (EAU-GAN) offers a novel approach to address these challenges by leveraging the power of attention mechanisms in deep learning. This model employs an attention-driven generator that adaptively focuses on critical regions in the underwater image, thereby effectively highlighting obscured details while suppressing unnecessary noise. The discriminator, trained adversarially with the generator, ensures the generation of high-quality, naturalistic images. The innovation of EAU-GAN lies in its attention-driven generator that adaptively concentrates on crucial regions within underwater imagery. This targeted focus enhances obscured details and attenuates extraneous noise, markedly improving image clarity and color fidelity. Experimental results show that EAU-GAN outperforms other methods in both qualitative and quantitative aspects.

articleTitle: Research of mask wearing detection method using Improved YOLO network
abstract: Mask wearing detection technology is a practical and research-oriented area within object detection. Due to the complexity of mask wearing detection scenarios, issues such as small target detection and low image clarity often result in missed detections and false alarms. The YOLO algorithm, known for its fast detection speed, is commonly used in mask wearing detection. However, the original YOLO algorithm struggles to achieve satisfactory results in dense crowd scenarios. Therefore, this paper proposes an improved YOLOv5 algorithm based on the BiFPN structure and incorporating attention mechanisms to enhance the accuracy of mask wearing detection while maintaining real-time performance. The proposed approach firstly introduces the Bidirectional Feature Pyramid (BiFPN) structure into the backbone network to enhance the feature extraction capability. Additionally, attention mechanisms are incorporated to filter out irrelevant information, conserve computational resources, and improve the detection performance for small targets. Experimental results on a custom dataset demonstrate that the YOLOv5_BiFPN algorithm achieves a 4% improvement in accuracy and an 11.7% increase in mAP50 compared to the original YOLOv5. Moreover, the inclusion of attention mechanisms further boosts the accuracy by an additional 1.6%. These findings confirm that the improved YOLOv5s model exhibits superior performance in the task of mask wearing detection.

articleTitle: Sampled-Data Output Feedback Control of Linear Stochastic Systems with Noisy Sampling Intervals
abstract: The sampled-data output feedback control problem for a class of linear stochastic systems with noisy sampling intervals is studied. First, by using the relative properties of Wiener process, the conditional expectation and the law of total expectation, the dual randomness caused by the stochastic system and noisy sampling intervals is decoupled. The linear stochastic system is converted into an equivalent discrete-time system via the lifting technique. By the properties of matrix exponential function, together with the Kronecker product and the confluent Vandermonde matrix, the mathematical expectation of a product of multiple matrices is computed. The sampled-data output feedback controller is designed to stabilize the closed-loop system. Finally, a numerical example is given to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed design approach.

articleTitle: Set-Membership Filtering of Neural Networks with Medium Access Constraints and Packet Dropouts
abstract: This paper is concerned with the set-membership filtering problem for Neural Networks subject to medium access constraints and packet dropouts. First, neural networks are modeled as Markov jump systems with multiple modes by the stochastic characteristics of medium access restrictions, and the incidence of packet dropouts is described by a random variable that is governed by the Bernoulli distribution. Secondly, sufficient conditions for the existence of the required set-membership filter are derived in terms of the convex optimization approach, and the filtering error is constrained to the supplied ellipsoid set by addressing optimization problems and a reasonable estimation set. Finally, the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed filtering algorithm are verified by simulation examples.

articleTitle: Optimization of Spatiotemporal Dynamics in the Gierer-Meinhardt Model using a PD Control Strategy
abstract: While the spatiotemporal dynamics of reaction-diffusion systems have been extensively studied, the control of spatiotemporal evolution dynamics in reaction-diffusion systems remains an unresolved issue. The Gierer-Meinhardt reaction-diffusion system is a typical mathematical model to describe chemical and biological phenomena. By controlling the Turing patterns within the system, it is possible to make relatively accurate predictions and regulate the development trends of the reactants. However, there has been relatively limited research on the control of Turing patterns in Gierer-Meinhardt systems. In this paper, we propose a proportional differential control strategy for the Gierer-Meinhardt system with diffusion terms, aiming to regulate the spatiotemporal dynamics of the model through the controller.

articleTitle: Functional Failure Probability Analysis Method of Dispatching Automation Master Station System Based on Logistic Regression Model
abstract: The dispatching automation master station system (DAMSS) is an important component of power grid, responsible for real-time monitoring and control of the power grid’s status. Its stability and reliability directly affect the safe operation of the power grid. Once the DAMSS experiences functional failures, it can pose significant safety risks and lead to serious power grid accidents. To address this issue, this paper proposes a functional failure probability analysis method of DAMSS based on logistic regression model. This method thoroughly analyzes the risk factors that may cause functional failure and establishes a logistic regression model capable of analyzing the functional failure probability. The model can make full use of the data information retained during the operation of DAMSS, using the status of risk factors as evidence input to the logistic regression model, and obtain the functional failure probability. Finally, a case study is conducted on a specific DAMSS to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Author Keywords: the dispatching automation master station system

articleTitle: Decentralized multi-variable successive loop closure
abstract: The successive loop closure control approach is popular in engineering practice due to its ease of use. However, in most cases, the successive loop closure approach, for each loop closure, is in the configuration of single-input and single-output, which limits the usage of the control of multi-variable processes with coupled effects. In this paper, we extended the traditional successive loop closure control approach to multi-variable processes. To further improve the practicalness of the proposed method, in each closure, the decentralized integral controller will be designed. A sufficient condition for the existence of a controller to ensure the decentralized unconditional stability of each loop is proposed, under which the tuning of the loop gains becomes easier. Illustrative example is proposed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Face Anti-Spoofing Based on 3D Learnable Convolutional Operators
abstract: In face recognition systems, Face anti-spoofing (FAS) plays a crucial role in ensuring security and reliability across various applications such as identity verification and access control. Traditional methods primarily rely on two-dimensional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for extracting discriminative features from facial images, which have achieved significant success in distinguishing real faces from spoof attacks. However, these methods may encounter challenges in capturing temporal dynamics and modeling long-range dependencies inherent in liveness detection. This paper aims to address the limitations of existing methods by leveraging the advantages of three-dimensional convolutions and vision transformers for facial liveness detection. By combining 3D convolutions that capture spatiotemporal features with vision transformers that excel at capturing global contextual information, we can effectively enhance the accuracy and robustness of liveness detection systems. Additionally, we introduce learnable gradient operators to the 3D convolution operations, enabling adaptive learning of gradient information by the model. We evaluate our proposed method on multiple publicly available datasets and compare it against current state-of-the-art approaches. The results demonstrate lower average classification error rates, showcasing the superiority of our approach.

articleTitle: Preview Path Tracking Control for Autonomous Vehicle with Actuator Saturation
abstract: For autonomous ground vehicles, ignoring the actuator saturation problem caused by mechanical structure can lead to poor path tracking performance. In this paper, we propose a preview based path tracking control strategy, where actuator saturation is taken into account such that precise and computationally efficient path tracking performance is achieved. Both preview path model and actuator saturation model are integrated into the cost function, and a LQR based optimal controller is designed. Finally, the joint simulation experiments using Carsim and MATLAB show that the path tracking performance of autonomous ground vehicles with the proposed method is satisfactory.

articleTitle: Asynchronous switched LPV control for quad-tilt rotor UAVs against actuator faults and persistent external disturbances
abstract: An asynchronous switched linear parameter-varying (LPV) fault-tolerant control method is proposed for quad-tilt rotor UAVs to address actuator faults and persistent external disturbances. The nonlinear longitudinal dynamics of quad-tilt rotor UAVs with both abrupt and time-varying actuator faults are converted to a switched LPV system. A group of LPV controllers are designed, and each of them is adaptable to a specific subspace of parameters. Closed-loop stability and ℒ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> disturbance attenuation performance of the underlying switched LPV system are analyzed using multiple parameter-dependent Lyapunov functions and the persistent dwell-time technique, where delays in the detection of actuator failure are taken into account. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed switched LPV fault-tolerant control scheme.

articleTitle: H∞ control of fractional-order singularly perturbed systems: The 1 < ν < 2 case
abstract: This paper addresses the problems of the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> analysis and control of fractional-order singularly perturbed systems with the commensurate order 1 < ν < 2. Based on the bounded real lemma for fractional-order systems and singular fractional-order systems, the sufficient conditions for the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performance analysis of fractional-order singularly perturbed systems are firstly presented in terms of -independent linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Then, the state feedback controllers are designed, and the sufficient -independent stabilization conditions are established via bilinear matrix inequalities(BMIs). Moreover, by the provided iterative algorithm, these BMI-based conditions can be solved based on LMIs. Finally, two numerical examples are exploited to verify the effectiveness of the proposed results.

articleTitle: Observer based Rigid Body Attitude Tracking Using Vector Measurements Directly
abstract: This paper considers the construction of attitude tracking algorithms of a rigid body in the absence of angular velocity measurements, based on the typical observer-controller framework. Compared with the classical attitude tracking algorithms, the proposed method utilizes the inertial vectors measurements directly in an explicit form, without any reconstruction of the attitude vectors. To analyze the stability of the observer-controller, a strict Lyapunov-like function is adopted for the controller part. Simulations are conducted to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement of EV Charging Stations Based on Genetic Algorithm
abstract: Under the influence of the energy crisis and global warming, electric vehicles have been recognized by people all over the world as clean energy vehicles. However, the rapid growth of electric vehicles has brought challenges to electric vehicle charging station placement. To solve the optimal placement problem of electric vehicle charging stations, this paper proposes a kind of method for electric vehicle charging station placement by using genetic algorithm optimization. In the proposed method, the comprehensive cost of electric vehicle charging stations is defined first. Then, the placement of electric vehicle charging stations is optimized by minimizing the comprehensive cost of electric vehicle charging stations. Finally, the optimal location of charging stations and capacity of charging stations is determined by using genetic algorithm optimization. The simulation results show that the proposed method can give the optimal location and capacity of charging stations based on the real road map.

articleTitle: An interactive method for multi-satellite imaging mission planning in complex environments
abstract: Existing multi-satellite imaging mission planning methods mostly apply to scenarios with clear problem boundaries, explicit decision rules, and limited problem sizes. It is difficult to deal with the problem that the real environment is more complex and the action effect is more uncertain. This paper proposes a Human-machine interactive mechanism based on knowledge transfer strategy multi-objective evolutionary algorithm (HMIM-KTSMOEA) for Multi-satellite Imaging Mission Planning in Complex Environments (MSIMPCE). Firstly, a Human-machine interactive mechanism is proposed to deal with the dynamic changes of the environment effectively. Secondly, a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm based on a knowledge transfer strategy is proposed to improve the efficiency of MSIMPCE, which has complex constraints and large solving space. Simulation results show that HMIM-KTSMOEA has obvious advantages in solving the MSIMPCE problem in terms of task execution efficiency and response time.

articleTitle: Re-entry Trajectory Planning Algorithm for Reusable Launch Vehicle Based on RRT*
abstract: A re-entry optimal trajectory planning method based on the Rapidly exploring Random Tree* (RRT*) algorithm is proposed for the Reusable Launch Vehicle (RLV) under multiple constraints. During the longitudinal profile planning, a multi-constraint flight corridor is constructed in the altitude-velocity space according to dynamic pressure, load, heat rate and equilibrium glide condition constraints. In order to obtain a smooth, controllable altitude-velocity reference trajectory, three types of cost have been proposed, i.e., cost of control, smooth trajectory and range. By doing so, a feasible reversal point can be guaranteed which will be used to design the lateral trajectory to the heading alignment circle. Further, the RRT* algorithm is employed to solve the derived optimal problem quickly. The proposed algorithm transforms the re-entry trajectory planning problem under multiple constraints into a path cost setting problem in the RRT* algorithm that greatly improving the speed and reliability of trajectory planning. The simulation results show that the designed reference trajectory is smooth, the logic is simple and easy to implement in engineering.

articleTitle: A differential game model of joint emission reduction in dual-channel supply chain under channel conflic
abstract: The growing awareness of low-carbon lifestyle among consumers has prompted enterprises to engage in emission reduction. In low-carbon supply chain practices, joint emission reduction is widely used for win-win collaboration. In this paper, we develop a differential game model that involves one manufacturer and one retailer in a dual-channel supply chain under the low-carbon environment. We analyze the dynamic emission reduction decisions and discuss the impacts of consumer channel preference on optimal decisions. Our results show that as the consumer preference for the direct channel increases, the manufacturer’s optimal emission reduction effort also increases, while the retailer’s optimal advertising effort decreases. The emission reduction level of products monotonically increases over time, reaching a stable value, while the goodwill level initially decreases and then increases over time, ultimately reaching a stable value. The consumer preference for the direct channel has the same impact on the emission reduction level of products and goodwill level, but has an opposite impact on the profits of the manufacturer and the retailer.

articleTitle: A Temporal-Spatial Attention Encoder-Decoder Network for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting and Its Application in Hot Blast Stove Production
abstract: Deep learning has been widely used in multivariate time series prediction, which can automatically learn hidden information in historical process data. Due to the change of external conditions or the influence of unobservable variables, the sequence pattern of time series may change with time. There are also differences between local sequential patterns and global sequential patterns. In this paper, a temporal-spatial self-attention encoding and decoding (TSSA-ED) network is proposed. Firstly, the original data is divided according to different scale factors, and the sequence information in different scale data is extracted by TSSA-ED network. TSSA-ED network consists of temporal attention module and spatial attention module, which are used to capture temporal dependence and spatial dependence respectively. The input forms of the two modules are different, one is all time steps of single variable, and the other is all variables of the same time step. Finally, the model is applied to predict the dome temperature and exhaust gas temperature in the production process of hot blast stove, which proves the effectiveness of the proposed method. Compared with other traditional models, it is proved that the method proposed in this paper has higher prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Prediction Method for Domestic Used Car Selling Prices Based on CNN-BiLSTM
abstract: To address the issue of low accuracy in predicting used car prices, a prediction model combining Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) is proposed. The model takes standardized used car data as input and establishes a mapping between input and output by leveraging CNN (1-dimensional) for feature extraction and BiLSTM for time-series processing in the composite model. Furthermore, Random Forest and Support Vector Regression (SVR) are selected as comparative models to evaluate the predictive capability of the CNN-BiLSTM model. Experimental results demonstrate that the CNN-BiLSTM model achieves the highest accuracy, with an accuracy rate of 0.923, indicating the superior predictive performance of the model. This study can serve as a reference for practical used car price assessment.

articleTitle: Asynchronous sensor registration in the presence of outliers
abstract: In practical data fusion applications, measurement gross errors can be caused by network failures, non-line-of-sight propagation, attackers, etc. In addressing the problem of poor sensor registration accuracy due to measurement gross errors (outliers), this paper proposes an asynchronous sensor registration scheme in the presence of outliers. Real-time temporal synchronization is achieved through polynomial extrapolation according to the parameter estimation by the robust recursive least-squares (RRLS), followed by spatial registration correction of system bias using weighted recursive least-squares (WRLS). Simulation results demonstrate that when measurements contain random measurement noise, system bias and outliers, the proposed method is robust and offers better estimation of system bias compared to the conventional method.

articleTitle: A Residual-Variational Mode Decomposition to Detect Impact Signal
abstract: Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) has been widely used in signal process. However, number of modal and balance parameter limit the application of VMD seriously. To solve this problem, a novel method, residual-VMD (RVMD), is proposed in this paper. RVMD can be separated into two stages. In the first stage, VMD is run to decompose raw signal into a series of modals. Then, an improved ensemble kurtosis, named smooth ensemble kurtosis (SEK), is applied to evaluate the ratio of impulse component in each modal. Then, the modal which has the smallest SEK will be subtracted from the raw signal and replace the raw signal by the residual signal. This process will be repeated until the modal number is below 3. Then, the modal which has a larger SEK will be set as the input of the second stage. In the second stage, the balance parameter is obtained by a fix step length search method. Finally, the modal will be analyzed by envelope technology to observe the fault characteristic frequency clearly. The simulation and experiment results indicate the rationality of the proposed method. Meanwhile, the comparison results highlight its superiority than the others.

articleTitle: Prediction of gas utilization ratio based on singular spectrum analysis, improved PSO and KELM
abstract: The gas utilization ratio (GUR) in a blast furnace is directly linked to the efficiency, cost-effectiveness and environmental impact on the blast furnace ironmaking process. However, The stability of the published GUR time series prediction models need to be improved. This paper presents an improved particle swarm optimization (PSO) incorporating linearly decreasing inertia weights (LDIW) to optimize the kernel-based extreme learning machine (KELM) for single-step prediction. This paper uses singular spectrum analysis (SSA) to preprocess the data and extract the key components from the GUR time series to solve the problem of high volatility of the GUR time series. In addition, this paper introduces LDIW to improve the optimization ability of particle swarm optimization algorithm, which enhances the stability of a single-step prediction model. Then this paper uses the improved PSO algorithm to extract the optimal parameters of KELM, and establishes a single-step GUR prediction model based on the improved PSO-KELM. Finally, this paper uses the actual production process data of blast furnace to verify the prediction model. The results show that the prediction accuracy of GUR and the overall stability of the model are significantly improved, providing important guidance for the blast furnace ironmaking process.

articleTitle: Modelling and tensioned mooring control of a semi-submersible wind turbine
abstract: Our research subject is the 5MW semi-submersible wind turbine model released by the National Renewable Energy Laboratory of the United States. We investigated its motion response and mooring control technology under the combined influence of wind and waves. We have developed seven-degrees-of-freedom multi-rigid-body dynamics models for catenary mooring and tensioned mooring using the Lagrangian method in Matlab. We have also included external wind and wave loading models. The simulation compares the catenary mooring wind turbine model with OpenFast to verify the accuracy of the model. The fuzzy PID control rule is used to control the tensioned mooring wind turbine model by controlling the mooring line retraction and release using the anchor winch fixed on the platform. The research results show that the established wind turbine model is consistent with OpenFast. Under combined wind and wave conditions, the tensioned mooring wind turbine model with mooring control reduces the swing distance and improves stability.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning With Adjustable Convergence Rate for Data-Based Nonlinear Control
abstract: In this paper, a value-iteration-based off-policy Q-learning algorithm is developed. The proposed algorithm solves the optimal regulation problem of nonlinear systems with unknown dynamics. Under the off-policy mechanism, the algorithm utilizes the behavioral policy for full exploration, which is beneficial to avoid the target policy from falling into the local optimal solution. In addition, a relaxation factor is introduced to adjust the convergence rate of the cost function sequence. To implement the algorithm, the critic network and the action network are used to approximate the optimal Q-function and the optimal control policy, respectively. Finally, a simulation example is presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on the separation technology of SINS misalignment angles and installation error angles
abstract: When comparing the attitude information between the reference equipment and the measured SINS (Strapdown Inertial Navigation System), due to the influence of the calculated navigation coordinate system error of the measured SINS and the non-coincidence deviation between these two equipment, there will be two type of angle differences, i.e. misalignment angles and installation error angles, at the same time. The attitude measurement equation reflecting the above two angle errors is established in this paper, and the SINS attitude angle motion mode to realize the separation of the two angles is given, that is, the two axes of SINS are rotated in turn to make the rotation angles more than 30 (°). Through the measurement equations of the three angular positions before, after and in the middle of the rotation and solved by the least square method, the effective separation of the misalignment angles and the installation error angles can be realized.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Automatic Obstacle Avoidance and Handling System Based on PLC
abstract: This project adopts Delta PLC as the controller, and uses dual axis AC servo motion control platform as the control object to design an automatic obstacle avoidance and handling system. This system utilizes diffuse reflection photoelectric switch to detect the route obstacle information, and designs the software control system in WPLSoft software platform to realize the automatic obstacle avoidance of the handling system. At the same time, the login interface, the parameter setting interface and the main running interface were designed through Delta's HMI supporting software DOPSoft. Experiments have shown that after completing parameter settings through the human-machine interface, the handling system can achieve automatic obstacle avoidance, effectively improving handling efficiency and safety.

articleTitle: Proportional Multi-resonance Control plus Load Current Feedforward for CVCF Inverters
abstract: This paper proposes a proportional multiple resonance (PMR) plus load current feedforward (LCF) control strategy to address the problems of control inaccuracy and high harmonics for CVCF inverters. Firstly, a mathematical model for CVCF inverter is established. Subsequently, to mitigate the impact of the load on the output voltage, a unit load current feedforward control is designed. Meanwhile, the resonance gain coefficient, cutoff frequency, and proportional coefficients of PMR controller are individually designed based on the requirements of system stability, steady-state error, and controller bandwidth. Finally, experiments have shown that the proposed PMR plus LCF control strategy can force the CVCF inverters to produce high-quality output voltage. The proposed scheme can improve tracking accuracy when inverter is connected to a linear load, and effectively suppress harmonics when connected to a nonlinear load.

articleTitle: An Exact Method for Stabilizing Control Design of Planar Linear Periodic Sampling Systems
abstract: The invariance, which is referred to such properties that remain invariant under the coordinate changes, plays a key role in control theory. We present a method through invariance for the stabilization control design of planar linear systems with periodic sampling state-feedback. Using this method allows us to characterize the interrelation between the sampling periodicity and the feedback gain parameters so as to achieve stabilization. Thus, we can obtain all the feasible solutions of sampled-data state-feedback control. Illustrative examples are included to show the effectiveness of the theoretical method.

articleTitle: Optimal tracking control of two-time-scale system under cyber-attacks
abstract: In this paper, an optimal tracking problem of two-time-scale systems under cyber-attacks is studied. And an optimal tracking control method based on singular perturbation theory and reinforcement learning is proposed for the two-time-scale systems. Firstly, aiming at the singular perturbation parameter problem of the system, the system is decomposed into fast and slow subsystems by studying the singular perturbation theory. Secondly, the off-policy Q-learning is used to design the controller solution algorithm for the two subsystems respectively. The merit of the proposed algorithm is that the optimal tracking control law based on predicted states of systems can be learned using only measured data without knowing system dynamics. Besides, to solve the problem of system state data loss caused by cyber-attacks, a state predictor based on recurrent neural networks (RNN) is designed by using the historical data generated in the system operation. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is proved by simulation examples.

articleTitle: Double-Layer Following Controller for Autonomous Vehicles
abstract: In the context of vehicle platooning, scenarios involving high-speed overtaking, sharp turns, and speed variation for obstacle avoidance often compromise vehicle stability, thus severely limiting improvements in both safety and comfort. To address these challenges, this study designs and develops an algorithm based on the Dynamic Window Approach (DWA) and fuzzy adaptive Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) control. While ensuring safety, this algorithm enhances the comfort of autonomous vehicles. Simulation experiments demonstrate that, while maintaining a safe following distance, the algorithm exhibits outstanding robustness and safety in various experimental scenarios, significantly enhancing vehicle comfort.

articleTitle: Adaptive Equivalent Consumption Minimization Strategy for Fuel Cell Ships Suffering From Efficiency Degradation
abstract: In this paper, a strategy considering fuel cell efficiency degradation is proposed to deal with the impact of fuel cell performance degradation on Marine power system energy management. By characterizing the degradation behavior of fuel cell efficiency, a time-varying model was established to capture its dynamic nature. Based on the relationship between fuel cell efficiency and degradation rate, a fuel cell degradation factor was introduced to design the energy management objective function considering efficiency degradation, and the power of fuel cell and lithium battery was optimally allocated. The results demonstrate that compared to the typical strategy, the proposed method can increase fuel cell efficiency by up to 5.05% and reduce the equivalent total hydrogen consumption by 3.32% in slightly degraded, semi-degraded, and severely degraded stages. In the whole life cycle of fuel cell, the proposed method can optimize the overall energy consumption of Marine hybrid power system.

articleTitle: Leader-following exponential consensus control for discrete-time multi-agent systems with time-varying communication delay and unmeasured state: two general methods
abstract: This paper studies the leader-following exponential consensus of discrete-time multi-agent systems with time-varying communication delay by means of the relative-output-based and observer-based methods. In the presence of time-varying communication delay, the relative-output-based and observer-based protocols are provided respectively. Relying on the model transformation method, the exponential consensus problem is reformulated into the stability problem of the augmented time-delay error systems by means of an exponent transformation technique. Based on the delay-based multiple Lyapunov function, a sufficient condition to ensure the exponential consensus is formulated into linear matrix inequality by means of a structure separation technique. Simulation studies are utilized to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Novel Bi-stage Adaptive Search-Scale Algorithm for Continuous Optimization
abstract: This paper proposed a Bi-stage Adaptive Search-scale Algorithm (BASA). Some new mechanisms of search strategy, select strategy, and adaptive search-scale strategy were designed to improve the optimization performance of BASA, especially the ability to jump out of the local optimal solution. To evaluate the optimization performance of BASA, not only BASA but also 9 other algorithms are tested on 6 baseline test functions, whose results are used to compare with BASA, and analyzed the results from the perspectives of search speed and accuracy, verified the advantages of the BASA in solving continuous optimization problems.

articleTitle: Analysis on the Attitude Kinematic Equation of a Quadcopter with Rotor Failure
abstract: The challenge of fault-tolerant control (FTC) method for a quadcopter is that it is difficult to maintain full control of arbitrary states with rotor failure. In this paper, an attitude motion analysis method is proposed to explain the rationality of sacrificing the controllability of the yaw state from a mathematical perspective. Firstly, a model transformation method is proposed, which reformulates the problem as the attitude motion of a rigid body under torque disturbances in the spin-stable state. Secondly, a neural network-based method for solving the attitude kinematic equation of a spinning rigid body is proposed. Finally, the results of numerical experiments reveal a phenomenon wherein the numerical solution takes on a trigonometric form when the system is in the spin-stable state.

articleTitle: Solvability for a class of φ-Laplacian nonlinear fractional differential equations with parameters*
abstract: In this paper, a class of boundary value problems of nonlinear fractional differential equations with φ-Laplacian operator is investigated. Based on the Schauder fixed point theorem, a new existence result for positive solutions, in terms of the value of the parameter h is obtained. Finally, an example is given to illustrate the main result.

articleTitle: Scene Editing Based on NeRF
abstract: The NeRF has achieved impressive results in novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction, but beyond recovering the geometric structure of the scene, there is a need for more tasks to scene understanding and interaction. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a new scene editing technique by generalizing pixel semantics and colors rendering formulas, which can achieve the unique displays of the specific semantic targets or masking them. So far, most NeRF models have been designed to learn the entire scene. However, When there are many objects in the scene and the background is complex, it often leads to longer learning time, poorer rendering performance, and even many artifacts. Therefore, using the proposed scene editing technique, this article focuses NeRF on learning specific objectives without being affected by complex backgrounds. It results in faster training speed and greater rendering quality. Finally, to address the problem of incorrect inference in unsupervised regions of the scene, we design a self-supervised loop combining morphological operations and clustering at the output end of the NeRF. These improvements are applicable to all NeRF-based models.

articleTitle: A Periodic Recursive Network Based on Temporal Attention Convolution for Soft Sensing
abstract: Quality prediction ensures the safety of industrial production. However, the nonstationary period characteristic produced by repeated motions makes soft sensing difﬁcult. In this paper, a period recursive network (PRN) is proposed to achieve nonstationary quality prediction. At ﬁrst, period length of original data is calculated in the frequency domain space using fast Fourier transform (FFT). Secondly, original data is divided by period length and a temporal attention convolution network (TACN) is designed to extract the short-term dynamic features of each subperiod data. Then, a recursive structure is constructed to facilitate information transfer within individual subperiods and the features of multiple subperiods are concatenated recursively in PRN. The concatenated features have long-term memory across periods and will be used for soft sensing of quality variables. The quality prediction effect of PRN has been veriﬁed in a real thermal power generation process.

articleTitle: Fixed-time stabilization control of underactuated bridge crane system
abstract: A bridge crane system is an underactuated mechanical system with two degrees of freedom (DOF) and one control input. In this paper, the fixed-time stabilization control problem for this 2-DOF underactuated is studied. First, we approximately linearize the system around the origin based on the system’s actual control objective. And then, a coordinate transformation is constructed to change the linearized system to be a chain system. After that, we construct a sliding mode surface for the chain system and design a controller that drives the system to reach the sliding mode surface within a fixed time. This enables the fixed-time stabilization control objective of the bridge crane system to be achieved. Finally, the numerical simulation results verify the effectiveness of our developed control method.

articleTitle: The State of Charge Estimation of Lithium-ion Battery Pack Based on PSO-KELM
abstract: Accurately estimating the State of Charge (SOC) is of great significance for ensuring the safe operation of lithium-ion batteries and preventing overcharging or discharging. However, as SOC is the internal state of the battery unit and cannot be directly measured, it is difficult to obtain accurate SOC values. To improve the estimation accuracy of SOC, this paper establishes a prediction model using Kernel Extreme Learning Machine (KELM), and uses Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to optimize the kernel function parameter S and regularization coefficient C of KELM and determine the optimal values, a SOC prediction method for lithium-ion batteries based on PSO-KELM is proposed. The input of the PSO-KELM model is battery voltage, current, and temperature, the output is the actual SOC value. The results show that the root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and mean percentage error (MAPE) of SOC prediction are reduced to 2.76%, 2.18%, and 6.89%, increase coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) to 0.9919. The PSO-KELM model improves prediction accuracy compared to ELM and KELM models, and has good convergence and generalization properties.

articleTitle: Covert communication design based on Cooperative jamming technology
abstract: Wireless communication has a wide coverage in our daily lives. However, during the process of using wireless communication for information transmission, the transmitted information is easily stolen, causing significant damage to our information security. To address these issues, we have designed a digital filter using collaborative interference technology to achieve signal denoising and enhancement. Firstly, the target signal is subjected to noise processing to eliminate interference from eavesdroppers. Then, modulation and demodulation are performed at the signal-receiving port to restore the desired target signal. Finally, the noisy and denoised signal is compared with the target signal in the frequency domain and image. The experimental results show that Gaussian white noise can effectively reduce the reception performance of eavesdropping nodes and target nodes while separating this interference signal at the receiving node to achieve covert transmission of wireless communication.

articleTitle: Attitude Control Law Design Based on LQR for a Compound High-speed Helicopter
abstract: A new configuration of high-speed helicopter is taken as the research object, and its nonlinear flight dynamics model is established. Based on the small disturbance theory, the nonlinear model is analytically linearized to obtain the state-space equations of the compound high-speed helicopter in hover state. A state feedback linear quadratic regulator(LQR) is used to design the attitude control law, and the closed-loop control simulation is conducted in the Matlab/Simulink simulation environment. The simulation results show that the attitude control law designed in this paper can realize rapid and reliable tracking of the attitude angles, and meet the hover requirements of the compound high-speed helicopter.

articleTitle: Inverse Reinforcement Learning of Nonlinear Systems with Input Constraints
abstract: This paper proposes a model-based inverse reinforcement learning for nonlinear systems with input constraints. A saturation function is introduced to transform the original saturation optimal control problem into a new unconstrained optimal control problem. The recursive weight update law is established by using the approximate inverse Bellman error and the optimal controller error. Then, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through a simulation example.

articleTitle: Clicked:Curriculum Learning Connects Knowledge Distillation for Four-Player No-Limit Texas Hold’em Poker
abstract: Equilibrium solution is the core subject of imperfect information game. Although game solving paradigms vary from knowledge-guided tree search, through game reinforcement learning, to offline blueprint strategy pre-training and online adaptation, strategy transferability is the key to game solving, that is, how to train robust response strategies for various types of opponents. In this paper, we propose a CLICKED method of curriculum learning connects knowledge distillation to solve multi-player imperfect information games. Different kinds of four-player curriculum are designed for curriculum knowledge distillation. Based on this framework, we designed a four-player Texas Hold ’em Poker agent that competed in the 2023 AAMAS Imperfect Information Game and won the third place. In addition, the experimental results prove the feasibility of the curriculum learning connects knowledge distillation method.

articleTitle: Neural Network-Based Vibration Control of Flexible Two-Link Manipulator with Input Deadzone
abstract: A neural network (NN)-based vibration controller is designed to compensate for the impact of input deadzone on trajectory tracking and vibration suppression of flexible two link manipulator (FTLM). This article uses the assusmed mode method to transform the partial differential equation model of FTLM system into an ordinary differential equation model. Based on the dynamic model of the robotic manipulator, a full state feedback NN control is proposed. The first radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) is used to approximate the input deadzone effect, and the second RBFNN is used to approximate the unknown dynamics of the robotic manipulator. Then, the stability of the closed-loop system was analyzed using the Lyapunov direct method, and the semi global boundedness of tracking error and vibration error was proved. Finally, simulation was conducted on the Quanser experimental platform to verify the control performance of the neural network and compare it with the simulation results of the PD controller.

articleTitle: Activation Control Networks with Gradient Sparse Regularization for Mechanical Fault Diagnosis
abstract: Mechanical fault diagnosis has become increasingly important as the popularity and complexity of mechanical devices increase. Deep neural networks-based mechanical fault diagnosis methods perform well in terms of accuracy, but their poor interpretability makes them under-utilized in real industrial scenarios. To address this problem, this work proposes activation control networks with gradient sparse regularization. Specifically, firstly, a large number of interpretable features are constructed based on the monitoring signals, and then the activation control networks with gradient sparse regularization is used to adaptively select the effective features and give the feature importance ranking, which can be used as the basis for fault mechanism analysis. Also, the decision-making process of the activation control networks is well interpretable. Experimental results show that the proposed method has favorable fault diagnosis accuracy and interpretability.

articleTitle: Parameterized Design of Impact-Angle-Constraints Guidance Law Based on Fully-Actuated System Theory
abstract: To satisfy the terminal impact-angle-constraints, a guidance law based on the Fully-Actuated System Theory (FAST) is proposed. Without compromising the fully actuated characteristics of the control system, a second-order fully actuated model is established to describe the missile's dynamics in the longitudinal plane and the missile-target kinematics. By selecting the line-of-sight(LOS) angle as the constraints condition, a proportional-derivative feedback control term and a compensation term based on FAST are designed. This approach increases the design flexibility of the system and reduces the complexity of controller design. To improve the guidance performance of the direct parameterization design method based on FAST, limits are introduced for the LOS angle and the missile-target distance. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method ensures the missile can stably hit the target and satisfy the impact-angle-constraints.

articleTitle: Abnormal behavior recognition of automatic driving in urban road environment
abstract: With the rapid development of science and technology and the rise of artificial intelligence technology, the process of automatic driving technology is in full swing, but in the face of the complex and changeable urban environment in reality, the recognition of abnormal behavior of automatic driving (ABAD) is a difficult problem to be solved urgently. Restricted by economic, safety, legal norms and other conditions, it is extremely difficult to recognize the abnormal behavior of autonomous driving vehicles in the real environment. In order to solve this problem, based on the simulation environment, this paper takes the ABAD scene library as the center, and builds an ABAD recognition framework from four aspects: urban traffic environment, dynamic traffic scene, abnormal behavior classification and abnormal behavior recognition. In the experiment, the CARLA-SUMO co-simulation platform is used to obtain the vehicle data set with autonomous driving behavior (ADB) in the urban road environment. Finally, KNN, SVM, Naive Bayes, random forest and BP neural network are used to identify the ABAD, and their advantages and disadvantages are compared. The ABAD recognition framework constructed in this paper can effectively promote the simulation and test process of AD, and accelerate the realization of high-level automatic driving functions.

articleTitle: Learning Modality Residual Regularized Correlation Filter for Real Time RGB-T Tracking
abstract: With the development of image sensor technology, RGB-T tracking methods have demonstrated their potential performances in visual object tracking tasks. In order to effectively utilize the heterogeneity of visible images and thermal infrared images and handle the challenging scenarios (e.g., thermal cross, deformation and partial occlusion, etc.), in which several existing methods are limited in, a novel tracking framework using handicraft and tiny deep features is proposed in this paper. First, by integrating the residue of features extracted from two modalities, a modality residual regularization term is generated in regression of the correlation filter (CF) framework to learn more distinct features. Second, a progressive temporal regularization is introduced as well to handle the rapid object appearance variations. Moreover, a simple but effective dynamic model update and redetection mechanism is designed to further improve the robustness of the proposed tracker in complex scenarios. Exhaustive experiments are conducted on 284 challenging sequences on two tracking benchmarks, (GTOT and RGBT234), and proves the effectiveness of the proposed tracker in accuracy, robustness. Besides, the proposed tracking method has reached 65.34 FPS, which is faster than mainstream trackers.

articleTitle: Accurately Detecting Dense Small Objects from Aerial Images by Fusing Local Enhanced Features and Balanced Category Loss
abstract: Object detection from aerial images has been successfully used in intelligent transportation systems and disaster relief. Due to the large ranges of aerial images, disordered scenes, and various environments, accurately detecting valuable objects from aerial images is difficult. Current "You Only Look Once" detection algorithms commonly suffer from the problems of missed/false detection and imbalanced category detection, especially when detecting small objects. Thus, an improved network based on YOLOv5, named YOLOv5-EPD, has been developed to address the above problems. First, the adaptive up-sampling operator was embedded into the up-down path of PANet to enhance its ability in extracting local semantic features. Then, a large-size convolutional kernel was inserted into the down-up path of PANet to extend its receptive field. Therefore, the YOLOv5 network involving the improved PANet module is capable of obtaining richer semantic and spatial information on small objects. Furthermore, a dynamic cross-entropy loss has been developed to adjust the percentage of each category classification loss, to balance the detection accuracies of different categories. Experiments on a public dataset (VisDrone2019) showed that YOLOv5-EPD was superior to the existing detection methods, improving by 3.8% of mAP50 compared with the basic YOLOv5, which reveals the application potential of our approach in aerial images object detection.

articleTitle: Parameter identification and vibration suppression for three-dimensional Euler-Bernoulli beam
abstract: In this paper, the vibration suppression of three-dimensional Euler-Bernoulli beam based on parameter identification is studied. The appropriate control scheme is designed in the presence of unknown parameters and unknown disturbances. In this paper, a parameter identification method based on support vector machine (SVM) is proposed to identify the unknown parameters, and a self-evolving fuzzy neural network (SEFNN) is proposed to approximate the unknown disturbances. The boundary controller is designed based on the results of identification and approximation. Finally, the stability of the closed-loop system is analyzed by Lyapunov method, and the effectiveness of the parameter identification method and control scheme is verified by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: A Stacking Ensemble Learning Method for Non-Intrusive Appliance Load Monitoring
abstract: Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) collects the overall power consumption information from the power panel with advanced metering infrastructure, and obtains the operating states and power consumption information of each electrical appliance through load decomposition algorithms, so as to come up with appropriate strategies to reduce energy consumption and improve energy efficiency, which is of great significance for energy conservation and reduction. In recent years, NILM methods based on deep learning algorithms have received much attention and achieved good results, but the type of features extracted by a single deep learning model is limited, resulting in the model’s inability to overcome the bottleneck of accurate decomposition. To address the above problems, this paper proposes a deep ensemble learning framework for NILM, which takes the total active power sequence as input and synthesizes the advantages of multiple deep learning neural network models to further improve the performance of appliance identification and power disaggregation. Experiments are designed and conducted on the UK-DALE dataset to verify the effectiveness of the proposed deep ensemble learning method for NILM. The experimental results show that the method proposed in this paper has more advantages and is more promising in terms of various metrics compared to single deep learning approaches.

Index Terms: Root Mean Square Error Of Cross-validation

articleTitle: Multi-condition modeling and optimal control of boiler based on improved FCM clustering algorithm
abstract: Boiler is the main equipment of coal-fired power plant, which has complex and variable characteristics of multiple operating conditions due to different loads in daily production. The overall operational efficiency of the plant is directly affected by its control level, especially for the accommodation of the different operating conditions. In this paper, the improved fuzzy C-mean clustering algorithm is proposed to realize the classification of boiler conditions by extracting the features of boiler combustion history data and modeling each sub-condition using the prediction error method at first. Then a multi-model predictive control method based on T-S fuzzy theory is designed to control key variables such as active power in the boiler. In experimental study, real data is used to comparing the proposed with other commonly used methods, such as the conventional Fuzzy C-means clustering algorithm. The results show that the method proposed in this paper has obvious advantages in boiler modeling accuracy and control performance, which verifies the reasonableness for boiler condition identification as well as the practicability for real-world application.

articleTitle: Joint Model of Intent Recognition and Slot Filling Based on Graph Neural Network fusion of external knowledge base
abstract: Pretrained language processing models have shown significant results in spoken language comprehension tasks, particularly in joint modelling of intention recognition and slot filling. However, these models lack external knowledge support for complex and precise reasoning tasks, which is a limitation compared to human language understanding. This paper proposes a joint model for spoken language comprehension that utilizes the BERT pre-trained language model and combines the graph attention mechanism as a coding layer to semantically represent the input text. BiLSTM is used to achieve the fusion of external knowledge. The model is based on BERT fusion of external knowledge base. The joint model captures the association between the tasks of intention recognition and slot filling through joint training. Additionally, an external knowledge base is introduced to enhance the model's performance. Empirical analyses support that the unified model achieves exceptional accuracy in both intent recognition and slot-filling areas, outperforming other benchmark models.
