articleTitle: A new human motion recognition framework based on the fusion of joint data and RGB video
abstract: In the field of behavior recognition, the action recognition method based on joint data has achieved high recognition accuracy, but its recognition accuracy is not high in the recognition of similar actions that are easily confused. To solve this problem, considering that RGB video has more detailed motion information, a hierarchical recognition framework based on the fusion of joint data and RGB video data based on a spatio-temporal graph convolution network is proposed. First, the actions are classified according to the joint data; for example, similar hand movements are recognized into a class. Then, the optical flow network is used to extract the rich details contained in the RGB video, i.e. the optical flow slice data centered on the joint with human structural characteristics are constructed. Finally the data are sent into the spatio-temporal graph convolutional network for recognition of similar actions. The advantage of the proposed hierarchical recognition framework is that action recognition is divided into two levels. The first-level recognition can quickly identify the action by using the characteristics of the joint data, including only the coordinate information of the joints. The second level of recognition is similar action recognition by extracting local motion features from RGB video through optical flow network. Tests on the NTU dataset show that the accuracy of similar action recognition using joint data is only 80.15%, and the recognition rate of similar action recognition using the proposed hierarchical framework is 87.78%. It is proven that the framework is effective for similar action recognition.

articleTitle: FLONA: A Low-Latency, Low-Loss Optical Network Architecture for Multicast and Broadcast
abstract: With the increasing scale of Chip multiprocessors (CMPs), high-performance multicast and broadcast among multicores have become critical for improving overall chip performance. However, traditional bus-based, ring-based and tree-based optical network architectures cannot support multicast efficiently in terms of latency, power consumption, and scalability. In this paper, we propose FLONA, a low-latency, low-loss optical network architecture for supporting multicast and broadcast effectively. In FLONA, our designed layout of the two-stage serpentine-surround waveguide in communication subnetwork could reduce the number of waveguides and microrings and optical insertion loss. In addition, according to the partition rule of the clusters, our proposed wavelength assignment and communication mechanism are able to perform efficiently multicast and broadcast with lower latency and much fewer wavelengths, which further decreases the optical insertion loss and improves the scalability. Compared with traditional optical bus-based networks and tree-based networks, the simulation results based on the SPLASH-2 and PARSEC benchmark suite show that FLONA could decrease the end-to-end average latency and the worst-case optical insertion loss, and improve the network throughput.

articleTitle: An Improved Hierarchical Fused Fuzzy Deep Neural Network Method for Controlled Object Model of Furnace Temperature for MSWI Process
abstract: Addressing the challenge of precisely controlling furnace temperature, this study introduces a modeling strategy based on an enhanced hierarchical fused fuzzy deep neural network (HF-FDNN) model. Initially, an analysis of the control characteristics of furnace temperature identifies key manipulated variables (MVs). Subsequently, we refine the HF-FDNN algorithm within the task-driven layer to develop a model for furnace temperature control. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of proposed method through experimental results derived from real municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) process data.

articleTitle: Extended state observer-based generalized super-twisting control for flexible hypersonic vehicles
abstract: This paper investigates the anti-disturbance control design for flexible air-breathing hypersonic vehicles (FAHVs). Firstly, a control-oriented FAHV model is obtained using input-output linearization theory. Then, linear extended state observers (LESOs) with time-varying bandwidth parameters are developed to estimate and compensate the lumped disturbances of the FAHV system in real time. Time-varying bandwidths allow LESOs to resolve the conflict between peaking and rapidity. In addition, a generalized super-twisting (GSTW) sliding mode controller is designed by replacing the conventional discontinuous switching term with a nonsmooth term to track the desired velocity and altitude. The proposed GSTW control scheme can effectively eliminate unfavorable chattering problems. Finally, extensive comparative simulations are provided to demonstrate the feasibility and superiority of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Adaptive Improved Terminal Sliding Mode Tracking Control for 2-DOF Helicopter with Uncertain Parameters and Unknown Input Constraints
abstract: This paper studies the attitude tracking problem for 2-DOF helicopter system. An adaptive improved terminal sliding mode controller is proposed to address parameter uncertainties and unknown input constraints simultaneously. Specifically, an adaptive law is designed in the controller to eliminate the effects from uncertain parameters. In addition, the controller integrates terminal sliding mode and Nussbaum gain to counteract the impact of unknown input constraints. Finally, the effectiveness of the controller is substantiated through Lyapunov theory, and favorable tracking results are demonstrated by simulations.

articleTitle: Cross-coupling Attitude Synchronous Control of Satellite Formation via Fast Terminal Sliding Mode
abstract: In this paper, a novel attitude synchronous control strategy, by combining the cross-coupling synchronous method and non-singular fast terminal sliding mode controller (NFTSMC), is proposed for satellite formation systems with external disturbances and perturbations. First, the attitude dynamics and kinematics models of the considered satellite are presented. Second, to realize robust and fast attitude synchronization control, a NFTSMC is designed, whose convergence and stability are ensured based on Lyapunov theory. Then, an effective cross-coupling synchronous method, considering the synchronous error of adjacent satellites attitude control, is proposed, which can achieve the preferable unified regulation of satellite formation. Finally, sufficient numerical simulations are provided to verify the effectiveness and synchronizability of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Regulation-Triggered Batch Least-Squares Identifier based Adaptive Control with Unknown Control Coefficients
abstract: This paper focuses on regulation-triggered batch least-squares identifier based adaptive control for nonlinear systems with unknown control coefficients. Batch least-squares identifiers (BaLSI) are designed to estimate the unknown parameters, while a regulation-triggered condition is proposed to activate the BaLSI. Previous appeared excitation are stored and utilized for parameter updates at the triggering moments, based on which the persistently exciting (PE) conditions are no longer needed. Effects of unknown parameters can be eliminated after finite times of parameter updates. Compared with the existing results, the unknown control coefficients are considered, which may lead to singular control input. It implies that as the estimate of control coefficient approaches zero, the control input tends towards infinity. To address the aforementioned issue, two distinct control schemes have been proposed, which pertain to the parameter update law and the control law respectively.

articleTitle: Engineering Development of Highway Single Lane Autonomous Driving System
abstract: this paper describes a solution to develop a single lane auto drive system for expressway in an engineering way. In addition to the common adaptive cruise control and lane center keeping functions, this plan also includes an obstacle avoidance strategy that can avoid stationary targets and targets that suddenly appear in the target area, so as to improve the auto drive system of single lane expressway on the basis of the following function, lane keeping function, emergency braking auxiliary function and other functions. The test results show that the scheme can effectively avoid common abnormal conditions and achieve the purpose of enhancing the robustness of the auto drive system.

articleTitle: A pose estimation method based on RGB-D system in the process of attaching asteroids
abstract: Based on RGB-D system, a pose estimation algorithm framework integrating point cloud normal vector information, point cloud information and two-dimensional gray information is designed to solve the relative pose between spacecraft and non-cooperative target interest surface (NCTIS) during attaching asteroids. First, the framework fuses the organized point cloud obtained by the TOF (time of flight) camera with the color image to obtain the organized RGB-D point cloud data. Then, the normal vector feature of the point cloud is extracted and fused with the gray image information to perform variable scale template matching to track the NCTIS. The matching algorithm considering the normal vector feature improves the robustness and accuracy of the matching results. Finally, the relative pose between NCTIS and the spacecraft is estimated in real-time by the MRPs kinematics model based on the normal vector of NCTIS and the Kalman filter. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm framework is verified by ground experiments, and the accuracy and real-time performance of pose estimation meet the mission requirements.

articleTitle: Immersion and Invariance Adaptive SOSM Control for Uncertain Nonlinear Systems
abstract: This paper addresses the issue of designing a novel immersion and invariance adaptive second-order sliding mode (IIASM) control for uncertain nonlinear systems. First of all, an immersion and invariance (I&I) adaptive method based on the non-certainty equivalence (Non-CE) is analyzed to deal with the system uncertainty. On this basis, the second-order sliding mode (SOSM) control method is introduced to make the system state converge to zero in a finite time. Then, a new IIASM control strategy is designed to achieve excellent tracking performance in the case of system uncertainties. Further, the finite-time stability of the system is proved by strict Lyapunov analysis. Finally, a typical unmanned agricultural vehicle path-tracking simulation example is used to verify the superiority of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: An Implicit Gradient-Based Approach for Stackelberg-Population Security Resource Allocation Game
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to address a Stackelberg security resource allocation game for industrial network systems, where the attacker acts as the leader and the defenders as the followers. The followers form a distributed population game with graphical strategy interactions and capacity constraints. Then the optimal allocation strategy of the leader and the generalized Nash equilibrium of the followers together constitute a Stackelberg-population equilibrium (SPE), which can be attained by solving a bilevel optimization problem. To find the equilibrium, a distributed two-level learning dynamics based on implicit gradient and distributed population dynamics is developed. Additionally, a sufficient condition that ensures the convergence of the dynamics are proposed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed approach is verified through a numerical example and simulation.

articleTitle: Multi-Agent Spatial-Temporal Transformer for Traffic Signal Control
abstract: Multi-agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (MDRL) methods have demonstrated considerable promise in the optimization of traffic signal control (TSC) in road networks. Nevertheless, these methods are not without their limitations, including an increased level of complexity. In order to mitigate traffic congestion more effectively, multi-agent spatial-temporal transformer (ST-MAT) TSC model based on MDRL was proposed in this paper which employs a sequence model. The inclusion of the spatial-temporal attention mechanism in this model allows for the deduction of the spatial-temporal correlation between agents in the environment. This mechanism aids agents in dynamically perceiving the traffic environment and determining the importance of crossings. This study employs experimental trials conducted on the 4×4 synthetic road network and the real road networks of Ingolstadt. The results indicate that the ST-MAT model, when implemented in both simulation environments, successfully mitigates traffic congestion by reducing the average waiting time of vehicles to 14s and 40s, respectively. The utilization of the spatial-temporal attention mechanism enables agents to rapidly adjust to various traffic environments. The model shows commendable applicability in TSC tasks.

articleTitle: Research on Electric Hydraulic Power Steering Motor Control Strategies
abstract: In order to reduce energy consumption during the steering process of the electric hydraulic power steering system, employing a permanent magnet synchronous motor based on sensorless control technology as the steering assist motor is a feasible solution. This paper first analyzes the structure of the electric hydraulic power steering assembly, determines the speed regulation characteristics of the steering assist motor based on the load characteristics of the steering pump at different speeds. Based on this, a sensorless control strategy is proposed, utilizing a high-order sliding mode observer instead of the traditional sliding mode observer to mitigate the system chattering issues caused by the traditional observer. Through the establishment of a simulation model, the proposed control strategy is verified to possess strong robustness and disturbance rejection capabilities. Furthermore, the strategy is validated with actual steering conditions, demonstrating its favorable speed tracking performance.

articleTitle: Discrete-Time Distributed Least Square Algorithms for Linear Equations via Layered Coordination
abstract: This paper is concerned with the problem of designing discrete-time distributed algorithms for the least squares solution of over-determined linear equations via layered coordination. A row-column partition and a column-row partition are provided to partition the augmented matrix associated with the linear equations into several block matrices, respectively. By assigning an equation solver layer to computation and a data integration layer to data exchanges, a row-column partition-based discrete-time distributed algorithm and a column-row partition-based discrete-time distributed algorithm are proposed for solving over-determined linear equations, respectively. It is shown that the distributed algorithms proposed can reach a consensus exponentially on the least squares solution of linear equations. Finally, the effectiveness of the distributed algorithms proposed is validated via a numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Design and Validation of Pipeline Inspection Robot based on Panoramic Vision
abstract: Pipeline-type workpieces are prevalent in industrial production. However, manually inspecting the inner walls is an inefficient quality control activity that may pose safety risks to inspection personnel, especially for specialized workpieces with internal ramps. The complex internal structure further increases the difficulty of manual inspection. Therefore, designing a robot capable of navigating inside tube-shaped workpieces and stitching images of the inner walls into a single composite image is crucial for improving the efficiency of quality control processes for such workpieces. To meet this demand, we have designed a robot as an experimental platform capable of traveling and climbing ramps within pipes. The robot can handle a maximum climbing angle of 30 degrees and is equipped with four 180-degree wide-angle cameras arranged at 90-degree intervals, facilitating the capture of images around the pipe. Addressing the challenge of narrow environments inside pipes where conventional stitching algorithms may not be effectively applied, we have designed a stitching method capable of seamlessly stitching larger disparity images in narrow pipe environments. This algorithm optimizes the processes of feature point matching and optimal seam line selection, achieving higher-quality image stitching from the four cameras. The robot we designed will significantly enhance the efficiency of inspecting the inner walls of tube-shaped workpieces, particularly those with ramps.

articleTitle: Robust steady-state estimator for descriptor system with uncertain variances, measurement delay and multiplicative noise
abstract: The robust estimation problem is addressed for the linear stochastic descriptor system with uncertain variances, random one-step measurement delay and multiplicative noise. By utilizing the singular value decomposition method, fictitious noise method, and augmented state method, the original descriptor system is transformed into a reduced-order standard state space model with only uncertain-variance fictitious noise. Based on the minimax robust estimation principle and Kalman filter theory, the robust steady-state Kalman estimator, which includes the Kalman predictor, filter, smoother, and white noise deconvolution estimator, is presented in the sense that its actual estimation error variance is guaranteed to have the corresponding minimal upper bound for all admissible uncertainties. Additionally, the Lyapunov equation approach proves the robustness of the proposed estimator. An RLC circuit system simulation example shows its effectiveness and correctness.

articleTitle: Force Control of Polishing Robots Considering Sensor Measurement Sensitivity and Hysteresis Characteristics
abstract: In virtue of its excellent flexibility, high compliance, and convenient maintenance, pneumatic polishing equipment is widely used in the surface polishing of manufacturing products. However, due to the harsh working environment of polishing robots (e.g., high temperatures, humidity, and vibrations), the probability of inaccurate measurements is increased. At the same time, pneumatic systems have strong hysteresis and nonlinear characteristics because of the materials, friction, and gas resistance. The above issues will affect the accurate tracking performance of pneumatic control systems. Therefore, this paper proposes a force control framework considering hysteresis characteristics and sensor measurement sensitivity. Furthermore, an adaptive dynamic surface control method is designed to achieve precise force control under measurement sensitivity. In addition, the stability analysis is completed by using Lyapunov techniques, and all states of the closed-loop system are also guaranteed to be bounded. Finally, several groups of simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Optimization strategies for clearing the electric energy and FM market with combined thermal energy and storage
abstract: As a new type of regulation resource with two-way regulation function, energy storage is increasingly involved in automatic generation control and has become the key to the future frequency modulation (FM) auxiliary service market. In this paper, we propose an optimization strategy for market clearing of electric energy and frequency modulation based on the combination of thermal storage, which uses the security constrained unit combination (SCUC) model to determine the unit output plan and storage charging and discharging plan, and is based on the security constrained economic dispatch (SCED) model, with the objective of minimizing the total cost of the electric power system for market clearing. The system frequency stability is maintained by adjusting the output of generating units in order to respond quickly to changes in the system frequency. In this paper, we study the issues related to the participation of solo energy storage in the electric energy and frequency modulation market, including the market demand for frequency modulation auxiliary services, resource allocation strategy, security constrained unit combination (SCUC), and security constrained economic dispatch (SCED), etc., and utilize the data of frequency modulation auxiliary services provided by each unit in the power system to calculate the frequency modulation mileage and the capacity clearing price of each unit, as well as to construct the arithmetic example and evaluate its feasibility and economic benefits.

articleTitle: Planning and Scheduling of Integrated Electricity-Heat-Gas Energy Systems Considering Economics
abstract: With global climate change and environmental problems becoming more and more serious, the research and application of renewable energy and clean energy technologies have become the focus of attention. More and more substations incorporate renewable energy into the grid system. In this context, this paper proposes an optimal scheduling method for the integrated energy system containing wind power, hydrogen production and multiple energy storage. The model aims at maximizing the operating profit, takes into account the total energy sales revenue and the power purchase cost of the grid, takes into account the power balance and the constraints on the operation of the units and equipment, and performs the joint optimization of the hydrogen-heat-electricity multiple energy storage, and finally analyzes the benefits to the substation under different scheduling scenarios. The simulation results show that the proposed scheduling strategy can effectively reduce the grid power purchase cost of the substation and improve the system economy.

articleTitle: Two-Level Identity-Based Encryption Scheme for Internet of Things
abstract: In the application layer of the Internet of Things, there are multiple levels of user identities in the user management system. When the cloud and intelligent connected devices exchange big data among users, the sensitive data transmitted in the IoT are vulnerable to attackers. Therefore, how to build a secure Internet of Things data encryption scheme based on the identity level of the user is a critical issue. In this paper, we present a two-level identity-based encryption scheme for the hierarchical management system of the Internet of Things. The correctness and security of the scheme are analyzed. Compared with the lattice-based encryption scheme, our scheme has smaller keys and ciphertexts. To avoid the high computational complexity caused by the trapdoor delegation algorithm, our scheme is an efficient and practical two-level identity-based encryption scheme for the Internet of Things.

articleTitle: Complex Emergency Project Planning and Evaluation Methods Based on Multilayer Heterogeneous Networks
abstract: With the continuous development of economy and society, the emergency supply system has been widely developed, but how to realize the effective deployment of emergency units and improve the efficiency and effectiveness of emergency response is crucial to ensure the long-term stability of the city. This paper comprehensively summarizes the whole process of emergency supply work in the era of big data using a multilayer complex network model. It analyzes the planning and evaluation process of emergency supply plans and proposes a project portfolio decision method that takes into account both project attributes and topological attributes based on project association networks. Then, the selected projects are modeled in the supply network, and a pruning-based breadth-first search algorithm is used to select supply chains from the perspectives of timeliness and energy efficiency, and to formulate supply plans. Finally, the paper evaluates the plans from the perspectives of redundancy and riskiness, and proposes optimization strategies. To validate the proposed methods, the paper concludes with a case study on emergency supply for fire incidents.

articleTitle: DCFNet: A Distinction-aware Cross-stage Fusion Network for RGB-T Crowd Counting
abstract: RGB-T crowd counting gains robustness against poor illumination conditions by virtue of the complementarity of multimodal data. Although most existing methods have demonstrated promising results in fusing multimodal data, they suffer from two drawbacks. First, they overlook the information distinctions between different modalities, which is not conducive to exploring complementary information, thus potentially impeding fusion feature learning. Second, crowd information hidden in the hierarchical features is not fully mined, which makes it challenging to generate excellent density maps with limited feature representations. To overcome these drawbacks, we propose a Distinction-aware Cross-stage Fusion Network, namely DCFNet. It could effectively leverage information distinctions between modalities to preserve more complementary information and sufficiently delve into the hidden hierarchical information. Specifically, our DCFNet mainly comprises the Distinction-aware Multimodal Fusion (DMF) module and the Cross-stage Information Enhancement (CIE) module. The DMF module focuses on learning distinct information across modalities to raise the discriminable ability of fusion features and also provides a novel perspective for RGB-T crowd counting about how to explore valuable complementary information. Simultaneously, the CIE module aims to aggregate the cross-stage features and extract the maximum multi-level crowd information hidden in the hierarchical features, thereby enhancing the representation ability of the learned features. The DCFNet has been evaluated on two mainstream benchmarks, demonstrating its effectiveness and SOTA counting performance.

articleTitle: Dynamic-Memory Event-Based Output Feedback Security Control for Networked Delayed Descriptor Jump Systems Against Multiple Cyber-Attacks
abstract: This article studies the issue of output feedback control for descriptor Markov jump systems subject to spoofing attacks and DoS attacks via dynamic-memory event-triggered mechanism. By utilizing a group of historical transmitted data, the dynamic-memory event-triggered mechanism is quoted. Moreover, by building the improved segmented mode-dependent Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional, the exponential admissibility criterion for the controlled system is obtained by right of linear matrix inequalities. Lastly, the direct current motor model is exploited to testify the availability of suggested approach.

articleTitle: Secondary Aggregation Control Strategy for Typical County Territory Load
abstract: This paper proposes a strategy for secondary aggregation prediction optimization control to mitigate the peak impact of typical county territory loads, thereby achieving power balance. Initially, a secondary classification is established based on the differences in electricity consumption scenarios and customer satisfaction in county territory areas. and the adaptive fuzzy C-means algorithm is used to observe the differences in county typical load demands and latency. Subsequently, the LSTM model is employed to predict county typical loads and adjustable capacity for the formulation of control strategies. Finally, an optimization algorithm suitable for aggregated loads is proposed, with the objective function considering economic benefits and customer satisfaction, to minimize power control costs. The rationality and effectiveness of this strategy were validated through case studies.

articleTitle: Distributed Sampled-data-based Event-triggered Secondary Frequency Control for Islanded Microgrids
abstract: This paper porposes a distributed average integral (DAI) algorithm based on event-triggering for secondary frequency control in microgrids. Initially, the study considers a heterogeneous microgrid consisting of synchronous generators, droop-controlled inverters, and loads. The objective is to ensure zero frequency deviations for all nodes in the grid and the prescribed allocation of active power. Subsequently, in order to significantly reduce communication utilization, a DAI algorithm based on periodic sampling event-triggering is proposed, with data exchange occurring exclusively when predefined triggering conditions are violated. Furthermore, the stability of the closed-loop system is analyzed, based on which the sufficient conditions for consensus of system states are derived. Finally, simulation experiments are conducted on Kundur’s two-area four-machine test system. Through simulation verification, it demonstrates that the proposed event-triggered DAI algorithm is capable of realizing good performance in secondary frequency control while significantly reducing the utilization of communication resources.

articleTitle: Hybrid Sliding Mode Control of DFIG Wind Power Generation System Combining SMO and SMC
abstract: In light of the intrinsic nonlinear attributes and the indeterminate parameters associated with doubly fed induction motors (DFIG) within wind power generation systems (WPGS), proffering a methodology with the objective of attaining optimal power point tracking (MPPT) control becomes imperative. Henceforth, a Hybrid Sliding Mode Control (HSMC) strategy is posited as an innovative approach, tailored for the real-time synchronization of motor speed. This control paradigm amalgamates a sliding mode observer (SMO) harmoniously with a sliding mode controller (PEAL-SMC), the latter rooted in the power exponential convergence law (PEAL), giving rise to a composite framework denominated as Hybrid Sliding Mode Control (HSMC). Leveraging the capabilities of the sliding mode observer (SMO), we derive estimations for the stator current and rotor flux through an intricate analysis of the stator current and voltage parameters. Subsequently, employing these estimations, a computation is performed to ascertain the anticipated rotor speed. Transferring the ascertained rotor speed estimates into the realm of the PEAL-SMC, we seamlessly integrate them into the control tracking mechanism. The sliding mode controller, harnessing the power exponential convergence law (PEAL), is adept at augmenting the convergence speed of the system. This augmentation not only enhances the dynamic performance but also serves to diminish system jitter, thereby facilitating a more precise adherence to the reference speed. Via MATLAB/Simulink simulation, under step wind speed conditions, the proposed methodology not only guarantees the attainment of maximum power output but also exhibits a remarkable swiftness in convergence and commendable steady-state performance.

articleTitle: 3D Multi-object Tracking in Autonomous Driving: A survey
abstract: 3D multi-object tracking(3D MOT) is an indispensable component of autonomous driving because of its ability to perceive and track surrounding objects. In order to track the same object in consecutive frames, 3D MOT faces challenges such as object occlusion, abrupt motion, lighting variations and distortions, as well as scenarios with small and dense objects. In recent years, various methods have been proposed to address these issues. Therefore, it is crucial to analyze the commonalities and differences among different methods. Based on the relationship between detection and data association, this paper analyzes some mainstream methods in the recent three years. It categorizes them into three classes: tracking by detection(TBD), joint detection and embedding(JDE), and joint detection and tracking(JDT). Furthermore, for each method, we further divide it into several subcategories and summarize their approaches. Additionally, we compare the advantages and disadvantages of different methods and conduct a performance analysis on the nuScenes dataset.

articleTitle: Identification and location of distribution network cables based on multi-sensor system
abstract: In the current trend of domestic distribution network maintenance, the traditional power-off operation has been gradually replaced by power-on operation. To address the challenges of high labor intensity, low work efficiency, and safety risks associated with manual maintenance methods, researches on intelligent operation platforms for distribution network maintenance is developing rapidly. Specifically, quick and accurate identification of target cables for maintenance is essential for completing operations such as cable stripping and live wire connection in distribution network maintenance. However, due to the complex conditions of the environment, traditional methods can hardly specify the target, while the conventional deep neural networks cannot meet real-time requirements. Therefore, this paper proposes a system that utilizes RGB+Lidar to identify and locate the target cables. Besides, a lightweight image segmentation model with a straight-line attention module is developed to further improve accuracy. The verification on the testing set illustrates the satisfied speed and accuracy of the proposed method in practical scenarios.

articleTitle: Synchronization of Complex Dynamical Networks via Event-Triggered Pinning Impulses
abstract: This article studies the synchronization problem of complex dynamical networks. The impulsive control method is considered with a novel event-triggered pinning algorithm. Sufficient conditions on the network topology are obtained to ensure network synchronization. It is shown that synchronization can be realized with a careful selection of the pinning nodes. Furthermore, an adaptive coupling strength is incorporated into the network to allow network synchronization with an arbitrary selection of the pinning nodes. An example of a network with node dynamics described by the Chen system is studied to demonstrate the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving Vertical Federated Logistic Regression for Power Data Sharing
abstract: As a typical data element, the open of the electricity data has become an inevitable trend. However, frequent data exchanges in joint analysis can lead to uncontrollable privacy and security risks, as well as significant computational and communication overhead. To address it, this paper proposes a Vertical Federated Logistic Regression algorithm based on Secret Sharing (SSVF-LR). By randomly decomposing the intermediate data exchanged during the joint analysis into multiple secret shares, the algorithm achieves low complexity of privacy computation. This approach is beneficial for promoting the secure and open circulation of electricity big data. Finally, the proposed algorithm is validated on real electricity dataset. Experimental results show that, compared to the centralized logistic regression algorithm based on the single electricity data, SSVF-LR can effectively enhance the predictive performance, while the cost time is superior to the traditional federated logistic regression algorithm based on homomorphic encryption.

articleTitle: An Improved Multi-Objective Iterated Greedy Algorithm for Energy-Efficient Distributed Permutation Flowshop Scheduling Problem with Sequence-dependent Setup Times
abstract: Distributed energy-efficient scheduling has gained a lot of focus in industrial production in recent years. However, energy-efficient distributed permutation flowshop scheduling problem (EEDPFSP) with sequence-dependent setup time is closer to the actual manufacturing environment and has not attracted much attention so far. In this paper, energy-efficient distributed permutation flowshop scheduling problem with sequence-dependent setup time is investigated. An improved multi-objective NEH heuristic and an improved multi-objective iterated greedy algorithm (IMOIG) are proposed to minimize both total flowtime and total energy consumption. Effective construction, destruction and local search procedures are proposed in combination with a speed-scaling framework. Based on the sequence characteristics of the problem, the method of job block moving is proposed for local search. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is demonstrated through computational experiments by comparing with other four algorithms.

articleTitle: Hybrid Extended Kalman Filtering Triggered by the Degree of Polarization for INS/BPNS Integration
abstract: To handle the non-Gaussian measurement noise involved in the INS/BPNS (inertial navigation system/bionic polarization navigation system) integration, this paper proposes a hybrid extend Kalman filtering (EKF). Firstly, a new mode of the INS/BPNS integration is constructed by using the relationship between the E-vector angle and INS misalignment angle based on the inherent property of the polarized E-vector perpendicular to the scattering plane; Further, a maximum correntropy criterion-based EKF (MCC-EKF) is established based on the MCC theory to address the influence of non-Gaussian measurement noise; Based on above, a hybrid EKF is established, which is triggered between the EKF and MCC-EKF by the BPNS measurement’s degree of polarization to reduce the unnecessary computational burden. Simulation of INS/BPNS integration for an unmanned surface vessel navigation shows the proposed hybrid EKF can improve the navigation accuracy by curbing the adverse effects of the non-Gaussian measurement noise compared with the traditional EKF.

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving Average Consensus — A Lightweight Method
abstract: The average consensus problem is a crucial research topic in distributed systems. The realization of average consensus relies on explicit state information exchanging among neighboring nodes, which is unacceptable in cases where the state is private or contains sensitive information. Hence, it is essential to adopt privacy-preserving algorithms to safeguard the state information during consensus procedures. However, existing privacy-preserving average consensus approaches which guarantee convergence to the accurate desired value inevitably improve the topological complexity, increase computational cost, and reduce the convergence speed. In this paper, we propose a lightweight privacy-preserving average consensus method. The key idea of our method is a state conceal mechanism and a state-decomposition-selection algorithm. By selecting partial nodes in the network for state decomposition to achieve privacy preservation and increasing the step size in the consensus protocol, our method provides faster convergence speed and lower computational cost when compared with the algorithm in the seminal paper [1]. Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Position Control of X-Y Precision Motion Stage Based on Iterative Learning and Model Prediction
abstract: The X-Y precision planar motion stage is a highly advanced motion control device that has been widely utilized in various precision motion control fields. This platform achieves precise positioning and control of objects through precise motion along the X and Y axes, providing an outstanding solution for scientific research, industrial production, and other applications. The X-Y platform consists of two permanent magnet synchronous linear motors. In the three-loop control of the motor, when the current loop uses a PID controller, there is a problem in tuning the parameters. This paper replaces the original PID controller in the current loop with a model predictive controller. Simultaneously, addressing the issue of improving the tracking accuracy of the X-Y precision planar motion stage, a forgetting high-order variable gain PD-type iterative learning control is proposed. Subsequently, both of these control methods are applied to the Simulink model of the X-Y precision motion stage motor. This not only solves the complex problem of tuning the motor current loop parameters but also improves the tracking accuracy of the X-Y precision motion stage. The results indicate that when using both model predictive controllers and forgetting high-order variable gain PD-type iterative learning controllers for motor control, not only can the tuning of current loop parameters be omitted, but also tracking errors can be effectively reduced, and the system convergence speed can be accelerated.

articleTitle: A Congestion-Predicting Path Planning Algorithm for Narrow Lanes in Automated Warehouses
abstract: With the gradual development of intelligent logistics and multi-AGV (Automatic Guided Vehicle) systems, the application of automated warehouses is becoming more and more extensive. Among them, the path planning of AGVs is often a huge challenge. Under the specific constraints of road layout, the path planning methods described in the existing literature are often not good at avoiding congestion. In this paper, according to the limits of narrow lanes, we propose a path planning algorithm for predicting congestion. This algorithm is an improvement of the A-star algorithm, which introduces the current congestion cost and future congestion cost, and can plan the path to avoid the congested area, reduce the probability of runtime conflicts. Through simulation comparison, it is verified that the proposed algorithm has a good application prospect in alleviating traffic congestion.

articleTitle: Automatic Segmentation Algorithm of Solar Cells Based on Grid Corner Extraction
abstract: Defect detection in photovoltaic (PV) panels based on electroluminescence (EL) images has been a prominent approach in the field. These approaches rely on pre-segmented PV cells as input. However, practical EL images suffer from background interference and image deformation caused by variations in perspective, making the segmentation and extraction of PV panel cells challenging. To overcome these issues, algorithm ASSC(Automatic Segmentation of Solar Cells) is proposed. Concretely, a combination of Image processing techniques and convolutional network is employed to address these problem. Additionally, image deformation is tackled by implementing perspective correction, which transforms the PV panel into a front view. Moreover, the semantic segmentation network is leveraged to extract the grid corner points of PV panels. Compared to traditional image techniques, ASSC offers a more accurate solution without prior knowledge of PV panel specifications. Experimental results on a dataset collected on site demonstrate the effectiveness of ASSC which achieves an IoU(Intersection over Union) metric of up to 97.25%.

articleTitle: Self-Supervised Learning of 3D Point Clouds: A Survey
abstract: The use of 3D point cloud is widespread in robotics and autonomous driving systems. With the development of deep learning, an increasing number of models are being proposed to address tasks in 3D point cloud processing, including shape classification and 3D object detection. However, training these models requires large amounts of labeled data, which is expensive to obtain. Therefore, self-supervised learning methods for 3D point clouds have recently gained significant attention, which train the model with unlabeled data by designing pretext tasks. This paper aims to review these methods. Based on the pretext tasks designed, we divide those more than 30 existing methods into three categories: reconstruction-based, contrastive-based and MAE(Masked Autoencoder)-based methods. Then, we introduce the research motivations, implementations and characteristics of these methods one by one. Finally, two performance evaluation criteria are introduced and the performance of each self-supervised learning method is assessed and analyzed based on these criteria.

articleTitle: An Interpretable Semi-Supervised Learning Approach for Battery Lifespan Early Prognostic
abstract: Early estimation of battery lifespan holds significant importance in efficient battery health management. This paper presents an Interpretable Semi-supervised learning approach for estimating battery lifespans during their initial degradation stage. Specifically, a Physics-informed Autoencoder is introduced in the pretraining stage to extract features reflecting the early degradation mode of batteries by incorporating an electrochemical model into data-driven method. Moreover, to improve interpretability, an aging mechanism-based attention neural network is proposed to integrate electrode-level degradation mode with cyclic-based features for early battery lifespan prognostics. Additionally, a Bayesian Neural Network is incorporated into the model for uncertainty estimation. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated using the LiFePO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> dataset, demonstrating high performance in the early estimation of battery lifespan.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Control of AUV Formation Systems based on Adaptive Nonlinear Model Predictive Control
abstract: The objective of this work is to examine the difficulty of accomplishing multi-AUV trajectory tracking in underwater environments, which is essential for several underwater jobs like patrol, surveillance, and environment identification. The paper proposes a distributed nonlinear model predictive formation control based on adaptive prediction interval, which enables the achievement of AUV formation tracking and reduction in the computational burden associated with formation tasks. Firstly, a distributed auxiliary control law is proposed to ensure terminal convergence of the prediction interval of the AUV formation system. Second, by creating various constraint terms and adaptive prediction interval in the distributed nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC), the suggested technique tackles the problem of computationally cumbersome and input saturation. Then, by addressing a local MPC optimization problem that considers the state information of the AUV and its neighbors, the control input for every AUV is ascertained. Finally, the coordination and stability of the suggested predictive control system are shown by the presentation of numerical simulation results.

articleTitle: Anti-Swing Trajectory Tracking Control for Quadrotor Transport Systems Based on Uncertainty and Disturbance Estimator
abstract: When using quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicles (QUAVs) for cargo transporting, the underactuated nature of the QUAV and external disturbances pose significant challenges to task execution. To address the impact of external disturbances and reduce payload swing, this paper proposes an enhanced-coupling and disturbance-resistant trajectory tracking controller for a QUAV transporting system. By enhancing the coupling characteristics between the QUAV and the payload, the suppression of payload swing is achieved. Utilizing the Uncertainty and Disturbance Estimation (UDE) technology enables estimation and compensation for external disturbances. With the premise of satisfying the growth restriction condition, the inner and outer loop controllers can be designed separately. On this basis, the Lyapunov theorem and LaSalle invariance principle are utilized to demonstrate the asymptotic stability of the system. Simulation results indicate that the controller exhibits excellent control performance in the face of disturbances.

articleTitle: Cooperative Predictive Control for Mixed Vehicle Platoons on Curved Roads
abstract: This paper studies the cooperative control problem for a mixed vehicle platoon composed of connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) and human-driven vehicles (HDVs) running on curved roads. Firstly, we propose a distributed model predictive control (DMPC) algorithm for each following CAV in the platoon to maintain a constant speed and a constant inter-vehicle travelling path length along the curved road, where delayed trajectories of preceding vehicles are utilized as the reference. Considering the fact that HDVs in the platoon are inevitably subject to uncertainty due to drivers’ behaviors, simply following the preceding HDV’s trajectory may lead to undesirable behaviors, and hence we introduce a trajectory correction mechanism based on centerline of the path to correct the vehicle trajectory reference in the DMPC algorithm. This enables the closed-loop mixed vehicle platoon control system to achieve the desired inter-vehicle traveling path length and desired speed on curved roads. Finally, numerical simulation results are presented to validate the effectiveness of the proposed DMPC algorithm for the mixed vehicle platoon.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Evaluation Metrics for Plane-based Clustering
abstract: Clustering is a pivotal subfield within machine learning, with the evaluation metrics holding particular significance. Many traditional evaluation metrics are mainly used to evaluate point-centered clustering models. With the development of clustering models, many excellent clustering models are based on the plane as the center, so the use of these metrics in the plane-based clustering models adopts these metrics which mislead to suitable clustering results. In this paper, we introduce unsupervised evaluation criteria for plane-based clustering. Because both point-based and plane-based clustering models share the common goal of dividing data points into multiple clusters to ensure high similarity within the same cluster and low similarity between different clusters. Hence, in terms of evaluation metrics, the only necessary modification is to transform the measurement of the distance between sample points and cluster centers from the original metric to the measurement of the distance between sample points and the center of the plane. To validate our approach, we conducted comparative experiments on four plane-based clustering models using publicly available datasets. Comprehensive experiments indicate that our improved unsupervised evaluation metric for plane-based clustering performs better compared to the original point-centered metrics.

articleTitle: Scheduling Optimization Based on Flexible Manufacturing Systems Modeled With Timed Petri Nets
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of scheduling optimization in flexible manufacturing systems modeled with timed Petri nets by using the ant colony algorithm and combining the backtrack algorithm. In the flexible manufacturing process, potential resource failures may lead to deadlock issues in scheduling, which may result in inefficient resource allocation and even affect the completion of production tasks. To this end, the backtrack ant colony algorithm is proposed to optimize scheduling in the timed Petri net model and to overcome the slow convergence and susceptibility to local optimal inherent in existing algorithms. Specifically, in the initial state, the regular ant colony algorithm is used for path finding, but when ants encounter dead situations, i.e., they cannot proceed, the backtrack algorithm revives them and allows to choose new paths to ensure the discovery of optimal scheduling results. Finally, the algorithm is tested by using a timed Petri net that may enter deadlocks. Compared to conventional algorithms, the backtrack ant colony algorithm demonstrates shorter run times and is capable of providing high-quality scheduling solutions and accelerating convergence on complex network models.

articleTitle: Bandwidth-Aware Dynamic Event-Triggered Distributed Predictive Platooning Control of Heterogeneous Connected Vehicles
abstract: This paper presents a dynamic event-triggered distributed model predictive control (DMPC) strategy for heterogeneous vehicle platoons subject to disturbances and input constraints. A dynamic event-triggered mechanism considering bandwidth occupancy status integrated with a dual-mode control method is utilized to determine not only whether the optimal control problem should be solved or not but also the data transmission actions at each sampling time instant for each vehicle. In such a context, a dynamic event-triggered dual-mode DMPC algorithm is proposed to ensure the desired platooning control performance as well as the effective reduction of computational and communication loads. Building upon that, formal feasibility and stability analyses are correspondingly conducted, which provide theoretical validation for the proposed dynamic event-triggered DMPC strategy. Finally, a specific simulation example is given to demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed algorithm in terms of platooning control performance and communication resource efficiency.

articleTitle: A lightweight method for fatigue driving detection based on facial analysis
abstract: Fatigue driving detection is of significant importance for ensuring driving safety. Aiming at the issues of low accuracy and slow inference speed in existing methods for real-world driving scenarios, a novel lightweight method for fatigue driving detection based on facial analysis is proposed. Firstly, for each frame in the input driving monitoring video, the driver’s eye and mouth regions of interest (ROI) are extracted using face detection and facial key points detection algorithms which avoids the need for manual parameter tuning in traditional region extraction methods and can adapt to various head postures. Secondly, an efficient state recognition network for facial ROI called SRNet-FR is designed to recognize the open or closed state of the extracted eye and mouth region images, in which the Ghost module is used to make the model lightweight and a 3D non-parametric attention mechanism called SimAM is employed to improve the classification accuracy without introducing additional parameters. Finally, fatigue-related parameters are calculated based on the driver’s eye and mouth states of each frame, and the driver’s fatigue state is determined according to the established fatigue state determination rule. Experimental results show that the trained SRNet-FR achieves a high accuracy of 99.03% for eye and mouth state recognition under various head postures and in various driving scenarios which has a parameter amount of only 0.61M and a computation amount of just 16.45MFLOPs. The proposed method achieves an accuracy of 97.3% for fatigue driving detection on test videos which outperforms other compared methods and has an inference time of only 41 milliseconds for a single frame on the CPU platform.

articleTitle: Optimization of Energy Efficiency of Data Center Cooling Systems
abstract: As of 2018, China had more than 550,000 data centers, accounting for approximately 1.5% of the country’s total annual electricity consumption. Reducing energy consumption not only lowers costs but also aligns with environmental protection principles. Current research primarily focuses on IT equipment and air conditioning and refrigeration systems, as these components offer significant potential for energy savings. Instead of making adjustments to the original space environment and hardware facilities of the data center, this study proposes an energy efficiency optimization model by regulating the set values and parameters of the cooling system. This approach is particularly valuable given the increasing emphasis on energy efficiency in data centers. The cooling system of a data center is highly complex, with multiple variables, high feature dimension, time-varying working conditions, and strong uncertainty. This study employs an artificial neural network to model the energy efficiency (PUE) of a data center, using data collected from the operation of the cooling system in a data center in southwest China. Subsequently, an evolutionary algorithm is used to analyze and optimize the cooling system, controlling the set values to enhance the energy efficiency of the data center.

articleTitle: Incremental Learning Method for Robot Error Based on GWO-XGBoost Algorithm
abstract: In this paper, a method based on the GWO-XGBoost incremental learning model is proposed to improve the robot’s positioning accuracy. It is crucial to reduce the positioning error of the robot. In addition, the trajectory and position of the robot are always changing during the working process. Therefore, to address this problem, inspired by the idea of online learning, the XGBoost incremental learning model optimized with improved grey wolf algorithm is used to predict the positioning error of industrial robots. Firstly, the Grey Wolf algorithm is used to determine the optimal hyper-parameters of XGBoost model, then XGBoost is used for modelling prediction, and finally the accuracy and generalization ability is improved by online incremental learning. The GWO-XGBoost model has good fitting and prediction ability, the model is validated on Universal robots by online incremental training with good results.

articleTitle: Adaptive Sliding Mode Control for Trajectory Tracking in Four-Wheeled Mobile Robots Under Uncertainties and External Disturbances
abstract: In this paper, we propose an adaptive sliding mode control (SMC) design technique to track the desired trajectory of the skid-steering mobile robots in the presence of model uncertainties and perturbations. To enhance the stability of the robot and ensure accurate trajectory tracking, adaptive rules have been employed to estimate the upper bound of perturbations. This estimation, in turn, serves to stabilize the robot and guarantee the desired trajectory. Moreover, we analyze and calculate the convergence time of the sliding surface, ensuring its convergence within finite time. Additionally, efforts have been made to minimize the chattering phenomenon by smoothing the discontinuity of the sliding surface. Simulation results validate the efficacy of the proposed controller, demonstrating its ability to deliver acceptable performance in diverse scenarios.

articleTitle: Research on Scheduling Optimization of Multi-layer Four-way Shuttle System Based on Composite Tasks
abstract: Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems (AS/RS) play a key role in many applications, which include flexible manufacturing systems and dense storage. Reasonable and efficient equipment scheduling and vehicle path planning are two important aspects of AS/RS design. The type of AS/RS discussed in this article belongs to the four-way shuttle system. This paper takes the combined equipment of four-way shuttle and elevator of AS/RS as the research object. Considering the complex and diverse types of tasks in the actual working conditions, an optimal scheduling mathematical model for multi-type task operation and route planning problems of four-way shuttle system is established based on minimizing the total task completion time. An improved genetic algorithm is used to solve the problem to find an appropriate combination of four-way shuttle and elevator equipment to perform the task, so as to improve the system operation ability and reduce the invalid wait time. At the same time, a dynamic scheduling strategy is proposed, which constrains and optimizes the tier-changing phenomenon in the multi-tier four-way shuttle system to reduce the energy consumption and time consumption caused by unnecessary tier-changing. This article also proposes a collision free path planning strategy suitable for multi depth storage scenarios to improve the system's efficiency and avoid collisions. Through simulation example analysis and practical engineering project applications, the strategy proposed in this article has been verified to have significant optimization effects on the model.

articleTitle: Cloud Regularized Stochastic Configuration Network for Few-shot Fault Diagnosis of Process Industries
abstract: In the process industry, intelligent fault diagnosis methods utilizing data and machine learning (ML) serve as valuable tools for human experts, enhancing maintenance efficiency, process sustainability, and working safety. Nevertheless, a significant challenge in implementing intelligent fault diagnosis lies in the impracticality of acquiring sufficient training data for each fault type under real-world circumstances. In light of this issue, we propose an innovative few-shot fault diagnosis approach termed cloud regularized stochastic configuration network (Cloud-RSCN) for process industries. Concretely, a sample expansion method based on the bidirectional cloud generator of cloud model (CM) is developed to augment the feature space of existing limited samples and generate sufficient training samples for improving diagnostic accuracy, which firstly obtains the cloud feature space of each characteristic dimension and generates new samples through two consecutive random Gaussian distributions based on these cloud features. Additionally, L2 regularization SCN (RSCN) is employed as the fault classifier due to its sound generalization ability as an efficient universal approximator constructed under supervision with inequality constraint. Experimental results on the Teenesse Eastman (TE) process dataset indicate the proposed approach indeed performs favorably in fault diagnosis under few-shot scenarios.

articleTitle: Improved fractional order non-singular fast terminal sliding mode control of D-PMSG based on adaptive load torque observer
abstract: This article introduces an advanced approach in the realm of control strategies—Fractional-Order Non-Singular Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control (IFO-NFTSMC). The foundation of this strategy lies in the combination of an Adaptive Load Torque Observer (ALTO) tailored for direct-driven Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generators (D-PMSG). The primary objective is to address the speed loop of the Machine Side Inverter (MSC) with the aim of capturing the maximum power point of the wind turbine. Central to this control paradigm is the incorporation of an Improved Non-Singular Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Surface (INFTSMS) enriched with fractional terms, introducing heightened design flexibility. Moreover, an exponential function is integrated into the isovelocity term of the exponential reaching rate, and a smooth S-function replaces the original sign function to mitigate the chattering effect inherent in the controller. Following this, the ALTO assumes a pivotal role by offering feedforward compensation for the generated q-axis current, thereby augmenting the disturbance rejection capabilities of the controller. To assess the efficacy of the proposed IFONFTSMC+ALTO in comparison with other sliding mode controllers, simulation experiments were conducted on the D-PMSG under stepped wind speeds. The outcomes underscore the exceptional performance of the controller, revealing swift response times and surpassing its counterparts in terms of vibration suppression and disturbance rejection capabilities.

articleTitle: Safety control for a 2-DOF planar manipulator based on penalty Quadratic Program
abstract: This paper studies the safety control problem for 2-DOF planar robot manipulator. While quadratic program (QP) has proven to be a powerful tool to design the safety-critical controllers for nonlinear systems by combining control Lyapunov and control barrier functions (CLF and CBF), the application to robotic systems is not easy due to the complexity of the structure and multiple coupling constraints. In this paper, an alternative penalty QP is explored to address the safety controller synthesis process of the robot manipulator. First, backstepping approach is employed to derive the CLF constraint by taking into account the Euler-Lagrangian dynamics of the manipulator. Second, the energy-based CBF constraint is constructed to enforce safety of the controllers. Third, integrating the CLF constraint into the objective function as a penalty term formulates a safety QP with stability penalty. Finally, an automatically Lipschitz controller with a closed form expression is presented by solving the penalty-based QP problem. Simulations demonstrate our results.

articleTitle: Multi-Resource Allocation with Percentile Delay Guarantees based on Stochastic Network Calculus
abstract: Resource allocation has become increasingly vital in the era of advanced industrial informatization, where technology evolves rapidly, and the efficient use of resources is paramount. This paper adapts the Moment Generating Function-Stochastic Network Calculus (MGF-SNC) method, traditionally employed for probabilistic delay analysis, to resource allocation, specifically targeting Service Level Agreements (SLAs) response time constraints. Unlike methods that rely on average or worst-case response times, our approach focuses on the tail of response time distributions. This shift, enabled by the robust mathematical models of MGF-SNC theory, facilitates handling diverse resource configurations and complex scenarios with excellent scalability.

articleTitle: Event-triggered Prescribed Performance Control for Vehicle Platoons with Model Uncertainty
abstract: This paper investigates the event-triggered prescribed performance control for vehicle platoons with model uncertainty. Firstly, the radial basis function neural networks (RBF NNs) are used to estimate the unknown nonlinearity of the system. Then, a prescribed performance based algorithm is designed to achieve the platoon control by means of the backstepping technique. Besides, a relative threshold event-triggered strategy is proposed to reduce the communication burden between the actuator and the controller. Theoretical proof shows that the closed-loop systems is stable and the Zeno-behavior can be excluded, meanwhile the bounded tracking errors with prescribed performance are achieved. Finally, the simulation results show the feasibility and effectiveness of the designed algorithm.

articleTitle: Resilient MPC based on Input Reconstruction for Disturbed Nonlinear System with FDI attacks
abstract: A resilient self-triggered model predictive control (STMPC) approach based on input reconstruction is developed in this paper for disturbed nonlinear continuous-time cyber-physical system (CPS) against false data injection (FDI) attack. Firstly, an input reconstruction mechanism according to the key data is proposed based on the self-triggered aperiodic sampling characteristics and the FDI attack model to attenuate the impact of FDI attack on the controlled system. Secondly, the reconstruction parameter determination method is designed to balance the contradiction between system stability and triggering interval. Further, the stability properties of the disturbed nonlinear system based resilient STMPC algorithm are analyzed in detail. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed resilient STMPC is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Multi-physical feature extraction and selection method for global representation information of flame images in the MSWI process
abstract: The flame state recognition during the combustion stage of municipal solid waste is an important component of intelligent optimization control in the process of municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI). A single feature quantity cannot fully represent all combustion states. Using too many feature quantities will consume a lot of computer resources, and make timeliness worse. In response to the above issues, this article first based on the experience of domain experts and research achievements in related fields, divides the flame combustion state into four categories based on global information: normal burning, Channelling burning, partial burning, and Smothering; Then the flame image is de-fogged and denoted using pre-processing means such as artificial multi- exposure image fusion de-fogging algorithm, feature normalization, trap filtering, median filtering, etc., to obtain a clear flame image; Next, multiple features such as brightness, flame, color, and principal components are extracted from the flame image to represent the image from multiple views, and the multi-view features are reduced based on mutual information; Finally, a combustion state recognition model is constructed based on reduced image features and deep forest models

articleTitle: Sampled-data control for nonlinear systems with mismatched disturbances via a non-recursive design framework
abstract: In this paper, a sampled-data state feedback controller based on a non-recursive design framework is proposed for a class of nonlinear lower triangular systems with mismatched disturbances. Firstly, the continuous-time observer is discretized by the Euler method, and the continuous-time controller is discretized by the zero-order holding method. Then, by constructing a reasonable Lyapunov function and applying Gronwall-Bellman inequality, it has been rigorously demonstrated that the global bounded stability of the closed-loop system can be guaranteed by a appropriate selection of sampling period and scaling gain. By employing the non-recursive method, the proposed scheme avoids the problem of " explosion of terms " caused by recursive design procedures. In the meantime, a new discrete-time observer is designed to observe the disturbance of the sampling points given the adverse effects of the mismatched disturbances. Since both the observer and the controller are discrete in form, they are easy to implement on a digital computer. The efficacy of the proposed control scheme is validated through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Robust Attitude Control with Sigmoid Function Based ESO Compensation for Morphing Aircrafts
abstract: To solve the problem of compound perturbation in flight, such as parameter perturbations and deformation interference, a high-precision attitude control method with the SESO(SESO, Sigmoid-based ESO) compensator for a variable back-swept aircraft is studied. Firstly, a control-oriented mathematical model for the morphing aircraft control is established. Secondly, based on the back-stepping theory, the control problem of high-order complex nonlinear systems for such aircraft is decomposed into the design of control laws for low-order subsystems. And the back-stepping sliding-mode control law is designed for the attitude angle and angular velocity system; additionally, considering the large uncertainty in parameter perturbations and strong deformation interference, a composite extended state observer SESO is utilized to estimate the lumped disturbances and compensate them into the control law. Finally, the stability of the closed- loop system is proved based on Lyapunov theory, and the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through mathematical simulation.

articleTitle: Research on Vehicle and Pedestrian Object Detection Algorithm based on Enhanced YOLOv5s
abstract: Autonomous driving technology relies heavily on the accurate detection of vehicles and pedestrians. The swift and reliable identification of these objects in complex road environments has extensive implications for traffic congestion alleviation and accident prevention. However, current object detection algorithms used in autonomous driving and related fields face challenges such as misidentifying occluded targets, high computational complexity, and low detection accuracy. This paper proposes an enhanced vehicle and pedestrian object detection method based on YOLOv5s. Our approach addresses the detection requirements for small and occluded targets by incorporating the Mosaic-9 data augmentation strategy during the training process. To meet the low computational demands in vehicular environments, we replace the convolutional layers in the YOLOv5s algorithm with GhostNet modules. Furthermore, we introduce the Coordinated Attention module after the original YOLOv5s algorithm's feature extraction network to enhance the network's learning capability. Experimental results indicate that our improved YOLOv5s object detection network, compared to the original network, reduces the floating-point computational complexity by 2.1 GFLOPs while achieving an approximate 4% increase in average detection accuracy for vehicles and pedestrians. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in enhancing object detection performance in autonomous driving scenarios. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Research on Prediction Intervals of Greenhouse Tomato Yield Based on Improved Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Tomato is the main cultivated crop in China, and greenhouse tomato can improve the quality and yield of tomato by improving the planting environment. Predicting greenhouse tomato yield is an important basis for making production plan, and the accuracy of yield prediction directly affects economic benefits. In order to improve the accuracy of the prediction intervals model of greenhouse tomato yield, a new objective function was proposed to improve the Lower Upper Bound Estimation (LUBE) prediction intervals model. Then, based on the improved LUBE prediction intervals model, the particle swarm optimization algorithm (PSO) was further improved by adaptive inertia weight and escape strategy. Finally, a LUBE prediction intervals model based on the improved PSO algorithm was proposed in this paper. The prediction intervals of greenhouse tomato yield was simulated by using LUBE prediction intervals model, the improved LUBE prediction intervals model and the LUBE prediction intervals model based on the improved PSO algorithm. The experimental results showed that the prediction intervals coverage probability (PICP) of the LUBE prediction intervals model, the improved LUBE prediction intervals model and the LUBE prediction intervals model based on the improved PSO algorithm were 75%, 80% and 80%, respectively, and the prediction intervals normalized average width (PINAW) were 0.3938, 0.3725 and 0.3629, respectively. It can be concluded that the LUBE prediction intervals model based on the improved PSO algorithm has higher prediction accuracy and better fitting ability.

articleTitle: Multi-sensor Particle Filter Based on Improved Grey Wolf Optimizer
abstract: The particle degeneration is a significant factor effecting filter performance in traditional particle filter, which poses a challenge for its application in multi-sensor fusion. The resampling is a valid scheme to counter this issue, such as roughening, a prior editing procedure, and regularisation, but these measures are prone to generate the sample impoverishment. Different from these methods, this paper proposes a multi-sensor particle filter based on improved grey wolf optimizer (IGWO) from the perspective of intelligent optimal sampling. Firstly, the grey wolf optimizer is modified to acquire better exploitation and exploration abilities. Then, the IGWO is used to optimize the posteriori distribution of particles through guiding them to move towards the high likelihood region, which not only avoids the particle degeneration, but also holds the diversity of particles. Finally, a numerical example that an indoor localization for mobile robot with multi-camera visual system is provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Binocular Vision-based Speed and Separation Monitoring of Perceive Scene Semantic Information
abstract: Among the existing methods for realizing the safety of human-robot collaboration (HRC) under speed and separation monitoring (SSM), there are large safety zones, poor real-time performance, lack of information perception of the collaboration environment, and overly complex methods. Considering the characteristics of the binocular camera such as simple structure, low hardware cost, and strong ability to acquire depth information, in this paper, we propose binocular vision-based SSM(BV-SSM) to realize the tracking of robot joint coordinates by vision algorithms. The proposed BV-SSM adopts object detection algorithms trained on our self-constructed dataset to enhance the robot’s ability to perceive scene information, which not only reduces the computational complexity but also obtains an accurate and reasonable minimum safe distance by analyzing the speed directions of possible collisions under different motion states. Finally, the experimental tests are conducted on a six-degree-of-freedom industrial robotic arm with a ZED2i binocular camera, and the experimental results show that the proposed BV-SSM method can obtain an accurate and rationalized safety zone in real-time in HRC.

articleTitle: Bumpless Transfer Control for Multi-Equilibrium Switched Systems
abstract: This article is concerned with the issue of bumpless transfer control of multi-equilibrium switched systems. Stability conditions for the underlying systems are derived via the linear matrix inequality (LMI) formulation. In contrast to previous works, the proposed stability conditions exhibit enhanced clarity and brevity, facilitating their seamless integration with subsequent bumpless transfer control. Then, a bumpless transfer controller is developed to ensure system stability and suppress undesired control bumps. Compared to existing bumpless transfer methods, the proposed approach can effectively suppress control bumps stemming from multiple equilibria, leading to improved bumpless transfer performance. A numerical example is presented to illustrate the effectiveness and potential of the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Two Stage Distributionally Robust Optimization for Post-Disaster Material Supply Network
abstract: Material supply network for emergency rescue of natural disasters is of vital importance in reducing casualties and protecting people's lives and property. This paper introduces a post-disaster rescue material supply network. Due to the strong uncertainty of material demand in disaster-stricken areas and the difficulty in obtaining probability distributions with sufficient accuracy, we propose a two-stage distribution robust optimization method. We construct the ambiguity set of material demand in the supply network based on statistics such as the first and second moments from historical data. Then, the optimization problem is formulated as a two-stage stochastic robust optimization model. Linear decision-making rules and duality theory are jointly applied to facilitate solving process of the proposed optimization model. Via a numerical experiment, the effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated.

articleTitle: A genetic algorithm for meal delivery problem considering rider’s wage balance
abstract: Aiming at the imbalance of riders’ wages in the meal delivery problem, This paper studies the meal delivery problem considering the balance of riders’ wages, and comprehensively considers the platform delivery cost as well as the customer satisfaction. Then it constructs a joint optimization model of order allocation and route planning in meal delivery by minimizing the sum of the gap of riders’ wages, platform delivery cost and customer dissatisfaction. According to the characteristics of the problem, a heuristic algorithm based on the genetic algorithm framework is designed and combined with a variety of neighborhood operators to increase the search space to search for higher quality solutions. Finally, the effectiveness of the model and algorithm in this paper is validated by experiments. The research results provide decision support for rider order allocation as well as path planning for meal delivery problems.

articleTitle: MSOT-Q: Multi-Sensor Fusion SLAM with Object Detection Tracking for Quadruped Robots
abstract: In recent years, unmanned robots, particularly quadruped robots, have attracted considerable attention owing to their remarkable mobility and payload capabilities.
