This paper introduces a system to enhance the autonomous perception of quadruped robots through object detection and map building. The primary goal is to improve target tracking and map construction capabilities. To enhance navigation proficiency in challenging environments, we employ a hierarchical controller integrating a proportional derivative control scheme with the model predictive control algorithm based on differential evolution. This controller is strategically crafted to navigate challenging environments effectively. The system underscores the fusion of data from various sensors for simultaneous localization and mapping applications, leading to precise map generation and accurate target tracking. Notably, the dynamic window approach algorithm is utilized to determine the optimal trajectory for target tracking, achieving a harmonious balance between traversability and target localization. Rigorous testing in a demanding simulation environment affirms the effectiveness of the proposed system in significantly improving both target tracking and map construction for the quadruped robot.

articleTitle: Low-power and fast-transient capacitor-less LDO with double loops
abstract: This brief proposed a capacitor-less low-dropout regulator (CL-LDO) with two loops to reduce quiescent power consumption and keep fast transient performance at the same time. Using class-AB operational amplifier to replace Class A operational amplifier can greatly improve the load transient performance of (CL-LDO). However, the complex bias circuit of Class-AB operational amplifier significantly increases the static power consumption of the system. To solve this problem, a small-loop composed of five-transistor operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) is added to replace the large- loop composed of class-AB operational amplifier when the system work under low load current. The large-loop and small-loop are used to achieve the design requirements of high transient response and low static power consumption respectively, which greatly reduces the static power consumption of the regulator from 12uA to 3.4uA. Additional detection circuit needs to be introduced to the small-loop, this means that the system’s static power consumption will rise again, This paper put forward that using the output voltage of operational amplifier in large-loop and small-loop to represent the output current, and make system feedback load current signal to control circuit without introducing sampling resistance, making the system follow the load current changes automatically complete the opening and closing of the large-loop.

articleTitle: An online rock lithological detecting method using color and texture analysis
abstract: In the crushing and comminution process, different lithological rocks strongly affect the performance of crushing equipment. However, traditional lithological identification cannot be analyzed in a timely manner for processing control. Many rock lithological classification methods using color images have been proposed in the past, but few have successfully connected their results with online equipment monitoring. In this paper, we have developed an automatic vision system to evaluate rock lithology in real-time using color and texture features. The results show that the proposed method based on color and texture is robust and outperforms previous methods that rely on any single feature alone. This will help achieve reliable and precise control of the Semi-autogenous mill (SAG) feeding process.

Index Terms: Pixels In The Region Of Interest

articleTitle: Three-channel Residual Graph Convolutional Network for Semi-supervised Node Classification
abstract: Graph convolutional network (GCN) has recently gained significant success in node classification tasks. However, it still suffers from the problem of over-smoothing when stacking multiple layers, as well as the challenge of effectively integrating deeper-level relevant information between node features and the topological structure. To address these issues, this paper put forward a novel three-channel residual graph convolutional network (TR-GCN) model by removing the non-linear activation functions in deep GCN and adopting residual feature propagation, leading to the development of a residual graph convolutional structure. In the structure, a k-nearest neighbors feature graph is pre-built based on the similarities between nodes and combine it with the original topological graph as input to the parameter-shared residual graph convolutional module to extract common information. Additionally, an attention mechanism is introduced to adaptively adjust the weights of different embeddings, enabling comprehensive fusion of feature information. This attention mechanism allows the model to fully leverage information from both labeled and unlabeled nodes in semi-supervised node classification tasks, thereby improving classification accuracy. Extensive experiments are conducted on three benchmark datasets, and the results demonstrate that TR-GCN outperforms the baseline methods.

articleTitle: Research on tasks allocation of multi-AGVs System based on a hybrid genetic algorithm
abstract: This paper studies the task allocation model of a multi-AGV system, establishes a multi-AGV task allocation model that minimizes the maximum completion time and considers the constraint of remaining vehicle battery capacity. A hybrid genetic algorithm combining heuristic local search and adaptive weight adjustment is used to improve the local search capability of the genetic algorithm by incorporating heuristic information, thus enhancing the solution quality. The effectiveness of the proposed hybrid genetic algorithm is validated through benchmark datasets and experiments on application cases. The experimental results show that with the increase of the total amount of tasks, the hybrid genetic algorithm has more advantages in improving the efficiency of the system.

articleTitle: Survey of Opponent Modeling: from Game AI to Combat Deduction
abstract: Significant advances in game AI and military intelligent decision making have been achieved through the rapid development of intelligent games. However, the actual combat environment is highly complex, encompassing large state space and more unseen battlefield factors. As a result, applying game AI techniques to intelligent combat deduction still presents considerable challenges. Opponent modeling is one of effective approaches to addressing the complexity of game confrontation. Firstly, we focus on opponent modeling technology in game AI, analyzed the benefits and drawbacks of the relative opponent modeling technology used in game AI. And then we discuss the difficulties of transferring opponent modeling to combat deduction. Finally, we present the path for opponent modeling’s future development.

articleTitle: Research on Metal Magnetic Memory Effect Based Pipeline Inner Surface Magnetic Field Distribution Image Reconstruction Technology
abstract: Pipeline inner inspection technology based on metal magnetic memory effect can detect stress concentration regions accurately which are hazardous. Since the limits of installation conditions and the number of sensors, large errors between measured values and actual values of pipeline internal surface magnetic field strength always exist. In order to eliminate the effects of the errors on the inspect qualities, this paper presents a kind of metal magnetic memory based image reconstruction technology for pipeline internal surface magnetic field distribution. This paper researches the image reconstruction system construction for pipeline internal surface self-magnetic flux leakage, mathematical model building of image reconstruction system, reconstruction algorithms and the quality evaluation of image reconstruction. This kind of image reconstruction technology provides direct basis for researching on quantitative relations between stress or defects and Leakage magnetic field strength, and provides the basis for automation of pipeline inner inspection based on metal magnetic memory effect.

articleTitle: A Backstepping Finite Time Control Scheme for Bilateral Teleoperation with Phase Transition
abstract: This paper propose a novel backstepping finite-time control scheme for a bilateral teleoperation system with phase transition between constrained and free motion as well as considering model uncertainties, time-varying delays and external disturbances. A command feedback filter is used to estimate the delayed signals’ high-order differentiation to improve the stability of backstepping control in passive inputs situations. A backstepping controller with finite-time strategy is proposed to ensure the bilateral force tracking and position tracking performance, where radial basis function (RBF) is used to deal with the uncertainties and the external disturbances, and hyperbolic tangent function is introduced to deal with the estimation error. Finally, several numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed backstepping finite-time controller compared with the existing contributions.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Cooperative Guidance with Multiple Constraints Based on Proximal Policy Optimization
abstract: Collaborative guidance technology is a crucial means to enhance the effectiveness of strikes. To achieve precise collaboration among multiple missiles targeting a common objective, this paper addresses the issue of inaccurate calculation of the virtual impact point control expected flight time resulting from the use of fast iterative algorithms. We propose a method based on proximal policy optimization to calculate the virtual impact point. A collaborative guidance model under multiple constraints is established, and a proximal policy optimization algorithm is applied to optimize the collaborative guidance law. The calculation parameters of the virtual impact point are treated as actions of an intelligent agent acting on the environment, with velocity, desired pitch angle, and position coordinates serving as the algorithm's observations. A reward function reflecting the collaborative time is constructed, establishing a multi-constraint collaborative guidance law based on intelligent learning. Extensive simulation experiments targeting stationary targets demonstrate the rationality and effectiveness of the proposed method. After training, the intelligent agent provides different desired attack angles, and, based on the observation space, it can generate corresponding parameters. In some scenarios, the precision of hitting time surpasses that of fast iterative algorithms.

articleTitle: Robust H∞ Model Reduction for Fractional-order Two-dimensional Continuous Roesser System: The 1 < ε < 2 Case
abstract: This study explores robust H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> model reduction techniques for the two-dimensional (2D) fractional-order (FO) continuous Roesser system, where the FO is within the interval (1, 2). The FO-stable-region-analyze and matrix analysis methods are used to provide a sufficient condition to solve the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> model reduction issue for the 2D FO Roesser system in the form of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). This condition ensures the stability of the error system and bounds the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>-norm of its transfer function. The manuscript proceeds by giving a procedure for designing a reduced-order system model of the FO 2D continuous Roesser system. Robust H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> model reduction methods for FO 2D continuous Roesser systems with parameter uncertainties are then proposed based on the aforementioned results. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods, a numerical example is provided.

articleTitle: Hybrid Machine Learning-Based Methodologies for Fault Diagnosis, Prognosis and Health Management
abstract: The in-service equipment (i.e., aircraft, vehicles, ships) currently faces new challenges of increasing operational flexibility, reducing operating costs, improving reliability and availability while mitigating the environmental impact. Traditional maintenance and health trend analysis of in-service equipment involve time-consuming, repetitive, and labor-intensive activities based on the usage time or failure. This paper aims to systematically develop and implement diagnosis, prognosis and health management (DPHM) solutions by taking advantages of the computational intelligence-based and physics model-based methodologies. The complete DPHM scheme is formalized by integrating strategies that involve nonlinear filtering algorithms, deep neural networks, supervised learning and unsupervised learning algorithms, and concepts of multiple model, among others. Various evaluations, verification and validation with respect to detectability, diagnostics, prognostics by using performance metrics are conducted. The proposed autonomous, intelligent and functional DPHM strategies represent as innovative solutions for fleet-wide, automated, proactive health monitoring systems for industrial platforms.

articleTitle: Reasoning Document-Level Relation by Double Staircase Interactive Network
abstract: Document-Level Relation Extraction (Document-Level RE) was designed to automatically recognise entities and their relationships within text, representing them as structured data. It requires aggregating information from multiple sentences throughout the entire document for inference. Existing methods primarily rely on syntactic trees built upon the relationships between words in unstructured text to infer relationships between entities. Previous work may have focused more on local, shallow reasoning or external dependencies, neglecting deep, multidimensional complex reasoning. In response, we propose a double staircase interactive model. Initially, we construct a dependency matrix modeling various mention dependencies to assist entity reasoning in acquiring rich contextual information. Building upon this foundation, we integrate a structured attention network to obtain non-local interactions for entities, executing contextual reasoning and structural inference interactively, thereby learning deeper structural-aware document representations. Our model outperforms the SGR [28] model on the public dataset DocRED, improving its performance by 0.55. Furthermore, through discussion analysis and auxiliary experiments, we validate the validity of the model in cross-sentence reasoning.

articleTitle: Reinforcement learning-based prescribed finite-time optimal tracking control for a vehicle system regardless of initial position
abstract: The prescribed finite-time optimal tracking control (OTC) problem is investigated based on reinforcement learning (RL) for a vehicle system in this paper. A novel nonlinear mapping function is designed to develop a new approach of prescribed performance control (PPC) which is irrelevant to the initial position in the system. Meanwhile, the RL method adopting neural network with the actor-critic architecture is used to optimize the control input of the system. By means of a new prescribed finite-time performance function (PFTPF), a prescribed finite-time optimal tracking controller is obtained regardless of initial position of the vehicle system. The designed controller ensures not only that the tracking error satisfies the prescribed performance requirement, but also that all closed-loop signals in the vehicle system are bounded. Finally, the simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: Coordinated Control of Multiple Mobile Robots Based on Consensus Formation
abstract: In response to the low coordination efficiency of multiple mobile robots in industrial production, a multi-agent collaborative formation algorithm is proposed. The limited state of application of mobile robots in the production workshop is analyzed, and the working process of mobile robots is described using agents. In response to the above-mentioned issues, we propose a multi-agent collaborative formation algorithm based on cooperative control for multiple mobile robots. Finally, we validate the effectiveness and performance advantages of the proposed algorithm through a series of simulation experiments. Simulation experiments are conducted on the multi-agent collaborative formation algorithm in a simulated environment. The results show that the proposed algorithm can maintain good stability and obstacle adaptability during the entire movement period of the multi-robot formation. Further simulation experiments in the workshop demonstrate that the collaborative formation algorithm can organize multiple robots to form a formation in a relatively short time, sequentially complete dynamic obstacle avoidance, and effectively reduce conflict risks and spatial congestion levels.

articleTitle: Research on the allocation method of top-level indicators for automatic carrier landing
abstract: This paper establishes a set of indicator allocation system for the top-level indicators of automatic carrier landing system (ACLS), from procedure to method, from simulation to verification. In the indicator system, an error tree is established, the values of the top-level indicators are clarified, and error models for each system of the carrier-based aircraft are constructed. Based on the simulation results of the error models, a linear model relationship was creatively proposed between a single error source and the top-level indicators, and the correctness of the linear model relationship were verified through a large number of simulation tests.

articleTitle: Stabilization Optimal Control for Itô Stochastic Markov Jump System with Indefinite State
abstract: The paper focuses on the optimal control and stabilization of indefinite stochastic Markov jump systems with multiplicative noise. The sufficient and necessary condition of stabilization for Ito Markov jump system is given by the generalized algebraic Riccati equation (GARE). One of the key techniques is that extending the equivalence between the GARE and singular algebraic Riccati equation (SARE) into the system with jumping parameters. By the Lyapunov function, the stabilization problem under general uncertainty is transformed into the stability analysis under certain conditions. For the infinite-horizon case, the necessary and sufficient condition for the mean square stabilization of Itô stochastic Markov jump system in the mean square sense is obtained. Moreover, the cost functional of this system and it’s optimal controller are developed.

articleTitle: Fault-tolerant control for UAV based on deep reinforcement learning under single rotor failure
abstract: In order to achieve high-speed flight of a quadrotor UAV when one single rotor completely fails, a fault-tolerant control method based on deep reinforcement learning was designed. Since our policy is a low-level control, neural networks are used in reinforcement learning to directly map states to motor action values. The learning algorithm is developed based on the proximal policy optimization algorithm. By introducing PID lift correction into the actor-critic structure, both control accuracy and robustness are significantly improved. The proposed method has been tested in a flight simulator, and the results show that the reinforcement learning strategy is highly robust to model uncertainty and external interference.

articleTitle: A restabilizability criterion for perturbed Boolean control networks
abstract: This paper studies the restabilization problem of perturbed Boolean control networks (BCNs) by using semi-tensor product of matrices (STP). Firstly, function perturbations are classified into three categories. Through the analysis of these three types of perturbations, a necessary and sufficient restabilizability criterion is established, to check whether a perturbed BCN can be restabilized to the original state, by modifying some parameters of the old controller. Finally, the effectiveness of our results is illustrated by an example.

articleTitle: Short-term Wind Speed Prediction Based on Time-varying Filtered Empirical Modal Decomposition with Spatio-temporal Correlation Error Correction
abstract: The significant fluctuations and stochasticity of wind speed (WS) and the complex spatio-temporal coupling characteristics create challenges for harnessing wind power. To address this problem, a short-term WS prediction method based on time-varying filtering empirical modal decomposition (TVFEMD) with spatio-temporal correlation error correction is proposed. The TVFEMD method is introduced to mitigate the volatility in the original WS series, the temporal convolutional network (TCN) is applied to capture the long-term dependencies that exist within the time series, and the kernel density estimation (KDE) and the Copula function correction model are constructed respectively to explore the spatio-temporal characteristics of the error series, the error component is reconstructed, and the error correction is accomplished. The proposed method is evaluated for its effectiveness using operational data obtained from a north China wind farm, and the results indicate that the method adequately extracts temporal and spatial features with high prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Online Immediate Orientation in Monte Carlo Counterfactual Regret Minimization for Simultaneous Games
abstract: Recent research shows that simultaneous move games can be modeled as the imperfect information problem, more accurately in simulating the characteristics of simultaneous decision-making and gaining more favorable strategies. Furthermore, Monte Carlo Counterfactual Regret Minimization (MCCFR) is considered as a valid method for imperfect information. However, the convergence rate is seriously affected by sampling times and the high variance of estimations, which restricts the direct application to large simultaneous games. To address those challenges, we introduce an improved variant of MCCFR, namely Online Immediate Orientation in Monte Carlo Counterfactual Regret Minimization (OIO-MCCFR). OIO-MCCFR involves immediate rewards to orientate search. In addition, for reducing the excessive variance of estimation, control variate and state-action baseline are employed. Moreover, the new formulation has been proved to possess the probabilistic bound between the estimated unbiased regret and the accurate value. We evaluate OIO-MCCFR in the Goofspiel of diverse scales, which shows that our approach significantly outperforms vanilla MCCFR. More importantly, our experimental results also indicate that the larger the game scale, the more advantage of the OIO-MCCFR.

articleTitle: Event-triggered sliding mode control for networked switched systems with quantization parameter
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to propose an event-triggered sliding mode control for quantized switching systems to cope with the stability problem of switching systems under the event-triggered scheme. Firstly, this paper proposes an event-triggered mechanism based on quantization parameters, in which the dynamic quantization mechanism ensures that the system state stays within the quantization range, while the event triggering ensures the communication security, reduces the interference signals, and improves the resource utilization. Secondly, combined with the event-triggered control strategy, the sliding mode dynamics is deduced with the help of the construction of the sliding surface function, and the stabilization criterion with the perturbation attenuation performance of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> significance is established through the inequality technique, and on the basis of which a new type of control scheme is adopted to ensure the accessibility of the sliding surface. The Zeno behavior is eliminated by calculating the lower limit of the event triggering interval. Finally, the results are validated by simulations.

articleTitle: Approximate Process Model based Collaborative Control of Blast Furnace Material Level and Temperature
abstract: The cooperative control of furnace temperature and material level is a difficult problem in the process of blast furnace ironmaking. At the same time, the process is affected by many factors, such as nonlinear, strong coupling, long delay and uncertain interference. Aiming at the cooperative control of furnace temperature and material level in blast furnace smelting process, this paper proposes an approximate process model based on the dynamic changes of material flow and energy flow in blast furnace smelting process, taking water tank level and temperature control as the object. The model is a nonlinear model, and there is a certain coupling relationship between the two controlled quantities. It is difficult to realize the cooperative control of liquid level and temperature with conventional control methods. In view of the strong coupling between the two controlled quantities, this paper proposes an intermittent alternating control method. First, we deconstruct the system into two independent subsystems, and then independently adopt the linear quadratic regulator (LQR) method on each subsystem to first control the liquid level and then the temperature in one control cycle, and then control the liquid level and then the temperature in the next cycle. Alternate to achieve their specific control objectives. The simulation results show that the intermittent alternating control method can realize the control of the approximate model, and provides a new idea for the cooperative control of blast furnace temperature and material level.

articleTitle: Attention-based deep reinforcement learning approach for robot navigation in dynamic environments
abstract: The autonomous navigation of mobile robots in dynamic-static composite environments is a complex and challenging problem. The conventional obstacle recognition-path replanning approach is inadequate in terms of navigation efficiency and success rate in intricate surroundings. Our proposed End-to-End reinforcement learning autonomous navigation method from radar data to motion planning aims to enhance the autonomous navigation capability of mobile robots. We partition the LiDAR data into multiple regions based on the mobile robot coordinates and use an attention mechanism to extract semantic features of the environment. This enables the robot to perceive obstacles implicitly and adapt its motion speed and direction dynamically. Our approach was evaluated through simulation experiments in dynamic and complex scenes, and the results demonstrate that, even in the absence of map information, the method can achieve efficient and safe autonomous navigation in challenging environments.

articleTitle: Missile Aerodynamic Shape Optimization Based on Improved PPOD Method
abstract: In the field of aerodynamic shape design, the development of new vehicles is often faced with the burdensome task of aerodynamic simulation verification, a process that is not only time-consuming but also costly. To tackle these issues, the present investigation proposes an improved Proximal Policy Optimization with Demonstrations (PPOD) reinforcement learning approach, which enables the optimization of vehicle geometric configurations in a model-free, on-policy framework. Due to the high-dimensional nature of the geometric design variables, the action space is huge. Therefore, a spatial constraint is introduced on the action sampling process of the policy model. Moreover, to improve sample efficiency and reduce computational complexity, the current article establishes two data buffers, one of which introduces expert demonstrations, and the other stores the cumulative trajectories of the agent’s. The data is sampled proportionally from both buffers for learning purposes. Through the study of a conventional layout missiles, the results indicate that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms the traditional PPO algorithm in terms of optimization efficiency, further verifying the feasibility of the method in aerodynamic shape design.

articleTitle: Ordered Charging and Discharging Dispatch Strategy for Residential Electric Vehicles Based on V2G
abstract: With the increasing number of electric vehicles, the uncertainty and randomness of their charging demand seriously affect the stability of the power grid. Therefore, this paper proposes an orderly charging and discharging scheduling strategy based on V2G electric vehicles for residential areas. First, the EV charging load in residential areas is modeled according to users' driving patterns and travel characteristics using the Monte Carlo method. Then, considering the users' willingness to respond to the scheduling and the battery loss, a multi-objective optimization function is established based on the mean square deviation of the grid-side load and the users' charging and discharging costs. Finally, different charging and discharging strategies and different user responses are simulated and analyzed. The simulation results show that the proposed scheduling strategy can effectively reduce the peak-to-valley load difference, smooth the load fluctuation, and improve the users' charging economy at the same time.

articleTitle: DoS Attacks on Remote State Estimation: A Game-Theoretic Approach With Incomplete Information
abstract: In the paper, we address the security challenges involved in the remote estimation of Cyber-Physical Systems under Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks. To capture the interactive decision-making process between the attacker and the sensor, we propose a game framework with incomplete information, where the sensor (defender) possesses only statistical knowledge regarding the presence of DoS attacks. Both the attacker and the sensor operate under energy constraints. In our approach, we adopt a novel reward function within a single-subsystem CPS, and leverage matrix game theory to obtain the best-response strategies for both sides, leading to a Nash equilibrium. Furthermore, we extend the analysis to the attack-defense problem in CPSs with multiple subsystems, utilizing game theory as the basis. To address the computational complexity, we formulate the problem as an expected energy constraint problem, which reduces the computational cost compared to the original energy constraint problem. We also establish the existence conditions for Nash equilibrium strategies.

articleTitle: Jamming-free Impedance Control of UVMS Based on Contact Mechanisms for Peg-in-Hole Tasks
abstract: This work addresses the jamming issue for under-water peg-in-hole tasks. Owing to random currents, transient forces acting on the contact points during underwater peg-in-hole tasks may lead to jamming when inserting. To this end, a compliant jamming-free impedance controller is designed based on the contact mechanisms analysis. Firstly, general dynamic model of the underwater vehicle-manipulator system considering hydrodynamics is established, and the contact forces can be formulated intuitively by using the mass-spring-damper model. Secondly, the contact mechanisms of peg-in-hole tasks, when the peg has been inserted into the hole, are analyzed via the standard cylindrical model mainly including one-point and two-point contact states. To avoid jamming, the jamming diagrams of insertions are obtained by calculating the constraints of forces and positions in these two states. Then the adaptive parameters are derived from the jamming diagrams which indicate the deviation between current state and desired jamming-free state. Furthermore, the jamming-free impedance controller is designed considering the adaptive parameters. Finally, numerical simulations show that contact forces and moment are less than 0.5N and 0.4N·m respectively, and jamming can be rapidly mitigated, which demonstrates superiority of the proposed jamming-free impedance control strategy.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Vulnerability Assessment of Distribution Grids Containing Distributed Power Sources and Electric Vehicles
abstract: A deep learning-based vulnerability assessment method for distribution networks containing distributed power sources and electric vehicles is proposed, which adopts a probability distribution to describe the uncertainty of distributed power sources, and describes the load model of electric vehicles with a travel demand model based on the constraints of the road network and a charging demand model considering the psychology of users. After considering the base load, a probabilistic tidal current model with source-load spatio-temporal characteristics is used for tidal current calculation. The LSTM neural network is used to predict the load voltage, and then the distribution network vulnerability assessment is carried out to obtain the node vulnerability model and the final output results. A branch circuit in Dandong is utilized for testing to verify the validity of this paper.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Towards Lithium-ion Battery Capacity Region Aggregated Representation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method, Capacity to Vector (C2Vec), for predicting the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries. Unlike traditional techniques, this method adopts a self-supervised learning framework that employs a hierarchical contrastive approach within the time dimension. It learns regional aggregated representations from capacity degradation data and uses a regression network for downstream applications to directly perform multi-step forecasting, eliminating the need for additional auxiliary training sets or preliminary data decomposition and filtering. The efficacy of the C2Vec framework is attributed to its ability to capture complex degradation behaviors, enhanced by the use of the STL-BoxCox Block Bootstrap (SBB) algorithm and random cropping algorithm, thereby bolstering the robustness and accuracy of learned representations. Experimental results show that, on NASA battery datasets, C2Vec surpasses existing state-of-the-art models, achieving a substantial reduction in Global Average Root Mean Square Error (GARMSE) by 46.2%, and a decrease in Global Average Absolute Error (GAAE) by 11.2 when compared to models like CNN-ASTLSTM.

articleTitle: Multiple Gaussian Processes based Extended Target Tracking with Variational Inference
abstract: In this work, the multiple GP-based filter (MGP) is proposed for tracking an extended target with a random shape. This model is able to represent one or a group of targets, where the shape of each sub-target is described by the GP model. Utilizing the MGP method for extended target tracking, the mainly challenge are as follows: (1) the data association problem of the inter-cluster; (2) the challenge of approximating nonconjugate distributions. In order to solve the association problem of the measurement with the sub-targets, a latent variable is defined to correlate them. Due to the lack of conjugacy, the resulting posterior is not possible to find a closed-form analytical expression. This paper uses variational inference to solve the problem and approximate the true posterior. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is evaluated through simulation.

articleTitle: A Double Layer Coding-based Multi-task Service Composition Method in Cloud Manufacturing
abstract: This paper proposes a double layer coding-based service composition method by considering the simultaneous arrival of multiple order tasks in a cloud manufacturing environment. Different from the single-task service composition, task sequence and service sequence are separately modeled to describe the multi-task service composition problem. Under the requirements of minimizing manufacturing time, and cost, and maximizing reliability, the task sequences are improved by three task sequence evolution algorithms. Then, a dual population differential evolution algorithm (DPDE) is used for the evolution of service sequences to obtain an optimal task resource allocation set Finally, numerical simulation is established to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Thermal Hydraulic Analysis of High-Temperature Gas-Cooled Reactor Pebble-Bed Module Using a Systematic Parameter Estimation Approach
abstract: The world’s first high-temperature gas-cooled reactor pebble-bed module (HTR-PM) utilizes innovative nuclear reactor type and multi-module with one turbine system structure layout. Coordinated control and optimization of the nuclear system rely highly on first principle modeling of the process. A reliable mathematical model must be formulated with estimable parameters to accurately characterize the system behavior under different operating conditions. This paper focuses on performing thermal hydraulic analysis of the HTR- PM plant based on nonlinear parameter estimation. A systematic approach consisting of Bayesian estimation, estimability analysis, reliability evaluation and subset reduction is presented to tackle the coupling issue with the related thermal hydraulic parameters. The estimable subset is finally determined to ensure reliable parameter estimates.

Author Keywords: high-temperature gas- cooled reactor pebble-bed module

articleTitle: Event-triggered Relearning Modeling Method for System with Non-stationary Variable Operating Conditions
abstract: This paper proposes an innovative event-triggered relearning strategy for neural network modeling, to enhance prediction accuracy under the non-stationary and variable conditions frequently encountered in complex industrial environments. Firstly, the proposed approach divides the input and output datasets across different operational conditions, by applying a sliding window algorithm along with entropy to identify the boundaries of the input data. Following this, we utilize the prediction error from the current model, which is relevant to variable operational states, to construct an array of event-triggered conditions. Once these conditions are triggered, we employ the corresponding dataset to re-establish the model and predict the data under this operating condition. Compared with the traditional neural network model, the proposed model can produce a better estimation accuracy. Finally, numerical simulation tests are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results show that the proposed method can effectively improve the prediction accuracy of neural network model under non-stationary variable working conditions.

articleTitle: Residential Energy Demand Prediction Algorithm Based on Data-Driven Conditional Hidden Markov Model
abstract: Residential energy demand prediction plays an important role in achieving efficient and reliable operation of the power system. Effective demand prediction is necessary for providing a decision for user-side energy management and helping electric utilities balance power generation and consumption as well as developing optimal energy allocation schemes. To better capture the uncertainty of residential energy demand, this paper proposes a kind of conditional hidden Markov model (CHMM) based energy demand prediction algorithm to predict the energy demand of multi-residents under time-varying conditions. The proposed algorithm first clusters the states of CHMM by K-means. Then it adopts regression models to automatically estimate the transition probability and emission probability of CHMM directly from historical energy demand data. Finally, it predicts the energy demand by state transferring. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has high prediction accuracy in short-term forecasting compared with other prediction algorithms.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Battery SOH Estimation Method with CNN-LSTM Model and SSA Optimizing
abstract: Facing the bottleneck problems of lithium-ion batteries durability, precise estimation of state of health (SOH) is the key of the lithium-ion battery management system. This paper proposes a data driven SOH estimation method on the basis of a convolutional long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) model. The hybrid model leverages both the advantages of convolutional neural network (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM), in which CNN captures special features and reduces the dimension of the charge-discharge data while LSTM preserves temporal information of time sequences. In addition, the sparrow search algorithm (SSA) is integrated to optimize the key parameters including the number of neurons, initial learning rate and L2 regularization coefficients. A simulation experiment including comparisons with the existing classical SOH estimation algorithms is given to show the performances of the discussed SSA-CNN-LSTM method.

articleTitle: Robust time-varying Kalman smoothers with Uncertain Noise Variances
abstract: This paper addresses the design of robust Kalman smoothers for the time-varying system with uncertain noise variances. According to the unbiased linear minimum variance (ULMV) optimal estimation rule, the robust time-varying Kalman smoothers are presented. Specially, two robust Kalman smoothing algorithms are presented by the augmented and non-augmented state approaches, respectively. They have the robustness in the sense that their actual estimation error variances are guaranteed to have a minimal upper bound for all admissible uncertainties of noise variances. Their robustness is proved by the Lyapunov equation approach, and their robust accuracy relations are proved. The corresponding steady-state robust Kalman smoothers are also presented for the time-invariant system, and the convergence in a realization between the time-varying and steady-state robust Kalman estimators is proved by the dynamic error system analysis (DESA) method and the dynamic variance error system analysis (DVESA) method. A simulation example is given to verify the robustness and robust accuracy relations.

articleTitle: A fall detection method in elevators based on Graph Convolutional Networks
abstract: Falling is one of the serious health risks and is an increasing concern in society. Since the elevator is a closed and unnoticed space, falling in the elevator is even more dangerous. In this paper, we propose a fall detection method in elevators based on graph convolution networks. Firstly, the human body bounding box is extracted by a target detection network, and it is fed into the pose estimation network to extract the human skeleton key points, then we stack key points of consecutive frames along the time dimension to form a skeleton spatio-temporal graph. Finally, we propose a spatiotemporal fall detection method based graph convolution network (Fall-GCN) to detect falling, and it consists of three layers of spatio-temporal graph convolution modules, which can extract spatial and temporal information of skeletal data. Furthermore, we design a partitioning strategy for the falling behavior to improve the spatial modeling ability of graph convolution, considering the special kinematic characteristics of the falling behavior. We performed experiments on the public Fall Detection Dataset i.e., Le2i and our self-designed Elevator Fall Detection Dataset i.e., Fall_Elevator. The results show that our method can effectively detect falling and has high recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: Coordination Analysis of High-Order Multi-Agent Systems with Switching Topologies
abstract: In this paper, we study the coordination problems of a class of general continuous-time linear high-order multi-agent systems(MASs) with switching-directed topologies. By investigating the properties of the Lyapunov exponent of the normalized fundamental matrix of the system, we provide some sufficient conditions for the system to reach coordination. We give an equivalent description of the largest projection Lyapunov exponent by Hajnal diameter and projection spectral radius. The proposed approach can be used to investigate coordination problems of MASs proposed in other papers with switching topologies. The numerical simulations are provided to show the efficiency of our theoretical results.

articleTitle: A passage time prediction method of gates for passengers in subway stations
abstract: Predicting the passenger passage time of gates can help management personnel adjust subway station facilities in a timely manner to better adapt to the changing passenger demands, improve the overall performance of the subway network, and help better coordinate evacuation and rescue work in emergency situations. An improved time prediction model for the passenger traveling through gates is established based on the random forest optimized by the energy valley optimizer, providing a theoretical basis for scheduling, personnel management, and resource allocation. The passage time is taken as the output variable of the prediction model, and the factors related to the subway station gates and passengers that affect the output results are taken as input variables. The importance of different input variables on the impact of gate passage time is ranked based on the SHAP method, and the number of passengers is the most important influence factor. A gate simulation system based on the MassMotion software is built, and simulation experiments in different scenarios are conducted by changing the number and width of gates, as well as the number and attributes of passengers, to obtain traffic data under rich scene parameters, providing training and validation sets for the time prediction model. Compared with the random forest and the BP neural network methods, the accuracy of the prediction model for the passenger passage time of gates is concentrated between 85%- 100%, and the RMSE and MAE can be as low as 2.93 and 2.66.

articleTitle: Discussion of Sewage Sludge Co-incineration based on Dioxin Emission Numerical Simulation Model for Municipal Solid Waste Incineration Process
abstract: Co-incineration is one of the best ways to treat sewage sludge (SS) and municipal solid waste (MSW), but it is very important to understand its combustion and gas reaction in the grate to control the emission of pollutants. In this paper, the discussion of SS co-incineration based on the dioxin emission numerical simulation model for the MSW incineration (MSWI) process is proposed. Firstly, the numerical simulation model of DXN emission for the MSWI process is established in ASPEN Plus software by using collected sample data in an MSWI plant in Beijing. Then, the SS and MSW co-incineration numerical simulation model is constructed. Finally, based on SS data in reference, the discussion and analysis are made. These research results provide support for the future research on co-incineration of SS and MSW in Beijing.

articleTitle: Edge Computing Offload Optimization Strategy Based on Improved Particle Swarm
abstract: In multi-access edge computing, it is crucial to use computing offloading to ensure low processing latency for the task of the user device. This implies that efficient computing offloading is an effective way to reduce the average task latency problem. Therefore, this paper proposes an offloading strategy for multi-user multi-edge server scenarios by using an improved particle swarm. First, it takes transmission latency, processing latency, and the number of users into account when designing an objective function to minimize the average task latency. Then, the improved particle swarm algorithm with dynamic weights and learning factors is used to optimize the task offloading strategy. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can find a better offloading strategy compared with the classical particle swarm algorithm and the genetic algorithm.

articleTitle: Synchronization analysis of discrete-time coupled complex valued Markov jump neural network systems with two unknown transition probabilities’ Markov chains
abstract: In this paper, we provide a array of discrete-time coupled complex-valued markov jump neural networks (CMNNs) with two markov chains of partially unknown transition probabilities and distributed delays. First, for the system self-synchronization problem of the coupled CMNNs, by constructing the Lyapunov energy function and the Kronecker product, the system coupling force are used to propose a synchronization criterion that enables the coupled CMNNs to satisfy the mean-square asymptotic synchronization. Next, to validate the theories discussed in the paper, two examples of numeric experimental simulations are used.

articleTitle: Process Operational State Assessment Based on Stacked Enhanced Denoising Autoencoder
abstract: This paper presents a process operational state assessment method based on a deep neural network— specifically, the Stacked Enhanced Denoising Autoencoder (SEDAE)—tailored for complex industrial production data characterized by strong coupling, nonlinearity, and significant noise interference. The approach initially employs SEDAE to extract deep features closely associated with the operational states from process data. Subsequently, the extracted features are processed using a SoftMax classifier to accomplish the operational state assessment. Finally, the proposed method is validated through simulation using actual production data from the cyanide leaching process. The results demonstrate the superiority of the SEDAE model compared to others, maintaining a leading position under varying noise ratios. Even at a noise ratio of 60%, the SEDAE model sustains an accuracy level of around 90%.

articleTitle: Observer-Based Fault Estimation and Fault-Tolerant Control for Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: This paper focuses on discussing in heterogeneous multi-agent systems during actuator faults. First, a fault detection observer is designed using relative output estimation error and output estimation error to identify faults in the actuators. Second, using state observer and output feedback methods, a fault-tolerant controller is developed to ensure system stability in case of actuator faults. Simulation examples are provided finally to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed design methods.

articleTitle: Optimal mean-variance investment and reinsurance with a correlation under Heston’s SV model
abstract: This article investigates the optimal investment and reinsurance problem under the interdependence between the risk assets invested and insurers’ surplus process. Expressly, we consider the price process is described by Heston’s stochastic volatility model and the interdependence between the financial market and the insurance market described by the Wiener processes in models. For the optimal control problem of a nonlinear stochastic differential equation, a novel value function is established to solve the complex Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation. The closed-form expressions of the optimal strategies and the corresponding value function for this new problem are given under the mean-variance criterion. Finally, a numerical simulation example is provided to the impact of correlation on results and providing a reasonable economic explanation.

articleTitle: Observer based Online Identification of Aerodynamic Parameters for Hypersonic Gliding Vehicle
abstract: Aerodynamic parameters identification is a key enabling technology to improve the adaptivity of the guidance and control for hypersonic gliding vehicle. This paper seeks to propose a novel online aerodynamic parameters identification scheme under the framework of nonlinear observer. Firstly, the original nonlinear dynamics for the air-to-ground attack of the hypersonic vehicle is established, while the lumped aerodynamic forces are regarded as the external terms. Then, a nonlinear observer is employed to estimate the lumped aerodynamic forces, and the ultimate boundedness of the estimation error is guaranteed with Lyapunov theory. Finally, simulation results are undertaken to show the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: A Kidney Dynamic Ultrasound Image Segmentation Method Based on STDC Network
abstract: Ultrasound dynamic images of the kidney serve as crucial tools in renal diagnosis, dynamically displaying the anatomical structure and pathological information of the kidney. However, traditional ultrasound image segmentation heavily relies on the experience of ultrasound doctors, leading to inaccuracies due to repetition and redundancy. In this paper, we present a deep learning method based on Short-Term Dense Concatenate network (STDC network) for kidney dynamic ultrasound (KDU) images segmentation. STDC network adopts Short Term Dense Concatenate as the basic module. In the decoder, the learning of spatial information is integrated into the low-level layer through a single stream approach. Finally, fuse the low-level features and deep features to predict the final segmentation results. Experiments based on our self-collected dataset shows that our method achieves 0.966 in term of Jaccard, 0.983 in term of Precision and 0.982 in term of Recall in the segmentation task. Furthermore, we compare our network with other classic real-time segmentation models, showing that our method outperforms in both accuracy and speed.

articleTitle: Performance degradation prediction of aircraft cables for complex mechatronic products based on TCN-LSTM
abstract: To address the phenomenon of performance degradation and safety problems of aircraft cables under the action of various causes, we proposed a prediction method based on time-series convolutional networks combined with long and short-term memory network models to predict the cable performance status. First, we analysed the overall causes of cable performance degradation, and after concluding that the cable insulation state is the main cause, we selected four parameters that can reflect the cable insulation state information and determined the data set based on the analysis results. After that, we constructed a network model based on the data features and extracted the four parameters reflecting the cable insulation status under the convolutional network. Finally, the prediction results were obtained by bringing the feature data identified by Pearson correlation coefficient analysis and the influencing factors with high enough correlation into the TCN-LSTM based prediction model. The case study and the comparison of the prediction results of different networks verified that the prediction results of the constructed method are more relevant to the actual situation.

articleTitle: A reptile search algorithm-based optimal control method for the hybrid pressure retarded osmosis and photovoltaic system
abstract: Optimal control of photovoltaic systems (PV) and pressure retarded osmosis (PRO) systems has been a hot topic of research. The method used for maximum power tracking control has always deviated somewhat from the ideal and failed to achieve the expected results. The accuracy and speed of tracking in practical applications have always been a problem. Therefore, a metaheuristic-based Reptile Search Algorithm (RSA) is proposed to solve the MPPT control problem of this system. Solar irradiance, ambient temperature and operating conditions parameters are used as input parameters of the PV/PRO system, and power is used as the output. Finally, the results of RSA were compared with the incremental conductance (INC), perturbation and observation (PO) and grey wolf (GWO) algorithms.

articleTitle: Research on Improved Sliding Mode Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor based on Predictive Model
abstract: When the traditional Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) vector control system is disturbed by the outside world, it is easy to cause violent fluctuation of speed and current. To solve the above problems, an improved Sliding Mode (SMC) control system of Permanent magnet synchronous motor based on predictive control was designed. Firstly, an improved sliding mode speed controller was designed and applied to the speed loop. Secondly, an improved deadbeat predictive current control (DPCC) was designed and applied to the current loop, and a sliding mode disturbance observer was introduced into the feedforward path. Finally, the simulation results in Matlab/simulink show that the improved control system can effectively reduce the overshoot and enhance the anti-interference ability.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Novel Hybrid Aerial Underwater Vehicle with Foldable Wings
abstract: In recent years, hybrid aerial underwater vehicles(HAUV) have become a popular research topic due to their cross-domain advantages. In this paper, based on the bionic variant technology, we design a new folding wings hybrid aerial underwater vehicle. We are able to fold and deploy the front and rear wings at the same time by a single electric actuator. Then, we consider the aerodynamic characteristics of each wing type and determine the front and rear wing types. Finally, we conduct computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation of the aerial and underwater states of the vehicle to verify the feasibility and stability of aerial flight and underwater submergence of the vehicle.

articleTitle: Disturbance Observer-based Nonlinear Feedback Control for Quadrotor Suspended Payload Transportation
abstract: This paper investigates the control challenges associated with quadrotor suspended payload transportation in the presence of unknown disturbances. The control system is systematically divided into outer-loop and inner-loop subsystems during the design phase. In the outer-loop, a disturbance observer is initially devised to estimate external disturbances. Subsequently, a nonlinear control scheme for quadrotor transportation is proposed, featuring an adaptive term within the controller to effectively estimate the upper bound of observed disturbances error. The inner-loop employs the Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC) approach. Theoretical stability is rigorously established through Lyapunov analysis. The comparative simulation results demonstrate the exceptional performance of the proposed method, particularly in terms of mitigating payload swing and ensuring robustness.

articleTitle: Bi-objective Resource Allocation for Multi-product and Multi-stage Steel Production Systems
abstract: Reasonable resource allocation is the key to coordinated production among the processes in steel enterprises. This paper deals with a novel bi-objective resource allocation problem arising from steel production systems. One objective function is to minimize the sum of various costs related to transportation, fixed, shortage, and storage. The other objective function is to balance the machine’s workload in the same stage. A mixed integer linear programming model is developed for the concerned problem. Non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II is designed to solve it. Experimental results indicate that our algorithm can obtain multiple Pareto solutions quickly. Its excellent performance is verified, thus demonstrating that it is ready to be applied in practice.

articleTitle: A Multi-Step Predictive Formation Control Algorithm with Internal Collision Avoidance
abstract: This paper presents a coordinated formation control method for a multi-agent system to ensure collision avoidance among agents. The aim is to enable agents to achieve the desired spatial configuration through safe and collision-free paths. By predicting future states and sharing information, the method addresses detected collisions in the predictive time domain. Key components include the agents’ predictive model, planned formation trajectories, cost function for control and collision avoidance strategy, which form a solvable optimization problem to ensure the achievement of control objectives. Additionally, collision detection only considers neighbors within a finite distance as obstacles, reducing the number of collision constraints and thus computation time. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Chemical Fault Diagnosis Method based on DAM-CGRU
abstract: In order to better capture the complex relationship of chemical process data and improve the ability to identify various faults, a fault diagnosis method based on dual attention mechanism (DAM) and convolutional gating recurrent unit (CGRU) is proposed. Firstly, the chemical fault data is standardized and sub-sequence samples are divided using sliding window, and then high-dimensional local features and time series features of the subsequence are extracted through one-dimensional convolutional neural network(1D-CNN) and gate recurrent unit(GRU), and the improved attention score function is used to empower the variable dimension and time step dimension of the fault data respectively to enhance the model's attention to key variables and time nodes, and finally, the softmax classifier is used to classify various chemical faults. Verified and compared on the Tennessee-Eastman dataset, the experimental results show that the DAM-CGRU method can extract chemical fault characteristics better than the traditional deep fault diagnosis method and obtain higher diagnostic accuracy.

articleTitle: Application of interval multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm in reliability redundancy allocation problem
abstract: Reliability is an important factor considered in industrial system design. Adding redundant parts to the system can greatly increase its reliability, while the accompanying issues include increased system costs and weight. Redundancy allocation problem (RAP) is a problem of how to simultaneously optimize factors such as reliability, cost, and weight of a system through component selection and system structural design under given constraints. For situations where the reliability of individual components is uncertain, this paper proposes an interval multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm based on probability dominance (PD-IMOPSO). In this algorithm, a probability based interval order relationship is used to determine the dominant relationship of intervals. In addition, a crowding distance under interval conditions is proposed to measure the diversity of solutions. Finally, the effectiveness of this method is verified through an example of a supervisory control and data acquisition system (SCADA) for a long oil pipeline.

articleTitle: Nonlinear MPC based Whole-body Control for Mobile Manipulation
abstract: In the control of mobile manipulators, maintaining the manipulability of the manipulator, the fast mobility of the base, and the coordination of all joints enduring challenges. This paper proposes a whole-body motion controller for a nonholonomic mobile manipulator based on Nonlinear Model Predictive Control. By imposing constraint conditions, the controller avoids joint position and velocity limitations during the process of guiding the mobile manipulator to the target points. The controller maximizes the ability of manipulator to move in any direction, optimizes the mobility of base, and simultaneously minimizes end-effector velocity tracking error through the objective function. In a simulated environment, comparative experiments are conducted between the proposed controller and a whole-body motion controller based on quadratic programming. The results demonstrate the superior performance of our controller, producing motions that enhance manipulability, minimize tracking error, and meet the requirements for rapid mobility when compared to the latter.

articleTitle: Design of a Contactless Electrical Impedance Measuring System for Removing Coupling Capacitance
abstract: In the process of fluid parameter detection, conductance detection technology has the advantages of simple structure and good response speed. However, this method belongs to contact measurement, there are some problems such as electrode polarization and corrosion, which affect the measurement accuracy. In the process of measurement, only the conductance of the impedance is extracted, and its imaginary part is ignored, so the impedance information of the fluid is not fully utilized. In the process of fluid detection, there will be coupling capacitors between electrode, tube wall and fluid, and the presence of coupling capacitors will cause measurement errors. Aiming at the above problems, a non-contact resistance measurement system based on fluid detection is designed which can eliminate coupling capacitance.

articleTitle: Fixed-time line-of-sight guidance law for unmanned surface vehicle path following: theory and experiment
abstract: In this paper, the path following problem of un-deractuated unmanned surface vehicle (USV) based on fixed-time control strategy is studied, and a fixed-time line-of-sight (FTLOS)guidance law is proposed according to the line-of-sight (LOS) guidance. Through theoretical analysis and simulation experiments, it is proved that the proposed strategy can drive the USV to move along the desired path smoothly and quickly, and all the errors of the closed-loop system can converge to any small neighborhood of the origin within a fixed time interval. Then, the real ship experiment is designed through the self-designed USV control system and the USV control platform. The superiority and effectiveness of the FTLOS guidance law proposed in this paper are proved by comparing the experimental data with the proposed FTLOS and LOS.

articleTitle: Optimal control of rotor position estimation considering the influence of air gap changes in BSRMWR
abstract: The research addresses the issue of fluctuation in non-conductive phase response current peaks due to unstable levitation force during the startup phase of the Bearingless Switched Reluctance Motor with Wide Rotor Teeth (BSRMWR) in traditional pulse injection methods. This fluctuation results in increased errors in logical judgment and rotor position estimation. To tackle this problem, an optimized rotor position estimation method based on pulse injection is proposed. This method utilizes an adaptive filtering LMS algorithm to construct a mathematical model for the variation in inductance caused by levitation force fluctuations. It dynamically adjusts filter parameters to effectively eliminate interference signals within the response current peaks. Simulation experiments confirm the method’s effectiveness in reducing rotor position estimation errors caused by interference signals, providing a viable technical approach to addressing instability during the startup phase.

articleTitle: A Digitally Controlled Output Adjustable High Stability Relaxation Oscillator
abstract: In view of the problem that the output frequency stability of traditional relaxation oscillator is easily affected by the change of external conditions, a digitally controlled output adjustable high stability relaxation oscillator is designed. The oscillator uses digital signals to control the output of the bias current and the size of the capacitor in the capacitor charging and discharging loop in the relaxation oscillator, so that the oscillator is capable of adjusting the output frequency by means of digital control signals. A zero temperature coefficient current is also generated to minimize the effect of temperature on the output frequency. The overall circuit is built using SMIC 0.11μm process and simulated using Candace Virtuoso. Simulation results show that the circuit is capable of outputting a frequency signal of 10Mhz under digital signal control, and the temperature coefficient of the output frequency is 133.3ppm/°C in the temperature range of -40 °C to 125°C.

articleTitle: A Localization Algorithm based on Dice-Optimized Maximum Similarity Path and Sparrow Search Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes an innovative algorithm for wireless sensor network localization, termed as the Dice Similarity Coefficient Correction and Sparrow Search Algorithm-based Localization Algorithm (Dice-SSA). The algorithm enhances the traditional DV-Hop localization algorithm by employing two novel techniques. Initially, the algorithm introduces the Maximum Similarity Path to replace the distance between unknown nodes and anchor nodes. The similarity of paths between unknown nodes and anchor nodes is redefined using the Dice coefficient, introducing a new level of accuracy to the localization process. Finally, the Sparrow Search Algorithm is employed to refine the localization, further improving the algorithm's performance. This multi-layered approach offers a significantly advanced method for wireless sensor network localization. The effectiveness of the Dice-SSA algorithm is validated through simulation, demonstrating its superiority in terms of localization accuracy. In comparison to the traditional DV-Hop algorithm in specific network topological environments, the improved algorithm reduces errors by 79.26%.

articleTitle: Research on Optimized Thickness Design of Special Clothing for High Temperature Operation Based on Heat Conduction Equation
abstract: In this paper, a dummy wearing a special garment for high-temperature operation is used to maintain constant temperature to simulate the operation in a high-temperature environment. Therefore, we study the effect of changing the thickness of textile materials and the thickness of voids in the special garment on the outside temperature change of the dummy's skin. Meanwhile, we establish a model of partial differential equations by using the heat conduction equation. As a result, we give the solution methods of the boundary conditions and the coefficients of heat exchange. Based on this, establish an optimization model for the thickness parameters of the thermal protective clothing, further solving the problem through bi-objective optimization by using the bifurcated search algorithm.

articleTitle: RPANet: A Residual Pyramid Semantic Segmentation Network Based on Atrous Convolution
abstract: Semantic segmentation is a challenging task to achieve accurate pixel classification. Recent studies witnessed that residual networks can better solve problems such as gradient vanishing and exploding in neural network backpropagation. However, when objects are obstructed or certain target sizes are small, it can lead to insufficient feature extraction ability of the residual network. In this paper, we propose a residual pyramid network based on atrous convolution (RPANet) to obtain better semantic segmentation results and improve segmentation network efficiency. Specifically, we first put forward a novel residual pyramid architecture, which integrates contextual information with the relationship features between pixels, and outputs multi-level and different scale features. In addition, we propose multi-scale atrous convolutions, which can not only capture long-range contexts information and enlarge the effective receptive field, but also the size of the feature map is not reduced by the residual connection. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of our method on Cityscapes and CamVid datasets. We demonstrate that our method can improve the semantic segmentation performance reduce network complexity.

articleTitle: Dynamic Stability-Aware Scheduling based on Dueling Double Deep Q-Network in FJSP
abstract: The growing complexity of the industrial production environment introduces various uncertain events, resulting in increased process instability and reduced production efficiency. The stable scheduling method is crucial to ensure the continuous and stable operation of the production process. However, the existing dynamic flexible job shop scheduling problem (DFJSP) research lacks stability analysis of the scheduling method. To optimize the production process, we propose a dynamic stability-aware scheduling method based on dueling double deep Q-network (DSAS-D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>QN). The method solves DFJSP with multiple uncertain events and reduces the job processing time. Meanwhile, we analyze the stability of the scheduling method by describing the overall distribution of DSAS-D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>QN’s reward function values. The experiment shows that the proposed method can effectively reduce the processing time while ensuring the stability of the scheduling. Through stability analysis, we verify the adaptability of DSAS-D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>QN to unstable environmental changes.

articleTitle: A mask-wearing detection method in elevators based on improved deformable DETR
abstract: Wearing masks is an effective way to mitigate the spread of the virus, and it becomes even more crucial in confined spaces like elevators, where the virus can spread more easily. However, traditional manual detection methods are inefficient and not real-time. In this paper, a mask-wearing detection method in elevators based on improved deformable DETR (Mask deformable DETR(Detection Transformer)) is proposed. This method builds upon the foundation of deformable DETR, incorporating an efficient channel attention mechanism to assist residual networks in extracting mask features comprehensively. This mechanism enhances information on small-scale feature maps. Additionally, a conditional attention mechanism is introduced to expedite model convergence while improving the detection capability for small targets. Furthermore, a two-stage data augmentation technique tailored to the unique characteristics of mask-wearing data in elevators is designed. This method can increase sample quantity, balance sample categories, and enhance model performance. Experimental results demonstrate that this method can effectively recognize the mask-wearing status of elevator passengers, exhibiting a high level of recognition accuracy. It holds significant implications for practical elevator monitoring scenarios.

articleTitle: Robust sliding mode control for path following of a MSV via the triggering LOS guidance
abstract: This paper explores a resilient sliding mode control algorithm tailored for guiding a marine surface vessel (MSV) through a path without the constraints of continuously transmitting the guidance signal. The proposed algorithm comprises two key components: the Triggering Line-of-Sight (TLOS) guidance principle and the robust sliding mode control algorithm. The TLOS principle introduces a novel approach to reduce the transmission rate of the guidance signal. This reduction not only lowers the requirements for control design but also contributes to a smoother output signal. To ensure effective tracking of the guidance signals, a robust sliding mode control algorithm is developed, incorporating a proportional integral sliding mode manifold and an L-function. Consequently, the resulting control algorithm excels in terms of simplicity and anti-interference performance. The practical stability of the system is proved through Lyapunov theory. To validate the proposed algorithm’s advantages and effectiveness, a numerical example is presented, demonstrating its superior performance in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Hyper-heuristic Algorithm based on ε-Greedy for Solving the Online Seru Scheduling Problem *
abstract: We address an online seru scheduling problem with the uncertainty of new batch arrivals. First, the decision-making process for online seru scheduling is delineated. Subsequently, drawing on this process, we design three simple and effective scheduling rules that have different advantages. To optimize their inherent benefits, an ε-greedy based hyper-heuristic algorithm is designed to adaptively select the appropriate rule for online seru scheduling. Within this algorithmic framework, the three scheduling rules serve as low-level heuristics, while ε-greedy acts as a high-level strategy. The extensive experiments are conducted to demonstrate the performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Optimization of Scheduling in Steelmaking Production Considering Refining Routes Selection
abstract: In the steelmaking process, there exist the scenarios where the same steel grade can be processed through refining furnaces on different refining routes. To address the scheduling problem in steelmaking with multiple refining route options, the Flexible Job-shop Scheduling Problem (FJSP) is extended to establish a production scheduling model for steelmaking production considering refining routes selection, to minimize the maximum completion time. The model is solved by the designated algorithm with CPLEX optimizer. Computational experiments are conducted based on simulated production data, including comparative simulation experiments with different-scale datasets, to validate the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Diagnostic Tree Generation Method Based on Global Optimal AO * Algorithm
abstract: In order to improve the fault diagnosis efficiency of complex systems and reduce the maintenance cost, this paper proposes a diagnosis tree generation method based on the global optimal AO* algorithm. Based on the establishment of the correlation model between the system fault mode and the test vector, this method comprehensively considers the problems of fault occurrence rate and test cost,and uses AO * algorithm to generate the optimal diagnosis tree, which effectively guides the maintenance personnel to quickly locate the fault.

articleTitle: Control Strategy of Central Air Conditioning using RF-NSGA-II
abstract: Optimizing the control strategy of the central air conditioning system is crucial for conserving energy in buildings and facilitating the attainment of the dual carbon goal. To address the complex issue of equipment modeling in the system, the RF model is used to accurately depict the nonlinear relationship between system parameters and prediction objectives, which simplifies the modeling process. Then we establishes a dual objective optimization problem, aiming to minimize total power consumption while minimizing system efficiency. The NSGA-II algorithm is utilized to obtain a set of pareto optimal solutions, and then ASF is employed to identify the unique optimal solution. By implementing the derived control strategies, which involve adjusting the fan speed and equipment states, the central air conditioning system achieves reduction in power consumption by 14.5% and system efficiency by 56.31%. This validates the effectiveness of the proposed RF-NSGA-II model.

articleTitle: Stable truckload matching in the vehicle-cargo matching platform
abstract: In this paper we propose the applying of stable matching theory to vehicle-cargo matching (VCM) platform for truckload matching. Firstly, we filter the essential information into three stages respectively are the construction of primary vehicle capacity pool and cargo sources pool, optimal vehicle capacity pool and cargo sources pool, as well as the ranking of preferred carriers’ vehicles by shippers and the preferred shippers’ cargoes by carriers. Then we put forward a stable matching model of VCM platform to maximize the total matching degree between carriers and shippers. Finally, we illustrate the influence of stable matching on VCM platform in different market scale.
