The results show that the application of the stable matching theory can improve the actual total matching degree of the platform, and the influence of the stable matching theory on the total matching degree of the platform becomes more obvious with the increase of the market scale.

articleTitle: Analysis of Heat Dissipation Structure of Permanent Magnet Eddy Current Coupler based on Magnetothermal Multi-physics Coupling
abstract: To optimize the thermal performance of traditional permanent magnet eddy current couplers, the thermal-physical coupling method is employed to design and analyze the thermal structure of the permanent magnet eddy current coupler. Firstly, based on an analytical model established using the equivalent magnetic circuit method, with the structural parameters of the permanent magnet eddy current coupler as variables and torque output, thermal device temperature, and volume as optimization objectives, a semi- analytical method for thermal-physical coupling is proposed. This involves finite element iterative computation of the multi-physical field-coupled permanent magnet eddy current coupler, optimizing material parameters, and validating the heat dissipation coefficient. The results indicate that the thermal structure designed after comprehensive optimization of volume, performance, and other objectives exhibits superior performance. This study provides a basis for the design and performance optimization of the thermal device in permanent magnet eddy current couplers.

articleTitle: Adaptive PID Control of Furnace Temperature in MSWI Process Based on Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper tackles the challenge of effectively regulating furnace temperature in the municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) process. It proposes an approach that integrates reinforcement learning with traditional PID control. Firstly, an analysis of the characteristics of furnace temperature control is conducted to identify the key manipulated variables affecting it. Subsequently, a control strategy specifically tailored for furnace temperature is developed, employing online adaptive PID with a BPNN-fitted actor-critic network (BPNN-ACN-PID). Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through control experiments using actual process data from a MSWI plant in Beijing.

articleTitle: A Cybersecurity Named Entity Recognition Model Based on Active Learning and Self-learning
abstract: With the rapid development of Internet, there are more and more cybersecurity reports which contain valuable knowledge about the security events, but these data are difficult to utilize due to their unstructured characteristics. Named Entity Recognition (NER) from these unstructured texts is a critical and fundamental task for data utilization. Recently deep neural network-based models have achieved high performance in NER, however these models heavily rely on large amounts of labeled data. Since the labeled data is scarce in most professional domains, such as cybersecurity, and structure of the entities is very complex. To address these issues, we propose a semi-supervised entity recognition method based on active learning and selflearning, which mainly consists of two phases: entity recognition model construction and intelligent new training sample selection. In the first phase, an entity recognition model that integrates the pre-trained language model ALBERT is proposed, we employ a word-by-word processing way to solve the problems caused by word segmentation errors and polysemous words. In the second phase, we employ the active learning and self-learning strategies to select the most valuable data from unlabeled dataset, and then insert these data into the labeled dataset for iterative training, thus improving the performance of the NER model. To evaluate the performance of the proposed method, we collect data from several famous platforms, including CNNVD, FreeBuf Security Forum and SangFor Security Response Center, and the experimental results show that the proposed method not only improves the accuracy of entity recognition, but also effectively alleviates the problem caused by the scarcity of labeled data.

articleTitle: Path Planning for Underactuated Unmanned Surface Vehicle Swarm Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This research addresses the challenge of inadequately reflecting the kinematic constraints inherent in underactuated unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) within existing deep reinforcement learning (DRL) simulation platforms. A virtual ocean simulation platform is constructed using the Unity3D engine, specifically designed to incorporate kinematic constraints in underactuated USV swarm points-to-points path planning scenarios. Subsequently, an enhanced multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) algorithm is introduced for effective path decision-making. Finally, the Peaceful-pie toolkit facilitates seamless data interaction between Python and Unity, enabling cost-effective model training. Simulation experiments demonstrate that, in unknown environments, underactuated USV swarms can utilize sensor information to navigate collision-free paths towards designated target points.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of Networked Control Systems with Multiple Constraints
abstract: The stability problem for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) networked control systems (NCSs) under external disturbance, packet dropout and channel noise interference is investigated in this paper. External disturbance exists in the forward channel, packet dropout and channel noise interference coexist in the feedback channel and the occurrence of packet dropout is assumed to obey Bernoulli distribution. The stability conditions of the NCSs were obtained through system stability theory, frequency domain method and a variety of decomposition techniques. The results show that the stability of NCSs is affected by the inherent characteristics of NCSs, external disturbance, packet dropout and channel noise. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method is verified by a simulation example.

articleTitle: Abnormal condition identification for pulverizing coal system based on Object-Oriented Bayesian Network
abstract: The pulverizing system is a critical auxiliary subsystem for coal-fired power generation units, and its operational status directly impacts the overall safety and stability of the entire power generation unit. In addressing the challenges posed by the pulverizing system, this study presents an abnormal condition identification method based on Object- Oriented Bayesian Networks (OOBN) that integrates knowledge and data. The proposed approach establishes a Bayesian network abnormal condition identification class with high accuracy and superior diagnostic performance. Initially, the method builds an initial class structure based on existing knowledge. Subsequently, leveraging genetic algorithms, the class structure is refined through the encapsulation of super nodes based on operational data. Finally, the instantiation of objects according to the refined class structure results in the development of an OOBN-based abnormal condition identification model. During online operations, abnormal symptom information is acquired, and real-time identification of abnormal conditions is achieved through reverse inference. The feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method are validated on a real dataset of abnormal events in the pulverizing system.

articleTitle: Backstepping based High-order Sliding Mode Control for UAV Attitude Tracking
abstract: For realizing accurate attitude tracking with strong robust, this paper proposes a UAV attitude control method based on backstepping method and high-order sliding mode control Backstepping method is adopted to obtain desired attitude rate, and reduce the attitude control system to first order system. For the reduced order system, high order sliding mode control law is designed to guarantee the stability of the attitude controller and eliminate the chattering. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed attitude control method can track to given attitude fast with high precision and is insensitive to external disturbance.

articleTitle: Path planning for mobile robot based on deep reinforcement learning with double experience replay
abstract: To further improve the convergence speed of the deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm in the mobile robot path planning task. In this paper, an improved DDPG algorithm with dual experience replay (DER) buffer based on prioritized and positive experience screening mechanism is proposed. Firstly, a prioritized experience replay buffer is introduced to store the basic samples. Then, an additional positive experience replay buffer is added to store samples with greater learning value by utilizing the positive experience filtering mechanism. The double experience replay buffer solves the low sample utilization, thereby effectively improves the stability of the algorithm in dynamic environments. Simulation experiments show that in the path planning task, compared with the traditional DDPG algorithm, the reward value obtained by the proposed algorithm is significantly improved, and the network convergence speed is further improved, which provides a new scheme for path planning of mobile robot.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Boundary Control of a Flexible Marine Riser-vessel System Under Actuator and Structural Failures
abstract: This paper develops an adaptive fault-tolerant boundary control scheme for riser-vessel systems to deal with actuator failure and structural failure, simultaneously. The marine riser-vessel system dynamics is modeled by a fourth-order partial-ordinary differential equation. An adaptive fault-tolerant boundary control framework is proposed, which together with the designed adaptive update law guarantees the uniformly ultimately boundedness of the closed-loop system. The simulation results show that the developed fault-tolerant control method can still make the system state converge in a small area of zero in the presence of actuator failure and structural failure.

articleTitle: Control Valve Stiction Detection Based on the Improved Linear Regression Method
abstract: Accurate detection of control valve stiction is crucial for ensuring system stability and production safety in industrial process control. The stiction detection method based on linear regression fall short in identifying signal peaks and valleys due to the fixed window size, making it difficult to accurately determine stiction. To address this, an improved detection method is proposed, in which the algorithm automatically identifies the peaks and valleys in the signal, and dynamically selects the window size in conjunction with the signal characteristics, thereby enhancing the accuracy of stiction detection. Moreover, a curve shape index is introduced to reinforce the reliability of the detection results. The effectiveness of the improved linear regression method in control valve stiction detection and its advantages over existing methods have been validated with actual industrial data.

articleTitle: Extended State Observer Based Model Prediction Control for PMSM Field Weakening Control
abstract: This paper presents an extended state observer (ESO) based model predictive control (MPC) strategy for regulating the speed of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) during field weakening control, aiming to optimize the field weakening control performance in the presence of external disturbances and model uncertainty. An extended state observer is utilized to estimate disturbances caused by external disturbances and model parameter uncertainties, as well as nonlinear terms in the equations that are not easily handled. Through the incorporation of disturbance estimation and the anticipation of future disturbances within the prediction horizon, a predictive control law is derived by solving an optimization problem with constrains. Simulation results indicate that the proposed field weakening controller achieves better disturbance rejection, and solve the current and voltage constraints well.

articleTitle: Fast time-synchronized control of spacecraft Attitude Stabilization using scaled p-norm
abstract: The paper presents a method aimed at achieving rapid time-synchronized stability for flexible spacecraft attitude stabilization issues through the scaled p-norm technique. The norm-normalized sign function is integrated and fused with a disturbance observer to formulate the scaled p-norm controller. This controller’s action ensures that all state elements converge simultaneously to the origin. Simulation results indicate a substantial enhancement in convergence rate with the proposed approach, thereby enhancing efficiency and robustness in controlling the attitude of flexible spacecraft.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-based Data-driven Control Design for Motion Control Systems
abstract: Motion control systems are widely used in many fields of industry. Conventional control schemes are highly dependent on the system model to be designed. The performance of design would be greatly reduced, when the system exists unknown disturbances or uncertainty. Therefore, some scholars pointed out that the dependency on the system models can be eliminated by data-driven design schemes. In this paper, the reinforcement learning-based methods are included, which appeal to attentions gradually. The disturbances rejection problem for motion control systems is studied based on reinforcement learning. Considering the continuity of state space and action space, a method based on deep reinforcement learning algorithm is proposed to reject the periodic disturbances. Proposed deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) and twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) based algorithms are compared in simulation. The simulation results show that the periodic disturbances of the motion control systems can be rejected effectively with the proposed reinforcement learning controller.

Author Keywords: Twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3)

articleTitle: Leader-follower Formation Control for a Multi-missile System via Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: The methods for the formation tracking control problem are mainly based on nonlinear control theories. Usually, the control effect of such methods heavily depends on an accurate control model and a lot of controller parameters need to be selected properly. To cope with these shortcomings, a novel reinforcement learning-based formation controller is proposed for a leader-follower multi-missile system. The deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm is implemented to generate the formation control signals. An interaction environment containing a leader and a follower is formulated, in which a model-free optimal control policy is obtained by a training process. The convergent actor-network is tested for a multi-missile system. Simulation results show that the formation control objective can be rapidly achieved in spite of the change of leader maneuvers. There is no need to change the hyperparameters of the policy for different kinds of formation scenarios, which shows great advantages over the conventional nonlinear control theory-based methods in terms of parameter selection.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Fault Detection and Isolation for Continuous-Time Piecewise Linear Systems
abstract: In this article, the fault detection and isolation (FDI) problem for continuous-time piecewise linear systems with sensor outage faults is investigated via event-triggered (ET) mechanisms. First, the output space is defined, and the design method of FDI filters is proposed, in which it is necessary to re-divide the regions of the output space in the design of isolation filters after sensor failures. Then, ET mechanisms are designed on the basis of the filters gains, and an ET FDI scheme is constructed. Different from the existing results, the influence of sensor faults on the output space is considered, and the gains of the designed filters in the absence of ET mechanisms are still applicable after the ET mechanisms are introduced, while the ones in the existing results need to be redesigned. Finally, a simulation example is presented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Cloud Task Decomposition Based on Improved NSGA-II
abstract: This paper investigates task decomposition in the cloud manufacturing environment. Firstly, in this study, the multi-objective task decomposition method with the optimization goal of the maximum internal correlation of subtasks, the minimum external coupling between subtasks, and the mini-mum subtask workload balance is studied. Secondly, the non-dominated sorting genetic-II algorithm (NSGA-II) is improved from three aspects: initialization, parent selection, and mutation mode. Then, the improved NSGA-II (iNSGA-II) is used to solve the problem. Finally, the experiment is carried out to verify the effectiveness of the model and algorithm.

articleTitle: The Influence of Social Distancing Awareness on Epidemic Spreading in Social Networks
abstract: In this paper, we propose a epidemic-social distancing awareness dynamics model, and the impact of awareness of maintaining social distance on the spread of epidemics is investigated. The effect of maintaining social distance on eradicating epidemics is explored by analyzing the stability of the equilibrium state of the epidemic-social distance awareness dynamic model. When the infectiousness of virus is mild, the epidemic can be eliminated regardless of the individual’s awareness. When the infectiousness of virus is moderate, introducing some stubborn individuals can also eradicate the epidemic. When the infectiousness of virus is high, introducing some stubborn individuals can reduce the level of infection within the community. Using the real data from a sample of Australians, we apply the proposed epidemic-social distancing awareness dynamics model to explore the impact of maintaining social distance on COVID-19.

articleTitle: Controller design and stability analysis for singularly perturbed hybrid systems with multi-rate sampling
abstract: This paper investigates the stabilization problem of singularly perturbed hybrid systems with multi-rate sampling. Firstly, we establish a hybrid model to describe a class of singularly perturbed systems by designing a multi-rate sampling controller. Secondly, a sufficient condition is proposed to ensure that the considered systems are uniformly globally exponentially stable using the Lyapunov approach. Thirdly, we derive the bounds of the maximally allowable fast sampling interval, and analyze the relationship between the singular perturbation parameter and the fast sampling interval. Finally, a DC motor model is illustrated to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Consensus of the nonlinear multi-agent systems via event-triggered impulsive control
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the consensus for multi-agent systems (MASs) by employing a distributed event-triggered impulsive control strategy (ETICS). First, by combining the advantages of event-triggered control and impulse control, ETICS is designed to effectively avoid continuous communication and prevent Zeno behavior. Compared to traditional event-triggered control, ETICS is effective even when the information flow is a discrete signal. Second, based on ETICS, the sufficient conditions for consensus of MASs are derived by using the Lyapunov stability theory. Finally, the effectiveness of the ETICS employed in this study is confirmed through a numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Formation Assembly and Transformation Controller of Multi-UAV based on Sliding Mode Control
abstract: In this paper, the multi-UAV formation assembly and formation transformation controller is designed based on the theory of sliding mode control. The long wingman formation mode is selected. For the formation flight system of UAV, by selected the linear sliding mode surface, a controller of control the team formation of UAV is designed. Simulation experiments are done by the formation assembly of UAVs and the maintenance and transformation of column formation, zigzag formation, hexagon formation and rectangle formation. The results show that the UAV formation can track the desired track, maintain and change the formation.

Author Keywords: formation assembly and formation transformation controller

articleTitle: Research on target recognition method of robotic arm based on improved ORB
abstract: When a robotic arm is in motion, it typically cannot intelligently perform complex tasks in response to changes in the surrounding environment. Introducing a vision-based spatial target recognition method enables the robotic arm to accurately acquire spatial information about the environment, laying the foundation for autonomous execution of intricate tasks by the robotic arm. Therefore, this paper investigates vision-based spatial target recognition methods. The approach employed utilizes template matching based on descriptors. The feature point extraction is accomplished through the application of the Improved ORB (Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF) image feature extraction algorithm. Furthermore, an improved GMS (Grid-based motion statistics) fusion MLESAC (Maximum Likelihood Estimator Sample Consensus) algorithm is used to accomplish the matching between the captured image and the template image. The research results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve accurate, rapid, and stable target recognition.

articleTitle: Controller Design for Neutral Networks with Markov Jumps and a New Method for Exponential Stability Analysis
abstract: This study examines neutral neural network systems with Markov jump (MJNNNs)’ mean square exponential stability. When discussing the stochastic catastrophe problem in complicated systems, Markov jump is crucial. First, a simple Lyapunov Krasovskii functional (LKF) containing sufficient system information is established, the GFWM-based inequality and other integral inequalities, a movable parameter, and enough random vectors are then used to calculate a single integral term in the derivative of the built LKF.

articleTitle: Adaptive Genetic Algorithm for Acid Rolling Scheduling Problem in the Steel Industry
abstract: For an acid rolling scheduling problem arising from steel production system, a mathematical programming model was established to transform the violation states or jump values of adjacent materials' width, thickness, steel type, welding codes, etc., during the production process into transition costs between materials. An adaptive genetic algorithm (AGA) was proposed to address the characteristics of the problem. It utilizes an adaptive parameter control method to adjust penalty values for attributes with a higher number of violations, thus ensuring the algorithm’s applicability to a wide range of units. The model and algorithm were validated using a practical production case in a specific enterprise. Experimental results demonstrated that AGA reduces the violations in scheduling plans while lowering the jumps in attributes such as the width and thickness of adjacent materials. Consequently, it achieves the objectives of reducing unit switching times, decreasing production costs, and improving production efficiency.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Prescribed-Time Consensus for Multi-Agent Systems via Fully Distributed Strategy
abstract: This paper studies the prescribed-time consensus control for first-order multi-agent systems with undirected graph. In order to reduce the communication and computation resources, event-triggered communication is considered. To solve the event-triggered prescribed-time consensus problem, we design a node-based event-triggered controller whose coupling weights are updated based on an adaptive mechanism. Moreover, a state transformation is considered, and by analysing the prescribed-time stability of the transformed state, both the prescribed-time consensus and the boundness of controller are proved. Note that, with the adaptive updating mechanism, the parameters in the controller and the event-triggering condition do not depend on global information. Thus the proposed controller is fully distributed. Besides, the exclusion of the Zeno behavior is proved for the whole time except the preset settling time. Finally, a numerical simulation is given to validate the effectiveness of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: Radial Basis Function Sliding Mode Control for Two Axis Fast Steering Mirror
abstract: An adaptive radial basis function sliding mode algorithm is propose to control the two-axis fast steering mirror (FSM) with parametric uncertainties and external disturbance. The mathematic model of the two-axis FSM system was first decoupled into two separate simple models. Based on this decoupled model, a sliding surface is defined and taken as the only input to the RBF controller. The weights of the controller are tuned on-line based on the sliding mode reaching law. The stability of the controller system is provided by the Lyapunov theory. Simulation results show that this method is effective, and the robustness to parametric uncertainties and external disturbance is provided.

articleTitle: STFformer: An Effective PM2.5 Prediction Model
abstract: PM2.5 is an important indicator of air pollution index, and its accurate prediction is of great significance for urban air pollution prevention and control. In this paper, an effective prediction model named STFformer is proposed for PM2.5. Firstly, the original PM2.5 data is decomposed into seasonal component and trend component, which are predicted separately not as a whole to enhance the prediction accuracy. Then, for the seasonal component with dominant frequency, the Transformer equipped with Fourier attention is proposed to achieve effective feature extraction, and the multi-scale information contraction and expansion blocks using series of convolution are designed to achieve seasonal component prediction. Meanwhile, for the trend component, the MLP network with RevIN block is proposed to process the non-stationary information and the trend component is accurately predicted; Finally, experiment results on the PM2.5 data set and the public seasonal data set WTH show that the proposed STFformer achieves the best prediction accuracy in most cases compared with some typical time series prediction models and reduce prediction error by 2.5% to 3.6% at different time scales.

articleTitle: Robust Disturbance Rejection for Nonlinear Dynamic Systems under Multi-Source Complex Disturbances
abstract: To address the disturbance rejection problem of nonlinear dynamic systems facing complex multi-source disturbance, this paper proposes a novel control framework based on a full-order disturbance observer combined with H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> control theory. The proposed method categorizes all external disturbance into two major types, namely disturbance suppression and disturbance attenuation, to deal with complex multi-source disturbance from both perspectives. In conclusion, the algorithm was validated through numerical simulations and motor speed experiments. The results confirm that the proposed method exhibits excellent disturbance rejection performance and robustness when facing multi-source disturbances.

articleTitle: Command Filtered Backstepping based Load Frequency Control in Power System with Prescribed Performance
abstract: Load frequency is an important index to judge whether the power system is stable. In this paper, a prescribed performance controller based on command filter backstepping is designed to improve the control effect and reduce the influence of load fluctuation on the frequency of power system. Based on the prescribed performance control (PPC) strategy, the error conversion is realized to guarantees that the tracking errors of the system can converge to the range limited in the single-area power system model. Combined with the command filter backstepping, we avoid the complex calculation problem in the general backstepping method. The advantage of this control scheme is that the transient and steady state control performance of the power system can meet the prescribed boundary constraint. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed controller and guarantee that load frequency deviation converges to zero in a short time without large fluctuations.

articleTitle: STFE-YOLOX: A Small Target Recognition Network for Surface Mount Component Detection
abstract: It is of great significances for the accurate detection of surface mount components in the SMT (Surface Mounted Technology). However, due to the small size of the surface mount components and their dense distribution on the PCB (Printed Circuit Board), the accurate and effective detection of them has become a challenging task. This paper proposes an improved small target detection network based on YOLOX (renamed STFE-YOLOX), in order to solve missing and error problems in the surface mount component detection. Firstly, according to the distribution characteristics of surface mount components, a Moudle data enhancement strategy is proposed to improve the original network, which can broaden the range of data and enhance the model’s training effectiveness. Next, a MFFM (multi-feature fusion module) is proposed to fuse features of different levels in the network, which adds a detection branch for improving small target detection capabilities; The experiment results show that mAP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf>(%) and mAP50:95(%) of the proposed network in this paper reach 91.4% and 60.7% respectively on the surface mount component data set, it balances detection accuracy and speed better than the current standard detection models.

articleTitle: A Novel Path Planning Approach Based on Exploration-efficient Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Path planning for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in given environment has been widely studied. A novel path planning method for UAVs is put forward according to exploration-efficient reinforcement learning in this paper, which achieves more efficient path exploration while ensuring safe arrival at the destination. Firstly, the classical DQN is used as the main algorithm, and the reward function of the agent is reshaped. Secondly, noise parameters are added to the network structure, which helps to achieve more efficient exploration. Thirdly, by setting curriculum of different difficulty levels for gradient training of agents, decision-making experience can be obtained more quickly. Through simulation experiments, the method put forward is able to complete path planning tasks, require less running time and improve planning speed.

articleTitle: Optimal scheduling of integrated energy systems considering stepped carbon trading
abstract: In the context of "dual-carbon", in order to cope with environmental problems, effectively improve environment al friendliness, and further reduce the carbon emission level of the integrated energy system (IES), a low-carbon economic operation strategy for the IES is proposed. Firstly, a tiered carbon trading mechanism is introduced to control the carbon emissions of IES; then, an electric-hydrogen conversion device and a hydrogen storage device are introduced; based on this, an integrated energy low-carbon optimisation model is established with the objective function of minimising the sum of the cost of energy purchasing, the cost of carbon emissions, and the cost of wind abandonment; the CLPEX commercial solver is used to solve the model, and the effectiveness of the strategy is verified through the comparison of multiple scenarios.

articleTitle: MPPT Control Algorithm of Photovoltaic Array in Dynamic Environment
abstract: Maximum power point tracking(MPPT) is one of the key technologies of photovoltaic(PV) power generation system and an important way to improve the efficiency of PV power generation. In a dynamic environment, the power output characteristics of PV cells are multi-peak curves. In this paper, a particle swarm optimization(PSO) algorithm has designed to realize the maximum power output of PV arrays by initializing particle swarm individuals, conducting global scanning and mathematical calculation, and constantly updating individual and global optimal values. The BOOST circuit has been designed, and MATLAB/Simulink have been used for modeling and simulation. The experimental results show that compared with perturbation observation method and conductivity increment method,PSO has faster global search speed, higher tracking accuracy and better convergence ability for maximum power value under dynamic illumination.

articleTitle: Adaptive Secure Missile Guidance Against Additive and Multiplicative Cyber-Attacks
abstract: In this paper, a novel secure guidance law is proposed to address additive and multiplicative cyber-attacks injected into guidance commands. From an engineering perspective, the two kinds of cyber-attack are assumed to be bounded. Then, directed by Lyapunov theory, their bounds are estimated by designing adaptive laws. Meanwhile, the convergence of line-of-sight rates and angle errors is guaranteed, which helps to intercept the maneuvering target successfully with terminal angle constraints. Finally, numerical simulations show the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Vision Transformer based UNet with Multi-Head Attention for Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: In recent years, deep learning models, such as the UNet architecture, have shown great potential in medical image segmentation tasks. However, these models often require large amounts of annotated data to achieve high performance. In this paper, we propose a novel approach that combines the UNet architecture with the Vision Transformer with Multi-Head Attention model (MAViT-UNet) for medical image segmentation. Our method leverages the ability of ViT to capture long-range dependencies in images, while still benefitting from the UNet’s skip connections for local feature extraction. Through extensive experiments on various medical datasets, we demonstrate that our proposed Vision Transformer based UNet achieves state-of-the-art performance in medical image segmentation tasks, even with limited annotated data. The results suggest the potential of transformer-based models in the field of medical image analysis.

articleTitle: Research on road damage detection based on improved YOLOv8 in road scene
abstract: Road damage detection plays an important role in driving safety and road condition repair. Aiming at the existing inefficient and complex algorithms and methods, this paper provides an improved YOLOv8 detection algorithm: YOLOV8-MS(MPCA and Slim-neck), which combines precision and lightweight. Firstly, the Slim-neck structure is used in the head structure to reduce the computation. Secondly, the Multipath Coordinate Attention (MPCA) mechanism is added in the backbone structure, which increases the receptive field, improves the feature extraction ability of road defects, and reduces the interference of irrelevant features. Finally, we compare the improved YOLOv8 algorithm with other existing algorithms to verify the effectiveness of our proposed improvements. The experimental results show that in RDD2022 data set and self-built data set, compared with the original algorithm, the improved algorithm improves by 2.7% and 1.7% respectively with mAP50, and 1.9% and 0.6% respectively with MAP50-95. The computational complexity is reduced by 9.88%, which realizes the purpose of improving algorithm accuracy and lightweight.

articleTitle: Distributed Observer-based Cooperative Fault Tolerant Control for Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: This article investigates the cooperative fault-tolerant control problem for leader-follower multi-agent systems (MASs) with actuator faults. A type of distributed observer and fault estimator are constructed for each follower agent. By using the estimated state and fault information, the fault-tolerant control protocol is designed to guarantee cooperation of the MAS. It can be found that cooperation errors of all agents can converge to a predeterminate set around the origin under the proposed fault estimation and fault-tolerant control scheme. Finally, simulation results are utilized to verify the effectiveness of the approach in this paper.

articleTitle: Disturbance Observer-based Linear Metro Traffic Regulation for Two Intersecting Lines
abstract: This paper investigates the optimal control problem of subway transportation network with parameter uncertainties and external disturbances. Firstly, considering the delay arising from transfer stations, a linear discrete event state-space model is established for the considered two intersecting subway lines, which combines parameter uncertainties and external disturbances into a lumped disturbance. Then, a disturbance observer is designed to estimate the lumped disturbance. Based on that a tube model predictive control method is contrived to address potential delays. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed approach has been verified through numerical simulation. Compared with linear quadratic regulator and model predictive control algorithms, its superiority has been presented.

articleTitle: Machine Part Defect Detection based on Deep Learning:Key Issues Research
abstract: Due to the lack of noise removal of parts in conventional detection methods, the accuracy and real-time performance of detection are affected. To this end, this project proposes to study machine part defect detection methods based on deep learning. First, the impact noise detection and filtering in mechanical part images based on median filtering will be studied; secondly, using deep learning techniques, a multi-level classifier will be established to implement feature extraction of the entire connectivity hierarchy on this basis; finally, the posterior probability of the target image will be obtained according to the output results of the classifier. On this basis, a fault diagnosis method based on decision criteria is proposed, and the results of fault classification are used as the basis for fault diagnosis. Experiments prove that the algorithm proposed in this paper has better detection accuracy and detection time than conventional detection method

articleTitle: Research on helicopter electric tail rotor control method based on fuzzy neural network
abstract: The stability of the helicopter mandates the tail rotor’s high efficiency and reliability, and precise control over the distributed electric tail rotor is pivotal in enhancing yaw attitude control efficiency and maneuverability. This study presents a fuzzy neural network control methodology incorporating feed-forward compensation, aimed at achieving meticulous control over the distributed electric tail rotor system. Initially, a comprehensive analysis of the helicopter’s motion characteristics was conducted through six-degree-of-freedom physical modeling. Subsequently, a hybrid approach combining fuzzy control with neural networks was devised to optimize the balance between stability and dynamic response in the distributed tail rotor system. This method thoroughly accounts for the nonlinear control characteristics, integrating a feed-forward compensation mechanism to facilitate rapid responses to external perturbations through preemptive prediction of posture changes in the distributed electric tail rotor system. In the final phase, the entire distributed electric tail rotor control system model was constructed in MATLAB/Simulink, where the control strategy of dynamically adjusting the PI parameters through a fuzzy neural network algorithm underwent functional simulation. The findings demonstrate that, relative to PID control and fuzzy PID control, the neural network control method facilitates precise yaw angle control under varying flight condition

articleTitle: Research on Knowledge-based Assembly Process Planning Method Based on Representation Learning Reasoning
abstract: For multi-variety and small-batch assembly parts, the assembly process updates and iterations are very frequent. The assembly process planning method based on manual experience cannot effectively utilize the large amount of hidden assembly process knowledge generated during product iteration. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an effective assembly process planning method based on knowledge graph. Fristly, the entire assembly is constructed from each layer of assembly components to reduce the computational complexity of assembly process planning. Then, assembly process planning starts from the last layer of assembly components. The entire assembly process planning is obtained by concatenating the results of each layer’s assembly process planning from bottom to top. Assembly operations are determined based on the features of the base component and neighboring assembly components. If there is no corresponding assembly operation for the assembly features, the assembly operation can be inferred through representation learning. After that, arrange and combine all possible assembly solutions to form a feasible solution space. Inferring the optimal assembly process sequence through rules. Combining the optimal assembly sequence with specific assembly operations to complete assembly process planning. Finally, Macro and micro adjustments are made to the assembly process planning of different products in the same series by comparing the differences between current product and classic product. In this paper, the upper door of elevator is used as an example to verify the proposed method. The results show that the proposed method can effectively realize assembly process planning.

articleTitle: Application of Intelligent Management System for Defects of Substation Equipment
abstract: The safe and stable operation of electric power system is related to the national economy and people's livelihood. Transformer link in the power system is in a hub position, the number of substation equipment, wide distribution, equipment status directly affects the safe and stable operation of the system. Timely detection of defects and elimination of hidden dangers are the prerequisites for ensuring equipment safety and power grid safety. Relying on the "cloud, big things, mobile intelligence" technology, the project team of Guangdong Electricity Academy of Sciences comprehensively mines the defects and hidden danger data of the substation equipment, breaks the situation that the existing technical support system is independent and decentralized, the business efficiency is not strong enough, the carrying capacity of the substation defects management personnel is not sufficient, and the automation of control information is not sufficient, and explores the new mode of quasi real-time, senseless and precise control and control of defects and hidden danger. Exploring a new mode of management and control, the company has developed an intelligent system for defect management of substation equipment, which integrates data fusion, intelligent analysis, precision and high efficiency. It makes efficient use of the modern information platform, realizes equipment state evaluation and batch defect diagnosis through multi-dimensional analysis and multi-platform interaction, saves about 90% of workload, improves the quality and efficiency of defect analysis, and realizes the goal of doing practical things for the public and reducing the burden for the grassroots.

articleTitle: Research on fault diagnosis of rolling bearing based on Variational Mode Decomposition and Hilbert envelope spectrum analysis
abstract: Rolling bearing is an important part of rotating machinery equipment, so fault diagnosis is of great significance. A fault diagnosis method combining VMD (Variational Mode Decomposition) and Hilbert envelope spectrum analysis is proposed. First, the VMD method which optimized by Antlion optimization algorithm is used to decompose the original fault signal to obtain the IMF(Intrinsic Mode Function) component containing bearing fault characteristic information.,then the IMF component is analyzed by Hilbert envelope spectrum analysis to obtain the fault characteristic frequency. By contrast EEMD(Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition ) and VMD, The results show that the fault diagnosis method based on VMD and Hilbert envelope spectrum analysis can more effectively identify the fault of bearing rolling element.

articleTitle: Infrared and Visible Image Object Detection Method based on Generated Adversarial Network
abstract: Infrared image and visible image have many complementary features. Combining infrared and visible images for object detection can make full use of the complementary features from multi-band images and effectively improve the detection accuracy. In order to extract complementary features, a parallel convolutional neural network is designed. In parallel convolutional neural network, according to the characteristics of multi-band images, a deep network is designed to extract infrared features, while a shallow neural network is used to extract visible features. In order to improve the detection accuracy and effectively detect the difficult objects, an object detection method based on the generative adversarial network for infrared and visible images is proposed. The generative adversarial network is composed of generator and discriminator. The generator is set as the parallel convolutional object detection network, and the discriminator is set as the classification network. After continuous iterative adversarial training, the generative adversarial network can accurately detect objects in multi-band images.

articleTitle: Event-triggered Control of 2-D F-M Model with Deception Attacks
abstract: In this paper, an output feedback controller based on event-triggered mechanism is designed for the 2-D Fornasini-Machesini (F-M) system under deception attacks. As a kind of network attack, deception attacks disguise the attacker’s data information as the original transmission signal of the system. The aim of this paper is to design an event-triggered output feedback controller so that the addressed error system satisfies a predefined H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performance index. Sufficient conditions are given to ensure the 2-D augmented error system to be robustly stable leveraging Lyapunov theory and stochastic analysis, then the results are further extended to achieve the robust H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> stability for the augmented error system. Furthermore, the display expression of the controller parameters is obtained by solving a matrix inequality. Finally, the feasibility of the theoretical results is substantiated through simulation examples.

articleTitle: Filter-based Detection and Location of Dynamic Load Altering Attack in power Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: This work investigates the problem of detecting and localizing attacks on a class of power cyber-physical systems (CPSs) in the presence of dynamic load alteration attacks (D-LAA). The power CPS is modeled as a discrete-time system with an unknown input, assuming that the sampling process is periodic and the D-LAA is bounded. This study delves into the investigation of attack detection and localization within a specific category of power cyber-physical systems (CPSs) when dealing with dynamic load alteration attacks (D-LAA). A novel Maximum Correntropy Robust Two-Stage Kalman Filter (MCRTSKF) is proposed so that the accurate state estimation for power CPS is achieved in spite of anomalous noise. Meanwhile, some essential parameters for the designed filter are obtained through the fixed-point iteration-stop parameter selection method. Furthermore, based on the state estimate value, the attack detection and localization procedure is presented. Finally, the validity and effectiveness of the proposed attack detection and localization schemes are illustrated by case studies on an IEEE 9-bus system.

Author Keywords: Maximum Correntropy Robust Two-Stage Kalman Filte

articleTitle: Product Line Design Optimization Based on Fuzzy Utility
abstract: With the deepening of globalization, competition in the new market environment is becoming increasingly fierce, and the product life cycle is gradually shortened, as a result, customer demand becomes diversifying and differentiating. To expand market share, companies have to design a series of new products to meet various demands so that can survive in the fierce competition and rapid development. To closely describe customers' satisfaction, it is regarded as a fuzzy number to reflect the uncertainty of customers' preferences. Therefore, product line design based on fuzzy utility is proposed to better guide decision-making to expand the market share of enterprises, and ultimately enhance the market competitiveness of enterprises. In this research, the goal of maximizing market share has been established by the two-step method which is a classical method of a product line optimization method, and a nonlinear model is linearized by adding some middle variables to solve the exact solution of the problem. However, the exact solution is limited by the size of the problem, due to the larger scale in practice. We design an improved bacterial foraging optimization that combines genetic operators to solve large-scale problems. In the stage of experimental design, the correctness of the algorithm is verified by comparing exact solutions with optimal solutions with small-scale data. In addition, some larger-scale experiments confirm the versatility and stability of the algorithm.

articleTitle: High Precision Prediction of Hot Rolled Medium Plate Based on Stacking Model
abstract: In the production of hot rolled steel plates, thickness is a crucial quality parameter that significantly influences both the product's yield and the stability of the rolling process. Considering the characteristics of multi-variable, nonlinearity, and strong coupling in the plate rolling process, the prediction accuracy of existing theoretical models is not high. In this paper, an improved ensemble method based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) and Stacking is proposed. Firstly, the random forest (RF) algorithm is introduced for feature selection to enhance the rationality of input features. Secondly, various data-driven models for predicting steel plate thickness are developed, employing PSO to optimize the model parameters. The results indicate that the predictions from the data-driven model outperform existing theoretical models, and the optimized model demonstrates higher accuracy. To further enhance prediction accuracy, a Stacking model that integrates multiple machine learning algorithms is developed, and various Stacking strategies are proposed for comparison. The test results show that the Stacking model with RF as the meta learner and other models as the base learners performs the best. On the test dataset, the values for MAE, RMSE, and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> are 0.9429, 1.1176, and 0.9812, respectively. Compared with the best single model, these values are improved by 32%, 34%, and 8%, respectively. This enhancement meets the requirements for high precision and stable production.

articleTitle: A Distributed Simulation-to-Reality Transfer Framework for Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Recent works have demonstrated the applications of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) algorithms in many fields, including autonomous driving, finance, and games. However, how to transfer the MARL models trained in the simulation environment to the real world is a challenging issue due to the gap between simulation and reality. To address this issue, we propose a distributed simulation to reality (Sim2Real) transfer framework that encompasses three components, including a platform, MARL algorithms, and a distributed multi-agent Sim2Real transfer algorithm. In addition, to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, we design an experimental collaborative hunting task. The experiment results indicate that the proposed framework can enhance the real-world performance of MARL models.

articleTitle: A Gesture Recognition System Based On MEMS Accelerometer
abstract: With the development of mobile intelligent electronic devices, gesture recognition based on MEMS accelerometers has become a research hotspot. This paper proposes a gesture recognition system that utilizes an ARM processor, ADXL345 accelerometer, NRF24L01 wireless communications module, and LABVIEW. The system incorporates five accelerometers located on fingers to collect acceleration information from each sensor. The collected acceleration data is filtered and compared with pre-defined thresholds to determine the state of each finger. The system wirelessly transmits the status information of the five fingers to a receiver unit through the wireless communications module. The receiver unit analyzes the finger states and generates a final gesture identification value, which is then transmitted to the LABVIEW upper computer via a serial port. The generated gesture identification value is matched with image templates in LABVIEW to achieve gesture recognition. Additionally, the system enables human-computer interaction by allowing users to control web page access, image display, and robotic gripper movement through gestures.

articleTitle: Disturbance Observer-Based Improved Non-Singular Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control for the PMSM with Matched and Mismatched Disturbances
abstract: The permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) has been widely applied in electric drives. However, parameter perturbations and external disturbances can significantly affect the performance of the PMSM system. This is particularly true when these disturbances do not satisfy the disturbance matching condition, which can greatly increase the difficulty of motor speed control. To solve this problem, a composite control method utilizing an improved non-singular fast terminal sliding mode controller (NFTSMC) and a disturbance observer is proposed. Firstly, a nonlinear disturbance observer (NDO) based on the principle of higher-order sliding mode differentiator is proposed to estimate the matched and unmatched disturbances of the system. Secondly, to address the issue of conventional NFTSMC struggling to balance fast convergence and chattering inhibition, a new sliding mode reaching law (NSMRL) is proposed. This NSMRL can adapt to changes in the sliding mode surface and system state, while also providing further chattering inhibition. And an improved NFTSMC based on NSMRL is further designed. Finally, the NDO observations are incorporated into the improved NFTSMC through feed-forward compensation. The simulation results suggest that the proposed control strategy exhibits superior chattering inhibition ability, fast dynamic response, and disturbance inhibition effect.

Author Keywords: non-singular fast terminal sliding mode control (NFTSMC)

articleTitle: A Minimum-energy Trajectory Planning for an Inchworm-like Climbing Robot Based on IPSOIGSA Joint Algorithm
abstract: With the development of urban greening construction and the quick advance of modernization, there have been numerous high-altitude operations in a variety of fields, which are hazardous and have difficult working conditions. And in a variety of high-risk, high-intensity, highaltitude operations, climbing robots can take the place of humans. Climbing robots require strong endurance in order to complete high-altitude operations. This paper designs a high-altitude work robot, an inchworm-like climbing robot, based on the background and in combination with the research achievements in the field of climbing robots. This paper suggests an energy-optimal trajectory planning based on the IPSOIGSA joint algorithm for the two climbing gaits of the inchworm-like climbing robot in order to decrease energy consumption and increase endurance. According to the final simulation results, the intended trajectory uses less energy, the robot’s motion is stable, and the impact and vibration are also within acceptable limits.

articleTitle: Event-triggered interval estimation method for nonlinear system *
abstract: This paper presents a novel structure for the design of interval observers for continuous systems and introduces greater flexibility in parameter design compared to conventional interval observers. Additionally, an event-triggered mechanism(ETM) is employed to enhance the utilization of network resources and reduce computational overhead. Then the gain of the observer is solved by using a set of inequalities under sufficient conditions. Finally, the effectiveness of the designed interval observer is validated through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: An image classification algorithm for MSWI based on ResNet and attention mechanism
abstract: The municipal solid waste incineration has great advantages for resource recovery and utilization, and the stability of its combustion state is of great significance to the control process. However, the problem of low accuracy still exists in the classification of the images of municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI). For this reason, this paper proposes an image classification algorithm for MSWI based on attention module. The framework of ResNet is employed to improve the depth and accuracy of the network, which solves the problem of insufficient depth of the traditional network while suffering from the deficiency of slow convergence speed. Consequently, the attention module is embedded to solve the problem of different importance of different parts in the incineration flame image. The results show that the algorithm improves the recognition accuracy of municipal solid waste incineration flame images to 96.7%, and the convergence speed is significantly improved compared to other basic neural network models.

articleTitle: Tracking Group Consensus for Fractional-order Nonlinear Multi-agent Systems*
abstract: The tracking group consistency problem for nonlinear dynamic fractional-order multi-agent systems under undirected interaction graphs is discussed in this study. In double-integrator nonlinear multi-agent systems, a novel control method is presented, which can realize the group consistency with leaders. Introducing fractional-order Lyapunov method into fractional-order multi-agent systems, and some sufficient conditions are given for guaranteeing group consistency in nonlinear double-integrator dynamical systems. Finally, the proposed theory is validated using numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Cluster Synchronization of Heterogeneous Kuramoto Oscillators over Directed and Undirected Network Topologies
abstract: This paper studies the cluster synchronization of heterogeneous Kuramoto oscillators over both directed and undirected network topologies. It is assumed that there exist only cooperations among oscillators in the same cluster, while there may exist competitions between oscillators belonging to different clusters. A method based on Lyapunov functional is used to analyze the stability of frequency synchronization and some sufficient conditions are derived. It is shown that under a certain coupling structure, frequencies of the oscillators achieve cluster synchronization when the coupling strength within the intra-duster is strong enough, in which the lower bound of the coupling strength is clearly specified. Finally, some numerical simulations further visualize the cluster synchronization of ten oscillators in two clusters.

articleTitle: Optimal Residential Community Demand Response Scheduling Based on User Preferences and MILP
abstract: Demand response manages energy demand to match available energy in the smart grid. Residential community loads in the smart grid are diverse and flexible. To integrate user preferences with demand response scheduling for residential communities, a centralized demand response scheduling algorithm is proposed. In this paper, user willingness price is first introduced through fuzzy c-means to quantify user preferences. Secondly, a complete residential community DR scheduling algorithm is established based on use preference and mixed integer linear programming to minimize the total energy cost of the residential community. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can reduce the total energy cost of the residential community and communication traffic.

articleTitle: Quasi-synchronization for complex dynamic networks with parameter mismatch and deception attack: A dynamic event-triggered impulsive control method
abstract: This paper investigates the quasi-synchronization problem of master-slave systems in the face of parameter mismatch and deception attack by means of dynamic event-triggered impulsive control(DETIC) strategy. Firstly, ensure that the internal dynamic variables in the proposed control methodology can effectively eliminate Zeno phenomenon. At the same time, the impulsive controller is designed to take into account situations where attackers inject false information. Secondly, under the proposed dynamic ETIC strategy, sufficient conditions and error upper bounds are given for the master-slave system to achieve quasi-synchronization. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed strategy was validated by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Quality Prediction in Copper Flotation Process Based on SDGRU
abstract: Copper flotation plays a vital role in the extraction of non-ferrous metals. With the increasing demand for metals such as copper, the prediction of quality has become crucially urgent. It can help us identify potential quality issues in advance, reduce defective products and production costs, and ensure that products meet standards and market demands. However, in achieving effective quality prediction, the temporal dynamics and nonlinear characteristics of complex industrial processes must be fully considered. In recent times, the gated recurrent unit (GRU) has emerged as a powerful tool for extracting long-term features. While it primarily emphasizes the link between input time series and output, the focus in industrial processes lies in understanding the intricate dynamics of process variables and their influence on key quality metrics. To address the prediction of quality variables in the flotation process, a new quality prediction method called supervised differential gated recurrent unit (SDGRU) is proposed in this study, where differential input and quality variables are introduced to establish a new network unit, aiming to improve predictive performance. The feasibility and excellence of the proposed method is verified by comparing the prediction of copper grade indexes in the flotation process with other commonly used methods.

articleTitle: SLAM Algorithm Based on Heterogeneous Sensor Data Fusion
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM), as a key technology, has attracted widespread attention. However, laser-based SLAM technology suffers from significant drift issues. A heterogeneous sensor data fusion algorithm aimed at improving the performance of SLAM is proposed in this paper. First, data from laser radar and the Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) is collected. Then, the Cartographer algorithm itself employs the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) method to fuse the data from both sources, ultimately constructing a 2D SLAM framework for environmental mapping. Laser radar data and IMU data from three different experimental scenarios are collected, and the mentioned algorithm is utilized to fuse the data for map construction. The error between the constructed map and the real map is compared, demonstrating that the heterogeneous sensor data fusion-based SLAM algorithm in this paper outperforms single lidar Cartographer. It overcame the issue of rotational drift and exhibited promising application potential.

articleTitle: Conservatism-Relaxed Disturbance Observer-based Composite Control for Wheeled Mobile Robots Subject to Abrupt Disturbance
abstract: This paper investigates the robust and accurate control problem of wheeled mobile robot (WMR) systems with uncertain disturbance, especially exhibits abrupt changes. To end this, a conservatism-relaxed disturbance observer (CRDOB)-based sliding-mode controller is proposed under a composite control structure. To address the uncertainties of the abrupt disturbance, a CRDOB is designed without requiring any assumptions about disturbance boundary information. With aiding from a continuous gain-switching mechanism with reducing chattering of the SMC, a composite controller is developed to compensate for the residual-disturbance estimation error of the CRDOB, and then avoid large errors when disturbances instantaneous change. Simulations and experiments demonstrate the improvement of the tracking control performance and system robustness.

articleTitle: A self-recognition and removal system of ocular artifacts based on FastICA
abstract: Ocular artifact (OA) is a common interference in electroencephalogram (EEG) processing. Due to the aliasing of the frequency bands of the two signals, the self-recognition and correction of OA are difficult. Therefore, this paper proposes a FastICA-K-means-CEEMDAN-WTD model based on fast independent component analysis and k-means cluster recognition artifacts, combined with full set empirical mode decomposition and wavelet threshold denoising, which can complete OA self-recognition correction for multi-channel EEG data. Compared with some OA denoising models based on Independent component analysis (ICA) , this model has the following advantages: 1. It can realize self-recognition without a lot of prior knowledge. 2. No pre-training is required. 3. It does not need to add additional ophthalmic electrical signals as a reference. 4. It can prevent the loss of EEG signals to the greatest extent. Based on the above method, the recognition and processing of the motion imagination EEG signal collected in the laboratory can obtain 94.79% accuracy.

articleTitle: Fixed-time rotating consensus control for multi-agent systems
abstract: This paper investigates the fixed-time rotating consensus (FRC) problem for the leaderless multi-agent systems subject to the external time-varying disturbances. The communication topology among agents is described by a strongly connected directed graph. Firstly, a distributed controller is proposed to drive the agents such that they achieve the rotating consensus within a fixed time irrelevant to the initial conditions. An integral sliding mode control technique is then utilized to compensate the time-varying disturbances. Finally, simulation results are given to illustrate the performance of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: 3D Point Cloud Registration Method Based on Deep and Shallow Features Combined with Attention Enhancement
abstract: Most deep learning-based rigid registration methods of 3D point clouds cannot achieve high accuracy in the case of noise and partial overlap. Therefore, a point cloud registration network based on deep and shallow features combined with attention enhancement is proposed. Firstly, the deep and shallow features extraction module with rich local geometry provides point cloud features. Secondly, the attention enhancement module selectively enhances or suppresses the features. Thirdly, the constraint parameters prediction module adaptively matches the source and target point clouds in a learning way to obtain the association constraint parameters. Fourthly, the feature matrix matching module integrates the features, constraint parameters and target point cloud to obtain the predicted result. Finally, the singular value decomposition module obtains the accurate translation vector and rotation matrix. Experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively enhance the registration accuracy of partial point clouds, and it is insensitive to noise and outliers as well.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation and parameter optimization of downhole stratified flow measurement with CO2 injection
abstract: The density and viscosity of supercritical CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> are obviously affected by wellbore temperature and pressure. In order to provide the accuracy of downhole stratified injection CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> flow measurement, this paper constructs the downhole CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> flow metering nozzle model, first calculates the wellbore temperature and pressure field to obtain CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> density, phase state and other parameters, and then uses Fluent to simulate the relationship between differential pressure and injection pressure under different temperature and pressure to get the flow metering model. At the same time, in order to improve the pressure accuracy of the nozzle, the parameters of the pressure port position are optimized to obtain the best pressure outlet position. The results show that when the wellhead injection pressure increases to a certain extent, the injection pressure has little effect on the differential pressure, mainly because the density of supercritical CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> no longer changes greatly with the increase of injection pressure, which provides a reference for the wellhead injection pressure of downhole stratified injection CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The existing nozzle Flowmeter structure can meet the requirements of pressure extraction position for downhole CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> measurement. This study has certain practical significance for improving the test performance of nozzle Flowmeter and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layered measurement and control.

articleTitle: Underactuated USV Path Following Control Approach for Inland River Search and Rescue
abstract: With the increasing importance and complexity of searching mission in inland river, it is a current research hot topic to require underactuated Unmanned Surface Vehicle (USV) to offset the large drift angle caused by the harsh environment, so as to accurately and efficiently arrive at the accident site to search and rescue people who fell into the water. In response to the problem, this article designs a Line-of-sight (LOS) guidance method based on the Extended State Observer (ESO) to accurately estimate the time-varying large sideslip angle, consequently, achieving the desired heading angle. Taking into account the presence of unknown time-varying disturbances and dynamic uncertainties, this paper introduces an estimator to improve the Radial Basis Function (RBF) neural network and designs an adaptive path-following controller. By employing a Radial basis function neural network that utilizes estimator-based error estimation, the approximation of unknown terms in the model is achieved, resulting in enhanced transient performance and robustness of the controller. Ultimately, the effectiveness and robustness of the algorithm are validated through stability analysis and comparative simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Research on Aerial Photography Target Detection Methods
abstract: Aerial target detection is a detection technology that uses an aerial platform equipped with visual sensors and deep learning technology to autonomously identify and locate ground targets. This technology has been widely used in fields such as environmental monitoring, road traffic management, safety inspections, and epidemic control. In recent years, one-stage target detection technology has shown excellent speed advantages and has made significant progress in real-time detection. In that sense, the YOLO (You Only Look Once) series become the most classic single-stage object detector, have developed to the eighth version, which is called "YOLOv8". In our study, YOLOv8 is used as the baseline model to solve the challenges from aerial images. To make the YOLOv8 model better adapt to the current scenario, we introduce EIoU_Loss and SoftNMS mechanisms. The introduction of these technologies improves the accuracy of YOLOv8 in target detection. Our study found that EIOU_Loss can reflect the difference between target scale and confidence, so it has a better performance in vehicle detection. The SoftNMS mechanism has better performance in dealing with occlusion problems. On the other hand, we also use Automatic Color Enhancement defogging technology to deal with foggy scenes during the detection process. We conducted rigorous experimental verification of the model enhancement and defogging methods on the UAVDT dataset and VisDrone dataset. The results show that the introduction of these technologies improves the performance while ensuring the real-time performance of the detection model.

articleTitle: Robust Group Formation Tracking Control for Nonlinear Multiagent Systems
abstract: The issue of time-varying group formation tracking control for heterogeneous nonlinear multiagent systems (MASs) with unknown dynamics is studied in the framework of high-order fully actuated system approaches. To achieve the desired group formation tracking, a distributed robust control protocol is designed. The protocol consists of two components: The first is that the nonlinearities of MASs are eliminated by state feedback and the poles are configured in the light of performance requirements; the second is that robust control strategy is employed to compensate for uncertainties. Based on Lyapunov stability theory, the sufficient condition to achieve group formation tracking under the proposed control protocol is provided and proved. Simulation result illustrates the effectiveness of the theoretical result.

articleTitle: Visual-Inertial SLAM Technology Based on Monocular Infrared Camera
abstract: Traditional visual-inertial odometry based on visible light cameras experiences significant visual degradation in complex lighting environments, posing significant challenges for the practical application of SLAM systems. Thermal infrared cameras are less affected by changes in lighting conditions and can operate around the clock. However, due to issues such as weak textures, low contrast, and low signal-to-noise ratio in infrared images, existing SLAM methods are not directly compatible with thermal infrared cameras. Edge features exhibit minimal performance degradation in infrared images. To address these challenges, we propose an infrared visual-inertial SLAM method based on point and line features. This method employs techniques such as bilateral filtering, stripe noise filtering, and adaptive histogram equalization to enhance image contrast and filter noise, overcoming the issues associated with poor-quality infrared images. Subsequently, an improved feature extraction method is employed to extract point and line features and track them. Finally, real-time state estimation is achieved by nonlinear optimization that minimizes reprojection errors over a sliding window.

articleTitle: Bipartite Secure Consensus Control for Nonlinear Multi-agent Systems
abstract: This paper addresses the leaderless bipartite secure consensus problem for a class of discrete-time nonlinear multi-agent systems (MASs) with encryption-decryption algorithms (EDAs). Initially, the interaction dynamics between agents are portrayed through a signed digraph topology, wherein the edges encompass positive and negative connection weights. Subsequently, communication between agents and their neighbors is facilitated by employing EDAs. This method ensures that the agents’ original states are securely encrypted at each time instant, thus forestalling any potential data theft. At the same time, EDAs are used to recover the encrypted neighbor state information. Building upon the EDAs, a novel controller design methodology is proposed. This approach incorporates the encryption state of neighbors and the local agent’s actual status into the design methodology of the controller, aimed at achieving the desired bipartite secure consensus. Finally, the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed scheme are illustrated through a simulation example conducted in a framework of signed networks.

articleTitle: Construction and Analysis of a Simulated Lunar Surface Image Dataset for Lunar Rock Detection
abstract: Lunar rovers are effective long-range scouting tools for future lunar missions. However, unknown complex environments and randomly scattered rocks could impede rover navigation and safety. Accurate obstacle detection is essential for identifying hazards and intelligent path planning. Research progress is partly hindered by limited public lunar image dataset. To facilitate rock detection for lunar rovers, we construct a lunar-like surface image dataset using selective field image collection and annotation with a Segment Anything Model (SAM) assisted labeling tool. The dataset contains 659 images, split into training, validation and testing subsets. The experimental results demonstrated that the YOLOV5 and YOLOV5 object detection network models with attention mechanisms achieved the highest Precision of 0.878 and mAP of 0.783 when tested on this lunar surface dataset. The dataset provides a testbed to develop and evaluate rock perception algorithms, advancing lunar rover autonomy and hazard avoidance capabilities.

articleTitle: Modeling and Dynamic Locomotion of a Quadruped Robot with Spinal
abstract: The spine plays an important role in the high-speed gait of quadrupeds. In this paper, the Lagrange equation method is used to derive the local dynamics based on the parallel spine mechanism and the simplified overall dynamics of the spinal quadruped robot, then the mathematical models are verified in the simulation environment. Based on the dynamic analysis, the Model Predictive Control (MPC) is used to find the ground reaction force and the driving force of the spine, then joint torques of the quadruped robot are computed through force-position space mapping. Unlike existing spine type quadruped robots based on the principle of spring loaded inverted pendulum control (SLIP), the control framework proposed in this paper achieves accurate trajectory tracking. The control scheme achieved trot gait with a forward speed of 0.2m/s in the ADAMS simulation environment on the designed parallel spinal quadruped robot, accompanied by periodic movements of the body pitch and spinal extension and bending.

articleTitle: UAV Maritime Target Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv7
