abstract: On sunny days, due to the different flight heights and shooting angles of the UAV on the sea, there may be solar flares projected on the sea surface and mutual blocking targets in the aerial image, which may seriously interfere with the detection process. To solve the above problems, this paper proposes an unmanned aerial vehicle(UAV) maritime target detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv7. First, the YOLOv7 header network is improved by adding Coordinate Convolution modules and replacing Repconvolutions with Coordinate Convolutions to enhance the spatial awareness of the network. Secondly, the Convolution Block Attention Module(CBAM) is added into the feature extraction framework of YOLOv7 to improve the detection accuracy of small targets by enhancing the ability to extract the feature information of small targets. Finally, the NWD Loss Function is used to optimize the similarity of overlapping small targets. In this paper, the SeaDronesee dataset is used for testing. The experimental results show that the improved model can effectively improve the detection results of small targets, and the mAP value is 93.4 percent, which is 6.7 percent higher than that of the baseline method, and the effect is better than the mainstream algorithms such as SSD and YOLO series.

articleTitle: State Estimation for Markov Jump Systems with Nonlinearity and observation delay*
abstract: This paper is concerned with the state estimation of discrete-time nonlinear Markov jump systems with observation delays. By introducing a set of equivalent delay-free observations and defining a reorganized Markov chain, the estimation of delayed nonlinear systems is reduced to the one of delay-free Markov jump nonlinear systems. A minimum mean square error estimator is designed by minimizing the upper bound of the estimation error covariance matrix, where the upper bound of the error covariance matrix is determined by a set of auxiliary constant parameters. The filter gains are given in terms of a set of generalized coupled difference Riccati equations.

articleTitle: Research on oil field injection wells coupled flow simulation of wellbore-flow Controller-stratum and cooperative regulation model
abstract: Layered water injection process is a key means to improve the effect of refined water injection development. At present, the regulation of injection wells predominantly depend on manual experience and exploratory measurement and adjustment by instrumentation, which leads to time-consuming and wasteful deployment of several layers and a low rate of injection qualification. This paper presents a simulation model for layered injection wellbore-Flow Controller-stratum coupled flow, utilizing the principles of energy conservation and material balance criterion. The model provides a solution method for determining the injection volume of multiple layers, employing the Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) algorithm. Additionally, an optimization method based on the genetic algorithm (GA) is proposed, aiming to minimize injection error and wellhead pressure. Taking the X-01 well of 4-layer section as an example, the optimization decision process of the blending plan with the lowest cumulative injection error under different injection pressure requirements is simulated, and the global optimization performance of genetic algorithm (GA) and particle swarm (PSO) is compared and analyzed. The study shows that the model and method in this paper have high computational accuracy, strong global optimization ability, strong adaptability of the formulated regulation scheme, and little cumulative injection error, which provides a scientific decision-making method and excellent analytical tool for the formulation of refined regulation scheme for sub-injection wells, and it has good theoretical and practical value for the promotion of refined development of the oilfield.

articleTitle: Simulation of Moving Target Propeller Active Sonar Echo Signal Based on Underwater Acoustic Micro-Doppler Effect
abstract: Addressing the challenge of simulating target echo signals for active sonar in deep-sea environments, this paper proposes a method based on the underwater acoustic micro-Doppler effect for simulating propeller echo signals of moving targets. Initially, the BELLHOP ray acoustic model is employed to compute the target signal’s intrinsic ray, amplitude, phase, and delay information, thereby constructing the underwater propagation channel for the simulated sonar signal and adding noise. Subsequently, micro-Doppler feature detection technology from radar is adapted and applied to active sonar echo signal simulation, considering underwater acoustic characteristics. This approach enables micro-Doppler feature modeling of underwater target propellers to capture propeller-specific echo signals. The MATLAB simulation platform generates a Linear Frequency Modulation (LFM) detection signal, which, when transmitted through the underwater acoustic channel, forms an echo signal with micro-Doppler traits. This signal then reaches the hydrophone’s receiving range through the return channel, realizing micro-Doppler characteristic signal simulation for active sonar detection of moving targets. The simulation results indicate that, in deep-sea high-frequency active sonar scenarios, the proposed method significantly enhances the target signal characteristics within the echo signal compared to traditional methods, yielding a simulation closer to real sea trial received signals.

articleTitle: Second-Order Consensus for Heterogeneous Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems with Actuator Faults and External Disturbances
abstract: This paper investigates the second-order consensus for multi-agent systems (MASs) with nonidentical nonlinearities and bounded external disturbances under actuator fault condition. By combining a healthy control protocol and fault severity estimation, an active fault-tolerant method for solving the MASs’ consensus problem under actuator fault condition is developed. If the algebraic connectivity meets the requirement and the fault severity estimation error is less than the computed threshold, the fault-tolerant consensus can be achieved. Finally, the time-delayed Chua’s oscillator is employed in the simulation to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed control protocols.

articleTitle: Multi-robot path planning for persistent monitoring based on mode frequency optimization
abstract: Multi-robot systems have demonstrated significant advantages in various applications such as ground surveillance, environmental monitoring and patrolling of critical areas. However, in multi-robot collaboration, the periodicity of patrol paths can easily lead to leakage of patrol patterns. Therefore, it is particularly important to increase the randomness of robot patrol paths. To solve this problem, this study establishes a multi-robot path planning model based on the access period using the node mode frequency as an indicator to ensure the privacy and security of the path information during the patrol process. Through multiple simulations on the real road network, a highly secure multi-robot patrol path was successfully obtained. Compared with the genetic algorithm, the sparrow search algorithm is shown to have faster search speed and solution efficiency.

articleTitle: Near-real-time carbon measurement modeling for hydrogen production through hydrocarbon steam reforming
abstract: With the dual-carbon strategy, more accurate real-time carbon emissions data is required for hydrogen production companies. However, current carbon measurement methods of the hydrogen production process lack accuracy and timeliness. In this paper, we propose a near-real-time carbon measurement modeling for hydrogen production through hydrocarbon steam reforming. Considering the high fluctuation of raw materials in the actual process, the existing methods are limited to accurate carbon emissions. We construct computational models of process emissions and partial combustion emissions using Pressure Swing Adsorption (PSA) tail gas data. Moreover, CH4 emission is usually ignored in the HSR hydrogen production process. Therefore, we introduced a fugitive emission factor for the calculation of fugitive emissions through the material balance approach based on life cycle assessment. In addition, in order to analyse the key factors affecting the carbon emissions of the HSR process, we use sensitivity analysis methods to find critical variables. The results show that carbon emissions mainly come from process emissions and PSA tail gas combustion emissions, which are mainly influenced by tail gas composition and flow rate. The measurement model can provide a theoretical basis for the real-time carbon monitoring system of HSR hydrogen production and promote the low-carbon operation of related enterprises.

articleTitle: Optimization strategy of automatic generation control in frequency regulation market based on improved particle swarm optimization algorithm
abstract: Frequency stability is the most important prerequisite for the safe operation of the power grid. To ensure the safe and stable operation of all kinds of power equipment in the power supply system. The frequency of the power supply system must be maintained within a reasonable range. In this paper, a simulation study on the frequency modulation performance of the combined automatic generation control system based on the improved particle swarm optimization is proposed, and the bidding constraints of the energy storage market are introduced. In the aspect of regulation strategy, the thermal power unit is mainly responsible for the low frequency command, and the energy storage system is responsible for the high frequency command. The real-time management of state of charge can not only improve the performance index of frequency modulation, but also ensure the efficient and stable operation of energy storage system. The operation strategy of energy storage power station to participate in the market in real time. The influence of different types of disturbances and the demand of intraday frequency modulation market are also fully considered. Through the above methods, the frequency modulation performance index can be improved, the wear degree of thermal power units can be reduced, and the reliability of operation can be improved.

articleTitle: Research method on dynamic threshold of water environment risk driven by time series data
abstract: The determination of early warning levels and scientific research on water quality thresholds play an important role in the establishment of risk early warning systems for surface water pollution. However, due to the shortcomings of the current water quality threshold setting, such as single and static properties, it cannot be dynamically adjusted for special situations. Therefore, this paper proposes a dynamic threshold prediction method. First, through the historical data of water environment monitoring, the maximum value sequence data and minimum value sequence data of various monitoring stations are obtained, and a large amount of historical water quality monitoring data is obtained. At the same time, water level data from adjacent monitoring stations and water quality monitoring data are integrated. The proposed GCN-GRU model is used, in which the GCN part is used to learn the spatial characteristics between different monitoring points, and the GRU is used to learn the temporal characteristics of water quality data. Through accurate prediction of maximum value sequence data and minimum value sequence data, dynamic research on water environment risk thresholds is achieved, and comparisons are made with other time series methods. The results show that this method can provide more potential information based on water environment conditions and dynamically adjust the range of thresholds, thereby providing a scientific basis for river basin risk early warning.

articleTitle: Output Feedback Control of Safety-Critical Systems with Continuous Twisting Algorithm
abstract: Achieving an optimal balance among safety, performance and robustness is crucial for effective control of real-world systems. This paper presents output feedback controllers that leverage the continuous twisting algorithm (CTA), augmented with state observers employing second-order robust exact differentiators (RED) to yield output feedback (CTA-2RED). A safety-critical control framework is formulated utilizing control barrier functions (CBF) to safeguard the system states. The proposed controllers are manipulated via quadratic programming optimization. By filtering the control output of CTA-2RED via CBF, the system attains high performance while providing rigorous safety guarantees. The effectiveness of the proposed approach in ensuring both safety and performance is demonstrated through its application to a vehicle tracking problem in platoons of intelligent connected vehicles. Simulation results indicate that the CTA-2RED controller proficiently mitigates unmodeled disturbances within the vehicle’s actuation system, while the CBFs provide robust safety assurances for the vehicle.

articleTitle: Adaptive Sliding Mode Trajectory Tracking Control for a Dual-jet UAV with Time-varying Mass
abstract: This paper studies a class of unmanned aerial vehicle (DJUAV) with dual-jet as vector thrust system, and presents an adaptive trajectory tracking control scheme under the condition of time-varying mass. The proposed controller is divided into two sub-controllers, namely attitude and position controllers. Each controller adopts backstepping sliding mode control, and adaptive laws are designed to estimate the uncertain part of the system. In this work, a non-simplified six-degree-of-freedom UAV model is first established in the case of time-varying mass. Afterward, an adaptive sliding mode controller is designed to ensure that the system can track the desired trajectory in the face of the model uncertainty caused by its own time-varying mass. Lyapunov stability analysis ensures that the tracking error asymptotically convergent to zero. Numerical simulation demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed control algorithm.

articleTitle: CO2 Emission Prediction Method in MSWI Process Based on LSTM Compensated With ARIMA
abstract: Municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) processes emit the greenhouse gas carbon dioxide (CO2), contributing to global atmospheric warming. In order to achieve the dual carbon goal and protect the ecological environment, it is imperative to predict CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission concentrations and implement proactive control measures. Addressing these concerns, this study introduces a CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission prediction model for the MSWI process based on the LSTM-compensated ARIMA model. Initially, the ARIMA model serves as the primary predictor for CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions and calculates its prediction residuals. Subsequently, the LSTM model functions as a compensatory model, utilizing the predicted residuals as input truth values for constructing predictions. Finally, the predicted values from the primary and compensatory models are weighted and combined to yield the ultimate result. Experimental results, conducted using data from an MSWI plant in Beijing, demonstrate the efficacy of this approach.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Extended State Observer-based Finite-time Tracking Control for a Cross-media Vehicle
abstract: A fuzzy extended state observer-based finite-time cross-media tracking control approach is presented for a slender body cross-media vehicle(SBCMV) in the presence of unknown hydrodynamics and external disturbances. A novel fuzzy extended state observer, capable of intelligently adjusting the bandwidth to obtain excellent observation performance, is developed not only to estimate the vehicle’s velocity but also to handle the lumped disturbance of the system. Then the finite-time output feedback control scheme is developed by means of the presented observer and backstepping technique. The proposed control method does not suffer from the singularity problem in the traditional finite-time backstepping and is able to make all states of the SBCMV converge in a finite time without velocity measurement. The superiority of our work is manifested in the simulations.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Pore Morphology Prediction: Multi-Ghost Encoder Generative Network
abstract: Metal additive manufacturing technology is widely used in aerospace, defense and industrial manufacturing due to its utilization rate, customizable processing of complex structural parts and other advantages. However, due to its specific manufacturing process, there are still many quality problems in the products, especially in the repeatability and reliability of the deficiencies, seriously restricting its large-scale industrial production and application, of which pore defects for the most common defects, so there is an urgent need to develop quality control technology to improve the quality of additive manufacturing. In this paper, the complex correlation and intrinsic mechanism between pore morphology and various processing parameters in metal additive manufacturing process are deeply studied and analyzed. By proposing a multi-ghost encoder generative network, we aim to solve the problem of pore morphology prediction in the laser powder bed fusion process. An exhaustive pore morphology image dataset covering key processing parameters is used for the experiments. During the experiments we compare the performance of our method with existing methods in terms of porosity reconstruction, prediction accuracy and computational efficiency. Our method is effective in predicting and reconstructing different pore morphologies and is improved in terms of the number of parameters and training efficiency because of the Ghost module structure. The results of this study not only provide new perspectives on porosity control in metal additive manufacturing processes, but also open up new possibilities for deep learning applications in manufacturing.

articleTitle: Research on electromagnetic active damping control of permanent magnet electric suspension system
abstract: In order to solve the problem of under-damping of the permanent magnet electric levitation system, a scheme to add electromagnetic active control on the basis of permanent magnet electric levitation was proposed, which solved the problem of insufficient suspension stability of the system and was verified by experiments. In order to solve the problem of the poor disturbance suppression ability of the controller, an online optimization control algorithm for the permanent magnet electric and electromagnetic hybrid suspension system was proposed to further improve the anti-disturbance ability of the system. Firstly, the mapping relationship between the transient levitation force and the electromagnetic parameters and structural parameters of the permanent magnet electric suspension system is clarified, the expressions of the damping and damping coefficients of the permanent magnet electric suspension system are derived, and the problem of insufficient stability of the electric suspension system is pointed out. Secondly, the electromagnetic active control scheme is proposed to improve the stability of the system, and the controller is designed and verified by experiments on the basis of the permanent magnet electric and electromagnetic hybrid levitation model.

articleTitle: Adaptive prescribed performance neural control of flexible-joint manipulators with unmodeled dynamics and output constraints
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive neural control strategy for flexible-joint manipulator systems with unmodeled dynamics, output constraints and error compensation mechanism. By using time-varying barrier Lyapunov function, the tracking errors are constrained within a time-varying boundary. Through pre-setting the parameters of the time-varying boundary function, the steady-state and transient performance of the system can be guaranteed. The command filtered backstepping with compensation mechanism is used to ensure the trajectory tracking accuracy. Radial basis function neural network is utilized to approximate the unknown nonlinear functions. The uncertainties caused by unmodeled dynamics are dealt with a first-order dynamic signal. Furthermore, all signals in the closed-loop system are proved to be semi-globally uniformly ultimately bounded, and tracking errors can be retained within a prescribed bound. A simulation example demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Left Equivariant Filter with Autonomous Error Dynamics for Inertial Integrated Navigation Systems with Biases
abstract: A left equivariant filter to biased inertial integrated navigation system is proposed. The geometric property of the kinematics of inertial integrated navigation system has been leveraged to design filters with better property. The equivariant property has played a key role in the filter design of the kinematic systems on Lie groups. However, there are few works have considered the biases of the low cost inertial measurement unit (IMU) as they are difficult to be embraced into the kinematics on the Lie group. The recent equivariant filter provides a fully geometric Extended Kalman Filter (EKF)-like for a inertial navigation system including bias state, where a symmetry group defined by exploiting the semi-direct product structure is the key to the successful equivariant property. But, the resulting filter still involves the navigation state via the bias and is only suitable for relative measurement such as visual odometry. In this paper, we proposed a novel equivariant filter for biased inertial integrated navigation incorporating global measurement. The equivariance of the biased inertial integrated navigation system is substantiated by exploiting a novel direct product symmetry and the associated left group action. The resulting filter is also a fully geometric framework and leads to a autonomous error dynamics which is better than previous. The performance of the proposed filter is evaluated with field experiments of global navigation satellite system/ inertial navigation system, and demonstrates increased robustness to a wide range of erroneous initial conditions, and improved accuracy when compared with the other EKF-like approaches.

articleTitle: 3D Object Detection for Autonomous Driving: A Survey
abstract: In recent years, autonomous driving has attracted significant attention. 3D object detection is a crucial component of autonomous driving systems, because it provides essential information for downstream tasks such as target tracking, path planning, and obstacle avoidance. So, it is meaningful to review existing 3D object detection methods and highlight their strengths and limitations. LiDAR and camera sensors are commonly used by autonomous vehicles to collect point clouds and images. Based on the type of sensors used, we roughly categorize 3D object detection methods into three classes: LiDAR-only method, Camera-only method and LiDAR-Camera fusion method. In this review, we further categorize each class into several subtypes, and describe the core ideas of the methods in each subtype. Furthermore, this paper critically evaluates their strengths and limitations. Finally, by using public datasets, a comparative performance analysis of the methods is conducted.

articleTitle: Robot Navigation in Human-Robot Shared Environments Based on Social Interaction Model
abstract: Robot navigation in a dynamic environment shared with humans is a challenging task. Robot needs to process surrounding environmental data in real time and respond quickly. However, as the number of humans increases, the robot’s sensors recognize more obstacles, and the amount of information that the navigation algorithm needs to process also increases, resulting in a decrease in the performance of robot navigation. To solve this problem, we propose a robot navigation algorithm for crowd environments. This algorithm employs a model-based deep reinforcement learning approach as the underlying framework and utilizes graph convolutional networks to encode high-order interactions between people and robot as the state input for the deep reinforcement learning algorithm. We integrate multi-head attention mechanism into the graph convolutional network to assign weights to graph network nodes that are more in line with social behavior norms, and we also introduce a gating mechanism into the model to make it more lightweight. The incorporation of these mechanisms can significantly enhance the navigation performance of robot in dense crowds. We evaluated our method based on advanced crowd navigation baseline algorithms and confirmed its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control Based on Fractional Order Extended State Observer And Improved Grey Prediction
abstract: A Fractional Order Model Predictive Control (FOMPC) algorithm based on disturbance estimation and prediction is proposed. Disturbance in practical engineering can to some extent limit the performance of the model predictive controller. In order to overcome this limitation, this paper presents a FOMPC with a fractional order extended state observer (FOESO) and grey prediction method. Firstly, FOESO is designed to estimate disturbances in the system, and its convergence for disturbance observation is analyzed using frequency domain analysis. Then, a grey prediction model based on multi-cycle time series is used to predict the disturbances, and the predicted disturbance sequence is applied to the predictive model to improve prediction accuracy and further eliminate the influence of disturbances. Finally, the performance of the proposed FOMPC control algorithm is evaluated through a simulation example.

articleTitle: A Logistics Supplier Combination Decision Method Based on Hesitation Fuzzy BWM-TOPSIS
abstract: In the process of selecting logistics suppliers, a single logistics form is increasingly insufficient to meet the demands, necessitating the consideration of various forms of logistics in combination. To address the decision-making problem of logistics supplier combinations in uncertain environments, this paper proposes a robust decision-making method based on hesitant fuzzy BWM-TOPSIS. Firstly, experts utilize interval hesitant fuzzy values to construct a decision matrix. Subsequently, based on the Best Worst Method (Best Worst Method, BWM), the weights of attributes are determined, and the scores of solution attributes are calculated through an interval hesitant fuzzy aggregation operator. Then, drawing on the principles of the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to an Ideal Solution (Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to an Ideal Solution, TOPSIS), the distances between each equipment and the positive and negative ideal solutions are computed as inputs for the multi-objective optimization model. Finally, a robust optimization method is employed to solve the linear multi-objective programming problem. A case study is conducted on the logistics supplier combination decision problem of a certain enterprise, validating the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Bi-Level Optimal Control Based on Similarity Clustering for Wastewater Treatment Process with Greenhouse Gas Emissions
abstract: There is a global consensus on reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions to slow down global warming. GHG emissions from the wastewater treatment process (WWTP) have also received extensive attention. Therefore, how to reduce GHG emissions without increasing the operating cost and ensuring water quality standards for WWTP is a challenging problem. To cope with the issue, a bi-level optimal control strategy based on similarity clustering (BLOC-SC) for WWTP with GHG emissions is proposed. First, a bi-level optimization (BLO) model for WWTP is established based on the key process variables. Then, the model can describe the relationship among water quality, operating costs, and GHG emissions. Second, a multi-task optimization algorithm, based on similarity clustering, is designed to solve the BLO problem. Then, the algorithm can save computing resources and quickly solve the BLO problem to obtain the optimal set values for WWTP. Third, a fuzzy neural network controller is proposed to achieve accurate tracking of optimal set values. Finally, the simulation results, based on benchmark simulation model 2-GHG, indicate that BLOC-SC can achieve energy saving and emission reduction in WWTP.

articleTitle: Multi-commodity Flow Optimization Algorithm Among Multiple Communication Protocols
abstract: The effective traffic distributed solution is important to solve the dynamic network congestion problem. In this paper, we concentrate on the optimization problem of distributing traffic among multiple communication protocols in a network. The optimization objective is to minimize the maximum link utilization in the network to ensure network traffic balance. To solve the k-protocol multi-commodity network flow (k-MCF) problem, we propose a K-Protocol Network Flow Optimization (KPFNO) algorithm. In KPFNO, we apply the levy flight and elimination mechanism of the Cuckoo Search (CS) algorithm to search candidate solutions first. Then try to improve search efficiency through the designed adaptive neighborhood operators. In addition, we design the repair operator to avoid the waste of rational solution space. We provide experimental results and comparisons to show the advance and competitiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Unified Strategy for UAV Blade Fault Diagnosis Using Khan Observer and CNN Network
abstract: This paper presents a fault diagnosis algorithm for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) systems characterized by nonlinear terms and disturbances. The proposed method integrates the Khan intermediate observer and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), enabling the estimation of both the UAV blade state and the simultaneous estimation of sensor faults and disturbances. To induce fault conditions, two plastic strips were strategically applied to the upper surface of the blade, significantly altering its aerodynamics and thereby expanding the scope of the original system. The algorithm employs an intermediate variable to design an observer for the augmented system, providing a comprehensive view for the tester. This allows for the estimation of system states, faults, and perturbations. The Convolutional Neural Network serves as the residual generator, generating virtual residual signals. Furthermore, a proportional-integral action is introduced to estimate UAV blade faults. Simulation results on a quadrotor UAV system validate the efficacy of the proposed method in accurately estimating blade faults and disturbances.

articleTitle: Ultra-local model Predictive Current Control of phase-shifted full-bridge Based on Kalman Filter
abstract: The paper proposes an ultra-local model predictive current control strategy to improve the stability and robustness of the phase-shifted full-bridge(PSFB) converter under parameter mismatch causing by operating conditions changes. Firstly, analysis is conducted to show the effect of circuit parameter mismatch on the anticipated current estimate in the PSFB converter circuit. Secondly, an ultra-local model is built for the PSFB converter by analyzing the total disturbance of the circuit. Ultimately, the unknown nonlinear total disturbance part of the model is estimated using a Kalman filter, which is then integrate in model predictive control algorithm to enhance the control effect. The experiments on a semi-physical simulation platform demonstrate that the proposed strategy effectively suppresses the steady-state error caused by parameter mismatch when compared to the conventional predictive current control scheme. It increases system resilience and anti-disturbance capabilities in the event of parameter disturbances, as well as its capacity to adapt efficiently to changes in working conditions.

articleTitle: Interpretability Analysis and Transferability Evaluation of Domain-Adversarial Regression Adaptation Model based on Tensor Representation*
abstract: In recent years, deep transfer learning technology has been introduced to solve online remaining useful life (RUL) of rotating machinery under unknown working conditions. However, the self-driven prediction of online sequentially arrived data lacks sufficient model explanation and lack of credibility. To solve these problems, a tensor domain adversative regression prediction method is proposed with adaptive knowledge transfer. First, the tensor Tucker decomposition was used to find the key features in RUL transfer prediction, and the interpretability was analyzed at the geometric level. Then, the weighting mechanism was constructed, which was jointly optimized with tensor domain-adversarial training to achieve online RUL transfer prediction. Second, the degradation trend information was extracted based on core tensor. And the multi-scale evaluation criteria of transferability were established by combining the time series information measurement at different levels, in order to clarify the contribution and rationality of offline data and online data and provide an intuitive migration understanding. Finally, this paper takes rolling bearing as an example, and runs experiments on IEEE PHM Challenge 2012 and XJTU-SY datasets, respectively, and the experimental results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Early Multi-fault Diagnosis of Lithium Battery Under Dynamic Working Condition
abstract: The frequent occurrence of battery pack failures brings a great threat to the development of electric vehicles. Battery pack faults are generally multiple and diverse and have similar fault characteristics, which are difficult to distinguish and detect, and are not conducive to fault diagnosis and classification. Therefore, this paper proposes a new sensor connection topology to distinguish the types of faults within a battery pack, such as connection faults, sensor faults, and cell short-circuit faults. In particular, for connection faults, the topology proposed in this paper can more accurately locate the specific point of the connection fault. In addition, due to the large inconsistency of the battery pack data, and the fault features inside the battery are very tiny in the pre-fault period. To address this problem, this paper proposes a battery feature extraction method based on the autocorrelation coefficient, which can effectively avoid the problem of battery inconsistency and amplify the fault features. Finally, for the automatic identification of faulty cells, this paper proposes a fault value calculation method based on Kullback-Leibler (KL) dispersion, which can effectively identify faulty cells. The method validates the performance of multiple fault detection under UDDS operating data, and the results show that the method proposed in this paper can effectively detect and differentiate multiple faults in battery packs.

articleTitle: Navigation radar image fusion of different scales based on improved wavelet transform rules
abstract: Due to the disadvantages of the image fusion system such as unclear target contour of long-range radar image, insufficient perceptual range of near-range radar image and insufficient detail of traditional wavelet transform fusion rules for processing high frequency coefficients, the fused images cannot meet the requirements of large information volume, high definition and small discrepancy. To solve this problem, the maximum Brenner region energy wavelet transform image fusion (MBREWTIF) algorithm is proposed, Firstly, the alignment of the two radar images is realized to prepare for the next step of algorithmic fusion. Secondly, an improved fusion rule for high frequency coefficients is devised based on the wavelet transform image fusion algorithm. Finally, the Brenner region energy method is developed by combining the energy gradient of the Brenner function method and the improved fusion weight in the region energy method. The simulation results verify that the proposed MBREWTIF algorithm improves the content and clarity of image information and reduces the discrepancy in the dual radar fusion process compared with other existing algorithms.

Author Keywords: the maximum Brenner region energy wavelet transform image fusion

articleTitle: Prediction of remaining useful life of lithium batteries based on Decayable-LSTM
abstract: Data-driven techniques have been extensively employed in practical applications involving lithium-ion batteries. However, the accuracy of these methods heavily relies on the quality and quantity of the collected data. The presence of missing values, resulting from external factors, poses a challenge in effectively leveraging the collected data. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel approach that utilizes long short-term memory (LSTM) to extract valuable features from randomly missing data. Additionally, an interactive network organized in a tree structure is employed for predicting the remaining useful life (RUL). Experimental results on the NASA dataset demonstrate the superiority of our method, achieving a lower root mean square error(RMSE) of 0.01265 ± 0.001 for RUL, surpassing other data-driven methods.

articleTitle: Adaptive fault-tolerant visual control of robot manipulator based on unequal-actuation scheme
abstract: This paper presents a novel adaptive visual servo controller for controlling a manipulator with unknown time-varying actuator failure and uncalibrated camera, which allows the output capacity of actuators that drive the same joint different. Since the actuators that drives the same joint in parallel are not identical, an unequal-actuation scheme is given to guarantee that every actuator’s output dose not exceed its maximum output capacity. Additionally, to identify the unknown time-varying failure, this paper adopts a widely used actuator failure model to describe the potential failure and proposes a new adaptive law based on Lyapunov’s method to compensate the unknown failure. Furthermore, the convergence of the image error and the whole signals in system are proved to be stable. Finally, The simulation results are provided to evaluate the good performance of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: Networking and Resource Allocation for Industrial Internet Scenarios base on 5G networks
abstract: In industrial Internet systems, data is the core, networks are the foundation, and security is the guarantee. In order to achieve the overall goal of upgrading industrial Internet technology, efficiently utilizing production factors and improving the level of Internet industry, the emerging technology of Internet scenario networking has emerged, which links and integrates all elements of the industrial production process. This paper is based on the existing networking mode of industrial Internet and explores the fusion networking mode of 5G+time-sensitive networking (TSN), analyzes the enhanced technology of 5G+new radio (NR) basic configuration. We strive to meet the requirements of industrial Internet scenarios with the optimal resource allocation strategy and improve the success rate of executing computing tasks in Internet systems. And we promote the deep integration of TSN technology and 5G technology, and lay the foundation for adapting to the trend of industrial Internet scenario networking. The advantages of combining edge-cloud fusion computing technology with elastic optical transport network in terms of migration delay, migration cost, and resource balance are verified through the example of industrial automated guided vehicles (AGVs).

articleTitle: Predicting Solar Irradiance Intervals for Power Generation Systems
abstract: To address the inadequacy in interval prediction accuracy of solar irradiance in photovoltaic power generation systems, this study establishes a predictive model based on Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average Model (ARIMA). The model achieves the prediction of the overall distribution of solar irradiance intervals under unknown sample conditions. First, to overcome the non-stationarity issue in the high-complexity and strongly nonlinear solar irradiance time series, the Variational Mode Decomposition method is employed to decompose the original solar irradiance time series. Next, using the ARIMA model, point predictions for each component are derived. Finally, employing non-parametric Gaussian Kernel Density Estimation, the error between the point prediction results and the original data is estimated, yielding the interval prediction results for solar irradiance. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to other models, this interval prediction model better addresses the bias in prediction results caused by the fluctuation and randomness of solar irradiance.

articleTitle: Multiclass Generalization Memorization Machine
abstract: Recently, generalization memorization machine (GMM) has been proposed with zero empirical risk and well generalization in small sample size binary classification problems. This paper extends the GMM into multiclass classification. Different from the one-vs-one (1v1) or one-vs-rest (1vR) strategy, we propose a Multiclass Generalization Memorization Machine (MGMM) by only solving a quadratic programming problem, Compared with the strategy of extending the classical support vector machine into multiclass classification proposed by Crammer et al. MGMM has stronger generalization capabilities. The Crammer’s strategy was proposed two decades ago. Since its generalization ability is limited by the potential higher empirical risk, the extend of useage is less than the 1v1 and 1vR strategies. Correspondingly, our MGMM always obtains zero empirical risk theoretically and preserves the well generalization from the GMM. Preliminary experimental results verify the advantages of our MGMM compared with several state-of-the-art multiclass classification methods.

articleTitle: YOLOv7-TDP: A Network on the Defects Detection in Catalyst Coating of PEMFC
abstract: Proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) is one of the main development directions of new energy and clean power in the future. As the core raw material of hydrogen fuel cell, membrane electrode has engendered ever greater scholarly interest because its performance directly determines the performance and service life of the fuel cell. However, due to the diverse range of defect types, scales, and structural shapes encountered in the production of membrane electrodes for proton exchange membrane catalysts coating, along with the irregular distribution of these defects, achieving rapid and accurate detection poses a significant challenge using existing methods. This limitation adversely impacts cell performance and subsequent processes. A fast detection network based on deformable convolution and disparity-size target detection layer YOLOv7-TDP is proposed for the defects of proton exchange membrane fuel cell catalyst coating. Firstly, the mechanism of coating defects is studied, and a dataset of the defects of proton exchange membrane catalyst coating is constructed, which mainly consists of four main defects, including bubbles, particles, spots, and voids. Secondly, a novel enhanced variable shape feature extraction module is proposed for various defects with irregular distribution, shape and scale. By incorporating deformable convolution, the defect feature extraction network is enhanced to encompass a broader range of defect texture features, which ensures a more comprehensive and inclusive analysis. Finally, a large size target detection layer is added to the model head to increase the detection capability of scale-proportional disparity defects, which better fit the large size defects. The experimental results on the dataset show that the mean accuracy (mAP@IoU=0.5) of the algorithm is 94.1%, which is 8.6% higher than that of the baseline network, and the detection speed is up to 100 fps, which effectively improves the detection accuracy and speed of defects on the surface of catalyst coating.

Author Keywords: proton exchange membrane fuel cell catalyst coating

articleTitle: Flocking Modeling and Robustness Evaluation Based on Heterogeneous Network
abstract: Considering the complexity and heterogeneity of agents in the flocking system and the diversity of relationships between agents with different dynamics. This paper initially proposes a flocking system modeling method based on heterogeneous networks, grounded in the Cucker-Smale flocking model with a leader-follower mechanism. Simulation experiments verify the superiority and reliability of the modeling method on three network topologies. Then, a flocking system robustness metric, improved Meta-Path(Im-MP), is proposed by combining the concept of Meta-Paths in heterogeneous networks. Finally, a comparison is made with the commonly used robustness metrics, and it is verified that the Im-MP metric is more suitable for evaluating the robustness of flocking systems.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization of Cloud Manufacturing Service Combination Based on Manufacturing and Logistics Coordinate
abstract: With the continuous emergence of new technologies, the manufacturing industry is facing unprecedented challenges. Manufacturing services typically involve various types of production equipment, diverse suppliers, and varied customer demands. Optimization in this context often encompasses multi pie objectives, necessitating timely adjustments in service comb ¡nations to meet customer needs. Traditional manufacturing models evidently fall short in resource allocation within manufacturing supply chains. Cloud manufacturing, proposed as a novel manufacturing model, aims to optimize resource allocation through the combination and configuration of resources, there by enhancing the efficiency of manufacturing supply chains. Logistics, as a crucial component within manufacturing supply chains, underscores the significance of coordinating the optimizad on of manufacturing and logistics services. This research focus es on the multi-objective optimization problem of cloud manufacturing service combinations. Building upon the execution process of manufacturing and logistics services for complex product manufacturing tasks, a novel mathematical model for the optimization of manufacturing resources and logistics resources i s constructed. The model utilizes the NSGA-H algorithm to coordinate the optimization processes of manufacturing and legistics resources. Finally, a case study demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: SWCB: An Efficient Switch-Clustering of Bandit Model
abstract: Bandit model is a general framework for solving the cold-start problem in recommender systems. In recent works, clustering strategies have been adopted in the bandit settings to further mitigate the lack of information for new users and items. Although these approaches prove to be effective, their performance may suffer from the clustering efficiency. On one hand, quickly identifying the underlying cluster to share the information has a significantly impact on retaining new users with low levels of interaction in the early stages of recommendation. On the other hand, problems like overfitting might result from repeatedly using the same clustering algorithm on the same set of users, which may decrease the recommended performance over an extended period in the later stages. To address these issues, we propose a Switch-Clustering of Bandit (SWCB), which utilizes the Bandit framework to enable online recommendation as well as new user clustering in the cold-start phase. In particular, the proposed model improves the efficiency of recommendations by switching the clustering algorithms automatically. SWCB can quickly identify the underlying clusters by splitting and merging operation. When clustering metric updated by Bandit reaches a certain threshold, SWCB alters the way of user clustering, thus speeding the information retrieval in the cold start stage and helping to retain new users of online recommendations. We evaluate the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed model on one synthetic dataset and two real-world datasets. Compared with the baseline bandit models, SWCB gets higher rewards within the rounds of the cold-start phase.

articleTitle: AE-RRT*: Adaptive Ellipse-Based Optimal Path Planning
abstract: Rapidly-exploring Random Tree Star (RRT*) is a well-known sampling-based planning approach, an improvement over the traditional Rapidly Exploring Random Tree (RRT) algorithm. It is suitable for high-dimensional spaces, dynamic environments, and various complex geometric structures. However, the primary challenge of RRT* is its significant computational complexity, especially in high-dimensional spaces. To address these limitations, we propose an improved optimal path planning algorithm, namely the Adaptive Ellipse RRT* (AE-RRT*). The AE-RRT* builds on the RRT* algorithm, integrating heuristic search principles, dynamic ellipse optimization strategies, and phased exploration strategies to improve the performance of the path planning algorithm. In the random sampling phase, heuristic principles generate specific random points, significantly reducing the search space. The dynamic ellipse optimization strategy adjusts the shape of the ellipse dynamically, aligning the sampling region more closely with potential paths. The phased exploration strategy thoroughly explores the search space in the initial stages and focuses energy on path optimization in the later stages. Simulation results indicate that, compared to commonly used traditional algorithms and their enhancements, AE-RRT* can achieve superior convergence performance.

articleTitle: SAPO: A UAV path optimization method through situation assessment
abstract: UAVs have become popular across various fields due to their low cost and high performance. UAV path planning, which is the basis and key of UAV motion control, is critical to achieving the autonomous intelligence of UAVs. However, offline planning’s performance is limited by the updating frequency of map information, making it challenging to optimize paths when faced with various obstacles and expanding spaces. To address this, researchers have focused on online path planning to obtain optimal paths through greedy calculations based on local details. However, local information-based planning can risk falling into local optimal solutions due to the non-convexity of path planning problems, affecting overall optimality. To solve this issue, a path optimization method based on situation assessment is proposed, which utilizes a neural network to extract critical features from sensor data. The motion state is then analyzed in conjunction with the path planning algorithm to optimize any local path that is not conducive to stable motion. By correcting the established path, the method avoids falling into the local optimal and invalid path, improving the optimization degree and feasibility of the path. Additionally, the continuity and smoothness of the trajectory are considered, and the large arc and long curve trajectory are used instead of short, broken lines to ensure the stability of the motion state. Simulation results show that the optimized path has better stability and optimality than the original path.

articleTitle: Robot Crowd Navigation Incorporating Spatio-Temporal Information Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Ensuring the safe and efficient navigation of mobile robots in crowds is crucial for their wide application in human society. However, robots face many problems in dense and dynamic crowd scenes, such as complex spatial relationships and difficulty accurately modeling time evolution. Therefore, we propose a novel GG-SAC method to capture spatio-temporal information for robot crowd navigation. Firstly, we utilize the graph attention network to capture complex spatial relationships. Secondly, the gate recurrent unit is introduced to model the temporal evolution of the robot-crowd interaction. Finally, we input the fused spatio-temporal features into Soft Actor-Critic algorithm, a graph-based deep reinforcement learning framework, to train navigation policy. Simulation results show that our method outperforms other methods in terms of success rate and social interaction. Furthermore, our method has good generalization ability for crowd size.

articleTitle: A Constrained Decomposition Grids Approach for U-shaped Disassembly Line Balancing Problem Considering Destructive Disassembly
abstract: With the growing urgency of environmental protection, the disassembly line balancing problem has garnered significant attention. Considering some products cannot be reused even after disassembly, this paper introduces a disassembly line balancing model for U-shaped lines that incorporates destructive disassembly modes. The disassembly process is described using an AND/OR graph. Two objectives are taken into account to maximize the total profit and minimize idle time. A constrained decomposition approach with grids for evolutionary multi-objective optimization with a destructive probability generation operator is developed to solve the problem. The practicality of this algorithm is validated through a series of experiments involving products of varying sizes. Furthermore, a comprehensive evaluation is conducted by comparing it with three peer algorithms. Numerical results convincingly demonstrate the proposed model’s effectiveness and superiority.

Author Keywords: constrained decomposition grids approach for evolutionary multi-objective optimization

articleTitle: Long-term Solar Irradiance Forecasting Based on TimesNet with Multiple Weather Parameters
abstract: In renewable energy grids, solar irradiance prediction is significant for electric operation planning. The emphasis of our work is forecasting irradiance changes over multiple days ahead using hourly irradiance data in association with weather parameters such as temperature, humidity, barometric pressure, wind speed, and cloud cover. Specifically, a framework based on TimesNet was proposed for 4-day global horizontal irradiance (GHI) forecasting and a comparative experiment was conduct with three well-performing models in long-term forecasting tasks. The experimental results indicate that the suggested method outperformed the accuracy when compared to other models, with MSE 0.198, MAE 0.259, RMSE 0.445 and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> 0.787.

articleTitle: Salient object detection based on adaptive difference of Gaussian feature pyramid network
abstract: The classical center-neighborhood contrast theory, based on a biologically sound architecture, is widely used in the field of salient object detection under traditional methods, but has rarely been introduced into deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs). To take advantage of this biological property, this paper proposes a network that fuses center-neighborhood contrast with the help of a difference of Gaussian (DoG) feature pyramid. The existing difference of Gaussian pyramids utilize predetermined Gaussian kernel sizes that remain fixed throughout the training phase and therefore may not accurately measure the true pop-out attribute of the salient object. Based on such a premise, this paper proposes a Gaussian difference feature pyramid network with adaptive kernel properties, which takes the Gaussian kernel size as a learnable weight, and with the help of the gumbel_softmax's derivability, achieves the dynamic adjustment of the standard deviation of initial Gaussian kernel. Comparison experiments are conducted between the proposed model and eight popular saliency detection algorithms on five common datasets, taking the mean absolute error (MAE) and the maximum F-measure as evaluation matric. The experimental results show that the proposed model has achieved better detection performance for salient objects than the competing approaches.

articleTitle: Backstepping Course Control of Marine Vessel Using Gaussian Process Regression With Event-Triggered Learning
abstract: In this letter, we present a backstepping control approach for the ship course control nonlinear systems that is partially unknown, also the event-triggered learning is developed for collecting to training data. We employ gaussian process model to learn the unknown partially system using measurement data, while the proposed control law is active. Our approach uses an efficient event-triggered learning scheme that exclusively collects informative data to update the estimated model used for control. The stability of this control algorithm has been rigorously proved by Lyapunov stability theory. So, the resulting control law guarantees that the course angle error is globally uniformly ultimately bounded. Finally, in the simulation example, we modeled and conducted simulation experiments on the "YuLong" vessel at Dalian Maritime University. Our method demonstrates excellent course control performance, as indicated by the results obtained.

articleTitle: Evidential Clustering with Soft Pairwise Constraints
abstract: Constrained clustering, a prominent field in data analysis, integrates prior knowledge or constraints into the clustering process. This paper introduces a novel extension to the Evidential C-means (ECM) algorithm, incorporating soft pairwise constraints to enhance clustering performance in scenarios with available prior knowledge. The proposed method significantly augments the algorithm's capabilities, providing a more nuanced approach to modeling relationships between data points through soft constraints. Unlike traditional hard constraints, the introduced soft constraints accommodate uncertainty, enabling a realistic representation of complex data relationships. Additionally, an adaptive metric overcomes the limitations of the Euclidean distance, adept at handling non-spherical classes. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of these extensions, showcasing superior performance compared to other constraint-based methods while requiring fewer constraints for accurate clustering outcomes. The applicability of the proposed method is demonstrated through experiments on real datasets, including a medical image segmentation application.

articleTitle: Transform Nonlinear Programming Problem to Initial-Value Problem to Solve, Part 2: To the Infeasible Region
abstract: A dynamic method to solve the general Nonlinear Programming (NLP) problem, inspired by the Lyapunov continuous-time dynamics stability theory in the control field, is proposed. The optimal solution is regarded as the stable equilibrium point of a finite-dimensional dynamic system and solved in an asymptotic manner. Under the premise that the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) optimality condition exists, the Dynamic Optimization Equation (DOE) is extended to the infeasible region following the work in Part 1 of the paper and its solution will converge to the optimal solution of the NLP globally. The expressions of the Lagrange multipliers and the KKT multipliers during the entire optimization process are also presented. Again using the matrix pseudo-inverse, the DOE is valid even without the linearly independent regularity requirement on the nonlinear constraints. Through the extension proposed in this part of the paper, it is shown that the NLP may be transformed to the Initial-value Problem (IVP) to be solved efficiently, with arbitrary initial guesses.

articleTitle: Robust Constrained Consensus with Guaranteed Differential Privacy and Accurate Convergence
abstract: Not only is constrained consensus widely used in cooperative control and sensor networks, it is also a fundamental building block in numerous distributed computation algorithms such as multi-agent optimization and distributed Nash equilibrium seeking. We propose a new robust constrained consensus algorithm that is robust to persistent and independent noises added for the purpose of differential-privacy protection. In fact, the algorithm can ensure both accurate consensus and rigorous ϵ-differential privacy (even when the number of iterations tends to infinity), which, to our knowledge, has not been achieved before in constrained consensus algorithms. Since channel noise in communications can be viewed as a special case of differential-privacy noises, the algorithm can also be used to counteract communication imperfections. Numerical simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Search Parameter Optimization of Phased Array Radar with Multi-antenna Array Based on Proximal Policy Optimization
abstract: An optimization algorithm of multi-antenna array radar search parameters based on proximal policy optimization is proposed to solve the problem that the parameters of traditional single-antenna array radar optimization model is hard to solve in complex multi-antenna array scenario. Firstly, considering the constraints of multi-antenna array scenario, combined with the actual search task requirement of airborne radar, an optimization model of multi-antenna array radar search parameters based on the maximum expected discovery distance of the target is established. Secondly, the dual observation space and composite reward function with discount factor are introduced to transform the above optimization problem into a dynamic decision problem of reinforcement learning, in which the solution of model parameters is realized by executable action output by the policy network. Using the Actor-Critic algorithm structure, combined with methods for solving extreme value of function, the weight of each antenna array and the corresponding sub-airspace search resource allocation coefficient are updated online. Finally, the simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can quickly make accurate autonomous decision based on the airspace-target set covering model and the threat of each target, and the performance of proposed algorithm is significantly better than the traditional algorithm in the multi-antenna array scenario.

articleTitle: Multi-attention graph convolutional network for skeleton-based action recognition
abstract: Action recognition is a challenging task in computer vision, playing a pivotal role in understanding human behavior. Graph convolutional neural networks naturally excel in extracting spatiotemporal features from human skeleton sequences, finding extensive applications in skeleton-based action recognition. Skeleton sequences contain rich information across the dimensions of time, space, and channels. However, current methods lack a balanced design for information extraction in these three dimensions, with many models being overconfident during the training process. In this paper, we present the Multi-Attention Graph Convolutional Network (MA-GCN), utilizing attention modules designed across these three dimensions for the purpose of feature extraction and fusion. We construct channel and spatial attention modules separately by using different pooling methods, establish temporal attention module through a combination of local context and global context. During the training process, we utilize label smoothing regularization to constrain the model, enhancing its generalization ability. We conducted extensive experiments using the NW-UCLA, NTU RGB+D, and NTU RGB+D 120 datasets. Our approach demonstrated its effectiveness by surpassing the baseline method by 0.5%, 0.3%, and 0.4% on the two large-scale datasets.

articleTitle: Attitude Tracking of Near-ground Quadrotor: A Switched Linear Parameter Varying Approach
abstract: This paper is devoted to the attitude tracking problem of a near-ground quadrotor, where the aerodynamic force of propellers is impaired under the ground effect. An altitude-dependent dynamic model for attitude control of the quadrotor is formulated with consideration of actuator dynamics, upon which an attitude tracking system for near-ground quadrotor is obtained, instead of only considering the altitude control problem via altitude-dependent total lift force in the past studies. By selecting the altitude as a scheduling variable, the attitude tracking control system is further described via a switched linear parameter varying scheme, which has not been considered before. The stability condition and the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performance are obtained, then an altitude-dependent attitude controller is designed, where the effectiveness and advantages are demonstrated via simulations.

articleTitle: Small Sample Data Augmentation Method for Photovoltaic Power Generation Based on Improved Variational Auto-encoder
abstract: This study proposes a combined model of attention-enhanced Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and Variational Auto-Encoder (VAE) to address the challenge of augmenting small sample data, aiming to tackle the issues of limited training data and imbalanced supervised learning in photovoltaic power prediction for newly established solar power plants. Firstly, weather clustering using K-means is applied to the data. Subsequently, VAE extract reliable local features within short time windows, encoding information. Concurrently, LSTM networks integrate with attention mechanisms to infer long-term correlations within the time series. Finally, an isolated forest method is employed to analyze the quality of generated data, further assessing its quality level. Validation experiments conducted on data from a new photovoltaic station compared the proposed approach with an existing VAE data generation model, confirming the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method. This study offers a robust solution for addressing data scarcity and imbalance issues in photovoltaic power prediction.

articleTitle: Lidar and Camera Heuristic Learning Method for Target Detection
abstract: Lidar and camera are crucial to intelligent mobile platforms to perceive environment. Generally massive data are annotated manually to training deep neural networks for target detection. However, manual labelling of large amounts of sample data would cause exorbitant costs and inefficiencies. To improve the learning efficiency, a Lidar and camera heuristic learning method is proposed for target detection of mobile platforms. Considering the different detection capabilities of Lidar and camera for different features in different scenes, the detection results from different sensors are used to train another sensor respectively to improve the detection models. Firstly, targets are detected from real-time sensor data by pre-trained models associated with Lidar and camera separately. Then the semantic relevance of detection results are evaluated by data association to obtain association matrix and consistency vector. Finally, detection models of Lidar and Camera are trained with associated detection results respectively to improve performance continuously. The experimental results show that the workload associated with the manual labeling of different detection samples is reduced effectively, and the training efficiency of target detection models is improved greatly.

articleTitle: Ant Colony Enhanced Q-Learning Algorithm for Mobile Robot Path Planning
abstract: Q-learning algorithm is a common method for solving robot path planning problems. However, it is not only significantly time-consuming, but also prone to getting stuck in local optima. This paper presents an enhanced approach to the Q-learning algorithm by incorporating ant colony optimization, which leads to better convergence of the Q-learning algorithm and reduces the number of iterations and computational time. Firstly, the Q-table and initial paths are constructed through interactive training between the agents and the environment. Secondly, the ant colony algorithm dynamically updates the pheromone matrix and iteratively adapts the path search strategy in the Q-table. Experimental results illustrate that the enhanced Q-learning algorithm exhibits superior performance compared to the original Q-learning algorithm in path planning simulations, as indicated by three evaluation metrics. Furthermore, improvements are observed in terms of the length of the shortest path and the quantity of turning points, yielding smoother paths.

articleTitle: Multi-condition flotation process condition recognition method based on deep learning and multivariate data pre-processing
abstract: The state and trend of flotation surface foam play a crucial role in flotation operations as they provide important indications of working conditions, index predictions, and operational volume adjustments. While researchers have focused on manual feature design of froth images or automatic extraction of depth features and their relationship to flotation conditions, the information contained in the flotation process variables and the importance of data pre-processing are usually overlooked. To address these shortcomings, this study proposes an integrated framework for flotation process data preprocessing and condition recognition. It includes a fast imputation algorithm based on multi-condition data center of mass (FCKNN) for overcoming the challenges of imputing missing values in on-line industrial processes, as well as a high-precision work condition recognition method that fuses deep visual features with key process variables. Finally, the framework was applied to the gold flotation process. The experimental results show that the proposed framework can perform work condition recognition with high accuracy and solve the challenge of online missing value imputation.

articleTitle: GAT-based Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithm for Real-time Task Scheduling on Multicore Platform
abstract: The scheduling of real-time and dependent tasks on multicore systems plays an important role in influencing system performance. During the scheduling process, multiple constraints should be taken into account, e.g., task dependency, real-time response, and energy efficiency. The complex task scheduling problem makes it difficult to balance solution quality and computation time. Existing works either use time-consuming methods to find optimal solutions or get feasible solutions through heuristic methods. In this paper, we propose a GAT (graph attention network)-based deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithm to solve task scheduling problems. This method combines the benefits of deep learning (DL) networks and reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms. It can achieve adaptive learning and adjust information features by constructing the GAT to model the dependencies between tasks. At the same time, we use the soft actor-critic (SAC) algorithm to optimize the task scheduling policy to minimize the makespan of scheduling results. The experimental results show that our method outperforms other scheduling methods regarding scheduling efficiency (the quality of task scheduling problem) and algorithm running time.

articleTitle: Multiscale Superpixel Affinity for Improved Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Weakly supervised semantic segmentation based on image-level labels typically employs strategies of modifying and expanding class activation map(CAM) seeds to achieve semantic segmentation. However, network downsampling can reduce the edge perception of the CAM, leading to problems of under-activation and over-activation, which consequently affect the segmentation quality. To address these issues, this paper proposes a weakly supervised semantic segmentation method based on multi-scale superpixel affinity(MSPA). In this method, a classification network is first used to generate CAMs, which are then refined using a pixel adaptive module to generate pseudo-masks and provide semantic labels for superpixels. Simultaneously, a fully convolutional network is utilized to extract full-size image features, which are mapped onto the superpixel segmentation map to obtain the feature representation of each superpixel. Subsequently, based on the feature representation of superpixels, the affinity between superpixels is calculated. The superpixels associated with foreground and background categories are then clustered separately to generate foreground probability maps and background probability maps to supervise the localisation of the CAMs. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves segmentation accuracies of 67.02% and 67.74% on the validation set and test set, respectively, on the Pascal VOC 2012 dataset. This leads to more accurate activation of the CAMs and clearer categories, which significantly outperforms the compared methods in this paper.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Prediction for Aero-Engine based on Ghost-LSTM Model
abstract: Prediction and health management (PHM) stands as a key area of research in multiple application domains, with the prediction of remaining useful life (RUL) serving as a crucial component within PHM. The aero-engine is an important component related to aircraft flight safety. Accurate prediction of aero-engine RUL is of great significance in real life. In recent years, data-driven approaches for aero-engine RUL prediction, particularly those based on deep learning techniques such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), have exhibited remarkable achievements. However, to address the computational intensity associated with current RUL prediction methods, a novel model named Ghost-LSTM has been proposed, combining the Ghost module with LSTM. This approach effectively extracts deep information from the Ghost feature map through cheap convolutional calculations, while simultaneously capturing temporal information using LSTM. The proposed method has been validated using the C-MAPSS dataset, demonstrating its ability to sustain high-precision RUL prediction performance while also exhibiting superior training speed compared to other existing methods.

articleTitle: Fully Distributed Integral-Type Event-Triggered Formation-Containment Tracking Control for Heterogeneous Multi-agent Systems
abstract: This article considers the time-varying output formation tracking problems for heterogeneous multi-agent systems with multiple leaders. A fully distributed integral-type event-triggering control protocol without using any global information is proposed. Then, by introducing an auxiliary function, minimum triggering interval (MTI) can be always strictly positive which is a stronger condition than simply ruling out Zeno behavior. By constructing a novel Lyapunov function for ETM design and stability analysis, the control objective is achieved. Finally, the effectiveness and performance of the theoretical results are validated by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Active steering angle tracking control of steer-by-wire system under different external disturbance
abstract: In the context of vehicle intelligence, steer-by-wire (SbW) has great potential for development and has become a current research hotspot. A challenging key technology of the SbW system is the steering angle tracking control under the effect of wheel-ground coupling resistance torque. In this paper, a method is proposed to provide the wheel-ground coupling resistance torque of the system by controlling the motor to track the desired torque to apply reaction force to the SbW system, which is referred to as reaction force analog control. The reaction force analog control strategy based on proportional integral (PI) control is proposed for the brushless DC motor (BLDC) with Hall sensor. Meanwhile, a method for estimating the angle and velocity of the BLDC based on Hall sensor is presented for field-oriented control. Besides, a steering angle tracking control strategy based on PI control is designed for the permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) with resolver to achieve excellent steering performance. The proposed algorithms are validated with different driving test cycles from ISO standards via hardware-in-loop experiments. The experimental results show that the designed reaction force analog control can accurately track the desired resistance torque and the proposed active steering angle tracking controller achieves high-precision steering angle tracking performance under external disturbance, which it well meets the requirements of embedded applications.

articleTitle: Iterative identification methods for multivariable input piecewise nonlinear finite impulse response moving average systems
abstract: Multivariable nonlinear systems involve multiple input and output variables, posing challenges in system identification and control design. This paper focuses on the identification issue for multivariable input piecewise nonlinear finite impulse response moving average systems with two-input and single-output, in which the two input nonlinear modules contain dead-zone nonlinearity and variable-gain nonlinearity respectively. By utilizing the switching function and key term separation technique, we derive the system identification model that contains all the linear and nonlinear parameters. Building upon this identification model, we develop an extended gradient iterative algorithm and an extended least squares iterative algorithm by integrating the auxiliary model idea with the iterative identification approach. Furthermore, we provide a comprehensive analysis of the computational efficiency of these two iterative identification algorithms. Finally, we validate the reliability and effectiveness of our proposed algorithms through a simulation example.

articleTitle: Encryption-Decryption-Based Feedback Control for Parabolic PDE Systems under DoS Attacks
abstract: This paper investigates the output feedback stabi-lization problem for a parabolic partial differential equation (PDE) system which is subject to denial-of-service (DoS) jamming attacks. In order to protect privacy, the sampled data is encrypted and decrypted using the secret key before and after passing through the network, respectively. The close-loop PDE system model under network attacks based on privacy protection is established. Following the model, sufficient criteria for guaranteeing the stability of the system are put forward. Then employing the Linear matrix inequality (LMI) technique we can get the controller gain. Finally, simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: The density estimation of group targets based on state information
abstract: In view of the problems of unstable image quality, large demand for training data and high computational cost, which are existed in the method of group targets density estimation based on image information, a new method based on state information and combined with statistics is proposed. Specifically, the state information derived from target tracking with GLMB filter is used as sample data, and the kernel density estimation (KDE) with adaptive bandwidth is introduced to calculate the probability density function (PDF) and visualize the density distribution of group targets.
