The results of simulation show that the proposed algorithm can effectively visualize the density distribution of group targets, and the mean square error can be reduced by nearly 60% after the introduction of adaptive bandwidth.

articleTitle: Whole-body Dynamic Collision Avoidance with Time-varying Control Barrier Functions
abstract: Recently, there has been increasing attention in robot research towards the whole-body collision avoidance. In this paper, we propose a safety-critical controller that utilizes time-varying control barrier functions (time varying CBFs) constructed by Robo-centric Euclidean Signed Distance Field (RC-ESDF) to achieve dynamic collision avoidance. The RCESDF is constructed in the robot body frame and solely relies on the robot’s shape, eliminating the need for real-time updates to save computational resources. Additionally, we design two control Lyapunov functions (CLFs) to ensure that the robot can reach its destination. To enable real-time application, our safety-critical controller which incorporates CLFs and CBFs as constraints is formulated as a quadratic program (QP) optimization problem. We conducted numerical simulations on two different dynamics of an L-shaped robot to verify the effectiveness of our proposed approach.

articleTitle: GLMDST: Chinese Dialogue State Tracking Framework Driven by LLM
abstract: Dialogue State Tracking (DST) is an important component in task-oriented dialogue systems. Accurate dialogue state tracking is essential for generating correct dialogue actions and appropriate natural language responses. However, annotating conversation states is notoriously difficult, leading to a scarcity of DST datasets in languages other than English. With the development of DST, high-quality annotated Chinese conversation datasets have gradually emerged. Despite the emergence of available Chinese conversation datasets, research on the Chinese DST task remains relatively limited.The emergence of Large Language Model (LLM) such as GPT-3 and ChatGPT has sparked considerable interest in evaluating their effectiveness across different tasks. However, the performance of LLM in Chinese DST remains to be explored. In this study, we introduce GLMDST, a Chinese DST framework powered by a smaller open-source bilingual model called chat-glm3-6b. GLMDST demonstrates outstanding performance in experiments on mainstream Chinese DST benchmarks such as CrossWOZ and RiSAWOZ, showcasing excellent adaptability and generalization capabilities.

articleTitle: Based on Event-triggered mechanism of Leader-following H∞ consensus for multi-agent systems under deception attacks
abstract: In this paper, the H∞ consensus of mean-square asymptotic stability problem for multi-agent systems (MASs) suffering deception attacks and time-delays is studied, and utilizing event-triggered mechanism (ETM) to reduce more communication resources. According to the requirements of the controller, the ETM can adjust the frequency of event triggering. Due to the presence of time-delays in the system, for the convenience of discussion, the original system is transformed into consensus problem of the system is transformed into the stabilityan error system through the model transformation, that the H∞ problem of the error system. Then, the problem of the system is analyzed utilizing Lyapunov-Krasovskii functionals (LKFs), and by solving linear matrix inequality (LMI) can obtain parameters such as controller gain and trigger matrix. Finally, the numerical simulation is used to verify the theorems and the effectiveness of the LKFs used in this problem.

articleTitle: Imitation Learning from Suboptimal Demonstrations via Discriminator Weighting
abstract: Imitation learning algorithms for robotics applications require sufficient optimal data to learn well-performing strategies. State-of-the-art approaches utilize pre-labeled data or interaction with the environment to filter suboptimal data, which is time-consuming and laborious in reality. In this paper, we propose a new approach that avoids manual labeling or environment interaction. We design an additional discriminator for the behavioral cloning approach to distinguish the optimal and suboptimal data in order to influence policy learning and avoid suboptimal behaviors. Within this framework, we design a new imitation learning algorithm that utilizes the output of the discriminator as weights to learn efficiently on datasets containing suboptimal data. We evaluate the performance of the proposed method in four environments and compare it with three benchmark methods. The results illustrate that our method has better performance when dealing with datasets containing suboptimal data. The method we proposed can distinguish data with higher values in the dataset and enable the agent to learn high-performance policy from imperfect demonstrations or a small amount of data.

articleTitle: OTFS-NOMA System Resource Allocation Scheme Based on SADEBOA Algorithm
abstract: This paper investigates the power allocation problem in the downlink of an Orthogonal Time Frequency Space-Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (OTFS-NOMA) system under high-speed conditions, with the objective of maximizing system capacity and rate. A novel Butterfly Optimization Algorithm based on Differential Evolution (DE) and Simulated Annealing (SA), referred to as SADEBOA, is proposed. In the global search phase, SADEBOA incorporates DE to enhance the global search capability of the Butterfly Optimization Algorithm (BOA), mutating the optimal individual and guiding the population towards the optimal individual's location. In the local search phase, SADEBOA combines SA to accept a local optimal solution as a new solution with a certain probability, introducing a certain bias that is more likely to approach the optimal solution. Comparative simulations are conducted with BOA, MSBOA, DA, and RSO algorithms, as well as traditional power allocation schemes. The simulation results demonstrate that, compared to the baseline BOA algorithm, MSBOA, DA, and RSO algorithms, SADEBOA achieves performance improvements of approximately 15%, 5.3%, 21.2%, and 28.4%, in enhancing OTFS-NOMA system capacity.

articleTitle: Asynchronously Event-Triggered Time-Varying Formation Tracking for UAV Swarm Systems With Switching Directed Typologies
abstract: This paper investigates the asynchronous control problem of event-triggered time-varying formation tracking (TVFT) for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm systems with switching directed typologies. The proposed event-triggered mechanism (ETM) can reduce superfluous communication resources by executing the control task only when the triggering condition is satisfied. Meanwhile, the Zeno behavior is excuded as well. In addition, the asynchronous phenomenon between the event-triggered instant and the switching instant is taken into account, which is more practical and complicated in the system under consideration. Subsequently, The TVFT control scheme, the ETM and the persistent dwell time signal are collectively designed to guarantee the globally uniformly asymptotic stability of the UAV swarm system. The efficiency and merits of these designed methods are affirmatively demonstrated through conclusive simulation results.

articleTitle: Detection of False Data Injection Attacks Based on Spatio-Temporal Characterization in Smart Grids
abstract: With the increasing popularization of information and communication technologies, the development of smart grids has also emerged. However, the high reliance on information technology puts the grid at risk of malicious attacks. False Data Injection Attack (FDIA)have become a serious threat to the smart grid. While most of the current methods for detecting FDIA focus on determining whether the grid has been subjected to such attacks, they often overlook the importance of considering the topology and temporal correlations within the grid data and are unable to localize their attacks. To address this limitation, we have proposed a novel multi-label attack localization detection method based on spatio-temporal features. Our method considers both time and space and enables the localisation of attacks. Spatial feature extraction is conducted using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), which is subsequently subjected to feature filtering through an Attention Mechanism. The filtered features are then channeled into both Long-Term and Short-Term Memory network (LSTM) via a channel fusion process. This intricate process allows for the extraction of spatio-temporal features, ultimately facilitating the accurate localization of attacks. To evaluate the efficacy of our approach, we conducted extensive simulation experiments using the IEEE 14bus system and the IEEE 118-bus system. The results showcase remarkable performance with an overall accuracy of 99.6% for the former and 98.7% for the latter, underscoring the effectiveness of our proposed model.

articleTitle: Static Security Assessment with Accuracy Evaluation Based on Neural Networks
abstract: Focusing on assessing the safety status of power systems, static security assessment involves solving huge amounts of nonlinear power flow equations for analyzing the successive processes of power redistribution and component outages after an initial contingency of the grid, a neural network model that makes fast approximations of power flows during the successive process is proposed. This model also predicts the cascading processes of line failures with an indicative function, which considers overflows of lines and the corresponding line failures. Thus, this model is also used to predict the grid topologies during the cascading line failure process, whose accuracy is also estimated. The effectiveness of the proposed model is verified on the IEEE 5, 24, and 118-bus systems.

articleTitle: Outlier detection based on novel Robust Gaussian process: Applied to complex nonlinear system
abstract: As industries increasingly digitize, data-based technologies are becoming more widespread, placing higher demands on data quality. However, industrial processes are complex and subject to various interferences, resulting in detected data that inevitably contains outliers. To address this issue, outlier detection techniques are becoming increasingly indispensable. This paper presents a Gaussian process-based outlier detection method that is well-suited for complex and nonlinear industrial systems. This method combines a newly proposed robust Gaussian process with a specially designed outlier determination criterion. The approach allows for faster model training and more accurate outlier detection without the need for manual decision thresholds. To confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method, we compared it with various traditional outlier detection methods as well as mainstream robust Gaussian process-based outlier detection methods in the numerical simulation stage. The superior performance of the proposed method was confirmed in both artificial and real datasets.

Index Terms: Area Under Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve

articleTitle: Distributed platooning control of connected and automated vehicles under Event-based encryption-decryption
abstract: The paper investigates the problem of distributed vehicular platooning control under the premise of privacy preservation. First, an encryption-decryption scheme is introduced to secure the data transmitted among vehicles, preventing potential external breaches that might compromise the confidentiality of the original vehicular data, thereby enhancing the privacy and security of vehicle interactions. Second, an event-triggered mechanism is utilized to enable data exchanges among vehicles only when specific conditions are met. The employment of such event triggering significantly reduces the utilization of communication resources, thereby improving communication efficiency. Then, a distributed platooning control strategy is proposed to ensure that each vehicle within the platoon achieves the desired tracking performance. Finally, stability analysis of the closed-loop event-triggered encryption-decryption platooning control system is conducted. The feasibility and the efficacy of the control strategy are demonstrated through a specific numerical example.

articleTitle: Research on fault diagnosis methods for certain civil aircraft based on human-machine interaction data enhancement
abstract: The structures of modern civil aircraft are becoming more and more complex, particularly with regard to aeroengines, where faults are often challenging to detect in the early stages. The implementation of Engine Control Units (ECU) in aviation provides an avenue for storing a substantial amount of historical operational data, forming the basis for data-driven fault diagnosis of aeroengines. In order to conduct research on defect diagnosis, this paper gathers the historical operation data of a certain type of civil aircraft. However, the majority of historical data consists of normal operation data, creating an imbalance between data classes, especially in terms of fault data. In addition, the complexity of engine operation modes, with dynamic operations like acceleration and takeoff having shorter durations and less data compared to horizontal flight modes, exacerbates the imbalance in data classes. The imbalance between data classes and imbalance in data classes result in missing and false alarms of many diagnosis results of this type of civil aircraft by using existing fault diagnosis technique. Furthermore, autocorrelation between variables and distinct dynamic characteristics further complicate the issue. To address these challenges, a fault diagnosis model based on a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network was developed to extract dynamic characteristics from the system. Human-machine interaction was employed to identify areas of missing and false alarms, addressing the imbalance in two types of samples. Imbalanced data was then enhanced using the Generative Adversarial Network (GAN), and the training process was manually reinforced. Experimental results demonstrated that the fault diagnosis model, augmented through human-machine interaction data enhancement, effectively captured dynamic characteristics in the data of a specific civil engine. It enhanced dynamic mode data samples and reduced the rates of missing and false alarms, validating the feasibility of the model.

articleTitle: LOCO-PCR: A Novel Outlier Removal Method with Local Correction for Feature-based Point Cloud Registration
abstract: Finding reliable correspondences between two point clouds is crucial for feature-based point cloud registration (PCR). In this paper, we present a novel outlier removal method, which locally corrects (LOCO) the initial correspondences to generate more correct correspondences, denoted as LOCO-PCR. First, we use spectral matching technique to find some potential inliers, called super seeds. For each super seed, we first find its k neighbors and then construct new local correspondences by local feature matching. Second, we propose a local hypothesis generation module to generate more accurate hypotheses. We construct global and local consensus sets based on the spatial compatibility of initial global correspondences and new local correspondences, respectively. Subsequently, we input each global and local consensus set into the weighted SVD algorithm to generate candidate rigid transformations. Finally, we propose a cross hypothesis selection strategy to select the best model from the global and local hypotheses as the final result. Our method can be combined with different local 3D features without training, further improving the accuracy and stability of feature-based point cloud registration.

articleTitle: Situation Awareness Method for Electric Vehicles Charging Pile Clusters Based on Edge Computing
abstract: In response to challenges characterized by strong randomness, wide spatial distribution, and high power demand within short time frames by a large volume of Electric Vehicles (EVs), a situation awareness method for electric vehicle charging pile clusters is proposed based on edge computing. In this method, some factors such as EVs charging, EVs flow speed in road network are comprehensively considered by using edge computing, a physical framework is established for situation awareness electric vehicle charging pile clusters and some computational resources are reasonably allocated. In view of situation awareness for Electric Vehicles Charging Pile Clusters, an Isolation Forest(IF) Algorithm is used to perceive of the operational status of electric vehicles and the Variational Mode Decomposition(VMD) algorithm is used to understand the operational characteristics of electric vehicles. On this basis, the power demand of EVs charging is forecasted by Using Multilayer Perceptron(MLP) neural network model and the Gated Recurrent Unit(GRU) algorithm. Finally, the case is studied and the proposed method is feasible.

articleTitle: Dynamic Event-triggered Consensus Control for Discrete-time Stochastic Markov Jump Multi-agent Systems with Probabilistic Time-varying Delays
abstract: Dynamic Event-triggered consensus control for a class of discrete-time stochastic Markov jump multi-agent systems with probabilistic time-varying delays is investigated in this paper. The systems with probabilistic time-varying delays are equivalent to the time-varying delays systems with random coefficients through a Bernoulli variable. We convert consensus control problem to stability problem by Laplacian matrix properties. A dynamic event-triggered strategy is introduced into the designing of the consensus protocol in order to improve energy utilization efficiency. The new criteria for the mean square consensus are presented by designing a suitable Lyapunovkrasonvskii functional, stochastic analysis and matrix inequality techniques. In the end, the effectiveness is given by simulation example.

articleTitle: Indoor Positioning Model Based on Principal Component Extraction of Support Vector Regression
abstract: The use of the WLAN Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) for indoor positioning has gained significant attention due to its advantages such as cost-effectiveness, low hardware power consumption, and ease of implementation. However, the presence of multipath and shadow effects often hinders traditional positioning algorithms from achieving satisfactory results. To address this challenge, the paper proposes a method that utilizes a feature data dimensionality reduction algorithm to extract features from the raw data, thereby improving positioning accuracy. This method utilizes relative errors as characteristics of the fingerprint database to establish a regression map between RSSI values and positioning coordinates using Support Vector Regression (SVR). The algorithm's positioning performance is evaluated in simulation environments, and the study analyzes the factors that influence the algorithm's performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA)-SVR algorithm outperforms other methods, in terms of higher positioning accuracy and better robustness. This approach shows promising potential for enhancing indoor positioning accuracy and overcoming the limitations of traditional algorithms in challenging indoor environments.

articleTitle: SAM-LSCI: Leveraging Local Spatial Context Information to Refine Image Segmentation
abstract: The Segment Anything Model (SAM) has manifested remarkable strides within the domain of image segmentation. Nonetheless, SAM grapples with two predominant challenges in specific scenarios: the emergence of "mask holes" and the coarse boundaries of the masks. To ameliorate these issues, we have proposed a architecture named SAM with Local Spatial Context Information (SAM-LSCI). This architecture ingeniously amalgamates and reutilizes the pre-trained SAM structure to elevate the segmentation quality while maintaining zero-shot image segmentation performance. We have appended a Local Spatial Feature Enhancement Module, predicated on Convolutional Neural Networks, to the original image encoder of SAM to compensate for the deficiencies of ViT in capturing image details. Furthermore, we introduced a learnable Global Context Token to augment the masks' quality further. The qualitative and quantitative experimental results on the HQSeg-44K dataset unveil that, compared to SAM and HQ-SAM, SAM-LSCI can generate masks of superior quality.

articleTitle: Gaussian Filter Estimation Framework for Nonlinear Systems with Multiple Non-Ideal Scenarios
abstract: This paper concerns a Gaussian filter estimation framework for nonlinear systems with multiple non-ideal scenarios. Multiple non-ideal scenarios can be modeled by stochastic uncertainty, correlated noise and packet dropout compensation. The stochastic uncertainty of the system is embodied in the multiplicative noise of synchronous correlation in the process equation and the measurement equation. The correlated noise is described by the process noise and observation noises at the same time. When the estimator does not receive any measurement data, the prediction compensation mechanism is used to compensate the measurement information. Firstly, in the time update process, a two-step prediction method based on projection theorem can simultaneously achieve decorrelation of multiplicative noise, process noise and measurement noise. Then, during the measurement update, the measurement information provided based on the prediction compensation mechanism is used to update the measurement based on the projection theorem. A recursive Gaussian filter estimation framework is designed. Finally, the proposed estimation framework is numerically implemented based on the third-degree spherical-radial cubature rule. Two simulation examples show that the proposed algorithm achieves numerical stability and effectiveness when applied to state estimation problem.

articleTitle: Research on Emotion Prediction Based on Emotional Changes in Dialogue Scenarios
abstract: In recent years, the application of emotional analysis in dialogues in human-computer interaction has received increasing attention. The main difference between emotional analysis in dialogues and emotional analysis in single sentences is the contextual information that influences the emotional tone in dialogues. Previous studies have used deep learning to model context information and output the speaker’s current emotional state. In this study, we first proposed a sample angle selection mechanism to resolve the difficulty of uneven distribution of sample labels. Then, we designed a parallel convolutional neural network structure that uses both speech and text modal input signals to predict the emotional changes of the intervened (human) before and after being intervened by the external intervener (robot), and then predict their emotions. The proposed method was experimentally verified using the IEMOCAP dataset, and the results showed that the accuracy of the proposed method was improved compared to the results before incorporate the sample angle selection mechanism, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multi-UAV collaborative target allocation Based on Two-Way Knowledge Transfer in complex environments
abstract: Multi-UAV collaborative target allocation (MUCTA) refers to the reasonable allocation of limited UAV resources according to the location of each UAV and target point in a complex simulation environment, so that the UAV population can avoid the threat source and effectively attack target points in different locations at the same time. During the planning process, large-scale UAVs and target points greatly increase allocation conflicts and the iterative calculations of the planning system lead to a less efficient planning system. To improve the efficiency of multi-UAV collaborative target allocation, this work proposes a Differential Evolutionary Algorithm Based on Two-Way Knowledge Transfer (TWKT- DE). Firstly, the constraints of UAVs are linearly weighted and transformed into a new objective function. The value of violated constraints is an important evaluation index of UAV allocation conflict. This method can effectively reduce the allocation conflict between UAVs. Secondly, the initial UAV allocation scheme is obtained by the DE algorithm and defined as reference knowledge, and the selection probability between tasks updates the UAV allocation scheme. Finally, the method effectively improves the efficiency of the planning system search by guiding the search direction of the planning system through the two-way transfer mechanism and reducing the redundancy of the allocation scheme. Experiments 1 and 2 validate the proposed algorithm, respectively, and the results verify the outstanding performance of TWKT-DE in dealing with multi-UAV collaborative target allocation with low allocation conflicts, high collaborative capability, and high planning efficiency.

articleTitle: Multi-source Data Fusion Network for Sea Fog Detection
abstract: Sea fog seriously affects the safety of maritime activities. This paper presents the development of a dataset for sea fog detection research and a multi-source data fusion sea fog detection network called MDF-SFNet. We collected all sea fog events observed in the Yellow Sea and Bohai Sea regions (118.1° E-128.1° E, 29.5° N-43.8° N) from March 2016 to December 2022. The Himawari-8 satellite data and sea surface temperature data are from the National Meteorological Center of China. This portion of the dataset is then accurately labeled to produce the final dataset. In addition, this paper proposes a multi-source data fusion sea fog detection model. This model not only takes advantage of Transformers to extract global input information, but also considers the traditional method of sea fog detection by meteorological experts based on physical characteristics and threshold methods. In the model, we introduce a gate module named Gate for adaptive threshold selection, an FFN module for multi-source data fusion, and an encoder module to facilitate dense prediction. MDF-SFNet extracts features from visual and meteorological physical properties, and continuously fuses the two features within the model. Experimental results show that our model achieves superior sea fog detection performance, with an F1 score of 0.742, a POD (probability of detection) of 0.753, and a CSI (critical success index) of 0.576. MDF-SFNet shows improved detection performance compared to existing state-of-the-art deep learning networks for sea fog detection.

articleTitle: Talent Prediction Based on Switching Strategy Algorithm of Residual Grey Model
abstract: The surge in demand for medical equipment necessitates accurate prediction of talent demand in the medical industry, becoming a crucial support for the strategic planning of talent and human resources in universities. However, the difficulty in effectively collecting talent data in the medical equipment industry results in limited availability of talent demand data. At the same time, existing research focuses only on the linear or nonlinear single relationship of talent demand sequence data, thereby reducing the accuracy and robustness of predictions. In this paper, we propose a Switching Strategy Algorithm based on Residual Grey Model (SSA-RGM) to address the above issue. SSA-RGM is a hybrid model that includes a novel residual grey model, commonly used simple linear regression model, and a switching strategy based on optimal fitness. In this model, we introduce a residual operation based on the grey model and, for the first time, incorporate a penalty factor to mitigate the impact of linear shifts in small-sample data within nonlinear systems. Furthermore, we adopt the principle of optimal fitness to select the best model in the hybrid model. Experimental results on six real-world datasets show that SSA-RGM achieves the best talent prediction performance in various settings.

articleTitle: Cross-level Diffusion-based Affinity Learning for Unsupervised Salient Object Detection
abstract: Numerous bottom-up salient object detection (SOD) methods rely on local similarity (affinity) to construct, which ignores the relationships among non-adjacent regions. To solve this problem, we propose a novel framework based on absorbing Markov chain (AMC) with cross-level diffusion-based affinity learning, namely CLD. In the AMC model, high transition probability implies reliable relationships among regions. For this purpose, a dense transition probability matrix is learned by a cross-level diffusion strategy. First, to comprehensively reveal the relationship among regions, multi-level features are extracted and are used to calculate multiple initial sparse affinity matrices. Second, the tensor product in the iterative diffusion process has the property of capturing the high-order relationships among features. Thus, by iteratively updating sparse affinity matrices, multiple-level features are effectively fused. Finally, through a weight learning paradigm, outlier data is removed and noise is fully suppressed. Meanwhile, learning weights are also assigned for each sparse affinity matrix and they are integrated into a dense transition probability matrix. Furthermore, to fit salient objects at multiple scales, we propose a refinement model MCLD which is a Bayesian framework under the guidance of high-level features. The MCLD aggregates saliency maps generated by CLD at different scales, and calibrates their shortcomings to produce more stable results. Extensive experiments on five challenging datasets indicate that the proposed method outperforms ten state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: Using an Improved Dynamic Learning Evolutionary Algorithm to Solve Many-objective Service Resource Combination Optimization Problem in Crowdsourcing Design
abstract: With the development of social productive forces, a new service-oriented crowdsourcing design model is emerging. The quality of task implementation and consumer satisfaction greatly depend on the optimal selection of service resources in crowdsourcing design processes. The current research primarily focuses on optimizing quality of service (QoS) such as time and cost, either through single-objective or multi-objective optimization. As individual needs increase, the requirements for different QoS also increase gradually. This leads to a many-objective combination optimization problem. Thus, this paper models and solves the problem from the perspective of many-objective optimization. Firstly, a many-objective optimization model is constructed according to the characteristics of service resources in crowdsourcing design, and an evaluation system of crowdsourcing design service resources is established. Secondly, a dynamic learning evolutionary algorithm based on adaptive resource allocation (DLEA-ARA) is proposed to adjust the computing resources according to the convergence difficulty of the problem. At the same time, niche technology is introduced to enhance the diversity maintenance ability. Finally, the proposed DLEA-ARA is compared with other state-of-the-art many-objective evolutionary algorithms (MaOEAs) under simulation data sets, and the results show the superiority of the proposed DLEA-ARA.

articleTitle: Surface Defect Detection of Mobile Phone Screen Based on Generative Adversarial Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel defect detection method for mobile phone screens based on Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). It aims at solving the overfitting problem due to insufficient data and enhancing the effectiveness of the detection network. To achieve the goal, we first present Multiscale Generative Adversarial Networks (MsGANs) to expand the dataset. As two important components in MsGANs, multi-scale generators and pyramidal discriminators are obtained by optimizing the structure of Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (CGANs). Multi-scale generators are built from coarse to fine, where the global generator produces images with lower resolution, and the local enhancer provides missing details to ensure the creation of excellent images. Pyramidal discriminators utilize three distinct scales of image feature pyramids. Further-more, we establish the multi-label classification network to tackle the defect detection problem that multiple categories of defects are involved in a single sample. A pre-trained ResNet-50 is used to extract high-level image features. Finally, the experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of MsGANs combined with ResNet-50 for mobile phone screen defect detection.

articleTitle: Research on Direct Voltage Sliding Mode Control for Distributed Power-Collection and Cascaded Boosting-Voltage Converter
abstract: Distributed power-collection and cascaded boosting-voltage (DPCB) system suffers from slow dynamic response speed and complex parameter design under the traditional cascaded double-loop PI control structure. In this paper, a single loop Silding model control strategy is proposed to improve transient and steady state performance. Two aspects are studied as follows. First, based on the analysis of system operation, the average state-space equation is built. Second, a single loop SMC control strategy is designed to heighten dynamic performance after established the average state-space equation. Finally, simulations are carried out to verify the proposed strategy feasibility and effectiveness.

articleTitle: A fault diagnostic method for rotary mechinery based on the improved variational mode decomposition and AlexNet
abstract: This paper introduces a novel fault diagnosis method for rotary bearings combining improved Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) with AlexNet. In this method, VMD is employed to decompose bearing vibration signals into multiple Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs), then the pearson correlation coefficient is adopted as the primary IMF selection criterion based on the correlation between the original signal and the decomposed signal. Ultimately, all selected IMFs from the fault vibration signals are input into AlexNet to identity the four fault modes of rolling bearings. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits more superior diagnostic performance than the undenoised method.

articleTitle: Prescribed-time consensus tracking of heterogeneous multi-agent systems over clustered wide-area networks
abstract: This paper investigates a prescribed-time consensus tracking control of a heterogeneous multi-agent system over a wide-area network. Firstly, a wide-area network is modeled by a clustered graph. Secondly, an internal model based observer is designed to estimate the state of the exogenous system. Then a predefined-time control strategy is proposed for the multi-agent system to reach output tracking. Thirdly, sufficient conditions are obtained for output tracking based on the general Lyapunov function theory and output regulation technique. Finally, simulation results are presented to validate our theoretical results.

articleTitle: Simulation analysis of magnetic focusing for buried pipeline
abstract: The detection of buried pipelines is urgent, as they are prone to leakage due to their harsh underground environment. The transient electromagnetic method is the most commonly used detection method, which has the issue of magnetic signal not focusing, and the response signal reflects the average metal content over a large range. To address the issue, the concept of magnetic focusing has been proposed. Three types of magnetic focusing coil structures were designed, and the distribution characteristics of magnetic signals were solved through two-dimensional simulation. It was found that conical coil, double coil overlapping, and double coil non overlapping all have good focusing effects. Finally, the correctness of the proposed structure is verified through 3D simulation.

articleTitle: Video compression at extremely low bit rates
abstract: Traditional video compression standards include AVC, HEVC, VVC, and AVS. These algorithms may result in ringing and blocking artifacts at extremely low bit rates, which can seriously affect video transmission quality. To address these issues, we propose a novel video compression method that combines super-resolution technology with traditional compression standards. In the encoder, we first down-sample the high-resolution input video and then use the HEVC algorithm to encode the low-resolution video into a bitstream. In the decoder, the HEVC algorithm decodes the received bitstream and inputs it into a super-resolution network to reconstruct the original high-resolution video. On the one hand, transmitting low-resolution video can reduce the required bandwidth, effectively mitigating the impact of ringing and blocking artifacts at extremely low bit rates. On the other hand, super-resolution technology can filter out ringing and blocking artifacts during the process of restoring high-resolution video. The experimental results show that our proposed method can achieve a better PSNR performance than the traditional HEVC algorithm on the standard HEVC Dataset.

articleTitle: Performance recovery control of aero-engine based on stochastic configuration network
abstract: In this paper, a performance recovery control method is proposed for the aero-engines under performance degradation. Firstly, in order to improve the estimation accuracy of the degradation factors and thrust for the aero-engines with less sensors, a Kalman Filter based on stochastic configuration network(SCN) is proposed. Then, a performance recovery control method is developed based on the estimated degradation factors and thrust. It features by strong self-learning and adaptive ability, which could achieve nearly the same thrust as the aero-engine without performance degradation. Finally, experimental results show that the proposed method can not only restore the thrust of aero-engine effectively, but also demonstrate a dynamic adjustment time of 3s without overshoot.

articleTitle: Efficient Industrial AGV Pose Estimation System in Both Indoor and Outdoor Scenario
abstract: With recent advancements in mobile robotics and autonomous driving, multi-sensor fusion technologies have produced significant improvements for precise pose estimation system of mobile devices. However, due to the high computational requirements of multi-sensor fusion algorithms, there are challenges in integrating multiple sensors into automated guided vehicles (AGVs) because computing resources are limited these platforms. Balancing high localization accuracy with low computational load has become a major issue in AGV development. To address this problem, this paper introduces a novel multi-sensor fusion framework employing the error state Kalman filter. The framework combines the inertial measurement unit, Light Detection and Ranging, and ultra-wideband sensor data. Special sensor placement and algorithm optimization in the system are used to achieve reliable 6-DOF pose estimation. The experimental results show that the proposed pose estimation system is more efficient and accurate compared to existing multi-sensor fusion methods.

articleTitle: Networked cruise control method of high-speed EMU under transmission delay
abstract: In response to the problem of speed cruise control in high-speed EMU, considering the delay of state transmission, and proposed a networked cruise control method. First of all, the high-speed EMU vehicle-speed cruise system is modeling the level linkage system with elastic coupling of the workshop. Secondly, considering the delay problem in the system state sensing, a state-based feedback-based speed control method is proposed. Finally, with the help of the Razumikhin method, the system closed-loop stability was analyzed and the controller design method based on the linear matrix disagreement was given. The proposed method can not only ensure the stability of high-speed EMU speed control system, but also has good control effect. Finally, a numerical simulation example is given, and the results show that the proposed method can reduce the relative velocity by 68.6%.

articleTitle: Platoon Control of Connected Vehicles via Safe Reinforcement Learning Based on Lyapunov Based Soft Actor Critic Algorithm
abstract: This paper addresses the platoon control problem of connected vehicular systems subject to safety constraints. A constrained Markov Decision Process model is established. A novel safe-reinforcement-learning control method based on the Lyapunov-based Soft Actor-Critic (LSAC) algorithm is developed, where the LSAC algorithm is designed to maximize the reward while minimizing the safety cost, ensuring minimal risk of collisions. Comparisons between the safe-reinforcement-learning control via LSAC algorithm and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on electric load forecasting based on RBF
abstract: Accurate power load forecasting is of great significance for grid planning and economic operation of power systems. In order to improve the accuracy of power load forecasting, this paper proposes a short-term power load forecasting method based on particle swarm algorithm (PSO) optimized radial basis (RBF) neural network. The method takes RBF neural network as the basic algorithm for short-term load forecasting. Considering the problems of the algorithm’s parameter setting and the tendency to be trapped in the local optimum, the PSO algorithm is used to optimize the parameters of the algorithm, so as to obtain a better forecasting model. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can improve the prediction accuracy to a certain extent and has certain practical application value.

articleTitle: Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on TimesBlock and Multi-scale CNN
abstract: To address the problems of low diagnostic accuracy, large model size and long inference time in rolling bearing fault diagnosis with many fault categories, an end-to-end data-driven rolling bearing fault diagnosis method based on TimesBlock and Multi-scale CNN is proposed. The proposed method achieves an average accuracy of 99.0% on the CWRU rolling bearing dataset and the number of model parameters is reduced by only 1/3 compared with the same accurate model. This study demonstrates the applicability of TimesBlock in the field of bearing fault diagnosis. The small size and high accuracy means that the model can be run in real time on edge computing platforms with smaller memory and lower computational power.

articleTitle: A Combinatorial Optimization Method for Free-Time Orbital Pursuit-Evasion Game
abstract: The orbital pursuit-evasion game has become a hotspot in space engineering research. This paper proposes a combinatorial optimization method to solve the orbital pursuit-evasion game based on the Hill-Clohessy-Wiltshire equation. First, the dynamics of the pursuer and evader are presented under HCW. Next, the game is modeled as a free-time differential game, which is transformed into a two-point boundary value problem considering necessary conditions. Subsequently, based on the necessary conditions of terminal costates for the saddle point solution, the original problem can be transformed into finding a set of a four-dimensional problem. Then, a combinatorial optimization method is proposed based on the Improved Grey Wolf Optimizer and Sequential Quadratic Programming for the free-time orbital pursuit-evasion game. Numerical simulation results demonstrate the proposed method is effective and efficient.

articleTitle: Research on coordinated and optimized scheduling strategy for new energy consumption based on clean heating
abstract: To expand the space for new energy grid-connection and address the issue of wasted wind and solar energy, this study primarily centers on the clean heating system that combines cogeneration units, wind turbines, photovoltaic power plants, conventional units, electrode boilers, and heat storage devices. The goal is to minimize the comprehensive cost of clean heating, a collaborative operation and energy management optimization strategy is proposed, incorporating restrictions related to maintaining a balance in electrical power and thermal power. By establishing a mathematical model and analyzing the system's capacity for incorporating new energy sources and the comprehensive operating costs of the system in various scenarios, the effectiveness of the model was verified.

articleTitle: Obstacle detection on tunnel walls based on fusion of images and point clouds
abstract: This paper proposes a novel attention weight ratio object detection model that integrates image and point cloud features for detecting obstacles on the tunnel wall facade. In previous researches, only point clouds were typically used as inputs for 3D object detection. However, in practical operation, point clouds may be obscured by water mist sprayed by cleaning vehicles. Thus, this paper introduces camera image data as supplementary input to address this issue. Based on this, this paper proposes a fusion module that uses attention dynamic selection mechanism to complement the fusion of point clouds and images. Compared with the traditional single modal model PointPillar and the classic multimodal model MV3D, our proposed model not only demonstrates excellent detection accuracy on the standard test set, but also demonstrates its excellent robustness in challenging water mist environments, resulting in a significant improvement in precision. These experimental results fully validate the advantages of our proposed bimodal feature fusion model in terms of performance and robustness. Therefore, this model effectively overcomes the problem of inaccurate obstacle detection under water mist interference and demonstrates its potential application in complex environments.

articleTitle: An Improved STARK Tracker with Gaussian Distributed Focal Loss
abstract: The occlusion and motion blur in datasets pose significant challenges in the field of object tracking. To enhance the tracking performance, this paper proposes an improved STARK tracker with Gaussian Distributed Focal Loss (GDFL), in which bounding boxes are characterized as probability density distribution. GDFL models the bounding box as a Gaussian distribution based on the target’s visibility, and dynamically evaluates loss between distributions, which is more suitable for tracking tasks involving occlusion and motion blur. The advantages of our proposed method are verified by extensive experimental results on the Object Tracking Benchmark (OTB) dataset.

articleTitle: Backward Transmission Detection of Pulsed Laser in Cloud Based on Semi-Analytical Monte Carlo
abstract: The distribution of liquid droplets and ice crystals in cloud is completely random, and traditional analytical methods for describing laser propagation in multiple-scattering media could have a significant impact on the estimated results. Therefore, a Monte Carlo simulation method for photon transport process in laser backscattering based on the superimposed scattering theory is proposed. A corresponding photon backward transmission model is established, and the semi-analytical Monte Carlo (SAMC) method is adopted to simulate the laser backscattering signal waveforms and backward scattering ratios at different spatial points of the laser detection system. The results showed that as the concentration of cloud particles increased, the probability of photon reception increased, and the intensity of backward scattering increased. Under representative particle number concentration of stratocumulus, cumulus clouds, and cumulonimbus clouds, the probabilities of photons received by laser echoes were 0.49%, 0.26%, and 0.16%, respectively. The backscattering of clouds is not only related to the particle number concentration, but also to the particle size and absorption under different cloud types. The morphology and particle number concentration of multi-scale cloud particles are important factors affecting laser pulse signal backward scattering, which provides a basis for pulse laser detection system to identify cloud phase information for different cloud types and detect particle concentrations.

articleTitle: Design of Multi-Robot Communication and Human-Computer Interaction Interface
abstract: The purpose of this research is to build a multi-robot system, establish an efficient communication process between multiple robots, and enable the system to complete basic functions such as navigation and obstacle avoidance. On the basis of this system, a graphical interface is designed, through which the user can intuitively understand the important information such as the motion state and position state of each robot, and can send preset control commands to realize the real-time control of the robot cluster.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Control-based Equalization of Lithium Battery under Different SOC Distributions
abstract: In order to solve the problem of inconsistent energy in the charging and discharging process of lithium battery pack, this paper proposes an equalization method based on fuzzy logic control (FLC). The state of charge (SOC) of the battery is used as the equalization variable, in the topology of a double-layer equalizing circuit based on inductance, the SOC is weighted to study the performance of the proposed equalization method. In addition, three evaluation criteria (equilibrium time, SOC equalization degree and energy loss) are used to evaluate the performance of the algorithm on four different initial SOC distributions. Finally, the performance of the improved equalization algorithm is compared with the mean difference algorithm and the average SOC value as the input of FLC. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified by simulation data.

articleTitle: Joint Application of Intent Recognition and Slot Filling in Query Question-Answering System for Wind Farm Faults
abstract: Intelligent question-answering systems have significant advantages in the fault querying for wind farms. However, due to the unpredictability of faults in a wind farm and the scarcity of data, some problem-understanding models in such question-answering systems face challenges when dealing with small datasets for a specific task. This is mainly reflected in the lack of flexibility of the models and the need to optimize too many parameters during the fine-tuning phase. Therefore, this paper proposes a joint model of intent recognition and slot filling with an adapter structure based on a robustly optimized bidirectional encoder representations from transformers pre-training approach. The joint model is optimized by fine-tuning the position of the adapter and the reduction factor. The experimental results show that the proposed model significantly improves the accuracy of intent recognition and slot filling subtasks compared with some other joint models, thus confirming its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Control for 4WID-4WIS Electric Vehicles under Steering System Failures
abstract: The four-wheel independent drive and four-wheel independent steering (4WID-4WIS) configuration enhances distributed control in intelligent electric vehicles. As a typical over-actuated system, its application in distributed control can provide various fault-tolerant control solutions to ensure vehicular safety. This paper proposes a hierarchical tire force allocation strategy for the 4WID-4WIS configuration based on constraint optimization. Additionally, it introduces an adaptive fault-tolerant control specifically for steering system failures. When steering failures arise, the fault-tolerant control system discerns the fault and sustains trajectory tracking performance using fuzzy control and control reallocations. Simulation results demonstrate that our strategy maintains trajectory tracking control performance, even under complete steering failures. In contrast, the vehicle loses control without fault-tolerant control, resulting in significant trajectory tracking errors in identical fault scenarios and raising the risk of serious traffic accidents.

articleTitle: Tracking Control for Robot Manipulators Exploiting Time-Delay Estimation
abstract: In this paper, a weak model dependent robust controller is proposed for robot manipulators to address modeling errors and disturbances and then to improve tracking accuracy. Firstly, the mathematical model of the robot manipulator is established according to the Euler–Lagrange equation. To address modeling errors and disturbances, the controller is designed by the time-delay estimation (TDE) method. Besides, in order to further reduce the tracking error, a linear quadratic regulator (LQR) auxiliary controller is designed and then the original error is corrected. In addition, the stability of the closed-loop system is strictly analyzed using the Lyapunov theorem. Finally, a series of experiments is conducted on a 6-DOF robot manipulator. It is shown that the weak model dependent robust controller proposed in this paper tracks the reference trajectory more accurately, and the tracking error is significantly lower than classical controllers. The proposed control method will serve as a reference for controller design of high-precision robot manipulators.

articleTitle: Privacy Preserving-Based Approach for Economic Power Dispatch in a Smart Grid
abstract: The economic power dispatch is a widely recognized optimization issue in a smart grid that intends to minimize the total cost of generation while meeting individual generator constraints and total demand. However, current algorithms fail to protect the private information of individual generators. In this paper, a privacy preserving-based optimization algorithm is proposed for the economic power dispatch problem under directed graphs. By adding carefully designed randomness into optimization dynamics, our proposed algorithm is guaranteed to protect the sensitive information of generators against internal honest-but-curious attackers while achieving the optimal solution. In the end, numerical simulations are shown to illustrate and confirm the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Performance-Oriented Event-Triggered Merging-Following Control of Multi-Lane Vehicles
abstract: This paper focuses on the merging-following control of vehicles standing on different lanes in presence of performance requirements and limited communication resources. A constraint of tracking error is developed to prescribe the performance, and then addressed via error mapping transformation, leading to a prescribed performance control (PPC) algorithm that can make the both distance and angular errors between consecutive vehicles evolve within the prescribed region. Then an event-triggered control protocol driven by the performance function is incorporated to reduce the signal transmission frequency between the controller and actuator with a performance-communication balance. Based on the Lyapunov stability proof, it is verified that all signals in the vehicular system remain uniformly ultimately bounded. A numerical simulation is presented to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Distributed Economic Dispatch Based on Gossip Algorithm in Smart Grid with Time delays
abstract: Due to the prevalence of communication link delay in communication networks, the study of communication delays in smart grids and their impact on economic dispatch is of great practical value. In this paper, a Gossip-based economic dispatch protocol perfected under constant time delay is considered, and it is proved by augmented matrix theory and matrix perturbation theory that a sufficiently small control gain parameter always exists to guarantee the convergence over a constant delay in the communication network. Iterative update rules are given when the neighboring generation units do not receive the initial state due to the time delay to ensure the optimal solution can be obtained. Finally, simulation cases are provided to verify the effectiveness and plug-and-play capability of the algorithm, as well as its feasibility for large-scale systems.

articleTitle: Study on Shoulder Edge Breakage during the CSSCGP Based on MQBNet
abstract: As a crucial step in the Czochralski silicon single crystal growth process (CSSCGP), the shoulder plays a significant role, and the shoulder edge is a vital feature for determining whether the process can smoothly proceed to the next stage. Existing methods for shoulder edge recognition, relying heavily on manual discernment, suffer from issues such as cost inefficiency and low effectiveness. To address this, this paper proposes a data-driven approach for shoulder edge recognition based on Multi-granularity Quadratic convolutional and Broadcast self-attention Network (MQBNet). First, a Quadratic convolutional network (QConv) with strong feature extraction capabilities is adopted to extract fine-grained features from the signals. QConv with different kernel sizes is used to capture features at multiple scales. Subsequently, a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network is used to capture long and short-term dependencies. The broadcast self-attention mechanism is then incorporated to obtain crucial feature information. Finally, the reliability of the model is validated through industrial field data.

articleTitle: Turing Pattern Dynamics of the Oregonator Model Based on PD Control Strategy
abstract: Currently, there have been numerous remarkable achievements in the spatiotemporal dynamics research of chemical reaction-diffusion models. However, the existing literature on the control of spatiotemporal dynamics in these models is quite limited. Therefore, we propose a proportional-derivative (PD) control strategy for effective control of the spatiotemporal dynamics of the Oregonator chemical reaction-diffusion models under the influence of cross-diffusion. This control strategy aims to both suppress Turing instability in the system and induce changes in the pattern structures of the system. In this study, we utilize linear stability analysis to derive conditions for the occurrence of luring instability in the model. Through numerical simulations, we validate the significant impact of the PD controller on the spatiotemporal dynamics of the model.

articleTitle: Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Using Enhanced Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Networks
abstract: Accurate and timely forecasting of photovoltaic (PV) power generation is essential for ensuring the stability of power systems. Traditional studies often overlook the impact of anomalous information on PV power due to the inherent uncertainty and variability in solar and weather conditions. In this study, we propose a model that combines Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) with an attention mechanism to improve the capability of predicting anomalous information in PV power generation. The developed model is implemented on a 1 MW PV power station, and the results demonstrate the method’s effectiveness in achieving accuracy and adaptability compared to existing approaches. This research addresses the challenges in PV power prediction and contributes to the ongoing efforts for a sustainable energy future.

articleTitle: Network Traffic Intrusion Detection Based on Multi-Scale Convolution and Enhanced Temporal Convolution
abstract: In order to enhance the accuracy of network traffic intrusion detection and address the issues of complexity and lengthy training associated with traditional models for network traffic intrusion detection, this paper proposes a hybrid intrusion detection model that integrates Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN). The approach employs Multi-Scale One-Dimensional Convolution (MSC) and an improved Temporal Convolutional Network with Attention Mechanism (TCNAG) for spatial and temporal feature extraction learning. Finally, the model is trained and utilized for detection by combining it with a SoftMax classifier. TCNAG introduces an attention mechanism after the residual blocks of the traditional TCN and replaces the conventional fully connected layers with a global average pooling layer to avoid parameter redundancy, thus reducing the model's detection time. Experimental evaluations conducted on the UNSW-NB15 Dataset demonstrate that the proposed hybrid model exhibits lower time consumption and superior performance metrics compared to other commonly used algorithms.

articleTitle: Predefined-Time Synchronization of Coupled Different Dimensional Neural Networks
abstract: This paper aims to study the predefined-time synchronization of coupled different dimensional neural networks (CDDNNs). Firstly, by designing appropriate controller and Lyapunov functional, a sufficient condition for the predefined-time synchronization for the CDDNNs without time-varying delays is established. Secondly, we derive a predefined-time synchronization criterion for CDDNNs with time-varying delays by constructing another novel controller and using some inequality techniques. Finally, the accuracy of the synchronization conditions is verified by an example with MATLAB simulation results.

articleTitle: A Restricted Resampling Algorithm of Particle Filter for Gmapping
abstract: Gmapping is a method that estimates the movement trajectory of a robot through particle filter and builds maps. Resampling is important process for Gmapping which can make effective particles replace ineffective particles. Selective resampling algorithm determines whether to perform resampling in gmapping by comparing the dispersion of normalized particle weights with a set threshold. But this method results in some ineffective particles being computed for a long time before resampling, which affects the mapping accuracy and stability. To address this issue, this paper proposes a restricted resampling algorithm to strengthen the weight of effective particles and weaken the weight of ineffective particles, and then compute the dispersion of normalized particle weights. Experimental results indicate that restricted resampling produces maps more accuracy and stability than the selective resampling, with clearer textures and outlines.

articleTitle: Convolutional and Transformer Fusion Network Based on Cross-Attention for Occluded Person Re-identification
abstract: Occluded person re-identification studies the problem of cross-camera retrieval of pedestrians in occluded scenarios, which faces problems of insufficient feature representation and low retrieval accuracy. Most existing methods are based on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) methods, which design different network structures and modules, but none of them can avoid the long-range dependency problem caused by the insufficient global receptive field that always exists in CNN-based methods. With the effective application of transformer in vision (ViT), some pure transformer schemes have also been proposed to accomplish the task of occluded person re-identification problem, but they are still deficient in achieving translation invariance. Considering this situation, this paper proposes a Convolutional and Transformer Fusion Network (CTF-Net) that combines the advantages of the above two types of methods, which utilizes the cross-attention block to interactively fuse semantic information between CNN features and ViT sequences, and obtains pedestrian features that are more robust and representative in dealing with occlusion interference. Experimental results show that our method not only outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods on occluded person re-identification datasets, but also has excellent performance on general person re-identification datasets, demonstrating its strong robustness against occlusion interference, as well as good generalization performance and excellent application scenario scalability.

articleTitle: Multi-objective robust PID controller tuning using state transition algorithm
abstract: In many control systems, achieving high accuracy, rapid response, and robustness depends on the precise configuration of controller parameters. This is particularly true for Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controllers, widely used in various applications for their efficiency and adaptability. However, the tuning of these parameters becomes challenging due to conflicting control performance requirements, particularly in uncertain multi-input multi-output (MIMO) systems. In this paper, the PID controller design problem is formulated as a multi-objective optimization problem (MOP) by minimizing balanced robust performance criteria and integral squared error (ISE). The multi-objective state transition algorithm (MOSTA) is applied to solve the MOP and obtain Pareto optimal solutions, representing the optimal trade-offs among conflicting objectives. Then, the parameters of a robust PID controller are determined for a MIMO system by using a visualizing multi-attribute decision-making (V-MADA) approach, achieving a more comprehensive evaluation and a better understanding of the decision-making process. The efficacy of this multi-objective robust PID controller design is demonstrated through its application to the supper maneuverable F18/HARV fighter aircraft. The results show that the PID controller designed by MOSTA and V-MADM exhibits superior robustness. The proposed method offers valuable insights for various engineering applications that require the design of robust PID controllers with multiple performance objectives.

articleTitle: Android Monitoring Application Development Based on Suspension Durability Testing System Cloud Platform
abstract: The suspension durability testing system is a fundamental tool to simulate the actual working condition and complete the durability fatigue life testing of the indoor automotive air suspension. The cloud platform of the suspension durability testing system makes it possible to carry out remote desktop monitoring of the system. However, due to its intrinsic monitoring attributes, the scope of the application is limited. In this paper, we develop an Android mobile monitoring Application, By analyzing the principle and requirements of the cloud platform, we extensively design the status monitoring and state control function of the mobile terminal to the testing system. Specifically, we utilize the synergy of the JDBC interface and MQTT communication protocol to realize the system. The testing results show that the development of the Android application of the suspension durability testing cloud platform can accurately reflect the operation status of the system, and can load and control the testing system in time, which achieves the expected development effect.

Author Keywords: the suspension durability testing cloud platform

articleTitle: Linear/Quadratic Decomposition and Chaotic Features of the Lorenz Systems
abstract: This note talks about linear and quadratic decomposition remodeling and chaotic trajectories of the continuous-time Lorenz systems. More precisely, the Lorenz state-space differential equations are equivalently divided into linear and quadratic terms, based on which chaos dynamics are revisited by modifying or weighting the quadratic term and checking sign variation, respectively. The study shows that the quadratic term plays a key role in chaotic trajectories and behaviours of the Lorenz systems, which are summarized as a chaos conjecture, together with observation arguments and examples. Illustrations clearly reveal efficacy of the suggested linear/quadratic decomposition approach for chaos analysis.

articleTitle: Design and optimization of DC-DC Converter Based on Soft-Switching Control Strategy for special vehicle
abstract: This paper optimises the design of a bi-directional DC-DC converter to be more compatible with the characteristics of the special vehicles' on-board grid. Utilising the four-switch Buck-Boost (FSBB) DC-DC converter, link to soft-switching technology, a bidirectional DC-DC Converter is put forward based on a parameter adaptive soft-switching control strategy. The FSBB converter’s conventional control strategy has been summarized to address the challenge of achieving high efficiency, power density and dynamic response over a wide input voltage range. This converter work for a connection between the DC bus of high voltage and the energy storage system, which can be adjust for power batteries and supercapacitors. We propose a soft-switching control strategy based on parameter adaptation and test it using MATLAB/Simulink. In the experimental part, the FSBB converter enables Zero Voltage Switch (ZVS) of four switching tubes over the full operating voltage range and is suitable for special vehicle on-board grids with good dynamic performance at high frequencies.

articleTitle: A predefined-time resilient control for cyber-physical systems against false data injection attacks*
abstract: A novel adaptive predefined-time resilient control is proposed for cyber-physical systems with stealthy false data injection attacks. As the sensors are attacked by ill-disposed hackers, the state information cannot be measured exactly. The system dynamic of the compromised states is deduced theoretically, characterized by nonlinear uncertainty dynamics and unknown control directions at the last step. In the framework of backstepping recursive procedures, an adaptive resilient controller is developed, the stability time and convergence accuracy of the output tracking error can be preset by controller gains. Especially, the Nussbaum functions are adopted at the last step in the adaptive control. Finally, a numerical example is conducted to verify that the proposed control can provide a favorable predefine time stabilization performance.

articleTitle: Possibilistic c-Means Clustering Algorithms Based on Adaptive Nearest Neighbors
abstract: Possibility C-Means Clustering (PCM) removes the constraint of FCM on membership degree. However, the traditional PCM algorithm tends to encounter coincidence cluster problems during clustering, and its performance is poor when dealing with unbalanced data. To solve the problem of PCM algorithm, this paper proposes a novel algorithm called Possibilistic c-Means Clustering Algorithm Based on Adaptive Nearest Neighbors (PCM-AN). Integrating the CAN model, PCMAN introduces robustness weights to the compatibility degree between sample points and clustering centers, enhancing the local robustness of the model. Utilizing the sparse structural features of adaptive neighbors, PCM-AN emphasizes the divisibility between distinct data clusters. Consequently, PCM-AN algorithm excels in highlighting the relationship within data structures and enhancing separability among various data clusters. In this paper, an artificial two-dimensional dataset, UCI standard test datasets, and image datasets are used for experiments. The experimental results demonstrate that the clustering performance of PCM-AN algorithm has obvious advantages over other improved PCM algorithms.

articleTitle: Multi-Robot Path Planning for Sweep Coverage On 2-D Area
abstract: In this paper, the sweep coverage on a 2-D area is studied by utilizing multi-robot. Based on spatial resolution requirements and sensor sensing capabilities, the target area can be discretized into multiple grids to be covered. The sweep coverage of an area can be transferred into a multi-robot coverage path planning problem (mCPP). In order to solve this problem with less optimization computational cost, a novel partitioning method is firstly proposed to divide the target area into sub-areas, and an improved spanning tree coverage algorithm is then proposed to solve the path planning of a single robot covering its sub-area. Finally, the simulation results are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Streaming Media Load Balancing with Improved Genetic Algorithm
abstract: The load balancing algorithm of streaming media server is facing unique challenges. Different from the traditional Web server, the streaming media server needs to consider the characteristics of real-time, bandwidth occupation and multimedia data transmission. Therefore, the traditional load balancing algorithm is not necessarily suitable for streaming media servers, and needs special design and research. Aiming at the network requests of streaming media server clusters, a multi-dimensional matrix evaluation method based on streaming media characteristics is proposed, the genetic algorithm is improved, and it is applied to the dynamic load balancing algorithm scheduling scenario, and analyzed and simulated. Experimental results show that the algorithm can effectively reduce the average execution time of all requests, speed up the average response time and improve throughput.

articleTitle: A Human Motion Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv5s and ST-GCN
abstract: Aiming at the problem that existing human motion detection algorithms have low recognition accuracy on complex backgrounds, this paper proposes a human action recognition algorithm based on improved YOLOv5s and ST-GCN. Firstly, based on YOLOV5s, the human body is extracted by adding a saliency (SANet) module, adding a convolutional attention (CBAM) module, and replacing the loss function to the original network. Secondly, the Alphapose algorithm was used to extract the key points of human bones and input them into the Spatiotemporal graph Convolution network (ST-GCN) to complete the action recognition. Meanwhile, in order to increase the model’s ability of capturing the tiny human actions, the Channel Attention (SENet) module is added on the basis of ST-GCN network. Experiments show that the fusion algorithm can effectively improve the recognition of human behaviors in different scenes, especially the detection of head movements, and the effect is obvious, about 15.3%. The detection of arm movements is the best, with a top5 accuracy of 99%.

articleTitle: An Automatic and Active Fire Protection Self-control Non-Blaze Surrounding System
abstract: To address the challenges posed by the potential toxicity and slow response of traditional fire suppression systems in high-security areas such as archives and museums, this study presents the design of an active fire suppression oxygen reduction automatic control system, hereinafter referred to as the Non-Blaze Surrounding system. This system consists of a nitrogen production module, an environmental monitoring module and is capable of real-time adjustment of oxygen levels within the space. By reducing the supply of oxygen, the possibility of fire occurrence is diminished while also safeguarding personnel. Experiments conducted in a custom-designed storage facility for cultural relics demonstrated the system’s ability to stabilize oxygen concentration at 16%, thereby validating its functionality and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Multi-objective flexible job shop scheduling based on Pareto quantum particle swarm optimization algorithm
abstract: The single particle swarm algorithm exhibits deficiencies in optimality, diversity, and convergence speed when addressing the multi-objective optimal scheduling problem in flexible job shops. In this research, we introduce a multi-objective Pareto quantum particle swarm algorithm. To aviod the algorithm falling into the problem of local convergence, three initialization strategies are proposed to enhance population quality. Additionally, a crowding degree mechanism is employed to enhance the distribution of the Pareto front, thus improving solution diversity and quality. Experimental results on Kacem and Mk standard examples validate the efficiency of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Minimum entropy control of COT distribution in feeding process of industrial ethylene cracker
abstract: Industrial ethylene crackers have many tubes. It is difficult to control each tube COT (Coil Outlet Temperature) accurately. The traditional feeding operation in the industrial ethylene cracker is to form a cascade control structure with PID controllers, where the average COT of multiple tubes is chosen as the master control loop and the fuel gas flow rate is chosen as the slave control loop. The good average COT control result cannot guarantee the small COT deviation of each tube. Uneven COT distribution may cause process limit violation and prolong the feeding process. Therefore, it is important to control the COT distribution evenly in the feeding process. In this work, to address the problem of uneven distribution of COT in the feeding process, an advanced COT distribution control method is proposed. The fuel gas flow rate is regarded as the manipulated variable of the COT distribution, and the probability density function (PDF) model is applied to describe the distribution of COT. The PDF model based minimum entropy controller has been developed and solved with Bayesian Optimization (BO). The simulation and industrial application results have verified the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Building Recognition of Aerial Images Based on Improved Unet Network
abstract: Due to its simple and efficient design, the Unet network has demonstrated outstanding performance in the field of building identification. Compared to other networks, the Unet network has higher flexibility and detailing capabilities when dealing with buildings with complex contours and irregular shapes. In this paper, a novel Unet structure is proposed to improve the accuracy of building recognition. An attention mechanism is added to the lateral skip connections of the Unet network, which combines different levels of information to enhance the signals in the region of interest.The original convolutional layer module in the feature extraction part is re-parameterised to a symmetric convolutional structure, so that the model obtains better feature expression. And a dilated convolutional module of different sizes is added at the end of the feature extraction to enlarge the receptive field. The experimental results show that the proposed method is effective in segmenting building images. The pixel segmentation accuracy reaches 94.5% and the intersection of union is 85.71%.Both of them are better than the traditional Unet network.

articleTitle: Generalized Extended State Observer Based Control of Hydraulic Active Suspension System With Quantization
abstract: This paper studies the generalized extended control problem of the hydraulic active suspension system with quantization. The aim of this paper is to design a generalized extended state observer to estimate the unmeasurable state and to design a controller using the estimated value to make the hydraulic active suspension system reach the control target under the influences of the quantized input signal and the quantized output signal. Moreover, considering that road disturbances do not match the input channels, special controller matrices are used to prevent disturbances from having a direct effect on the controlled output channels. Finally, an example simulation of the quarter-vehicle hydraulic active suspension system is given to verify the validity of the designed controller.

articleTitle: A GRU-based Time-Space reconstruction network for dome temperature prediction of hot blast stove
abstract: Neural network soft sensor methods are widely used in industrial process quality prediction.
