Currently, gatecontrolled neural networks with long short-term memory capabilities are effective in dealing with non-linear time series data in industry to predict important variables. However, the actual industrial processes are complex and involve numerous variables. The simple gated recurrent GRU unit cannot effectively handle features with varying information loads in neural networks. Therefore, this paper proposes a GRU-based time-space reconstruction neural network (TSR-GRU). The network can reconstruct the features from two dimensions of time and space, and it can adaptively assign different weights to different features to enhance the feature extraction ability of the network. Finally, the network proposed in this paper is applied to the dome temperature prediction of hot blast stove, which verifies the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Obstacle Avoidance of Manipulator Based on Artificial Potential Field in Joint Space
abstract: In order to reach the target pose with the least amount of joint motion and implement the obstacle avoidance, an improved artificial potential field (APF) for the manipulator in the joint space is proposed in this study. The kinematic model of the manipulator is established by using the modified D-H method. The simplified model of manipulator and obstacles are established, and the potential collision detection algorithm is realized by analyzing the relative position relationship. The potential field gravity is mapped in the joint space, and the potential field repulsion received by each connecting rod is decomposed into the first three joint spaces for potential field force synthesis, so as to reach the target pose under the guidance of resultant force. The proposed APF algorithm is validated by the experiments on the UR3e manipulator.

articleTitle: Dynamic event-triggered control for fractional-order multi-agent systems
abstract: This paper investigates the predefined-time leader-following consensus for fractional-order multi-agent systems. Under the fractional-order distributed dynamic event-trigger control scheme, sufficient consensus criteria of fractional-order multi-agent systems are established. In addition, the absence of Zeno phenomenon is illustrated by employing contradiction approach. A simulation example is presented to imply the efficacy of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: The Multi-formation tracking of multi-UAVs subject to communication delays utilizing impulsive control
abstract: This paper concerns on the problem of multi-formation tracking for multi-UAVs with communication delays. Dividing the multi-UAVs into several subgroups, in each of which the followers are desired to maintain the predefined geometric formations and move as a whole simultaneously with their own leader. According to Lyapunov stability theory, the control objective is proven to be achieved theoretically under some certain conditions by utilizing the impulsive strategy. Finally, our theoretical results are illustrated effectively by conducting a numerical example.

articleTitle: Research on Collaborative Control and Path Planning Methods for Surface and Underwater Multi-agent Systems
abstract: In this paper, we study the path planning and control problem in surface and underwater multi-agent systems, propose a formation control method for efficient obstacle avoidance, and combine it with path planning to realize formation work. Firstly, an affine formation control algorithm for surface-underwater collaborative control is designed to realize the maneuvering control of the formation. Three obstacle avoidance schemes are proposed for effective obstacle avoidance based on the various obstacle distributions. Then, global path planning is carried out on the target area, and local path planning is carried out by using the A* algorithm combined with the obstacle avoidance strategy, and the results of the planning are optimized according to the demand. Finally, the effectiveness of the method is verified by simulation experiments.

articleTitle: A Preliminary Study on a Common Control Structure in the Water Supply Industry
abstract: The residual chlorine Concentration of outlet water from Drinking Water Treatment Plants (DWTP) is an important indicator for drinking water. However, it is currently common that even if the chlorine system has an automatic dosing function, manual intervention is still required. In the chlorine renovation project, Nantong Water Group attempted to solve this problem. During the process, a control structure diagram was drawn based on its actual situation. However, no control method research has been found for the control structure where the main feedback is controlled externally and the secondary feedbacks are controlled internally. Therefore, this paper aims to communicate with professionals and enhance their attention to this structure. Also, this paper proposes a control method for this structure, which has shown excellent practical application results.

articleTitle: Weighted Fusion Robust Fractional Order Kalman Filter with Correlated Noise
abstract: The research results of Kalman filter can be applied in many fields such as weather forecasting, satellite positioning, aerospace and so on. The traditional Kalman filter generally considers mostly integer-order systems, while the Kalman filter estimation using fractional-order systems can obtain estimates closer to the real system, thus reducing the actual system error. In this paper, for the fractional-order system with uncertain noise variance and noise correlation, model transformation is carried out to transform the correlated noise of the fractional-order system into uncorrelated noise. Then a locally robust Kalman filter is proposed for this system, and the system with multiple sensors is weighted by matrix-weighted fusion method for weighted state fusion. The simulation results show that the algorithm is effective and feasible.

articleTitle: Data-driven Dissipativity Analysis of Perturbed Linear Time-invariant Systems
abstract: In this article, we consider the data-driven dissipativity analysis of perturbed linear time-invariant (LTI) systems. Both cases are considered when input-state trajectories and input-output trajectories are available, and the dissipative conditions are provided respectively. Compared with existing studies under the assumption of additive noise, we consider the case where system matrices contain some uncertainty, and we also derive a detailed discussion of the constructed input-output-equivalent system. A numerical simulation is provided to verify the effectiveness of theoretical result.

articleTitle: A LiDAR-Inertial Odometry by Fusing Adjacent Frames with Point Selection
abstract: LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) is the most commonly used sensor for autonomous driving. Spinning LiDAR is fabricated by stacking laser emitters and receivers in the vertical direction to form a 3D LiDAR, resulting in a low vertical resolution. Geometric features may be lost during scanning. The issue will be worsened in outdoor situations where the LiDAR is measuring over long distances. To address this issue, we propose a novel LiDAR-inertial Odometry (LiO) system that utilizes two frames of point cloud simultaneously, providing additional geometric information. Firstly, the previous frame’s point cloud is evaluated to determine whether it should be used, based on a set velocity threshold. Then, two frames are projected onto the same momentary coordinate system for point cloud de-distortion. To reduce the computational burden of processing two frames simultaneously, we have adopted a point selection approach. During the process of optimizing iterations, the points used to calculate residuals and construct maps are selected to achieve a balance between accuracy and efficiency. The method proposed in this study is based on the LIO-SAM implementation and has been tested on the KITTI and M2DGR datasets. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method enhances the localization accuracy and reduces the run time.

articleTitle: A Multimodal Genetic Algorithm based Parameter Optimization Method for Flight Control System
abstract: Many engineers face challenges in parameter design and adjustment for complex systems with internal implicit relationships, particularly in flight control systems. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often struggle to fully consider the system's pre-constraints. This paper proposes a multimodal parameter design algorithm aimed at exploring the solution space comprehensively. It addresses the non-convexity of the solution space in the parameter design process of carrier-based aircraft flight control systems, as well as the challenge of reaching the global optimum due to multiple constraints. The algorithm leverages the mutual attraction and repulsion characteristics of genetic algorithm evolution. Additionally, it utilizes niche technology based on the K-means clustering algorithm, enabling multiple populations to search their respective spaces and obtain feasible solutions in different regions of the solution space. This approach facilitates exploration of feasible parameter regions and their relationships within the flight system, while also providing insights into the characteristics of the solution space.

articleTitle: Mach Number Prediction of Wind Tunnel Flow Field Based on RBFNN and LSTM
abstract: With the development of aerodynamics, wind tunnel experiment has become an important part of aircraft development in aerospace, automobile manufacturing, bridge construction and other fields. In the process of wind tunnel experiment, the speed and accuracy of Mach number prediction directly affect the quality of wind tunnel, which needs to be accurately predicted and controlled. In this paper, a RBFNN model is adopted as the structure of Mach number prediction model for steady wind tunnel flow field, and a LSTM-based Mach number time series prediction model is established for dynamic data.

articleTitle: Research on Path Tracking Optimal Control of Two-wheel Mobile Robot Based on Adaptive Dynamic Programming
abstract: Wheeled robots are widely used in production and service. However, how to improve the stability and accuracy of tracking and reduce energy consumption has always been a problem that needs to be improved in the field of mobile robots. In order to solve these problems, we designed a path tracking controller for two wheeled mobile robot based on Adaptive Dynamic Programming. Firstly, Action Dependent Heuristic Dynamic Programming structure that meets the tracking control requirements is selected; then the path tracking control system of the two wheeled mobile robot based on the execution dependent heuristic dynamic planning is designed; finally, the system tracks the circular path to test the controller performance. The experimental results show that the control system designed in this paper has better tracking accuracy, faster convergence speed and can reduce the energy consumption in the control process.

articleTitle: Dynamic Task Planning: An Integrated Approach with Scene Relation Perception and Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Confronted with the limitations of conventional Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) in dynamic and unpredictable kitchen environments, this paper introduces a novel task planning methodology that leverages the synergy between advanced scene graphs. This interdisciplinary approach begins with the construction of a detailed task directive-target state dataset, which serves as the foundation for refining the capabilities of VisualBERT, a vision-language model. Through fine-tuning, VisualBERT becomes adept at accurately interpreting complex scene dynamics and anticipating the target states to achieve the task query. This is followed by the creation of an extensive knowledge graph containing important parameters of actions and objects. This knowledge base is instrumental in generating PDDL domain and problem files, taking into account both initial and target states. It plays a crucial role in the flexible subtask sequence generation for dynamic environments and tasks. Our proposed method significantly enhances the adaptability to real-world variability, thereby enabling dynamic task planning within domestic kitchen environments efficiently.

articleTitle: Research on defect detection method of automotive running lights based on keypoint identification
abstract: As a novel type of automotive signal light, running lights are gradually being utilized in automobiles. In view of the defect characteristics of automotive running lights, this paper proposes a method for accurately locating the defective parts through the detection of keypoints. Based on YOLOv7, a keypoint detection network called YOLO-kpt specialized for automotive running lights is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the network incorporates PConv to replace some conventional convolutions, effectively reducing the number of parameters. Secondly, a new convolutional calculation module called ResPC is proposed, inspired by the advantages of residual networks, which integrates PConv. Lastly, YOLO-kpt employs two SPPCSPC modules to further enhance the network’s feature extraction capability. Experiments carried out using a self-built dataset show that the YOLO-kpt proposed in this paper is able to accurately detect the defective parts of automotive running lights with an average Euclidean distance of only 1.8383 pixels for the keypoints error.

articleTitle: Consensus Problem Based on the Hierarchical Control for Multi-Quadrotor UAVs
abstract: This paper considers the consistent cooperative control of multi-quadrotor UAVs with virtual leader under general directed graph. Based on the hierarchical control, a novel controller, depended on location, velocity and acceleration information of the neighbors in a directed topology, is proposed for multi-quadrotor UAVs. Moreover, the coupling term between position and attitude system is processed by the scaling principle. Finally, the consensus control of five quadrotor UAVs is tested, which verifies that the designed controller is effective and can achieve control objectives.

articleTitle: The Melanoma Object Detection Based on the Improved YOLOv5s Lightweight Bidirectional Feature Fusion Network
abstract: Melanoma is a malignant skin tumor. In order to improve its detection accuracy as well as reduce its hardware requirements for medical diagnosis, a lightweight bidirectional feature fusion network based on the improved YOLOv5s is proposed. Firstly, in order to enhance the feature extraction capability from melanoma images, we integrate the SimAM attention and Ghost module into a fused module in order to replace the original feature extraction module in YOLOv5s. Then, a bidirectional feature pyramid network structure is added to enhance the network’s feature fusion performance for melanoma feature. In final, the involution neural network operator is introduced to reduce the network’s redundancy. The Experimental results show that the improved YOLOv5s achieves a 5.8% higher mean average precision compared to the original YOLOv5s model. Its accuracy of benign melanoma detection increases 6%, and accuracy of malignant melanoma detection increases 5.5%. Also, the proposed model’s size is only 4.6M that obtains a 68.1% reduction from the original YOLOv5s model size. Therefore, the improved YOLOv5s can enhance the melanoma’s detection performance and thus is more suitable for deployment on medical equipment.

articleTitle: High Precision Camera Calibration Method Based on Full Camera Model
abstract: In existing camera calibration methods, the principal point coordinates are commonly treated as the distortion center. However, in reality, the principal point coordinates and the distortion center are not strictly identical. Failing to distinguish between them can lead to a reduction in the accuracy of camera parameter calibration. Based on this, a high-precision camera calibration method based on full camera model is proposed. This method comprises the following steps: Firstly, the initial camera parameters are obtained using the Zhang Zhengyou calibration method. Secondly, based on the camera's internal and external parameters, the centers of circles in the image and in the world coordinate system are projected onto the normalized plane to obtain the actual and ideal points of the circle's center on the normalized plane. The actual point on the normalized plane is then corrected using the full camera model. Next, the distortion center and distortion parameters are calculated from the positional relationship between the actual point and the ideal point on the normalized plane. Subsequently, the corrected actual points on the normalized plane are projected back onto the image plane, and camera calibration is performed again. Finally, high precision camera calibration is achieved after several iterations of projection and calibration. Experimental results demonstrate that this method significantly enhances the accuracy of camera calibration.

articleTitle: Dynamic event-triggered bipartite fixed-time consensus control of delayed multi-agent systems with general directed typologies
abstract: In this paper, for a class of first-order nonlinear multi-agent systems(MASs) with input delay, the fixed time binary consensus problem under general directed graph is studied, and a fixed time consensus(FTC) protocol based on dynamic event-trigger mechanism is proposed. The system state converges to two values of the same numerical value but opposite sign in a fixed time, and the upper bound of the convergence time does not depend on the initial state. Finally, a simulation example verifies the validity of the proposed fixed time binary consensus algorithm and the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Hybrid vector-based predictive current control strategy for three-phase L-shaped grid-connected photovoltaic inverters
abstract: With aims to address the problems of high total harmonic distortion (THD) and incomplete voltage vector control range of the traditional two-vector and three-vector grid side current control, this paper proposes a hybrid multi-vector predictive current control strategy (HMPC). The control strategy merges the optimum combined voltage vectors from two-vector and three-vector control. These two voltage vectors serve as the fundamental variables for the predictive current control of the two-vector model, which predicts the current’s future value. Technical term abbreviations will be defined upon first use. The strategy comprises of four essential voltage vectors per control cycle (three effective voltages for bi-vector control and one for tri-vector control). At a reference current of 10A, the current harmonic distortion rate of the hybrid multivector control is lower than that of bi-vector and tri-vector controls (2.98% for bi-vector, 2.48% for tri-vector, and 1.13% for hybrid multivector), making it more robust.

articleTitle: Model predictive control for hydrogen production system of pyrolytic gas production
abstract: In order to solve the problem of low thermodynamic efficiency of traditional steam-enhanced reforming reaction systems, this paper uses Aspen Plus<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> software for chemical process simulation to build a complete process for hydrogen production from pyrolysis gas. It conducts detailed modeling of gas purification, enhanced reforming, calcination and regeneration, dehydration and drying, pressure swing adsorption(PSA) and other units. The model predictive control(MPC) is designed according to the optimal parameter ratio. The simulation results show that compared with the traditional proportion integration differentiation(PID) control, under the same feed condition, the response time of the MPC controller is reduced by 390s and 186s, respectively, under the step response and slope response tracking curves. The MPC controller’s IAE(Integral Absolute Error) value is minor, and the control effect is better than the PID controller. The enhanced reforming hydrogen production system of pyrolysis gas combined with MPC control can realize the stable operation of the system and higher energy efficiency. It can be used as one of the ways to produce hydrogen from gas at present and has specific practical application value.

articleTitle: Research on weight prediction method based on IJSOA-BPNN for cigarette filter rod
abstract: The weight of filter rods is an important indicator for monitoring the production quality of cigarette filter rods. This paper proposes a prediction method for filter rod weight, which is based on IJSOA-BPNN. The improved jumping spider optimization algorithm (IJSOA) is used to adjust the threshold value of the BP neural network to compensate for its susceptibility to local optimum. The trained BP is applied to the prediction model to predict the weight of the next moment of the filter rod forming machine. The results show that the proposed algorithm achieves the specifications including RMSE of 1.6159, MAPE of 0.0018, and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 93.35%, which are superior to BPNN and JSO-BPNN in terms of prediction accuracy and stability.

articleTitle: Delay-Dependent Stability Analysis and Controller Design for LFC System under Hybrid Attacks
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of load frequency control (LFC) for power systems with electric vehicle (EV) under hybrid attacks, including time-delay attacks (TDA) and denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. The open network communication environment makes the LFC system vulnerable to cyber attacks. First, a multiple time-varying delay linear model of the LFC system with EV under hybrid attack is modeled. Then, a less conservative asymptotic stability criterion is proposed through the Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional (LKF) and delay-dependent region partitioning approach. Additionally, the output feedback controller gain problem is also solved by the convex optimization method. Finally, a numerical example and the LFC model system are exploited to illustrate the effectiveness and superiority of the theoretical results.

articleTitle: VRU Detection Based on Inverse Perspective Mapping and Deep Learning in Lightweight Embedded System
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for real-time detection and warning of vulnerable road users (VRU) in lightweight embedded systems, enhancing the efficiency of Bird's Eye View (BEV) image stitching. By exploiting the geometrical characteristics of image mapping, a rapid BEV transformation method is proposed, aiming at effectively detecting VRU in front of the vehicle. Central to this approach is the innovative combination of image distortion and inverse perspective mapping into a unified map through a specially designed map fusion algorithm. This fusion not only streamlines the BEV stitching process but also aligns the size of the EBV image with the input requirements of the detection model, thereby reducing preprocessing time and computational load. Empirical results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly reduces time consumption by approximately eight times compared to traditional method, marking a notable advancement in the field of real-time VRU detection for intelligent driving systems.

articleTitle: Improved compressed sensing channel estimation algorithm for MIMO-OFDM systems
abstract: The signals in MIMO-OFDM systems have good sparsity characteristics, and the channel estimation problem can be transformed into a sparse signal recovery problem using compressed sensing theory. This paper proposes an adaptive compressed sampling matching and tracking algorithm based on zebra optimization (ZOA-CoSaMP), which utilizes the ZOA algorithm to optimize the atomic matching process of the CoSaMP algorithm. The generalized Jaccard coefficient is used for atomic secondary screening to improve the recovery accuracy, Simultaneously introducing a power function type variable step size strategy to achieve sparsity adaptation. Finally, it was demonstrated through experimental simulation that compared to the CoSaMP algorithm, this algorithm has better estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: Nonlinear disturbance rejection control for quadrotor attitude via finite-time state observer
abstract: In this article, to improve disturbance rejection characteristics and implement fast-tracking of angles, a nonlinear disturbance rejection control for quadrotor attitude via finite-time state observer is studied with an inner-outer loop control framework. In the inner loop system, a finite-time nonlinear disturbance observer (FTNDO) and a controller with robust control law are employed to estimate and compensate the disturbances, respectively. The finite-time technology is used to improve the convergence rate of the system. Additionally, a composite nonlinear feedback controller (CNFC) is devised for the outer loop to improve transient performance. The stability of both loops is analyzed individually, and the effectiveness of the proposed approach is verified through numerical simulations and platform experiments.

articleTitle: Aperiodically Intermittent Control Synchronization of Coupled Complex-Valued Neural Networks
abstract: In this paper, coupled complex-valued neural networks (CCVNNs) are considered. Two types of aperiodically intermittent control schemes are designed to ensure synchro-nization of CCVNNs with and without time-varying delays respectively. By utilizing some novel inequality techniques and Lyapunov stability theory, several intermittent synchronization criteria are established. Finally, a numerical example is given to demonstrate the effectiveness and correctness of the obtained theoretical results.

articleTitle: Secure Strategy Design for Networked Control Systems under Multiple Cyber-attacks over a Multi-channel Framework
abstract: This article is concerned with the secure strategy design for a class of discrete-time linear networked control systems subject to multiple cyber-attacks over a multi-channel framework. The multiple cyber-attacks discussed are groups of different attacks, which are random in sequence and can happen in any channel independently or simultaneously. No priority and duration limits are required for each type of attack in the multiple cyber-attacks, the dynamics of which are modeled by a Markovian chain. Moreover, a Bernoulli process is introduced to describe the channel conditions under attacks. A secure strategy based on Markovian-based observer is designed to guarantee the stability of the system with the ability to resist interference and adapt to multiple cyber-attacks. Finally, simulations are presented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Bispectrum analysis and Convolutional Neural Network Based Feature Extraction and Classification
abstract: Presently, the dominant technologies in device condition detection is to analyze ID vibration signals from time domain, frequency domain, or time-frequency domain. Based on statistical feature parameters calculation or adaptive features extraction, feature mining and condition classification is achieved. However, the initial signs of equipment failure are indistinct, and the characteristic frequency of the vibration signal itself is very weak and sparse. Moreover, with noise interference, the SNR (Signal-to-Noise Ratio) of the signal is quite low, which increases the difficulty of characteristic information mining for ID vibration signals. Therefore, in order to address these issues and fully utilize the phase information of condition signals, in this paper, a feature extraction and classification scheme based on bispectrum analysis and convolutional neural network is constructed. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of this scheme, providing a reference for device health condition recognition.

Index Terms: Activation Function Of The Hidden Layer

articleTitle: An improved Siamese network for object tracking with graph network and attention mechanism
abstract: Object tracking is an important and challenging task in computer vision. However, most tracking algorithms are susceptible to challenges such as appearance variation and complex background. To improve the tracking performance, a Siamese network for object tracking with graph convolutional network and attention mechanism is proposed. Graph convolutional network can aggregate feature information from neighboring nodes, and the attention mechanism can improve the weight of critical features of the target in the tracker. Extensive experimental results on the Object Tracking Benchmark (OTB) datasets validate the advantages of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A heterogeneous multi-UAV task allocation method based on extended CBBA
abstract: Task allocation is one of the key issues of UAV mission execution, the Consensus Based Bundle Algorithm (CBBA) can solve the problem of single UAV multi-task allocation, whereas the traditional CBBA can only be assigned to one UAV for each target. We extend the CBBA to the case of multiple UAVs executing a single target, and expand the homogeneous UAVs to heterogeneous UAVs with different functions of reconnaissance and strike, proposing an improved CBBA with dual replication of the reconnaissance/strike UAVs and targets separately, in order to solve the task allocation problem of UAVs carrying heterogeneous airborne reconnaissance and strike equipments. Simulation results show that the proposed extended CBBA can well solve the heterogeneous multi-UAV coalition executing multi-task allocation problem.

articleTitle: OIPQ: A feature extraction algorithm based on ORB, Image Pyramid, and Quadtree Partition
abstract: The front-end feature extraction part of the ORB-SLAM2 algorithm extracts feature points through the use of a fixed resolution size grid for each layer of the pyramid image, causing the loss of some high-quality feature points and thus affecting the effectiveness of feature point matching. In the ORB-SLAM2, the feature selection method used is an approach based on the division of quadtrees, which suffers from a too-deep division, resulting in the poor real-time performance of the overall algorithm. To solve these problems, this paper come up with a feature extraction algorithm (OIPQ) based on ORB, Image Pyramid, and Quadtree Partition. It dynamically adjusts the grid size based on the number of feature points allocated in each layer of the image pyramid and also restricts the quadtree partitioning depth based on the number of feature points in each layer. These improvements aim to enhance the algorithm’s efficiency.

articleTitle: Extended Kalman Filter-Based Sensor Fault Detection for Nonlinear Stochastic Systems with Strong Noise
abstract: The problem of sensor fault detection is investigated in this paper for nonlinear stochastic systems with strong noise. Firstly, the state estimation of nonlinear systems is realized by the extended Kalman filter. To suppress the influence of strong noise, a new residual generator and residual evaluation function are designed using the weighted moving average method. Based on the stochastic analysis theory and the definition of fault detectability, a sufficient condition is derived to guarantee the fault detectability in probability. At the same time, the quantitative relationships are analyzed among fault amplitude, window length, false alarm rate and missed detection rate. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed fault detection method is verified through a numerical simulation for the rotary steerable system.

articleTitle: Interpretable Neural Networks for Mechanical Fault Diagnosis in Strong Noise Condition
abstract: Deep learning has made significant progress in the field of mechanical fault diagnosis, but in real industrial scenarios, noise poses challenges to the accuracy and generalization of these models. Currently, some deep learning-based fault diagnosis methods take into account the effect of noise, but complex network structures and poor interpretability limit their practical application. Therefore, this work proposes a novel interpretable neural network for mechanical fault diagnosis in strong noise condition. First, considering the poor interpretability due to the complex structure of traditional deep neural networks, a feature mapping layer based on hybrid kernel function is proposed for mapping raw monitoring signals into high-dimensional space. Specifically, forward propagation and back propagation algorithms are designed for weight updating of the hybrid kernel function-based feature mapping layer. The exponential function and segmentation function are also introduced to constrain the boundaries of the weights. Secondly, a neural network based on multi-head attention mechanism is developed for high-dimensional feature learning. It can help the network adaptively select effective features and reduce the impact of noise on fault diagnosis performance. Experimental results show that the proposed method can adapt to mechanical fault diagnosis in strong noise condition, providing favorable accuracy and robustness. Notably, the proposed method has favorable feature learning transparency and interpretability.

articleTitle: Image Anomaly Detection via Reverse Informative Distillation
abstract: Image anomaly detection is a significant application in the context of large-scale industrial manufacturing. To enhance the performance of image anomaly detection, we propose a superior approach called the reverse information distillation (RID) model, which is based on the reverse knowledge distillation (RD) model. Within the knowledge distillation process, we employ informative knowledge distillation (IKD) to extract informative knowledge and provide a strong supervisory signal to mitigate overfitting issues. Furthermore, we introduce an attention module in the fusion and compression of features, resulting in the creation of an attention bottleneck embedding (ABE) module that mitigates the loss of feature information. Experimental results on the public MVTec AD dataset demonstrate that RID achieves an AUROC of 98.9% in anomaly detection, with corresponding AUROC of 98.2% and PRO of 94.9% in anomaly localization. The effectiveness of our method is demonstrated by its superior performance compared to RD.

articleTitle: Dynamic Event-triggered Control for Leader-following Consensus of Multi-agent Systems in Input Time Delay and Random Packet Loss Networks
abstract: In this paper, the leader-following consensus of linear multi-agent systems (MASs) in input time delay and random packet loss networks is investigated. To realize leader-following tracking, a novel distributive input control protocol is proposed. In this input protocol, Bernoulli stochastic variables are given to characterize random packet loss, which occurs asynchronously between the controllers and actuators within agents. Then, a dynamic event-triggered mechanism is designed to avoid continuous communication, in which internal dynamic variables are employed to decrease the number of triggers and exclude the Zeno phenomenon. In addition, by utilizing the graph algebra, stability analysis and linear matrix inequality (LMI) approach, some sufficient conditions are obtained for the consensus of this MASs. Finally, the effectiveness of our approach is illustrated by simulation examples.

articleTitle: A Method for Estimating Fish Biomass Based on Underwater Binocular Vision
abstract: This paper presents an underwater binocular vision-based fish biomass estimation method using instance segmentation and 3D reconstruction. To validate the system's effectiveness in aquaculture environments and the accuracy of measurement results, three datasets are proposed in experimental and breeding settings. These datasets are respectively used for training and validation of the instance segmentation network; dimension estimation; and mass fitting and estimation. In this work, we introduce pyramid squeeze attention and triple attention in the backbone of instance segmentation network to enhance segmentation accuracy. In the context of free-swimming conditions, where fish often assume non-orthogonal positions relative to the camera's optical axis and exhibit non-linear body shapes, we introduce a stereo disparity map optimization method. This method generates smooth and accurate point cloud and triangular mesh of fish targets, allowing for the estimation of fish fork length and body width based on 3D information. The LAR is also used to estimate the mass by taking the fork length and body width as independent variables.

articleTitle: Weighted measurement fusion filter for multi-sensor uncertain systems with time-correlated measurement noises*
abstract: This paper is concerned with the globally optimal fusion estimation problem for multi-sensor stochastic uncertain systems with time-correlated measurement noises. First, the considered system is transformed into a normal system with uncorrelated white noises. State augmentation and measurement difference are the key technologies. Then based on full-rank decomposition and weighted least-squares method, the weighted measurement fusion filter is proposed in the sense of the linear minimum variance. The proposed weighted measurement fusion filter has lower computational cost and the same accuracy as the centralized one for the same initial values. It is globally optimal. A tracking system example shows the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Novel Super Twisting Observer Based Integral Terminal Sliding Mode Control for MIMO Nonlinear Systems With Uncertainties*
abstract: In this article, a novel super twisting observer (STO) based integral terminal sliding mode control (ITSMC) strategy is proposed to discuss the multi-input multi-output (MIMO) nonlinear systems with uncertainties. Firstly, the idea of proportion-integration-differentiation (PID) is introduced to design the integral-type terminal mode function. Secondly, the exponential reaching law is proposed to improve the convergence speed of sliding mode variables. The super twisting estimation algorithm is utilized to deal with the problem of model uncertainty and external disturbance of the system. Further, the ITSMC-STO strategy is constructed to improve the control performances which are tracking accuracy and anti-disturbance. Finally, the simulation results by the two-tank liquid level system as a typical process example is applied to confirm that the strategy proposed has good performances than the other methods.

articleTitle: Design of Military Chess System Based on Alpha-Beta Pruning Algorithm
abstract: Computer gaming, also known as machine gaming, is an important research direction in the field of artificial intelligence and a highly intelligent and challenging research content. Military chess is an important branch of computer game. In order to solve the problems of slow searching rate and low winning rate in the process of military chess, the author adopts a two-dimensional array to represent the information of chess board and pieces, which is simple in designing and occupies less space. Firstly, the board and pieces are scanned according to the rules of military chess to find out the moves that are in accordance with the rules in the current position; secondly, the number of nodes in the search process is reduced by combining with the Alpha-Beta pruning algorithm; lastly, the basic value of the board, the estimation of the identity of opponent’s pieces, the flexibility of the pieces, and the value of the position of the pieces are considered; the Alpha-Beta pruning algorithm is improved on the basis of the Great Big Minor algorithm, which can greatly improve the search rate and the winning rate of the game. It can greatly improve the efficiency of the search, and can greatly improve the probability of victory within a certain period of time.

articleTitle: Research on sensing properties of a compact optical fiber microcavity fluorescence sensing probe
abstract: In this study, we successfully developed a compact optical fiber fluorescence probe based on a microcavity structure, which can be employed for the precise measurement of physical or chemical parameters. The fabrication process of this microcavity structure is simple, and it effectively amplifies the internal fluorescent signal. Using this structure combined with Rhodamine B, we conducted temperature measurements within the range of 20°C to 40°C. The results demonstrated that changes in fluorescence intensity accurately reflected temperature variations. Building on this structure, we incorporated etched quantum dots of CdTe/CdS with high specificity and completed concentration detections for Cd<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> ranging from 3 μM to 160 μM. The findings revealed that the probe exhibits good linearity within the Cd<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> concentration range of 10 μM-110 μM, with a detection limit as low as 3 μM. In conclusion, this microcavity-structured probe is not only easy to fabricate but also demonstrates excellent compatibility with various fluorescent materials, offering a robust tool for future environmental and health monitoring.

articleTitle: Bearing fault feature information extraction method based on GA-FMD and EK composite index
abstract: In view of the rolling bearing vibration signal with large noise is in the lead to the problem of the bearing fault information is difficult to effectively extract of the proposed based on GA-FMD and EK composite index of bearing fault characteristic information extraction method. Firstly, in order to overcome the shortcoming of feature mode decomposition (FMD) needing to rely on human experience to set the key parameters, a genetic optimization algorithm (GA) based on Teager energy operator as the fitness function was proposed to adaptively determine the input parameters of FMD. Then, according to the composite screening index EK(EHNR-K) composed of harmonic ratio and kurtosis, several modes of FMD with parameter optimization are decomposed, and the mode with the largest EK value is selected as the intrinsic modes with sensitive fault characteristic information, so as to remove the noise-dominated mode and redundant mode. Finally, the selected intrinsic mode components were reconstructed and the envelope spectrum was analyzed to realize the feature extraction of signal fault information. The simulation and experiment show that this method can extract bearing fault effectively and distinguish bearing fault effectively compared with other traditional decomposition methods.

articleTitle: Equilibrium Control of Complex Dynamical Networks with Hybrid Pinning Coupling
abstract: A complex network may be pinned to an equilibrium point by adding feedback controllers to few nodes, which uses the interaction between adjacent nodes. However, when the variable of the isolated node’s dynamics is more than one, the network may use the connection in its all variables to make the network achieve an equilibrium point. This may bring heavy communication burden with the increase of the network size and complexity of network topology. To address this problem, a hybrid pinning coupling strategy is proposed to enable a complex dynamical network achieve an equilibrium point. In the approach, one random selected variable of each node interacts with its whole neighbors, and the other variables of the node interact with that of only one randomly neighbor node. Experiments show that the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Research on System Level Calibration Method of Strap-down Inertial Navigation System
abstract: In order to effectively improve the accuracy of strap-down inertial navigation, it is necessary to recognize and compensate the error of high-precision inertial navigation system. In this paper,not only the conventional error parameters such as zero bias error, scale factor error, and installation error of the inertial measurement assembly are considered from the system perspective, but also quadratic term coefficient error of accelerometers, the rod arm error, and the time asynchronous error are analyzed. By designing the calibration paths to rotate and stop around the three sensitive axes of the inertial component to stimulate the error parameters of the inertial measurement component, a high-dimensional Kalman filter is established to recognize the error parameters. At the same time, this paper carries out Sage-Husa adaptive processing for the traditional Kalman filter noise parameters. The simulation results show that the designed system-level calibration method can estimate all the error parameters, which is of great significance for improving the accuracy of inertial navigation.

articleTitle: MSWI process parameter prediction based on improved case-based reasoning
abstract: To accurately predict the key parameters of the municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) process, this paper proposes an improved case-based reasoning (CBR) predictive modeling method based on a deep Q network to realize the case adaptation process. First, the MSWI operation process is analyzed to screen out the relevant feature variables and build the corresponding case base. Second, the K-nearest neighbor (KNN) algorithm is used to realize the case retrieval process of the parameter prediction, and cases similar to the current incineration state are obtained. Then, based on the "Learning-Evaluation-Revision" idea, the case difference adaptation knowledge between similar cases and the feature variables of the current state is learned through the deep Q network to realize key parameter prediction. Finally, the actual data of a solid waste incineration plant are used to predict the key parameters of the furnace temperature and flue gas oxygen content. The results show that the proposed method can accurately predict the MSWI process parameters.

articleTitle: Anti-false Alarm Method of Methanol Three-column Distillation Monitoring
abstract: The methanol three-column distillation process is often affected by noise and random interference, which causes the normal data to be misreported as fault data when monitoring the distillation process. In order to reduce the false positive rate and improve the process monitoring effect, this paper presents a novel method combining Butterworth Low-pass Filter (BLPF) and Principal component analysis (PCA). The method firstly uses BLPF to filter the original data, then establishes a PCA process monitoring model on the filtered data, and finally verifies the data of a methanol production plant in Zhejiang. The results show that this method has better monitoring effect than the traditional PCA method, and can effectively deal with the problem of high false positive rate caused by noise, and has practical application reference value.

articleTitle: Bridge Monitoring Data Reconstruction Based On N-BEATS-Transformer Model
abstract: In bridge monitoring practice, the loss of sensor data due to uncertainty occurs from time to time, in order to ensure that the data can be used for subsequent bridge analysis, this paper combines the N-BEATS algorithm with the transformer network on the basis of the transformer network, constructs the N-BEATS-Transformer combinatorial model, and uses the deflection data of Meixi River Bridge as the dataset, and conducts training and testing of the model. The experimental results show that the combined N-BEATS-Transformer model has higher prediction accuracy, with lower RMSE and MAE compared to the single Transformer, which are 0.1138 and 0.0824, respectively. The combined model has been used in bridge monitoring systems, and practice has shown that the combined model can meet the needs of bridge deflection data reconstruction, which is conducive to the use of data for subsequent bridge analysis.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection for Surface of Industrial Products Based on Patch Kernel Density Estimation
abstract: Visual anomaly detection is a crucial problem in computer vision, commonly employed in industrial product quality inspections. A new model called Patch Kernel Density Estimation (PaKDE) is proposed in this paper. The proposed model integrates a pre-trained deep convolutional neural network (CNN), an embedding vector generation module, a subsampling module, a kernel density estimation (KDE) classifier module, and an anomaly map generator module to realize anomaly detection for surface of industrial products. Firstly, a pre-trained deep CNN is used to extract image features. Then, embedding vectors of features are generated and subsampled. Finally, a KDE classifier is trained using representative features. Experiments on the industrial inspection benchmark dataset show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance: 89.6% on image-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and 85.0% on pixel-level AUROC.

articleTitle: Distributed Finite Time Formation Control and Obstacle Avoidance for UAV Swarms
abstract: The flight formation of UAV swarms will be seriously affected by the obstacles in the flight environment. Aiming at the problem of flight formation maintenance and obstacle avoidance control, the distributed finite time formation control protocol and obstacle avoidance control protocol are designed in this paper. First of all, in the process of UAV swarms movement, each UAV only needs to adjust the relative position with the adjacent follower UAV and leader UAV to maintain formation. Therefore, on the basis of obtaining the relative state information between adjacent UAVs, a finite time formation control protocol based on terminal sliding mode is proposed. In this control protocol, an adaptive robust term is introduced to suppress the influence of disturbance on the formation system, and the stability analysis and proof of formation system under this control protocol are given. Secondly, based on the improved artificial potential field algorithm, the obstacle avoidance control protocol is designed, and the formation control protocol and obstacle avoidance control protocol are weighted to prevent the UAV swarms from being unable to form a given formation or avoid obstacles. Finally, the effectiveness of formation control protocol and obstacle avoidance control protocol is verified by mathematical simulation.

articleTitle: CMFPN: A Cross-Modal Fusion Prediction Network for Precipitation Nowcasting
abstract: Precipitation nowcasting is crucial and fundamental for various public services, ranging from heavy rain warnings to flight safety. In order to further improve the prediction accuracy of the spatiotemporal sequence forecasting problem, we propose cross-modal fusion prediction network. By design the correction module and multi-scale feature extraction module, the features of multiple data sources are mined and cross-fused, thereby enhancing the overall performanc. Experiments in a real-world radar echo data-set of South China show that compared with the ingenious PredRNN++, TrajGRU methods, and newly proposed Rainformer and simVP, our network performs better on the precipitation nowcasting metrics, as well as occupies small GPU memory.

articleTitle: Research and Design of University Library Equipment Management System Based on WeChat Applet
abstract: In the rapidly advancing information society, university libraries are continually introducing high-tech equipment with the aim of improving the quality of services for students. However, the management of a multitude of devices has become increasingly complex. This paper presents the development of a highly efficient library equipment management system that utilizes the ease of use, convenience, and widespread popularity of WeChat mini-programs to effectively address the challenges associated with library equipment management. By digitalizing the equipment management process, the system enhances operational and maintenance efficiency, elevates the effectiveness of equipment management, and optimizes services for readers.

articleTitle: Temperature Prediction of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Data-driven Approach
abstract: In order to avoid the damage of permanent magnet synchronous motor caused by the high temperature, this paper proposes a method for predicting the temperature of permanent magnet synchronous motors based on XGBoost. The method mainly consists of three parts: first, normalize the data, then use Bayesian optimization to find the optimal hyperparameters for the model, and finally train the model using XGBoost Comparing with the training results of other artificial intelligence algorithms, the precision of the temperature estimation can be improved by the proposed method, which is verified by the experimental results.

articleTitle: Optimization Method for Predictive Models Based on ARIMA Time Series and K-means Clustering Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a method for optimizing prediction models based on the ARIMA time series and the K-means clustering algorithm to address the challenge of solving world puzzle games. The method aims to offer players a diverse range of challenges by anticipating and predicting imbalances in difficulty and content in advance. To achieve this, the paper first establishes an ARIMA time series model to fit the data and calculate the goodness of fit. Subsequently, employing keywords such as vowels, consonants, word composition, and usage, the K-Means clustering algorithm is applied to compute the clustering center of the data and generate a clustering result graph. Finally, different regression models were established for the characteristics of various difficulty samples, and the words were digitally encoded. The least squares method was used for fitting. Faced with different attempts, a reasonable prediction interval was obtained based on the analysis results. Experimental results indicate that, in comparison to traditional algorithms, the proposed method demonstrates higher accuracy in predicting word attribute classifications. The findings of this research offer an effective approach for game developers to manage puzzle game difficulty, enabling better balancing of game challenges and enhancing the gaming experience and engagement for players.

articleTitle: A Calibration-Free Visual System for Device Pose Estimation
abstract: This paper focuses on device pose estimation in automation processes and an innovative calibration-free visual system is proposed. We introduce a novel solution employing three orthogonal cameras to form an efficient relocalization system. Through the analysis of scene images captured by these cameras, we determine the position of cameras and their orientation in three-dimensional space. By processing the scene images captured by cameras, we extract crucial position and pose information of cameras in the spatial domain. Our method boasts notable advantages in terms of efficiency and speed.

articleTitle: An Effective Collaborative Localization Method for Multi-Robot System without Sufficient Landmarks
abstract: This paper investigates the collaborative localization problem of multi-robot systems in environments where GNSS signals are denied and landmarks are not sufficient, where an effective low-cost multi-robot collaborative localization method is proposed. The robots in the system are equipped with low-cost sensors for odometry measurement, and they observe each other and communicate with their neighbors to share their orientation and mutually observed position information. In this way, the collaborative localization task is achieved at lower communication and sensor costs. Given these information, the multi-robot collaborative localization problems are converted into solving nonlinear least squares optimization problems via Gauss-Newton algorithm. Simulation experiments verify that method proposed is effective, the localization results are expected to be satisfactory though landmarks are not sufficient.

articleTitle: Passive Laser Array Positioning: Real-Time Object Positioning System Based on Transformer
abstract: Currently, positioning primarily relies on sources such as Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, or visual cues. However, these methods have limitations in precision, sampling rate, and environmental requirements, potentially restricting their applicability across various scenarios. To enhance real-time positioning performance, this study devised a system based on laser arrays for positioning. By leveraging a Transformer model, it made real-time predictions on collected temporal signal sequences, achieving passive real-time object positioning. The study compiled a dataset from sequential signals generated by 24 sets of laser tube pair arrays. It compared the predictive performances of methods including Transformer, LSTM, GRU, and CNN + GRU. Results show that the proposed system attained a positioning accuracy of 0.2 cm and a positioning delay of 4.74 ms, demonstrating superior attributes: high precision, sampling rate, low latency, robust interference resistance, and cost-effectiveness. This provides a viable and effective solution for real-time object positioning.

articleTitle: IOPA-FracAT: Research on Improved One-pixel Adversarial Attack and Fractional Defense in Hyperspectral Image Classification
abstract: The introduction of deep learning arouses great success in hyperspectral image (HSI) classification. However, adversarial attacks on the deep model that substantially affect the HSI classification performance by some imperceptible perturbations have achieved significant concerns. In this paper, we propose an improved semi-black-box attack method called improved one-pixel attack (IOPA), which focuses on deceiving HSI classifiers by modifying only one pixel with high intensity in high-dimensional HSI data. Building on this insight, we incorporate the adversarial examples generated by IOPA into the training set and further introduce a fractional-order adversarial training (Frac-AT) defense method. Frac-AT, with the memory properties of fractional-order optimization, better enhances the robustness of neighboring boundary samples, outperforming traditional adversarial training. To visualize the attack effects of IOPA and the defense effects of Frac-AT, we create a hyperspectral adversarial map. The experimental results demonstrate that IOPA outperforms existing state-of-the-art attack methods for HSIs. Moreover, implementing Frac-AT based on IOPA enables HybridSN to enhance the defense capability of the model against various adversarial attacks while also improving the robustness of boundary samples, thereby enhancing overall accuracy.

articleTitle: Path Planning Optimization for Obstacle Avoidance in Unknown Environment
abstract: In this paper, the path planning for a robot in an unknown environment is considered. To enable the robot to reach the target point while ensuring obstacle avoidance, a novel framework based on the Artificial Potential Field (APF) method is proposed. The APF consists of two components: an attractive potential field generated by the target point and a repulsive potential field created by the perceived obstacle feature points. The robot is guided under the APF to optimize its path towards reducing the potential value. Furthermore, three robotic modes are proposed to avoid the robot getting trapped in local APF minimum. Each mode is equipped with corresponding potential fields and control laws, enabling the robot to complete the task along a shorter path by appropriately switching its mode. At last, the effectiveness of our proposed method is illustrated via a numerical example.

articleTitle: Output feedback control for nonholonomic systems with time-varying function constraints
abstract: In this paper, the stability problems of nonholonomic systems with nonlinear uncertainties, state constraints and input saturation are studied. Different from the existing work, we use a radical-type Lyapunov function and L function to solve the symmetric time-varying state function constraints, where the constrainted boundary is not only time dependent, but also depends on the partial state of the system. The nonlinear term caused by input saturation is compensated by Nussbaum function. Through coordinate transformation, the influence of unknown control coefficient is well dealt with. By constructing a switching control strategy, an adaptive stability control scheme based on output feedback is proposed, which ensures the stability of the closed-loop system and does not violate the symmetric time-varying state function constraints.

articleTitle: Research on Tire Defect Detection Based on Improved YOLOv5
abstract: An improved YOLOv5s-based method is proposed to address the challenge of accurately recognizing tire defects in this paper. In detecting process, the accuracy of YOLOv5s is low because the up-sampling module of the original YOLOv5s algorithm causes the network to lose information due to insufficient consideration of the distance between pixels. In this method, the up-sample operator of YOLOv5s is replaced by the carafe up-sampling operator. By adding the up-sampling kernel and the dot product operation of adjacent pixels in the input feature map, the spatial perception of up-sampling is strengthened, and finally the performance of segmentation task and the accuracy of image processing task are improved. The experimental verification is carried out on a complex datasets including four kinds of tire defects. Compared with the original YOLOv5 algorithm, the recognition accuracy is significantly improved. Specifically, under real-time performance constraints, the proposed method improves the recognition accuracy of mAPO.5 dataset by 2.9%. The results indicate that the proposed method enables accurate recognition of tire defects in complex backgrounds. Furthermore, it demonstrates better recognition precision than YOLOv5s.

articleTitle: Improved probabilistic roadmap method based on obstacle distance sampling
abstract: Sampling-based algorithms are widely used to solve path planning problems, and PRM is one of the most popular ones. Random Sampling PRM is the classic version of the PRM series, which has the advantages of simplicity and robustness, but also suffers from low success rate, long collision detection time and low path quality in narrow environments. To address these issues, an improved PRM algorithm based on obstacle distance sampling is proposed. A sampling strategy based on obstacle distance is used in this algorithm, so that more sampling points appear in narrow areas, thereby improving the success rate of the algorithm in finding paths in narrow areas. In addition, a collision detection method based on obstacle distance is proposed in this paper, which reduces the time required for collision detection and improves the efficiency of the algorithm. Further, in order to improve the quality of the path, the proposed algorithm uses triangle inequality and dichotomy to optimize the path. Finally, the proposed algorithm is compared with Random Sampling PRM, MSAPRM and Gaussian PRM through simulation experiments, and it is verified that the algorithm has certain advantages in the success rate, time and path length of finding paths in narrow environments.

articleTitle: SGD-based adaptive NN backstepping control design for a linear motor system
abstract: In this paper, the motion control problem for a linear motor system is solved by using a new adaptive neural network (NN) control strategy. This control method combines the stochastic gradient descent (SGD) algorithm and the adaptive NN backstepping technique, which results in good control performance in dealing with system uncertainties. The weights, widths, and centers of NN can be continuously updated and optimized such that the system uncertainties can be well approximated by the NN. Based on Lyapunov stability theory, it can be proven that the motion error eventually converges to a small neighborhood of the origin. Finally, the practicality of this method is verified through experiments.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking of Quadrotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Based on Adaptive Backstepping Sliding Mode Control
abstract: The Quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) exhibits high agility and maneuverability, making it widely applied in scientific research, including military and civilian applications. However, during UAV flight, external disturbances and parameter uncertainties are present, which significantly impact the tracking performance of quadrotor UAV. To address this issue, this paper proposes a trajectory tracking method for quadrotor UAV based on Adaptive Backstepping Sliding Mode Control (ABSMC). This method introduces the backstepping technique in the construction of the sliding mode controller and incorporates an adaptive switching gain through a differential iterative approach in the design of the backstepping method. This adaptive sliding mode control effectively suppresses the chattering phenomenon of the sliding mode controller. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, stability analysis of the system is conducted using the Lyapunov function. Finally, simulation experiments are conducted to compare the Sliding Mode Control (SMC), Backstepping Sliding Mode Control (BSMC) and the proposed ABSMC method under the same experimental conditions. The results demonstrate that the proposed ABSMC algorithm exhibits superior control performance compared to the SMC and BSMC method, with faster response speed and stronger robustness. Additionally, this method effectively mitigates the chattering issue.

articleTitle: Design of a Two-link Robot to Perform the Straight-body Tkatchev Movement
abstract: In this paper, the characteristics of the straight-body Tkatchev movement for a two-link robot are explored by converting the movement into a motion control problem. The optimal conditions for the two transition phases from the bar to air and back to the bar are explored. The main contributions of this paper can be summarized in four aspects. Firstly, this paper analyzes the conditions that must be satisfied during two transition phases to calculate the optimal release and regrasp postures. Secondly, this paper discusses the range of distances from the global center of mass to the bar, to ensure that the robot can achieve a feasible posture in an actual straight-body Tkatchev movement. Constraints are deduced to represent all feasible initial states that satisfy the optimal transition conditions. Thirdly, leveraging the trajectory characteristics of the straight-body Tkatchev movement, this paper designs an algorithm to compute the optimal regrasp posture corresponding to the given initial states. Finally, the theoretical findings are validated by simulation with actual gymnast data.

articleTitle: A New Method for Optimization: Optimal Control
abstract: This paper focuses on a new method based on the optimal control theory to tackle the optimization problem. We transform the optimization problem into an optimal control problem, composed of a discrete-time linear time-invariant system and a cost function related to the objective function. We propose a new algorithm for obtaining the numerical solution to the optimal control problem, which uses the relation between the optimal controller of every two adjacent instants. By finding the zeros of the function associated with the initial control, the new algorithm decreases computation time effectively. The state trajectory of the system rapidly approaches the local minimum point of the original optimization problem without oscillation. Finally, we use numerical examples to evaluate our new algorithm.

articleTitle: SCMOT: Improving 3D Multi-Object Tracking via Semantic Inference and Confidence Optimization
abstract: 3D multi-object tracking (MOT) is a fundamental technology in autonomous systems, playing a pivotal role across applications like autonomous driving and intelligent transportation systems. Previous 3D MOT methods mainly rely on LiDAR point clouds for object detection and tracking, often facing challenges such as occlusions and sparse data. This paper introduces SCMOT, a novel multi-modal 3D MOT framework designed to address the limitations of existing LiDAR-based 3D MOT methods. SCMOT enhances 3D object detection by filtering and refining results using semantic information, thereby reducing erroneous or redundant detections. To improve data association and enhance tracking precision, a multi-modal cost function that combines prediction confidence, semantic cues, and distance information is presented. Moreover, SCMOT can be served as a plug-and-play solution, integrating with diverse point cloud-based 3D object detectors. Extensive experiments on the KITTI tracking dataset validate the feasibility and effectiveness of SCMOT in real-world autonomous driving scenarios.

articleTitle: Finite-time combination synchronization of neural networks with uncertainties via adaptive fault-tolerant control
abstract: In this study, problems of finite-time combination synchronization of neural networks with uncertainties are investigated using adaptive fault-tolerant control methods. When the neural networks system parameters and uncertainties are unknown, adaptive controllers are designed. The fault tolerance strategy ensures that when the system experiences stuck faults and actuator partial failures, the error dynamic system can still converge to the equilibrium point within a finite time. Finally, the correctness of the theorem and the effectiveness of the fault tolerant controller were verified through actual numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Optimal load dispatch for electric heating users based on CNN-BiLSTM model
abstract: Adopting electric energy to replace traditional coal-fired and gas-fired heating methods is conducive to realizing sustainable development. However, electric energy alternative heating loads are characterized by distribution and randomness, which makes it difficult for dispatch centers to regulate them directly. To address this problem, we propose a load-optimized dispatch strategy based on the CNN-BiLSTM model. Firstly, we propose various load characteristic indexes and introduce a CNN-BiLSTM model, which fuses the user load characteristics to forecast their loads. Secondly, we propose a dispatch strategy to maximize the economic efficiency of the dispatch layer while ensuring that the users get the best thermal comfort. Finally, we employ an enhanced particle swarm algorithm to solve the optimal dispatch results. The simulation results illustrate that our proposed optimal dispatch scheme better incorporates the characteristics of the user loads and thus maximizes the revenue of the dispatch layer.

articleTitle: Finite-time anti-disturbance control for fractional-order switched systems with actuator saturation
abstract: This study explores the finite-time anti-disturbance control for fractional-order switched systems with actuator saturation. Control inputs are subject to saturation during both continuous time intervals and switching instants. Leveraging the average dwell time method and Lyapunov stability theory, we establish conditions ensuring the finite-time stability of the closed-loop system. Meanwhile, the controller gains can be obtained by solving linear matrix inequalities. In addition, the biggest attraction domain is obtained by solving the proposed optimization problem. Finally, a numerical example is provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the designed controller.

articleTitle: Considering Normal Direction Constraints Real-Time Optimization Method for Active Optical Navigation System in Robotic Orthopedic Surgeries
abstract: Intraoperative optical navigation is an important technology in robotic orthopedic surgery. The optical tracking system (OTS) serves as the "eye" in intraoperative navigation and has a limited measurement volume (MV). When the position and attitude of the target tools fixed on the patient’s body or operation robot change, the target tools are easily moved out of the MV or the target tools cannot be seen by OTS, resulting in navigation failure. To solve this problem, we consider both the position and the normal direction constraints of the target tools, and incorporate them into the optimization formulation. In this article, a new real-time optimization method is proposed for changing OTS viewpoints in real-time to achieve continuous tracking of multiple dynamic target tools. Ultimately, simulation experiments are used to verify the effectiveness of the proposed real-time optimization method. When the position and attitude of the target tools undergo significant change, OTS can still continuously obtain measurement data from multiple dynamic target tools.

articleTitle: Predefined-time synchronization of different dimensional fractional-order chaotic systems
abstract: This paper studies predefined-time synchronization of different dimensional fractional-order chaotic systems. Based on Lyapunov stability theory and the definition of predefined-time stability, some sufficient conditions are given to achieve predefined-time synchronization of different dimensional fractional-order chaotic systems by designing a new feedback controller. Compared with some previous finite-time and fixed-time synchronization results, our results are more general. The validity of the results is verified by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Short-term Wind Power Prediction by Hybrid Neural Network Based on Information Decomposition
abstract: In response to China’s goal of achieving carbon neutrality in 2060, the Chinese government vigorously promotes the spot energy market, and the power generation prediction of new energy participation in the spot energy market is an urgent problem to be solved. In this paper, the Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) data and the historical wind power data are used to predict the day ahead of wind power. The strong randomness of wind power leads to low accuracy of ordinary prediction methods. In this paper, the historical wind power data was decomposed by using the Complementary Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (CEEMD) signal decomposition method. Decompose into high and low frequency signals, and add NWP weather data after decomposition. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) are used to extract data spatial features and input them into Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Neural network. The accuracy of wind power day-ahead prediction is improved by time feature extraction and effective gating structure. Through experimental verification and comparison, the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of the proposed method are lower than those of other methods. It is proved that the method presented in this paper can effectively improve the accuracy of day-ahead wind power prediction.

articleTitle: Fully Distributed Event-Triggered Observer-Based Leader-Follower Consensus Control for Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: In this paper, the leader-follower output consensus problem for linear heterogeneous multi-agent systems (MASs) is considered. Firstly, in order for all followers to obtain the matrices and state of leader, the adaptive observer is designed for each follower. Considering that the actual system has limited resources to communicate, event-triggering mechanism is designed to realize discrete-time communication between neighbor agents. Secondly, the regulator equation is solved online, then, based on the solution of regulator equation and the designed observers, the new controller is designed to solve the leader-follower consensus problem. Finally, a simulation is given, and the results show the effectiveness of the designed method.

articleTitle: Fuel-Optimal Orbit Transfer Trajectory Optimization Method for Satellites
abstract: With the dynamic development of space technology, the scale and diversity of missions to be carried out by satellites are constantly increasing. However, the lack of top-level decision-making capability at the mission planning level has resulted in inefficient planning and a waste of satellite resources, making it necessary to carry out mission planning for them. In this background, it is significant to study the problem of satellite orbit transfer trajectory optimization based on numerical optimization. Given the mission pre-planning and re-planning problem in the observation of ground point targets by the satellite, we have analyzed the time constraints, dynamics constraints, and other constraints imposed on the satellite in this process, and established a mathematical model for the mission planning problem of the satellite, taking into account the requirements of optimal gain in the process of observation and optimal energy in the process of attitude maneuver. Finally, the problem was solved by the Matlab GPOPS software package, which proved the correctness and effectiveness of this orbit transfer trajectory optimization method.

articleTitle: Distributed Asynchronous Periodic Event-Triggered Voltage Control of Microgrids With Different Checking Periods
abstract: The secondary control plays an important role in ensuring the power quality of AC island microgrid. Since the traditional time-driven secondary control strategy will cause communication redundancy, the event-triggered mechanism has been widely studied. Under the event-triggered mechanism, the DG performs necessary communication only when its own triggering condition is met. This paper studies the problem of secondary voltage control under periodic event-triggered mechanism, which can restore the output voltage to the reference value. At the same time, considering that each DG has a different sampling and checking period, this is a more general asynchronous communication problem. In the stability analysis, the conditions of event detection period and event parameters to ensure the realization of secondary control are given. Finally, the effectiveness of the mechanism is verified by several simulations.

articleTitle: KAS-YOLOv5: A Novel Target Detection Algorithm for Aerial Images
abstract: Target detection in aerial image is a challenging task due to the high proportion of small targets, severe occlusion, and large scale variations. In this paper, a novel KAS-YOLOv5 algorithm is proposed based on YOLOv5. First, the K-Means++ clustering algorithm is used to regenerate the initial anchor boxes suitable for the target size of the aerial image. Secondly, Adaptively Spatial Feature Fusion (ASFF) is used to solve the inconsistency problem between features of different scales in aerial images. Finally, a dynamic label assignment strategy Simplified Optimal Transport Assignment (SimOTA) is used to transform the label assignment into an optimal transmission problem, thereby improving the severe occlusion phenomenon. The experimental results demonstrate a high accuracy rate of 42.2% on the VisDrone2019 dataset, outperforming other algorithms.

articleTitle: Behavioral decision-making for autonomous driving using Soft Actor-Critic algorithm
abstract: In recent years, the advancement of artificial intelligence has significantly influenced the enhancement of automatic driving technology.
