In this paper, a cascade flight control method based on error transformation is proposed to solve the vision-based landing problem of a low-cost quadrotor on a non-cooperative mobile platform. The proposed controller is robust to uncertain and dynamic systems because it does not contain prior knowledge of the moving platform. Firstly, the error transformation method based on performance function is used to process the intermediate signal of backstepping control technology, which simplifies the control design. Secondly, for uncertain target motion states and large tilt-angle flight situations, quaternion-based attitude control is used to avoid singularity. Finally, Python and Gazebo simulation experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Iterative Greedy Algorithm for Scheduling of Continuous Annealing Process in Cold Rolling
abstract: With the rapid improvement of the overall manufacturing level in China, the demand for steel products by downstream manufacturing enterprises is more personalized. This trend has brought greater difficulties to the production planning and scheduling of steel enterprises. In order to solve production scheduling problems of continuous annealing process in cold rolling, a mathematical model is established by converting violations of width jump, thickness jump and annealing temperature jump into penalty values. An iterative greedy algorithm is designed according to the characteristics of the model. The model and algorithm are verified and tested by taking use of actual production instances of iron and steel enterprises. The experimental results show that the model is correct and the algorithm is effective. Scheduling plans obtained by the proposed algorithm is obviously better than scheduling plans based on human experience.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Control for MEMS Gyroscopes using Modified Neural Disturbance Observer
abstract: This paper proposes a neural-network-based disturbance observer and a neural sliding mode control method are proposed for MEMS gyroscopes. Due to the unknown time-varying angular velocity in the gyro system, the neural network technique is used to estimate the unknown gyro parameter. Meanwhile, a constrained input mapping is proposed to help initialize the range of the center and width of the ignition function in the neural network. With the estimated gyro parameter, a disturbance observer is established and is integrated with the sliding mode control technique to alleviate chatting in the control force. The disturbance observer, the sliding mode controller, and all the adaptive laws are derived under the framework of Lyapunov stability theory to guarantee the stability of the gyro control system. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Simulated Annealing Algorithm for Acid Pickling Scheduling in the Steel Industry
abstract: Scheduling the acid pickling process is an important decision-making problem in the steel manufacturing industry. When considering the smooth transition of material width and thickness between detailed plans in acid pickling scheduling, it becomes challenging to effectively control the number of peaks and valleys in thickness jumps. This issue arises because ensuring a smooth transition in width and thickness compromises the control over thickness jumps between detailed plans. In this paper, we propose a domain adaptive simulated annealing algorithm to address this problem and provide an effective solution. The algorithm ensures a smooth transition in width and thickness while effectively controlling the number of peaks and valleys in thickness jumps between detailed plans. Extensive computational experiments using actual factory data validate the proposed algorithm. The results demonstrate the superiority of the algorithm in solving the acid pickling scheduling problem, outperforming single simulated annealing algorithms and rule-based heuristic algorithms.

articleTitle: Optimal Saddle-Point Strategy of Reach-Avoid Game in Three-Dimensional Space
abstract: Reach-avoid game with two pursuers and one evader in three dimensions is the main topic of this paper. While the adversary tries to approach the plane, two pursuers establish a cooperative team, each with different speeds, to defend the plane against one evader via capture. The isochronous surfaces, i.e., Apollonius spheres, separate the dominance regions of both sides to determine the saddle points and value functions of the systems involved in the game of degree. Moreover, it is proved that the state-feedback optimal strategies are Nash Equilibrium. The possible degeneration of the cooperative team is also analyzed. At last, several simulation experiments are conducted to demonstrate the optimality of the proposed strategies.

articleTitle: ILO-based Actuator and Sensor Faults Estimation for Nonlinear Discrete-time Systems
abstract: This paper addresses the multiple faults estimation problem of actuator and sensor faults with using iterative learning observer (ILO) for nonlinear discrete-time systems. First, an augmented descriptor system including system state and sensor fault vectors is constructed to achieve multiple faults estimation purpose. Then, a novel iterative learning observer is proposed, and the nonlinear estimation error is deduced into a more compact system by using a reformulated Lipschitz property. Next, design conditions of the observers are derived into the LMI optimization problem where a slack variable and L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>. performance index is introduced to reduce the conservativeness and obtain a more excellent performance of fault estimation. Finally, numerical simulations of an example of a single-link robot arm are provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method and multiple fault estimation scheme.

articleTitle: Observer-Based Reinforcement Learning Control for Electric Servo Mechanisms With Disturbance
abstract: To achieve accurate control of electric servo mechanisms and overcome the impacts of unknown model information and environmental disturbances, this paper focuses on the mathematical model of electric servo mechanisms. It employs a Reinforcement Learning control algorithm based on an extended state observer for research. Differing from traditional control strategies, this study treats total uncertainty as potential model information to update the known model. Using the updated model information, it solves the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation for the optimal value of a given performance index online. To approximate the optimal strategy, the proposed strategy iteration algorithm iteratively updates the coefficients of the actor and critic networks within the actor-critic algorithm, solving the HJB equation online with updated dynamics. The effectiveness of the proposed novel Reinforcement Learning control algorithm is verified through simulations.

articleTitle: Adaptive Output-Feedback Control for Stochastic Mechanical System Based on Neural Network
abstract: This paper is concerned with the problem of adaptive output-feedback control for a class of mass-spring mechanical system with stochastic disturbances. The adaptive parameter is only one and the nonlinear terms are successfully handled without growth conditions by using the radial basis function neural networks approximation approach. Based on the adaptive backstepping technique, an adaptive output-feedback controller is constructed. It is proved that the designed controller guarantees the closed-loop system is semi-globally uniformly ultimately bounded (SGUUB). Finally, the simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the controller.

articleTitle: Survey on TCP Congestion Control in Ad Hoc Wireless Networks
abstract: Wireless Ad hoc network is a type of wireless network and it is the important part of the next generation network. Transfer control protocol (TCP) is the most important transport protocol over the Internet and became the indispensable part of the network stack, in which its congestion control algorithm is the core of the TCP protocol. TCP is originally designed for the wired network. If it still uses TCP original way to carry out the adjustment of the congestion window, it will send node to the network into the data packet far more than the network processing capacity, causing network congestion, resulting in space saturation. This paper introduces the causes of TCP congestion control in wireless Ad Hoc networks. TCP congestion in wireless Ad hoc networks is discussed in three aspects: hidden and exposed terminal, link asymmetry and network reorganization.

articleTitle: Pavement Defect Detection Based on Deep Learning
abstract: The existing methods for pavement defect detection currently suffer from issues such as low accuracy, poor real-time performance, and a high missed detection rate for small target defects. To address these challenges, we propose an enhanced pavement defect detection method based on the state-of-the-art YOLOv8s model with exceptional comprehensive performance. In this study, we leverage the optimized YOLOv8 convolutional neural network to swiftly and precisely identify longitudinal cracks, transverse cracks, alligator cracks, potholes, and other road surface defects. The approach aims to reduce false detections and missed detections while enhancing both accuracy and speed of detection. We improve the neck structure of the YOLOv8s model by refining the BiFPN used in the EfficientDet model, thereby boosting overall model accuracy. Furthermore, we introduce a GAM global attention mechanism after the SPPF module of the YOLOv8 model to further enhance object detection precision. Experimental results demonstrate a 1% increase in mAP value after these improvements from 87.2% to 88.2%. This method outperforms the original YOLOv8 model approach and effectively identifies road defects with efficiency.

articleTitle: Parameter-Dependent Lyapunov Function Based Interval Observer Design For Switched LPV Systems
abstract: This paper tackles the challenge of designing a polytopic switched unknown input interval observer for uncertain switched linear parameter varying (LPV) systems characterized by unknown yet bounded uncertainties and disturbances. The proposed solution introduces a switched unknown input interval observer (SUIIO) designed to estimate the lower and upper bounds of system states while remaining unaffected by unknown input disturbances. To establish the viability of such observers, the paper formulates sufficient Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMIs) conditions. These conditions are obtained using Multiple Input-to-State-Stable (ISS) parameter-dependent Lyapunov functions integrated with average dwell time (ADT). The efficacy of the proposed methodology is scrutinized through an evaluation of its performance in estimating lateral vehicle dynamics. This evaluation is conducted using Matlab-Simulink, providing a comprehensive assessment of the approach’s practicality and applicability in the context of lateral vehicle dynamics estimation.

articleTitle: Levitation control technology for high-speed maglev trains of PEM hybrid levitation
abstract: The high-speed maglev train has been successfully commercialized in Shanghai and Qingdao, but the electromagnet design technology and PEM hybrid levitation control technology of the suspension control system of its core part still needs to be studied. Constrained by the current density of the electromagnet coils , the levitation system of the traditional EMS-type maglev train commonly used at present has limitations, so the high-speed maglev scheme with PEM hybrid levitation system is designed to reduce the levitation power consumption. Firstly, both the design technology of the electromagnet and the levitation control strategy were studied for the demand of the PEM hybrid high-speed maglev train. By analyzing the model of PEM hybrid levitation system, the research of a zero-power controller based on state feedback was designed and carried out. Finally, based on the corresponding simulation experimental results, the effectiveness of the design scheme is verified.

articleTitle: Adaptive differential evolution for collaborative path planning of multiple unmanned aerial vehicles
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive differential evolution combined with dynamic Thompson sampling, called DE-DYTS, to solve the collaborative path planning problem of multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Compared to single UAV path planning, the coordination time and collision avoidance among UAVs are considered in this study. Dual-layer encoding is designed to reduce the number of path control points. Four differential evolution operators are used to construct a pool of candidate operators to improve the optimization efficiency. Dynamic Thompson sampling is employed to learn the expected returns of the operators. DE-DYTS is tested in three scenarios to evaluate its effectiveness and efficiency, and the results are statistically analyzed using the Wilcoxon rank sum test. Experimental results show that DE-DYTS achieves significant superiority over advanced variants of differential evolution, especially in scenarios with a large number of UAVs.

articleTitle: Decision Support for Beyond Visual Range Air Combat Based on HTN Planning and Machine Learning
abstract: Beyond visual range air combat (BVR) has become the main form of modern air combat. In order to solve the problem of pilot information overload in BVR air combat, this paper designs an assistance decision-making model based on Hierarchical Task Network (HTN) planning and machine learning algorithms to provide pilots with tactical strategies. This paper first designs a hierarchical task network in a BVR air combat scenario, as well as an efficient scoring system that can dynamically adjust the mission execution plan based on the situation in real time. Then a machine learning algorithm combined with data generalization was proposed to predict the launch effectiveness of missiles in different situations and optimize part of the scoring process. Finally, a human-in-the-loop confrontation simulation experiment was conducted, and the feasibility of the model and the effectiveness of the algorithm were verified by analyzing the winning rate.

articleTitle: Online Thickness Prediction of Hot Rolling Strip Based on ARO-XGBoost
abstract: An online thickness prediction algorithm for strip steel based on machine learning is proposed to address issues of strong coupling and low accuracy in the thickness mathematical model. Firstly, the rolling data is used to establish an online thickness prediction model by optimizing the eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm parameters based on the Artificial Rabbits Optimization (ARO) algorithm. Then, a self-learning system is deployed to optimize the results. Finally, the predicted outcomes will be compared with the actual thickness to verify the accuracy of the thickness prediction model. The experimental results show that the online thickness prediction algorithm can quickly and accurately predict the strip thickness. When the ARO-XGBoost model was used to predict the 3 mm, 4 mm, and 5.65 mm strips, Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) can be controlled within 11.5 μm, 12 μm, and 16.6 μm. The results can improve the accuracy of the thickness mathematical model for hot strip rolling and enhance the level of the thickness control system.

articleTitle: Ramp Merging Strategy Based on Dual-layer Optimization Model in Non-connected Scenarios
abstract: The ramp merging task is a major challenge in the development of autonomous driving technology. In scenarios where all other vehicles in the merging area are manually driven, the ego driving vehicle must rely on its own sensors and communication with the roadside unit to obtain environmental information, make decisions, and complete the merging task in a non-cooperative setting. However, the current research on ramp merging lacks the capability to dynamically adjust merging gaps and longitudinal speeds, and also exhibits limited interaction intelligence with mainline vehicles. To address this problem, this paper introduces a staged maneuvering model based on optimal control. Simultaneously, a merging strategy grounded on the dual-layer optimization model predictive control is proposed, empowering ego driving vehicles to make more intelligent and efficient merging decisions. Firstly, a python-based simulation platform is established to verify the ramp merge decision. After that, a staged maneuvering model is developed based on the optimal control method, and both the proposed merging strategy based on the dual-layer optimization model predictive control and the rule-based baseline control strategy are introduced. The merging process is then simulated under two scenarios using the baseline strategy and the proposed strategy, respectively. The results are analyzed, demonstrating that the proposed algorithm enables safer and smarter decisions. The proposed strategy achieves dynamic selection of the merging gap, thereby enhancing the intelligence of the ramp merging process, achieving both efficiency and safety, and providing a reliable method for vehicle ramp merging in non-cooperative environments.

articleTitle: Study of Hysteresis Modeling on the Pneumatic Muscle Humanoid Elbow Joint
abstract: The aim of this study is to explore the application of pneumatic muscles in a humanoid elbow joint, with particular attention to its hysteresis. The performance of pneumatic muscles during joint motion was analyzed Through establishing an experiment on pneumatic muscle output hysteresis and a pneumatic muscle pseudo-elbow joint platform. Pressure sensors and displacement sensors were used in the experiments to monitor and record the joint movement process, and the data were used to determine the hysteresis of the pneumatic muscles in the joint movement process. Through the study of the pneumatic muscle imitating the human elbow joint hysteresis, it was found that the pneumatic muscle has high flexibility and hysteresis, which can better simulate the movement characteristics of the human elbow joint. In this study, The hysteresis of pneumatic muscles imitating the human elbow joint was experimentally verified through isobaric experiments and isometric experiments, and its mechanism was preliminarily analyzed. To improve the accuracy in describing the hysteresis of pneumatic muscles, a new mechanical model is established, along with establishing the force-velocity relationship mimicking the motion process of skeletal muscles. The results show that pneumatic muscles have potential applications in imitating the human elbow joint.

articleTitle: A Novel Binary Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm for Feature Selection
abstract: Feature selection is an important task in machine learning and binary feature selection is a challenging problem due to the large search space. Swarm intelligent optimization algorithms have received great attention in solving numerous optimization problems. Among them, the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm has successfully solved many optimization problems. However, there are still some difficulties with PSO in discrete or binary versions that lead to slow convergence. To solve these problems, a novel binary particle swarm optimization (NBPSO) algorithm is proposed in this paper. NBPSO introduces a dynamic weight search strategy to meet the different requirements for solution performance in different stages. Meanwhile, it combines with Lévy flight search strategy to reduce the possibility of falling into local optimal solution. In addition, referring to the idea of genetic algorithm, we introduce a population improvement method of variation mechanism and high-quality individual replication to balance the exploration and development ability of NBPSO algorithm. In order to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method and explore its performance on the feature selection problem, we use several benchmark functions to test and conduct comparative experiments on six classical datasets. The results show that the overall performance of the proposed algorithm is better than other comparison algorithms.

articleTitle: STrCNeRF: An Implicit Neural Representation Method Combining Global and Local Features from an Image for Novel View Synthesis
abstract: Recently, Novel View Synthesis (NVS) methods based on Implicit Neural Representations (INR) have garnered widespread attention and demonstrated significant performance improvements. These methods primarily focus on how to use implicit functions to generate novel viewpoint images not present in the initial training dataset. However, it is noteworthy that current implicit approaches predominantly rely on pure Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) structures to approximate functions and train scenes, which constrains both the model's training speed and its generalization to new scenes, while overlooking the holistic and detailed information from the source views. To address these issues, we propose a hybrid information-based implicit neural network structure for novel view synthesis. Our network adopts a dual-path feature extraction architecture based on Swin Transformer and CNN, simultaneously capturing global and local features from input images. This enhancement contributes to improving the model's generalization performance in new scenes and reducing training time. Furthermore, by introducing an attention-based Feature Aggregation Module (FAM), our network excels in handling detailed features. Finally, we introduce Fourier feature functions to encode input features, enhancing high-frequency components in images and learning abstract feature representations at multiple scales. Extensive experiments confirm that our proposed network structure delivers superior qualitative and quantitative performance and higher reconstruction quality on real-world datasets and ShapeNet dataset.

articleTitle: Enhancing Sparrow Search Algorithm with Hybrid Strategy
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid strategy-based improved sparrow search algorithm (HISSA). Tent chaotic mapping is used in the initialization of sparrow population to make the distribution of sparrow population more uniform in the solution space and increase the diversity of sparrow population. An adaptive parameter strategy is proposed to adjust the proportion of producers, danger perceivers, and environmental security thresholds, effectively balancing the global search and local development of the algorithm. Then, in the producer position update stage, the exploration strategy of the golf optimization algorithm is integrated to improve the optimization accuracy and speed of the algorithm. In addition, a boundary contraction mechanism is introduced to allocate individuals beyond the boundary to an effective local range, avoiding the aggregation of boundary sparrow individuals and increasing the diversity of sparrow populations during the search process. Finally, simulation experiments are conducted on benchmarks. Compared with other algorithms, the HISSA has good accuracy and convergence performance.

articleTitle: Furnace Temperature Control for MSWI Process Based on Neural Network Predictive Controller
abstract: To tackle the challenge of controlling furnace temperature in municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI), which is critical for incineration efficiency and pollutant reduction, this paper introduces a model predictive control (MPC) strategy utilizing a back propagation neural network (BPNN). Traditional PID struggles with the nonlinearity and disturbances of process. Our approach involves constructing a BPNN-based prediction model to forecast future furnace temperatures. Using gradient descent, we optimize the objective function within a predetermined period, allowing for real-time adjustment of control variables. This effectiveness of method is validated through experiments with data from a Beijing MSWI plant, demonstrating enhanced tracking and disturbance management capabilities.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Control of Unmanned Vehicles Based on Linear Time-Varying Model Predictive Control
abstract: In order to solve the problem of large errors in the track tracking control of unmanned vehicles during running, a linear time-varying model predictive control (LTVMPC) device was designed, and the output and track error constraints were introduced. In order to avoid hard constraints leading to no linear solution in the rolling optimization process, relaxation factor vector extension was introduced into the objective function to solve the feasible domain, and then the LTVMPC optimization problem was transformed into an online quadratic programming problem. Aiming at the problem that trajectory tracking control is difficult to apply to the obstacle environment, combining with reinforcement learning algorithm, a trajectory planning layer is established on the trajectory tracking layer, and a double-layer trajectory tracking controller with autonomous obstacle avoidance function is designed to realize the autonomous obstacle avoidance function of vehicles in the course of trajectory tracking. Finally, Matlab/Simulink and vehicle dynamics simulation software Carsim were used to design the co-simulation. The results show that the method can adapt to the tracking of double-shift track under different speed conditions, and the tracking accuracy and vehicle stability are significantly improved.

articleTitle: A pedestrian detection method in unattended garage based on improved YOLOv7
abstract: In the intelligent stereo garage system, automatic detection of people in the garage area is crucial to realize unattended stereo garage and improve the safety of garage operations and access efficiency. In actual operating scenes, pedestrians are often blocked by vehicles or other background objects, which has become a key factor affecting its detection accuracy. Based on the current YOLOv7 framework with strong comprehensive detection performance, this paper proposes a detection algorithm named Cross-YOLOv7 that combines a new attention mechanism and cross-layer feature fusion. First, a new attention module named Coor-NAM is proposed to enhance the feature extraction of pedestrian target areas in garage scenes, especially unoccluded areas. Second, a new non-adjacent scale cross-layer connection method is designed to significantly improve the information interaction between features of different scales. It can enrich the semantic information of the features, and thus improve detection accuracy. The proposed method is evaluated on the garage pedestrian detection dataset and the public WiderPerson dataset. Experimental results show that compared with several typical detection methods, the detection accuracy (AP50 and F1) of blocked pedestrians in the garage scene with our proposed Cross-YOLOV7 can be improved by 4.6% and 5.66% respectively. Moreover, the detection accuracy on the public WiderPerson dataset can also be improved by 2.5% and 1.68%.

articleTitle: Short-term load forecasting study of distribution network based on FADJ-ASTGCN
abstract: With the construction of new power systems, the distribution network is gradually shifting from the receiving power network to the active distribution network. It needs to undertake more load management tasks, which puts forward higher requirements for load forecasting at various nodes of distribution network. A node load prediction method based on fully connected graph neural network model is proposed in this article to address the problems of insufficient spatiotemporal joint representation ability and prediction accuracy in existing power load forecasting models. First, a global information transfer mechanism is introduced in Attention Based Spatial-temporal Graph Convolutional Networks (ASTGCN), where each distribution node of the distribution network is connected to other nodes to form a fully connected graph structure; Then, the graph structure plus the input hourly, daily and weekly components together with the fully connected matrix is input into the spatiotemporal module composed of spatiotemporal attention mechanism and spatiotemporal convolutional network; Finally, the three component features are fused using a multicomponent attention mechanism to enhance prediction accuracy. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by comparing it with the existing methods using the U.S. real distribution network dataset and the U.S. transportation datasets PeMSD4 and PeMSD8 data as examples.

articleTitle: Optimizing Inland Waterway Surveillance with a Novel Dual-Mode UAV: Integration of Federated Learning into Flight Control Algorithms
abstract: This study introduces a novel Composite Vertical Takeoff and Landing Fixed-Wing Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (VTOL-FW UAV) tailored for inland waterway missions. Combining multirotor hovering capabilities with fixed-wing cruising efficiency, the UAV addresses challenges specific to these environments. Aerodynamic analysis guides the development of a bespoke propulsion and control system, validated through simulations and waypoint tracking. A dual-mode control strategy facilitates precise trajectory planning, integrating vertical takeoff in multirotor mode and horizontal cruising in fixed-wing mode, using a dual-loop PID control structure. Additionally, Federated Learning theory optimizes operational efficiency and decision-making intelligence while maintaining data privacy.

articleTitle: An Unbalance Compensation Method for Rotor System of Magnetic levitation motors based on beetle algorithm
abstract: In order to reduce the co-frequency unbalanced vibration of the rigid rotor system of the active magnetic bearing (AMB), the unbalance compensation method based on the notch filter is usually used. The structure of the filter can be improved, but the improved filter will affect the stability of the system. In order to avoid this problem, this paper proposes a novel method for suppressing the unbalanced vibration of AMB rotor system based on the beetle algorithm. The variable-step beetle algorithm is used to search for the unbalance parameters of the high-speed magnetic bearing motor, and then the unbalance parameters are used for the compensation current calculation of the magnetic bearing, so as to conduct the method of unbalanced vibration compensation. Simulations are carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method under the conditions of constant speed and variable speed of the motor, respectively.

articleTitle: Multi-objective optimization scheduling based on renewable energy uncertainty scenarios for the reliability of power system operation
abstract: Addressing the power system scheduling problem within the context of economic and emission factors, and taking into account the influence of renewable energy generation on stability and security, a multi-objective optimization scheduling framework is proposed grounded in uncertainty scenarios. Utilizing wind power as an exemplar, characterized by its typical volatility and instability, generates uncertain wind power scenarios through the application of Latin hypercube sampling. To provide constraints for uncertainty problems in multi-objective optimization scheduling, and thereby achieve high-level penetration scheduling of wind power. The fuel cost, wind curtailment cost, and rotating reserve cost constitute the economic cost target while considering constraints to ensure the reliability of power system operation. Employing a multi-objective gray wolf algorithm, the proposed model is solved, introducing the Pareto front-scale control strategy. The effectiveness of the proposed model is verified by analyzing examples from distributed energy systems and comparing it with several other multi-objective optimization algorithms. It exhibits superior global search capabilities and achieves more optimal Pareto front and compromise solutions. Effectively improve the penetration rate of renewable energy, and ensure the economy and environmental protection of power system energy consumption under the target of reliable operation.

articleTitle: Depth-independent Jacobian Matrix-based Event-triggered Model Predictive Control of 2-DOF Visual Servo System
abstract: For the model predictive control-based visual servo problem, low computational efficiency might cause poor servo effect or even servo failure under the limitation of the performance of computing platform. Therefore, a visual servo controller based on event-triggered mechanism and model predictive control is designed in this paper. The model predictive controller is established for the plant represented by the depth-independent Jacobian matrix to solve the optimal control problem with explicit constraints. And the event-triggered mechanism is introduced to the MPC to reduce the computational effort. Finally, the simulation experiment of 2-DOF manipulator proves that the event-triggered visual servo model predictive control scheme can greatly improve the computational efficiency without losing the control accuracy as much as possible.

articleTitle: Small Target Detection on Water Based on Improved YOLOv7 Unmanned Vessel
abstract: The problems of low detection accuracy and high leakage rate of small targets on the water’s surface when observed from the viewpoint of an uncrewed ship are proposed to be resolved by an improved YOLOv7 detection algorithm. Firstly, the parameter-free attention mechanisms SimAM and PConv are introduced into the network to enhance the model’s feature extraction for small targets and reduce the number of model parameters, and SimAM and PConv in the backbone are combined with ELAN1 to form a new efficient layer aggregation network module ELAN1-SAPC. Then, the Head part of the model adopts the newly proposed MP-CXOS structure, which can enhance the model’s focus on small targets and effectively reduce the loss of small target feature information. Finally, the loss function is optimized by incorporating the new NWD metric approach to improve the model’s ability to detect small targets and speed up network convergence. The data set is also processed using data augmentation to improve the model’s generalization. The experiments show that compared with the basic model, the mean Average Precision of the improved YOLOv7 model increases by 5.3 per cent, the F1 score increases by 0.06, and the number of parameters decreases by 20.0 per cent. Therefore, the improved model has significantly improved detection performance and is more lightweight.

articleTitle: A Robustness Improved Watermarking Scheme based on Invertible Neural Network
abstract: Image watermarking technology aims to embed secret information imperceptibly into natural images for authentication or copyright protection. Invisibility and robustness are two primary concerns for watermarking algorithms. Previous methods leveraging invertible neural networks (INNs) have achieved high security in steganography. However, they lack resilience to image modifications, leading to compromised decoding quality. Conversely, encoder-decoder frameworks excel in robustness but often compromise invisibility. In this paper, a novel end-to-end robust watermarking framework is proposed that seamlessly integrates INNs with an encoder-decoder paradigm. Additionally, an efficient channel attention (ECA) block is incorporated in the message extraction stage, enhancing watermark extraction and consequently boosting decoding robustness. Furthermore, a message feature loss is introduced to regulate the INN, thereby accelerating network convergence and enhancing performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our proposed scheme outperforms existing algorithms in both robustness and invisibility. When subjected to a combination of 13 noise attacks, including Gaussian noise, random cropping, and JPEG compression, our model achieves a bit error rate below 1% with an embedding information length of 64 bits. Notably, the watermarked images maintain high visual quality, with PSNR and SSIM values reaching 36dB and 0.95 respectively.

articleTitle: A Time Series Data Augmentation Method based on SMOTE
abstract: Neural networks have become a focal point in the realms of time series analysis and data mining. However, unlike in the field of images, time series datasets are typically smaller in scale and exhibit substantial imbalance in data types, making models prone to overfitting. The conventional SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique) method is widely used for addressing imbalanced datasets through data augmentation. Nevertheless, when applied to time series data, the classical SMOTE method struggles to effectively accommodate the characteristics of time sequences, resulting in suboptimal performance on time series datasets. To address this issue, this paper proposes an enhanced algorithm, namely M-SMOTE. This algorithm relies on specific partitioning rules to classify minority class samples into safe points and noise points. Subsequently, linear interpolation is applied only between safe points and the centroid of minority class samples (i.e., the mean of minority class samples), effectively mitigating issues related to data marginalization. Additionally, the M-SMOTE algorithm avoids the uncertainty associated with selecting the k value in traditional SMOTE algorithms. In situations where time series with similar features may undergo phase shifts, the method employs dynamic time warping to obtain more reasonable similarities between different time sequences. Comparative experiments are conducted using deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs). The results demonstrate a significant improvement in the performance of the mentioned models when trained on datasets processed using the M-SMOTE method. This approach provides an effective and innovative solution for addressing imbalance issues in time series datasets.

articleTitle: Medical Waste Recycling Path Optimization Algorithm Research
abstract: This paper introduces the optimization algorithm of medical waste recovery path, and proposes three methods: Saving Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization and Improved Genetic Algorithm. The topology method is used to model the internal environment of a medical institution, and the Delaunay Triangle Network is used to build the building terrain path model of the medical institution. Finally, the three path optimization algorithms of the Saving Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization and Improved Genetic Algorithm are compared. Through experiments, Improved Genetic Algorithm has strong path finding ability, has good parallelization and global search, and compared with the other two algorithms, it has obvious advantages in path length, path selection and running time.

articleTitle: Consensus Control for a Class of Feedforward Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: This paper studies the leader-following robust consensus problem of a class of nonlinear feedforward multi-agent systems (MASs). A novel distributed protocol is proposed to achieve leader-following robust consensus of MASs, as long as the topology is undirected and connected. First, the leader-following problem is transformed into a robust stabilization problem of an interconnected system composed of two error subsystems. Then, the objective of the paper can be achieved by analyzing the interactions between the error subsystems by using a small-gain theorem.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Single Image Dehazing Method Based on Multi-Feature Fusion
abstract: Dehazing plays a crucial role in enhancing image quality for successive image processing applications. However, current single image dehazing algorithms demonstrate varied performance on different scenes. In this paper, we introduce an adaptive image dehazing scheme designed to enhance dehazing efficiency. Our approach involves classifying input images into 6 scenes through multiple feature extraction and analysis techniques. We have developed a method to select the top three appropriate dehazing methods from 15 ones, based on a comprehensive fusion evaluation of multiple indexes for each scene. Moreover, we have created specific color cast correction means to tackle two distinct issues. Comparative experiments on various collection images have verified the efficiency of our proposed method.

articleTitle: A data-driven soft-sensing model of matte grade in oxygen-rich side blow bath smelting process
abstract: A data-driven soft sensing technique is proposed to predict the matte grade, which is aimed at the problem of delay in traditional methods for sampling and determining the matte grade in oxygen-rich side blow bath smelting (OSBS), resulting in the inability to control and optimize the process in real time. This method is based on real-time detected process data and utilizes particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm to optimize dynamic process features to construct the optimal input feature set. For the datasets after feature selection, a kernel based extreme learning machine (KELM) is used for regression model training. To adapt to the instant variations and dynamics of the copper smelting process, a local learning strategy combining sliding windows is introduced, which in turn builds an instant learning kernel extreme learning machine regressor. This instant learning regressor is particularly suitable for online learning and real-time prediction due to the simplicity, efficiency, and low time consumption of the KELM algorithm. The feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method are verified through experiments conducted with data collected on an actual smelting production line.

Index Terms: Activation Function Of The Hidden Layer

articleTitle: Fault Detection for Nonlinear Systems with Intermittent Measurement Transmissions Based on Fuzzy Hybrid Observer
abstract: This paper is dealt with the problem of fault detection for nonlinear systems with intermittent measurement transmissions. A new fuzzy hybrid observer scheme is presented to achieve the purpose of fault detection, whose correction terms are instantly updated while measurements are received. Specifically, under a framework of hybrid systems, the exponential convergence of the estimation error system is analyzed, and the asynchronization of the premise variables between the fuzzy systems and the designed observer is coped with the matrix transformation technique. Different from the existing observer schemes, the proposed one does not depend on the requirements of continuous or periodical communication and is more applicable in digital and networked contexts with limited bandwidth. Finally, simulation results are given to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Research on Model Predictive Control of Quadruped Robot Based on Improved Single Rigid Body Dynamics Model
abstract: The dynamic model of a rigid body is widely utilized to depict the overall motion characteristics of robots, particularly in the realm of motion control for quadruped robots. However, conventional approaches tend to oversimplify the angular motion equations of the single rigid body dynamic model, resulting in inadequate performance in terms of angular motion direction for the robot. This paper proposes an improved method for the dynamic modeling of a quadruped robot based on a single rigid body model. By preserving more linear terms in the angular motion direction compared to the simplified approach, a motion controller is designed for the quadruped robot. The controller consists of a model predictive controller based on the improved single rigid body dynamic model and a whole-body controller. Experimental results demonstrate that this motion controller exhibits excellent performance in tracking the angular motion direction of the quadruped robot.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Feature Selection Algorithm Based on Maximum Relevance Minimum Redundancy and Splicing Strategy1
abstract: To address the challenge of complexity and the difficulty in determining the number of optimal feature subsets in feature selection, this paper proposed an enhanced feature selection algorithm which can be used when preprocessing data in machine learning projects to improve the performance and efficiency of models. This method integrates the principles of maximum relevance and minimum redundancy with the splicing technique. This study also integrates the relationship between the number of feature subsets and the error rate, introducing weighted values to feature subset count and error rates. Experimental result conducted on UCI datasets demonstrates the method's capability to effectively eliminate irrelevant redundant features while maintaining accuracy. The approach significantly reduces the number of features.

articleTitle: Fatigue Driving Behavior Detection Based on PiPnet Improvement
abstract: Traffic accidents are a major social problem worldwide, resulting in a large number of casualties and property damage. In this paper, the driver fatigue detection system monitors the coordinates of the driver's eyes, eyebrows, mouth, and other facial landmarks of the head, and evaluates the fatigue state of the driver by analyzing the blinking frequency, yawning frequency, and head nodding frequency, which helps to improve road safety and reduce traffic accidents. In this paper, a facial landmark detection model CA-Mobilevitv2 is proposed on the basis of PIPNet, which is applied to the driver fatigue detection system in combination with face detection (Retinaface). CA-Mobilevitv2 uses a lightweight Coordinate Attention module embedded in MobileVitv2 as a backbone CA-Mobilevitv2 uses a lightweight Coordinate Attention module embedded into MobileVitv2 as the backbone network, which reduces the computational and parameter counts by 0.5GFLOPs and 5M, respectively; meanwhile, it adopts the strategy of fusing multi-layer auxiliary detection heads to fully utilize feature maps at different levels to improve the model's adaptability and robustness. Finally, adding the credibility prediction of each facial landmark neighbor to the PiP Regression detection header reduces the normalized mean error (NME) of the model by 0.51% on the challenge set of 300W dataset.

articleTitle: A collaborative combat decision-making method based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning
abstract: In the complex and unknown modern warfare, drone clusters may lose communication with the command center or within the cluster. Confronted with the problem of inflexibility, and fragility when using centralized control format and the issue of complexity when utilizing decentralized format, the multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient based (MADDPG-based) combat model with centralized training and decentralized execution is proposed to improve the collaborative ability of the drone cluster. The actor network in this model output an action that maximizes the expected rewards for the drone based on the observation, while the critic network only works during the model training to evaluate the actions. This algorithm does not require a differentiable communication channel between drones, which is suitable for the denial combat environment. The experimental results in the one-to-one interception and multiple-to-one interception scenarios demonstrate the good performance of the proposed method, and the drone could cooperate with other drones to intelligently and collaboratively accomplish the strike mission.

articleTitle: Flexible Landing Control of a Quadruped Robot’s 2-DOF Leg Using DDPG During Free Fall at Varying Heights
abstract: This paper presents a deep reinforcement learning-based method for two-degree-of-freedom (2-DOF) flexible landing leg for quadruped robots, which aims to mitigate the problem of high impact forces during free-fall landings at uncertain heights. First, a virtual model controller (VMC) for the 2-DOF leg is created in Cartesian space. Then, the hybrid control method is used, which utilizes a control policy during falling and fixed impedance parameters during buffering. In addition, a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) based control policy for the falling stage is developed, which aims to learn an impedance parameter adjustment policy specific to the free fall of the leg within a certain height range. Finally, the proposed method was validated by simulation experiments. This showed that it reduces the impact forces during landing more and more effectively with increasing height. At the same time, the reasons for the reduction in impact forces were elucidated by an analysis based on the relationship between impulse and momentum.

articleTitle: Design of multi-channel synchronization signal acquisition method based on FPGA
abstract: In the field of aerospace, engines play a vital role, and rolling bearings, as the core components within them, have a significant impact on the production and operation of the entire equipment system. Therefore, real-time monitoring of the engine to ensure the safe operation of the equipment is indispensable. Therefore, this paper designs and implements a multi-channel synchronous acquisition card system based on FPGA platform to realize real-time acquisition of engine vibration signals, and then analyzes its running state and makes accurate judgments. Aiming at the problems of slow information interaction speed and high bit error rate between FPGA and host computer, we design a message interaction optimization method based on UART, which successfully improved the speed and accuracy of data transmission. At the same time, in order to solve the problem of complex and difficult management of system parameters, we design a RAM based addressing storage method, which can effectively realize the long-term storage of parameters and ensure the stability of data. And the method adopts modularization and parametric design strategy, so it has high portability. The simulation results show that the signal-to-noise ratio of the method can reach 95dB and the power consumption is only 0.26W, which meets the requirements of vibration signal acquisition and power consumption. These characteristics make the system have high engineering application value in the field of aerospace engine monitoring.

articleTitle: Many-objective Optimization for Planning of Park-level Integrated Energy System Considering Integrated Demand Response of Industry
abstract: This paper presents a many-objective optimization framework designed for the planning of Park-level Integrated Energy Systems (PIES), incorporating the integrated demand response of the industrial sector. The framework introduces a motivation strategy that considers the quality of service for industrial production. Simulation results demonstrate that the established many-objective optimization framework effectively balances all objectives of PIES. The motivation strategy facilitates a reduction in energy consumption costs for the industry while minimizing changes to production schedules. Consequently, the planning of PIES is rendered more rational. Moreover, the motivation strategy, which incorporates the quality of service for industrial production, offers valuable technical insights for fostering collaboration between PIES and industrial sectors.

articleTitle: Convolution-Based Sequence to Sequence Model for the Next-Day Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
abstract: In photovoltaic power forecasting, problems such as seasonal characteristics change and insufficient historical data are often faced. And because of the randomness of actual weather changes, it is very difficult to forecast the power curve of the next day. In this paper, we propose a series of solutions to these difficulties. By the time series decomposition, we solve the problem of data distribution fluctuation caused by seasonal feature changes. By using the convolution-based sequence to sequence model, we effectively combined historical observed data with future forecasted weather data, and accurately learn the time correlation. We adopt the multi-kernel gated convolutional neural networks to achieve learning of accurate local cross features. By analyzing the correlation between the features and the actual power at different times of one day, we propose a time-specific forecasting layer. Experiments show that our method has significant performance improvement compared with baseline models.

articleTitle: Error Related Potential Detection Algorithm for Brain Computer Interface
abstract: The utilization of error-related potentials (ErrPs) in brain-computer interfaces shows great promise for improving control performance. However, several limitations, such as insufficient data and data imbalance, often impede the accurate recognition of ErrPs. This study proposed a Filter Bank Convolutional Neural Network (FBCNN) method to detect ErrPs. The architectural design integrates signals from various frequency bands and employs a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to capture spatial and time information within the signals. Furthermore, a time window that randomly shifts is devised to address variances stemming from different response times among subjects. Simulation experiments affirm the effectiveness of the proposed methodology. We also analyze the enhancement in system control performance by using ErrPs in correcting and rejecting erroneous commands in two scenarios.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Fast Information Consensus Filter
abstract: In distributed state estimation for linear systems with multi-sensor networks, the event-triggered fast information consensus filtering algorithm (ET-FICF) is proposed to address the problems of high communication burden and high number of iterations of the information consensus algorithm. The algorithm utilises a distributed fast consensus weighting algorithm based on alternating direction multiplier method (ADMM) to obtain the weight matrix. For the consensus iteration step, a specific trigger mechanism is designed based on hypothesis testing of Gaussian distribution. The proposed ET-FICF algorithm not only effectively reduces the communication burden, but also has a high consensus speed. Finally, the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm are verified by simulation examples.

articleTitle: Self-triggered Distributed Model Predictive Control for a Class of Nonlinear MASs under FDI attacks
abstract: An aperiodic self-triggered distributed model predictive control algorithm is proposed for discrete nonlinear multi-agent systems (MASs) having sensor-controller channel false data injection (FDI) attacks. An augmented state observer is designed to estimate the real state of the system, and the distributed predictive controller is built on the estimated state such that the MASs stabilize towards the origin. Meanwhile, the self-triggered mechanism is applied to the controller, wherein its triggering condition is derived from the decline of cost function to save computational resources. Then, the recursive feasibility of the optimization problem and the stability of the MASs under the self-triggered distributed model predictive control scheme are analyzed. Eventually, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Collaborative Encirclement of Multiple UAVs Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Multi UAVs collaborative encirclement, as an important component of multi UAVs collaborative tasks, has become a key growth point for future UAVs new combat capabilities. However, there are problems with low success rate, poor collaborative ability, and easy destruction of the encirclement formation in collaborative encirclement by multiple UAVs. To address these problems, this paper proposes a gradient reinforcement learning algorithm with multiple attention depth dual delay deterministic strategies. In this algorithm, the dual delay deterministic strategy gradient effectively solves the problem of excessive errors in UAVs collaborative decision-making caused by high output Q values of the Critic network. The multi head attention mechanism can improve the efficiency of UAVs collaborative decision-making. In the experiment, in order to adapt to the adversarial nature of both sides in actual encirclement, a deep deterministic strategy gradient algorithm was used to train the escape target. The escape target can autonomously adjust its escape strategy to escape the coordinated encirclement of UAVs as much as possible. The experimental results show that the UAVs trained by the proposed algorithm can efficiently complete collaborative capture tasks and has better convergence characteristics. Finally, the multi head attention mechanism was introduced into the multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient reinforcement learning algorithm, verifying its good applicability in improving the performance of multi-agent deterministic policy reinforcement learning algorithms.

articleTitle: Research on Control Strategy for Weighing Process of Ladle Furnace
abstract: Due to the uncertainties in the alloy weighing process, traditional control strategies struggle to meet the increasing accuracy requirements. This paper proposes a weight-flow dual-loop learning control strategy. The outer loop, weight control, utilizes an iterative self-learning algorithm to optimize the predefined S-shaped feeding flow curve, thereby mitigating the impact of system uncertainties and disturbances between batches on the final feeding error. The inner loop, flow control, employs a reinforcement learning PID algorithm to track the optimized flow curve obtained from the outer loop. It dynamically adjusts the control strategy through real-time interaction with the system to overcome within-batch disturbances and adapt to time-varying characteristics. Numerical simulations are conducted to verify the effectiveness, accuracy, and robustness of this control strategy.

articleTitle: Prediction of Cement Strength Based on Hybrid Neural Networks
abstract: Cement grinding is the last link in the cement factory, and its working conditions are complex, resulting in the optimization and adjustment of grinding parameters becoming complicated and difficult, while the prediction of the strength of the finished cement product has a crucial position in helping cement grinding to be better controlled. In order to better predict cement strength, this paper constructs a hybrid deep learning model combining convolutional neural network (CNN) and bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU) with an attention mechanism to solve the above problem. The model parameters are updated using stochastic gradient descent method and loss function during training. Finally, the validity, accuracy, and superiority of the CNN-BiGRU-Attention model were verified by using the data for testing and comparing it with other models using standard error and coefficient of determination as metrics.

articleTitle: Moving Object Recognition on Production Line Based on Adaptive Frame Differencing Algorithm
abstract: In order to solve the problem that the traditional moving object recognition algorithms for industrial production lines are susceptible to external interference in complex backgrounds and the recognition accuracy is reduced, this paper proposes a moving object recognition algorithm based on Adaptive Frame Differencing (AFD). Firstly, the contrast of moving object images on the production line is enhanced by using gamma transformation for image enhancement and bilateral filtering for noise reduction. Then, the AFD algorithm is used to combine the global distribution of image pixels to realize the dynamic adjustment of image threshold. Based on adaptive threshold, the proposed algorithm can achieve image segmentation and accurate recognition of moving objects under different backgrounds and external interference conditions. In order to verify the reliability of the algorithm, three sets of moving object image datasets under different conditions are tested. The accuracy and recall rate indicators are significantly improved.

articleTitle: Encoder Teacher-student Network for Foreign Object Intrusion
abstract: Foreign body intrusion in high-speed railway is often accompanied by the heavy loss of life and property. Therefore, the monitoring of foreign objects in the railway industry is of great significance to maintain the safe, reliable and stable operation of the entire railway. The continuous development of deep learning theory and the improvement of computation resource provide new possibilities for the identification and judgment of foreign object intrusion by using the existing cameras. In this paper, we propose an improving Teacher-Student network based on knowledge distillation, which is able to judge and identify foreign body intrusion through 2K video stream captured by the railway, and propose an attention mechanism based on probability density to effectively improve the model identification ability due to the needs of the railway scene. Compared with the supervised learning approach, this paper utilizes the unsupervised learning approach to effectively cope with the irregularity, complexity and even unknowability of foreign objects. Experiments on the private dataset prove that the AUC value can be as high as 0.99, the false positive rate and the false negative rate are less than 2%, and the real-time performance can meet the practical needs of the railway. Meanwhile, our model provides an alternative approach for foreign body intrusion.

articleTitle: Optimal scheduling of multi-energy medium in steel enterprises based on improved genetic simulated annealing algorithm
abstract: The scheduling of energy medium in steel enterprises is a complex problem of multi-media coupling and multi-period coordination. Considering the time-of-use electricity price, a mathematical programming model for the optimization of byproduct gas is established. Aiming at the above model with more variables and constraints, an improved genetic simulated annealing algorithm is proposed based on matrix real-coded. The initial population is generated by using the chaos theory which is characterized by randomness and ergodicity. The simulated annealing process and constraint handling strategies are carried out for new individuals to maintain population diversity. The comparison experiment simulation verifies that the proposed method can solve the problems of optimal allocation of energy medium and reduce the production cost.

articleTitle: Research on Brain Tumor Segmentation and Identification Technology Based on Improved Unet
abstract: Brain tumors are common neurological diseases that severely threaten human health and even life. The accurate extraction of brain tumor information through Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is crucial for assisting diagnosis. Manual segmentation of brain tumor subregions is time-consuming, prone to error, and highly subjective. Therefore, it is necessary to design accurate, efficient, and reproducible automatic segmentation methods. This paper proposes an improved Unet model for three-dimensional brain tumor image segmentation. First, given the variability of three-dimensional brain tumor images, we downsample the Unet model three times to extract image features, which not only reduces the number of model parameters but also retains the target edge features to the maximum extent. Second, to address the class ambiguity caused by the reduction of deep features, we introduce a Multiple-Attention based Feature Pyramid Network (MA-FPN) module in the encoding and decoding parts of the model to extract multi-scale information from images and enhance feature expression. Finally, we add an edge extraction module based on the basic encoder. This module combines the semantic feature information extracted by the backbone network and the edge feature information obtained from the input image through Canny operator and dilation mathematical morphology operation, thereby better learning the edges of three-dimensional brain tumor images. The comparative experimental results show that our proposed model significantly improves the accuracy of brain tumor segmentation compared to traditional Unet, PSPNet, ICNet, and Fast-SCNN, with increases of 3.9%, 1.3%, 5%, and 3.9% respectively.

articleTitle: Bi-Contrastive Alignment for Incomplete Multi-view Clustering
abstract: Multi-view clustering (MVC) represents a significant challenge in the realms of machine learning and data mining. Recently, the advent of contrastive learning (CL) has catalyzed the development of numerous innovative methods within this field. The efficacy of these methods typically hinges on the availability of consistent and comprehensive data. Nevertheless, real-world scenarios of data collection and transmission frequently encounter issues like partial unaligned-views (PU), which result in incomplete datasets and pose formidable challenges for effective MVC. To address this prevalent issue, our paper introduces an innovative framework, termed bi-contrastive alignment for incomplete multi-view clustering (BCA). BCA specifically targets the challenge of incomplete data stemming from PU. It encompasses a unique module, semantic guided bi-contrastive alignment (SGBA), designed to counteract the PU by harnessing semantic similarities. Moreover, the framework augments data alignment by integrating a contrastive learning-based corrective component into the loss function. The comparative experiments demonstrate that the ARI metric of our method surpasses the second-best contrasting method on all four datasets.

articleTitle: Predictive Control for Transient Energy Growth of Thermoacoustic Systems in a Rijke Tube subject to Thermal Inertia
abstract: In combustion systems with stable eigenvalues, the presence of non-orthogonal eigenvalues can trigger instability due to transient growth caused by disturbances. This paper focuses on the impact of thermal inertia in Rijke tube unstable thermoacoustic systems with minimal transient energy growth. It aims to design predictive control strategy the Rijke tube system, ensuring the system's stability while minimizing the performance index including the acoustic energy, its variation rate, and control energy. Firstly, an ODE model for the thermoacoustic unstable system in a Rijke tube, incorporating nonlinear heat release and thermal inertia delay, was derived using the Galerkin method. Secondly, the optimization problem of the transient energy growth performance was proposed and the solvable condition was also presented by solving the convex optimization problem. Furthermore, an optimized predictive controller was designed. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed control and optimization method can asymptotically suppress the pressure oscillations in the Rijke tube achieve the optimized transient energy growth performance.

articleTitle: Condition Monitoring System for Cryogenic Equipment Based on Industrial Internet Platform
abstract: As a crucial component of the superconducting tokamak fusion device, the large helium cryogenic system plays a pivotal role in ensuring the safe, stable, and efficient operation of future fusion reactors. To meet the stringent demands of high reliability and convenient maintenance for cryogenic systems, we have conducted research on the safe, reliable, and intelligent operation technology of large cryogenic refrigerators within the cryogenic system of the CRAFT (Comprehensive Research Facility for Fusion Reactor Mainframe). To achieve this, we have adopted a "platform + APPs" approach to construct the system framework. Through the interconnection of data collectors, we have integrated real-time data from both the cryogenic PLC control system and video monitoring system. Based on the C/S (client/server) software architecture of the industrial Internet platform, we have designed and developed a condition monitoring system for cryogenic equipment. This system integrates remote monitoring of cryogenic systems, equipment performance analysis, equipment information management, and other essential functions. It aids in intelligent operation and maintenance decision-making for cryogenic systems.

articleTitle: CCDC 2024 TOC
Generative Domain Generalization Network based on Local Maximum Mean Discrepancy for Bearing Fault Diagnosis of Wind Turbine
abstract: The wind turbines (WTs) usually work in the variable environment. It leads to a frequent impact force act on WT bearings in different working conditions. It would take a look as a typical cross-domain fault diagnosis (FD) issue. Nevertheless, Intelligent FD models may face challenges in generalization when confronted with novel working conditions and managing low-resource datasets. To address the aforementioned challenges, we present a Generative Domain Generalization Network based on Local Maximum Mean Discrepancy (GDGN-LMMD). Within the framework of GDGN-LMMD, we introduce a potential domain generation network (PDGN). The network aims to achieve domain generalization under low-resource datasets by enhancing the variety of sample distributions under known working condition. Furthermore, we introduce a new domain generalization network based on LMMD (DGN-LMMD). This network is tailored to extract domain-invariant fault information from the source domain and potential domains, enabling generalization to previously unseen working conditions. Ultimately, the comprehensive case study demonstrates that GDGN-LMMD enhances diagnostic accuracy in unseen working conditions.

articleTitle: The Design of Quadrotor UAV Based on Nonlinear Active Disturbance Rejection Control
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) itself has a complex nonlinear dynamic model and is vulnerable to external interference when flying in the air, a control scheme of quadrotor UAV based on nonlinear active disturbance rejection control (NLADRC) was proposed. Firstly, the virtual control variables were introduced to decouple the quadrotor flight system and establish a dynamic model. Secondly, the nonlinear extended state observer (NLESO) is used to estimate and compensate for the internal uncertainty and the external disturbances of the system in real time, which improves the robustness and anti-disturbance ability of the system. The tracking error is suppressed by nonlinear state error feedback (NLSEF) and compensation efficiency is improved. Finally, the stability of the system is proved by experimental simulation through the simulation platform. The results show that the control scheme proposed in this paper can ensure the quadrotor track the target trajectory quickly and accurately with the advantages of small overshoot, higher precision and strong anti-disturbance ability while maintaining stability.

articleTitle: H∞ Reliable Bumpless Transfer Control for Switched Systems: A Mixed State/time Dependent Switching Method
abstract: This study is devoted to reliable bumpless transfer control for switched systems with actuator faults. Through construction of a switching strategy and a class of reliable controllers via output feedback, the bumpless transfer performance and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> reliable property of the closed-loop systems are ensured. The switching strategy consists of two parts, that is dwell time and state-dependent switching ones. In the dwell time stage, a low bound of the subsystem activated time is introduced to restrict the frequent switching and designed to reduce the control bumps. The bumpless transfer performance of systems is guaranteed. In the second stage, only the controller states are used to generate the switching signals, which guarantees the feasibility in the frame of output feedback. Finally, to ensure the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> reliable property, the time-varying controllers are constructed, which work in the different switching stages. A verification of the developed control scheme is given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Switching Model Predictive Control With Actuator Saturation And Average Dwell Time
abstract: In this paper, for discrete-time switched systems with uncertainty, we study its saturation model predictive control (SMPC) under the average dwell time switching rule. Firstly, a factor greater than 1 is introduced in the differential operation of the Lyapunov function, allowing it to increase at the switching instant, thereby increasing the design freedom to adjust the average dwell time, that is, the switching frequency; Introducing auxiliary matrix and convex combination technology to transform actuator saturation constraints into constraints on the system state; Obtain the SMPC design method under the double constraints of average dwell time and state space. Secondly, an appropriate switching invariant ellipsoid is constructed to obtain a feasible solution for the SMPC control gain. SMPC combined with the average dwell time constraint can ensure the feasibility of the sufficiency condition for solving the control gain, the robustness and stability of the closed-loop switched system.

articleTitle: Nuclear Power Plant Control System Health Index Based on Combination Weighting of CPA Indexes
abstract: Safety of nuclear power plants is of vital importance. In this context, Control Performance Assessment (CPA) emerges as a valuable tool for the evaluation of control system performance within nuclear power plants, employing a range of pertinent performance indexes. A comprehensive health index for control systems can be obtained by applying weighted considerations to these indexes. This paper introduces a novel combination weighting approach for the CPA indexes applicable to control systems in nuclear power plants. In situations that historical abnormal data for control systems is insufficient, entropy serves as a weighting mechanism. Moreover, for systems characterized by prolonged degradation processes, a hybrid weighting strategy is proposed. This hybrid approach combines entropy weighting with weights determined through SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), which quantifies the significance of various indexes in anomaly diagnosis. The proposed weighting method has shown good performance through testing with real operational data of nuclear power plants.

articleTitle: LQG Control for Networked Control Systems with Unknown Packet Dropouts and Input Delay
abstract: This paper investigates the linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) problem for networked control systems (NCSs) with input delay and packet dropouts. In NCSs, packet dropouts occur in both the control-actuator channel and the sensor-estimator channel, and input delay happens in the control-actuator channel. It is noted that there is no acknowledgment of successful delivery of control packets, i.e., the user datagram protocol (UDP) case. Therefore, the famous separation principle fails. The contributions of this paper are two-folds: Firstly, an approximate estimation Kalman filter algorithm is proposed to estimate the state of the system. Secondly, based on the approximate estimation of the state , explicit expression of the optimal controller is given by solving the delayed backward and forward difference equations.

articleTitle: A novel solution for civilian UAV identification based on RFF and machine learning
abstract: The proliferation of civilian unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in recent years has raised significant concerns regarding security threats. Radio frequency fingerprint (RFF) classification has been widely used for detecting and identifying unknown UAVs. This paper proposes an efficient UAV identification scheme that utilizes the discrete wavelet transform coefficients of differential signals (D-DWT) and machine learning. In the detection phase, the scheme extracts the preamble information of each signal frame based on energy variations and correlation detection. In the feature extraction phase, the impact of carrier frequency offset (CFO) on identification accuracy is analyzed, and the differential signals are transformed into the wavelet domain to analyze the anti-interference performance of the DWT coefficients. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively improves RFF recognition accuracies in low SNR scenarios and exhibits excellent resistance to doppler frequency offset. Among various machine learning classifiers, the scheme achieves device classification accuracies of 97.91% and 98.38% in 0dB and 5dB scenarios, respectively.

articleTitle: Research on Cooperative Navigation Algorithm under INS/Ranging Condition
abstract: Aiming at the navigation problem in the global navigation satellite system (GNSS) denied environment, a cooperative navigation algorithm for multi-aircraft based on Unscented Kalman filter (UKF) is proposed by combining data link ranging with inertial navigation system (INS). In this way, the aircraft formation can adapt to the cooperative needs of multiple aircraft under the condition of losing satellite navigation. By introducing the adaptive node selection algorithm and using UKF to solve the nonlinear system, the estimation accuracy and robustness of measurement noise are improved compared with traditional formation navigation.

articleTitle: Analysis of future demand for a general-purpose UAV Attitude and Heading Reference system
abstract: The use of UAVs to carry out unmanned combat is becoming more and more prominent in modernized intelligent warfare, and even plays a decisive role in some local conflicts, and UAV equipment is further advancing to the main battle equipment. Facing the future UAV low-cost expendable, artificial intelligence and autonomy, ultra-high speed, ultra-time, high mobility combat and other war technology needs, this paper puts forward the technical characteristics that the Attitude and Heading System(AHRS) should have from the perspective of system requirement analysis, and elaborates on what technical paths are adopted to realize these technical characteristics.

articleTitle: Multi-rotor UAV path planning based on Model Predictive Control and Control Barrier Function
abstract: The safety of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) path planning in autonomous urban flight is challenging due to the presence of buildings. Previous studies have focused more on the distance between buildings and UAVs, but ignored the effect of UAV state on path planning. In this paper, we propose a path planning method based on model predictive control (MPC) and control barrier functions (CBF) for UAVs to effectively address the challenge of autonomous UAVs flight. By incorporating CBF and MPC, the MPC optimization is formulated to predict the UAV's flight path based on the current state of the UAV in the receding horizon before considering obstacle avoidance. The CBF constraint guarantees that there are no collisions between the UAV and obstacles, and that the MPC creates an optimal path. This method helps planners design control strategies that meet safety requirements. It improves the spatial configuration between the UAV and nearby obstacles, ensuring that they remain outside the safe range. The method has been verified through simulation and real-world experiments, demonstrating that the UAV maintains a safe distance from obstacles and can also find the shortest path during its flight.
