articleTitle: DET-Composite Secure Control for CPMG under Deception Attacks
abstract: In this paper, a dynamic event-triggered(DET) composite secure load frequency control strategy for the cyber-physical microgrid (CPMG) with the deception attacks is investigated. Firstly, to deal with the network resource limitation problem of the CPMG, a dynamic event-triggered mechanism is formulated, in which the attack estimation information is adopted to further enlarge the triggering intervals. Then, to defense the deception attacks actively, the attack estimator is formulated. It is worthy of pointing that the attack estimator utilizes the triggered control signals to save the network resource. Furthermore, the composited secure load frequency control strategy is constructed, which employs the estimated deception attack information, therefore the active defense performance is enhanced. Moreover, it is shown that the closed-loop system of the CPMG is input-to-state practical stable (ISpS). Finally, the case studies confirm the effectiveness of the proposed composite secure load frequency control method.

articleTitle: Prescribed-Time Stabilizaition of Linear Stochastic Parabolic Systems
abstract: This paper deals with a kind of prescribed-time stability (PTS) problem for a stochastic parabolic system with Dirichlet boundary conditions. A distributed controller is designed to ensure the stability of the system within the prescribed time (PT). It should be noted that the time of convergence is not dependent on the initial value, and it is also possible to be set in advance. Additionally, through analysis, the proof shows that the proposed distributed controller is bounded in the PT. While, the unknown external disturbances are taken into account and ensure the system’s performance in terms of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> by designing a state feedback controller. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control method is verified through a simulation example.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Control for Differential Linear Repetitive Processes Based on a Novel Reaching Law
abstract: In this paper, the sliding mode control problem of differential linear repetitive processes is addressed via the reaching law approach. A linear sliding function is first constructed based on the current process state. Reaching conditions of differential LRPs are defined, which combines the characteristics of continuous and discrete systems. Accordingly, a novel reaching law is proposed and the corresponding sliding mode controller is provided, which not only reflect the influence of signals in both directions (along the pass as well as pass-to-pass directions) but also guarantee the reachability of sliding domain. Through the introduction of a model transformation matrix, the sliding mode dynamics are obtained and the corresponding stability along the pass is achieved. Finally, a numerical example is presented to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Combining Gated SENet with ResNet Backbone for Image Classification
abstract: Image classification is a highly popular direction in the field of artificial intelligence, and its achievements hold significant reference value across numerous domains. Models and architectures such as ResNet, U-Net, Transformer, among others, are widely employed in various fields. Therefore, an efficient and accurate model plays a crucial role in image classification. In this paper, we propose a novel model named Gate Convolution SENet ResNet (GCSR-Net). It enhances the SENet module by introducing a convolutional layer and a gating unit, integrating these improvements into the original ResNet. The proposed GCSR-Net incorporates convolutional fusion to enhance its global contextual awareness and employs a gating mechanism to dynamically adjust the strength of feature information. It improves the accuracy of image classification and accelerates the convergence speed. Experimental results demonstrate its impressive performance on the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets, achieving a top-1 accuracy of 95.90% on CIFAR-10 and 80.32% on CIFAR-100, respectively. Furthermore, GCRS-Net converges after only 100 epochs without pretraining, accelerating by 50% in convergence speed. Therefore, the model proposed in this paper possesses reliability and robustness.

articleTitle: Gradient-Optimized B-spline Trajectory Planning for Unmanned Platforms
abstract: Local trajectory planning plays a pivotal role in ensuring the core functionality of autonomous driving systems. This paper presents a fast and lightweight B-spline curve optimizer for local trajectory planning in autonomous driving systems, incorporating three key metrics: safety, smoothness, and efficiency. The algorithm utilizes collision and collision-free trajectory gradient information obtained through A* search for efficient collision distance estimation, thereby generating safety metrics during trajectory optimization. The unconstrained optimization problem is addressed using L-BFGS, significantly improving solution efficiency. The algorithm’s effectiveness and real-time performance are validated through simulations and practical experiments.

articleTitle: Robust fixed-time consensus tracking control for multiple wheeled mobile robots
abstract: This paper investigates the fixed-time leader-following consensus tracking problem for multiple wheeled mobile robots in the presence of external disturbances, where both the dynamics and kinematics levels of multi-robot systems are taken into account. A novel fixed-time distributed estimator-controller scheme is proposed to achieve the consensus tracking within a fixed time independent of initial conditions. Based on Lyapunov stability method and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> theory, sufficient conditions and the upper bound of settling time for the closed-loop system are obtained, and the L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gain of the system is equal to or less than γ that shows strong robustness to the disturbances. Finally, the simulation results are given to show the feasibility and effectiveness of the designed control method.

articleTitle: Event-based fixed-time synchronization in Multi-layer networks under DoS attack
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of event-based fixed-time synchronization in multi-layer network under DoS attack. Unlike conventional fixed-time synchronization condition, this paper separately discusses the Lyapunov function under attack and unattack states. The event-triggered mechanism designed on this basis can avoid the appearance of Zeno behavior. Finally, numerical simulation verifies the validity of the theoretical derivation.

articleTitle: Adaptive Filtering Algorithm based on Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Real-time state estimation of dynamic systems is a basic task in control theory and signal processing. Kalman filter is a minimum complex optimal state estimator for linear state space models with fully known system parameters, which is widely used in industrial production. However, in practical problems, accurate models and linear state-space models are often difficult to satisfy. In this paper, by combining reinforcement learning and Kalman filter, an adaptive strategy of state space model is designed based on PPO algorithm to improve the performance of state estimation under the inaccuracy conditions of the system model. The algorithm is called Reinforcement Learning Kalman filter algorithm (RLKF). Finally, we prove by numerical results that the Reinforcement Learning Kalman filtering algorithm overcomes the model mismatch and nonlinearity, and the accuracy is better than the traditional filtering algorithm.

articleTitle: Prescribed-Time Control with Time Transformation Method for Nanopositioning Stages
abstract: Conventional sliding mode control methods often lack the capability to accurately predict and regulate convergence times, leading to uncertainties in high-precision applications. This paper introduces a novel prescribed-time control strategy that leverages an advanced time transformation method to ensure reliable trajectory tracking. This approach ingeniously maps the operational domain from a finite interval [0, ࣎) onto an extended infinite time horizon [0, λ), which significantly streamlines the stability analysis and eases the synthesis of the control law. The efficacy of the proposed controller is validated through simulations involving piezoelectric nanopositioning stages, wherein the results confirm its ability to maintain prescribed-time stability.

articleTitle: Balancing Operation Cost and Carbon Emissions in Multi-Energy Microgrid Scheduling Using Joint Operator Evolutionary Algorithm
abstract: A multi-energy microgrid (MEMG), incorporating a combined heat and power (CHP) system and electric vehicles (EVs), is an important infrastructure to meet multiple energy demands and reduce carbon emissions. However, operation cost minimization and carbon emissions minimization in the MEMG conflict with each other. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-objective optimal scheduling model for the MEMG, aimed at achieving a balance between operation cost and carbon emissions. Moreover, a novel multi-objective evolutionary algorithm (MOEA) called joint operator evolutionary algorithm (JOEA) is developed to solve this model. Experimental results indicate that JOEA has excellent performance on the proposed multi-objective optimal scheduling problem. In addition, JOEA is compared with several well-known MOEAs on this engineering problem and 20 benchmark problems. The comparison results show that JOEA outperforms other MOEAs and has competitive performance.

articleTitle: Asynchronous fault detection filter design for switched systems based on event-triggered communication scheme
abstract: This paper is concerned with the fault detection problem of switched systems under event-triggered transmission mechanism. A fault detection filter is presented as a residual generator to detect the fault signal. Then, a method of the merging switching signal is introduced, the augmented fault detection system with the merged switching signal is established. By using the Lyapunov stability theory and the average dwell time method, some sufficient conditions are obtained such that the augmented system is exponentially stable and satisfies H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> performance under asynchronous switching. Furthermore, the corresponding coefficient matrices of the fault detection filters are also presented with the explicit expressions. Finally, a numerical example is used to show the effectiveness of the approach proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: A Preference-based Reinforcement Learning Approach Using Reward Exploration for Decision Making
abstract: Preference-based reinforement learning solves decision making based on human preferences. By deriving a reward function from human preferences, the agent’s behavior aligns with human expectations, avoiding complex reward tasks. However, in preference-based reinforcement learning, a human teacher can only select one segment of trajectories from a pair, limiting reward function learning. Providing diverse trajectory segments can assist human teachers in better making a selection between two segments. To address this issue, a method is proposed to encourage the exploration of the reward model and thus promote generating more diverse trajectories. This encourages the exploration of the agent to provide a more diverse set of trajectories for the human teacher’s selection. Numerical studies demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method over other preference-based reinforcement learning methods.

articleTitle: Feature Selection and Hyperparameter Optimization for Combustion Status Recognition Model of MSWI Process Based on Parallel Differential Evolution
abstract: Accurately identifying flame combustion status during municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) is a crucial prerequisite for intelligent combustion control. Previous research in constructing identification models often relied on expert knowledge and extensive repetitive experiments to determine hyperparameters and feature selection parameters. The process of parameter determination was resourceintensive, demanding significant computational power. To tackle these challenges, a method using parallel differential evolution (PDE) algorithms for optimizing the hyperparameters of combustion state recognition models is proposed. Initially, feature parameters and model hyperparameters are encoded as chromosome groups for the differential evolution algorithm, followed by random parameter initialization. Then, the population is randomly divided into several subpopulations, and each undergoing parallel evolution. Evolution halts upon meeting specific stagnation conditions. Finally, the hyperparameters enabling the recognition model based on vision transformer and improved deep forest classification to achieve optimal performance. The effective of the proposed method is validated by using the actual data of an MSWI plant.

articleTitle: Multidisciplinary Optimization of Electric Helicopter Based on Genetic Algorithm
abstract: With the pursuit of green aviation, the electric helicopter has attracted wide attention because of its energy saving, environmental protection and low noise. This paper studies the multidisciplinary optimization of an electric helicopter based on genetic algorithm (GA). A multidisciplinary optimization analysis model of the electric helicopter consisting of weight efficiency, economic efficiency and flight performance is established. In addition, the GA is given to obtain the optimal design solution that meets the design criteria of the electric helicopter, in which the overall parameters are used as design variables, and the penalty function method is used to process the constrained nonlinear programming problem into an unconstrained problem. Finally, a calculation example verifies that the solution of GA is better than particle swarm optimization (PSO) under the multidisciplinary optimization analysis model.

articleTitle: Practical Predefined-time Sliding Mode Control for Uncertain Marine Natural Gas Engine
abstract: It is a significant and challenging task to realize the speed control of marine natural gas engines with uncertainty and external disturbances. In this paper, a new speed control strategy based on practical predefined-time stability and nonlinear sliding surface was proposed for marine natural gas engine. Firstly, the nonlinear uncertain engine mathematical model including complex intake dynamics and torque generation dynamics is established. Then, a nonlinear sliding manifold is designed using predefined-time stability theory to improve the tracking performance. In order to reduce response time of engine speed, a novel practical predefined-time reaching law is utilized for controller design. Further, strict theoretical analysis proves the stability of the closed loop system. Finally, in order to further prove the effectiveness and advantages of proposed approach, it was compared with traditional PID and non-singular terminal sliding mode (NTSM) control in simulation.

articleTitle: Numerical integration-based algorithm for efficient actual navigation performance of airborne integrated navigation systems
abstract: Flight management system is one of the core technologies of avionics system for large civil aircraft. Among them, the integrated navigation system is the core component of the flight management system, supporting trajectory prediction, autopilot, flight guidance and other key functions. The actual navigation performance (ANP) can reflect the navigation performance of the integrated navigation system at the current moment. Under the performance based navigation (PBN) mode of operation, a fast and accurate calculation of ANP is indispensable for the navigation and positioning solving and navigation mode management of the integrated navigation system of an airplane, and the key to the calculation of ANP lies in the accuracy and fastness of the calculation. Aiming at the above problems, the two-dimensional normal distribution characteristics of the position error of the integrated navigation system are studied, and an ANP evaluation model based on the two-dimensional error probability density function is established. The ANP evaluation process is simplified into a probability calculation problem. An efficient ANP algorithm for airborne integrated navigation systems based on numerical integration is proposed, which adopts Gauss Legende's efficient numerical integration method to accelerate the computation speed of the dual integration, and at the same time optimizes the existence interval of ANP based on the error distribution characteristics, and adopts the bisection iterative method to quickly compute the ANP value of the integrated navigation system within the interval. The simulation results show that compared with the traditional algorithm, the Gauss Legende numerical integration-bisection iteration algorithm greatly reduces the computation time and improves the computation efficiency while guaranteeing the accuracy, providing reliable support for the integrated navigation system of the aircraft to carry out the functions of navigation and positioning solving and navigation mode management.

articleTitle: Multi-MPC control of a solid oxide fuel cell system based on balanced decomposition
abstract: This paper studies the multi-MPC control of a typical solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) system. As a potential generation technology, the SOFC system has a series of merits, such as clear and pollution-free, all solid state structure, quiet operation, high reliability, and so on. However, it is not easy to design a controller for the SOFC system, as it is nonlinear and complex. This paper analyzes its model characteristics in details and finds that the SOFC can be turned into a Hammerstein-Wiener system. Thus, the included angle can be applied to measure its nonlinearity and a balanced multi-model decomposition method is proposed for the SOFC system, and then the multi-MPC is employed to design a control for it. Simulations illustrate that the proposed decomposition method and the multi-MPC can obtain better closed-loop performance than other methods.

articleTitle: Research on optical fiber SPR sensing technology enhanced by halloysite nanotubes
abstract: In this paper, a transmission fiber optic sensor based on surface plasmon resonance (SPR) was proposed to measure refractive index and temperature, which is enhanced by halloysite nanotubes(HNTs). The sensor employs a transmission structure with a gold film as the metal layer for exciting SPR. HNTS are then deposited on the gold film using electrostatic adsorption as a material to enhance the sensor's sensitivity. This allows for measuring refractive index sensitivity changes in the external solution. By encapsulating HNTs with a layer of PDMS, temperature can also be measured. Experimental results demonstrate that the sensor, enhanced by HNTs, achieves a refractive index sensitivity of 4147nm/RIU and a temperature sensitivity of -4.51nm/°C. The use of HNTs as an enhancing material offers low cost and simple fabrication, as well as strong biocompatibility and a large specific surface area. These unique features make the proposed HNTs-SPR sensor great prospects for high-sensitivity detection of biochemical quantities in the field of optical fiber sensing.

articleTitle: Observer-based Stability Analysis for a Class of Relay Control Systems
abstract: This note investigates the problem of stability analysis for a class of relay control systems. Base on full-order Luenberger observer and Lyapunov approach, the constructive sufficient conditions for the existence of the hyperplane-based switching law, which guarantees the stabilization of the closed-loop systems, are proposed. It is also shown that these conditions can be derived in terms of feasibility of a set of linear matrix inequalities. Finally, a numerical example is given to demonstrate the effectiveness of our methods.

articleTitle: Static Output-Feedback Integral Sliding Mode for T-S Fuzzy Descriptor Systems with Partly Unmeasurable Premise Variables
abstract: This paper focuses on the problem of designing static output-feedback sliding mode controllers for T-S fuzzy descriptor systems with partly unmeasurable premise variables. A canonical form-based static output-feedback integral sliding mode controller design method is proposed, where only the measurable premise variables are used. Measurable premise variables and unmeasurable premise variables in the T-S fuzzy descriptor are separated. The designing matrix in the output-based integral-type switching function is solved by a canonical form-based method. Both the finite-time reachability of the sliding surface and the asymptotic stability of the resulting closed-loop system are proved. Finally, an example is given to illustrate the effectiveness of proposed method.

articleTitle: An CSAR Imaging Strategy for Enhanced Ground Moving Target Tracking and Focusing
abstract: In recent years, the tracking and imaging of ground moving targets in Circular Synthetic Aperture Radar (CSAR) have garnered considerable interest among researchers. This paper introduces a rapid CSAR imaging strategy aimed at reducing calculation time and enhancing the focusing effect on moving targets. The proposed strategy enables real-time target search, tracking, and automatic selection of the imaging area based on the target’s real-time position.The first step involves determining the object’s motion trajectory using a combination of the target search algorithm and the Kalman filter. Subsequently, the imaging plane is selected based on the real-time position of the object. In the second step, full-aperture data is segmented into sub-apertures and then approximated as linear arrays for imaging. The final step involves sub-images fusion to produce the ultimate CSAR image.This method significantly reduces imaging time, yielding well-focused CSAR images and real-time motion trajectories of moving targets. The proposed algorithm is verified by both simulation and processing real data collected with our mmWave imager prototype utilizing commercially available 77-GHz MIMO radar sensors. Through the experimental results we verified the performance and the superiority of the our algorithm.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Pattern Optimization of SI Model Based on PD Control Strategy
abstract: Current research on the spatial patterns of epidemic models, both domestically and internationally, tends to focus on the impact of system parameters or diffusion coefficients on these patterns. However, studies on controlling these spatial patterns are relatively scarce. Effective control of spatial patterns in epidemic models can be crucial for predicting epidemic dynamics within specific areas. This article establishes an SI spatial epidemic model incorporating self-diffusion and cross-diffusion terms. A proportional differential controller is proposed to manage the spatial patterns of the SI model. Conditions are also provided under which the controlled system experiences Hiring instability. The effectiveness of the controller is validated through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Truncated Cauchy Loss for Outlier-Robust Blind Image Deblurring
abstract: In complex imaging environments, captured images often contain outliers like impulse noise, Cauchy noise, and saturated pixels, posing significant challenges for image deblurring. While existing blind deblurring methods can address outliers to a certain extent, the incorporation of intricate operations tends to amplify the complexity of the deblurring process. In light of these challenges, we present a simple yet robust blind deblurring algorithm for handling images with outliers. To alleviate the effect of outliers on kernel estimation, we introduce a truncated Cauchy loss function, which effectively suppresses outliers by truncating significant errors. Furthermore, we employ a statistics-based approach for outlier detection, eliminating the need for heuristic methods. The proposed approach is shown to be easily implementable and extendable for non-blind deblurring. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art methods for both blurred images with outliers and those without.

articleTitle: Secure Dispatch Strategy for Cyber-Physical Energy Systems under False Data and DoS Attacks
abstract: The confluence of myriad energy sources and the advancement of cutting-edge smart grid technologies have radically altered the landscapes of energy creation, distribution, and consumption. Amidst this epoch of transformative progress, which brings forth a wealth of benefits, there is an undeniable susceptibility to cyber-physical threats. This paper delves secure dispatch strategy for cyber-physical energy systems considering both false data and denial-of service (DoS) attacks. The strategy is designed by leveraging the distributed estimation and adaptive regulation, which offers strong security and resilience. To substantiate our findings and demonstrate the practical applicability of our proposed strategy, a comprehensive case study is provided, showcasing the strategy’s effectiveness and efficiency in safeguarding cyber-physical energy systems against false data and DoS attacks.

articleTitle: Quadratic Stabilization and ℒ2 Performance Design of Switched Uncertain Affine Systems
abstract: We deal with quadratic stabilization (QS) and ℒ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> performance design for switched systems which are composed of a finite set of uncertain affine subsystems. In each subsystem, there exists norm bounded uncertainty in the system matrix, and the vector field includes a nonlinear term with quadratic constraint. Under the assumption that there is a convex combination of subsystems’ affine vectors reaching the origin, we construct a convex combination of subsystems (CCS) without an affine vector, by using the coefficients in the convex combination of affine vectors. If the CCS is QS at the origin, then we design a state-dependent switching law under which the switched uncertain affine system (SUAS) is also QS at the origin.

articleTitle: Research on battery pack consistency assessment and fault diagnosis method based on anomaly factor
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) have become the main power source for electric vehicles and energy storage systems. However, inconsistency and internal short-circuit (ISC) faults of LIBs increase operational risks. In severe cases, thermal runaway accidents are triggered, posing a threat to the safety of users' lives and properties. Therefore, this paper presents research on risk warning strategies for inconsistency assessment and fault diagnosis of LIBs. First, in order to solve the problem of random noise in the measured voltages of the battery module, a data noise reduction method based on Savitzky-Golay filter is proposed. After that, the voltage differences between the cells of the battery pack and the median cell is calculated and recorded as the anomaly factor δ. Thus, the inconsistency assessment of the battery pack is realized. The battery pack fault diagnosis algorithm is constructed by using δ and sample entropy to realize early real-time fault diagnosis of battery packs. Finally, battery pack consistency and ISC faults experiments are performed. Experimental results show that the proposed consistency assessment and fault diagnosis method have good effectiveness, robustness and reliability.

articleTitle: Virtual Sample Generation Based on Regression Enhanced Generative Adversarial Network
abstract: The limited information and knowledge inherent in small sample sizes often result in poor generalization performance of constructed models. To address this issue, we propose a novel method for virtual sample generation (VSG) utilizing a regression enhanced generative adversarial network (REGAN). Initially, the variational autoencoder (VAE) serves as the generator within REGAN, with an additional regression layer incorporated to augment the regression information pertaining to virtual samples. Subsequently, both real and virtual samples undergo discrimination and prediction by the discriminator, thereby reinforcing the regression relationship among variables. Ultimately, optimal virtual samples are selected utilizing a co-training strategy. The efficacy of our proposed method is validated through experimentation on benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: Digital twin-based change control for supply chain system
abstract: To investigate supply chain system interruptions in the context of complex environmental influences, this paper proposes a digital twin-based change control for supply chain systems. Firstly, a dual-space four-layer digital twin supply chain system framework is introduced by combining digital twin technology with supply chain systems. Secondly, a dynamic model for the supply chain system is developed based on the structural characteristics of the supply chain system. To address uncertain parameters in complex environments, the digital twin similarity contrast method is employed for parameter determination. Thirdly, a change controller based on the output of a state observer is designed using a hysteresis switching law for the dynamic model constructed in this paper. The sufficient conditions for the solvability of the change control problem are provided utilizing the theory of minimax robust control. Simulation results show that the method in this paper is superior compared to the traditional change control.

articleTitle: Operation performance evaluation for electro-fused magnesium furnaces
abstract: The electro-fused magnesium furnace is a commonly used equipment in the metallurgical industry. Researching the performance evaluation of this device is beneficial for system optimization and holds significant importance. To this end, this paper establishes a comprehensive evaluation model for the operational performance of the fused magnesium furnace. For quantitative information, an evaluation model under specific production conditions is established based on an improved fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method. Subsequently, for qualitative information, a soft division model for production conditions is established. Finally, the method is applied to a simulated dataset to verify the effectiveness of the evaluation model.

articleTitle: Multi-robot real-time collaborative SLAM system based on 5G MEC framework
abstract: Aiming at the problem of insufficient computing resources for SLAM calculations in multi-robot systems, a multi-robot collaboration system based on the 5G edge computing platform (MEC) framework is proposed, and a map merge algorithm based on computer vision is designed. First, the main problems of SLAM map construction under multi-robot systems are analyzed, and solutions are given; secondly, a multirobot collaborative SLAM system based on 5G MEC is studied; finally, AKAZE feature detection is used to improve the map merge algorithm to enhance the global map. The algorithm’s performance and the system’s effectiveness are verified by simulation and physical experiments, respectively. The experimental results show that the real-time robot collaboration system based on the 5G MEC framework proposed in this article performs better in map merge. The algorithm has calculation speed and communication delay advantages and will promote research on 5G network applications in real-time robot collaboration.

articleTitle: Probability Analysis of the Failure of the Unmanned Power System in Antarctica Based on Fault Tree
abstract: This paper begins by analyzing the structural composition of the unmanned power system in Antarctica. The system is divided into components, including the diesel generator system, supervisory control system, communication system, energy storage system, and temperature control system. Based on the structural analysis of the system, a system fault tree is constructed with 'Failure of the Unmanned Power System in Antarctica' as the top event. Subsequently, a quantitative analysis of the fault tree is conducted using a combination of the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), expert semantics, and fuzzy mathematics. The calculation method for the occurrence probability of bottom events in the fault tree is introduced. The Binary Decision Diagram (BDD) method is then applied to calculate the failure probability of the top event in the fault tree. Finally, some key maintenance measures are proposed.

articleTitle: Multi-Reservoir Fully Connected Echo State Network for Wind Power Prediction
abstract: Optimized control of wind power plants has a high demand for wind power prediction accuracy. Accurate wind power prediction data enables wind power plants to better arrange production plans, improve energy utilization efficiency, reduce energy losses, and make the power grid operation stable. In this paper, considering the impact of wind speed instability and unpredictability on wind power generation prediction, a multi-reservoir fully connected echo state network (MRFC-ESN) is established. And the model is used to predict wind power generation. Firstly, this model draws on the fully-connected approach of neurons, and fully connects multiple reservoirs. Secondly, to demonstrate the stability and practicality of MRFC-ESN, the stability proof of MRFC-ESN is provided. Thirdly, MRFC-ESN uses gradient descent to optimize parameters. Finally, through the prediction of a set of wind power data, it is verified that this method achieves good results in wind power prediction.

articleTitle: Incremental Learning Classifier for Myoelectric Pattern Recognition Against the Interferences of Outlier Motion and Time-variability
abstract: Gesture classification models utilizing surface electromyography (sEMG) play a crucial role in controlling artificial hands. However, traditional classification models possess limited recognition capability, failing to meet users’ demands for new gestures. Furthermore, traditional classification models suffer significant degradation in recognition performance due to untrained motions and the time-variability of sEMG. To overcome these challenges, we proposed an incremental learning-based Gaussian-LDA hybrid classifier (GLHC) that integrates an ensemble of Gaussian one-class classifiers with multi-class linear discriminant analysis (LDA). In the GLHC model, Gaussian ensemble can reject outlier motions, while LDA can recognize target motions. Furthermore, two self-update mechanisms have been implemented to enhance the model’s recognition capability and counteract sEMG time-variability effects, respectively. Experimental results indicated that GLHC effectively mitigates both types of interference, with an online expansion of its recognition capabilities. Compared with traditional classifiers and class-incremental models from previous studies, GLHC demonstrated enhanced robustness and superior recognition performance.

articleTitle: A Direct Anti-high Repetition Jamming Design Method via The Minimum Interval Period Optimization
abstract: Semi-active laser detection is used extensively on many kinds of high-precision guidance weapon systems in the varied military fields. Although it is of high detection accuracy, this kind of detection mechanism, on the other hand, suffers from various laser interference modes which are added in view of the semi-active laser detection principle, covering from angle deception interference, synchronous forwarding interference, and high repetition frequency interference, etc. As a consequence, the overall performance is reduced accordingly. Among these types of deception interference, the high repetition frequency interference is the most effective one. In this work, to overcome this specific type of interference, a minimum interval period method (MIPM) is proposed to remove high repetition frequency interference and improve the detection accuracy of the laser semi-active guidance system. Numerical experiments validate that, this method is able to achieve good performance testing on the Semi-active laser detection under high repetition frequency interference via the False Alarm Probability (FAP for short) and Missed Alarm Probability (MAP).

articleTitle: H∞ Robust Control of Networked System under DoS Attacks and Dynamic Quantification
abstract: This paper investigates the design problem of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> robust control strategy for networked control systems with denial-of-service (DoS) attacks and signal quantization. Firstly, a Bernoulli variable determined by the signal-to-noise ratio is used to describe the probability of DoS attacks, and the dynamic quantization mechanism is utilized to reduce the communication burden of the network channels. In such a framework, the model of networked control systems with multiple constraints such as DoS attacks and external disturbances is established. Secondly, by means of Lyapunov stability theory and linear matrix inequality technique, sufficient conditions of exponentially mean-square stability for the networked control systems are derived, and the design method of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> robust control strategy is provided to realize the stabilization control of networked systems. Finally, the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed control method are verified by a simulation example.

articleTitle: Convergence Analysis of Dirac-GAN
abstract: Generative adversarial networks are powerful and widely used generative models, but they often face challenges in achieving convergence during the training process, which may lead to failures. As a univariate model of GANs, Dirac-GAN can effectively capture the relevant properties of GANs and significantly alleviate the analysis complexities. In this paper, we analyze the convergence of Dirac-GAN with regularization terms and gradient descent training. We leverage control theory and local linearization methods to establish conditions for the convergence of Dirac-GAN. These conditions constrain the value range of two crucial parameters, namely the regularization coefficient and learning rate, ultimately allowing us to derive the convergence rate of Dirac-GAN. We provide specific analyses of the objective functions of five common GANs, determining the corresponding convergence conditions and the optimal learning rate for achieving the fastest convergence. Finally, the theoretical results are validated through experiments.

articleTitle: A composite control method for industrial ship unloaders with time-varying rope length
abstract: In the design of unmanned ship unloaders, time-varying rope length and on-site sensor noises will bring great difficulties for anti-swing and positioning controls, which further affect the material-handling efficiency and safety. In this paper, a novel composite control method is proposed for industrial ship unloaders. Firstly, a discrete model of ship unloaders with variable rope length and damping coefficient was established. Secondly, an extended state extended Kalman filter (ESEKF) was proposed to solve the industrial sensor noises. Subsequently, an improved trajectory planning method using two-hump extra insensitive shaper (THEI) was proposed for anti-swing feedforward control. Moreover, a constrained model predictive control (MPC) with state error feedback was designed to deal with changes in rope length and other external disturbances. Lastly, both simulation and experimental results show that compared to typical methods, the proposed method has superior performance in terms of maximum load swing angle, residual swing angle, and positioning adjustment time, while also possessing anti-disturbance.

articleTitle: Lightweight Transformer based end-to-end speech recognition with patch adaptive local dense synthesizer attention
abstract: This paper proposes a novel Transformer model, called PALDSA-Transformer, for automatic speech recognition (ASR) tasks. In the model, the patch adaptive local dense synthesizer attention (PALDSA) is designed to capture the local context correlations and reduce attention complexity. In this paper, we study how to reduce the transformer model architecture complexity with a limited computing budget, leading to a more efficient architecture design.We introduce the Convolution Subsampling Module to the encoder and replace redundant pre-layer Normalization layers with a scaled post-layer Normalization in the Convolution Subsampling Module and Feed Forward Module. Compared with other variants of transformer-based methods, the experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a lower word error rate (WER) of 3.51%/8.82% for test-clean/test-other without a language model for only 8.6M parameters on the Librispeech dataset.

articleTitle: Direction-Independent Graph-Based GCN for Fall Detection
abstract: As the global population ages, the issue of falls among the elderly has become an increasingly pressing concern, garnering significant attention from the medical and research communities. Among the plethora of fall detection methods, inertial measurement units (IMUs) are favored by many researchers and practitioners for their capacity to capture real-time dynamic motion changes. However, the irregular change of direction during the fall process increases the difficulty of fusing and extracting features from the accelerometer and gyroscope data that are originally sensitive to the original direction. In response to this challenge, this study introduces the Direction-Independent Graph-Based Convolutional Neural Network (D-GCN). The D-GCN integrates features from acceleration and angular velocity data to form a novel topological representation. To assess the efficacy of D-GCN in fall detection, a dataset comprising 16 types of human movements, including 12 resembling falls and 4 actual falls, was established. The experiments demonstrate that this method achieves an accuracy of 0.901 on the dataset, which is an improvement of 11.9% over traditional machine learning algorithms.

articleTitle: A reliability-aware and energy-aware task scheduling algorithm for heterogeneous multi-core systems
abstract: Heterogeneous multi-core systems are widely used in high-performance computing applications. Reliability and low power consumption are important performance indicators of existing heterogeneous multi-core systems. The task scheduling algorithm with these two joint indicators as the optimization goal has important research significance. This paper designs a task scheduling algorithm for reliability and energy consumption awareness of heterogeneous multi-core systems. The algorithm is based on periodic real-time tasks with dependencies, and uses the redundancy of heterogeneous multi-cores to propose primary and secondary version backup technology for fault tolerance. The backup technology unifies the main task and the backup task and combines them with the DAG task model to construct a new task model. Reduce power consumption by introducing DVFS and DPM technology. DPM technology is mainly used for processor idle time, and consider using DVFS when the usage conditions of DPM are not met. In this paper, by comparing and evaluating randomly generated task models, the experimental results show that the algorithm has good performance in maintaining system reliability and reducing system power consumption.

articleTitle: Research on Fresh Air System Based on Improved Sparrow Search Algorithm Optimized Fuzzy PID Control
abstract: The fresh air system utilizes a fan to exhaust the dirty indoor air to the outdoors while sending fresh outdoor air into the room. In order to improve the control effect of fuzzy pid control algorithm, an improved sparrow search algorithm (ISSA) is proposed to optimize the parameters K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf>, K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ec</inf>, K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>, K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> and K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> of fuzzy pid control (ISSA-Fuzzy PID) to control the indoor temperature, humidity, and total volatile organic compounds (TVOC). Simulation results show that the improved sparrow search algorithm optimized fuzzy PID control has small overshoot, short adjustment time, strong adaptive ability, and improves the robustness of the system.

articleTitle: TS Model-based Composite Nonlinear Feedback Control Method for Heavy Haul Trains
abstract: As the mainstream method, heavy-haul-train-based transportation plays a significant role in bulk commodities’ transportation. To reduce the drivers’ workload and improve the control performance, the automatic control of heavy haul trains has come into being. In this paper, we propose a TS model-based composite nonlinear feedback (CNF) control method in which both the steady state and the dynamic process are considered simultaneously, which, however, differs from the existing results. The TS modeling method is introduced to address the nonlinearity of the dynamic model for heavy haul trains, while the corresponding CNF control is utilized to track the desired velocity and improve the transient control performance considering the input saturation. To facilitate the controller design, linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) are presented, which guarantees the tracking performance with a minimum disturbance attenuation level under a constraint input. Finally, simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Neural Adaptive Funnel Synchronization Control of Multi-motor Driving Systems
abstract: A funnel synchronization control strategy for a multi-motor driving system is developed to guarantee that the synchronization error can converge to a given funnel boundary. First, the tracking and synchronization problem is transformed into a stability problem by introducing a coupling synchronization error. This error is based on the tracking errors and synchronization errors between multiple motors. Second, a funnel function is constructed to actualize the state constraints, and a radial basis function (RBF) neural network is employed to estimate the uncertainty nonlinearities. Third, a funnel synchronization control protocol based on the backstepping strategy is proposed to ensure that each motor follows the reference signal and achieves speed synchronization. Finally, an example is given to demonstrate the viability of the proposed controller design strategies.

articleTitle: Dynamic Behavior and State Feedback Control of Hybrid Stochastic Infectious Disease System with Virus Concentration Perturbation
abstract: A stochastic hybrid dynamic system with infectious diseases in prey population was constructed, where the influence of random disturbances on virus concentration in the environment is considered. The uniqueness and boundedness of the global positive solution of the system were discussed, and the bifurcation behavior of the system around the positive equilibrium point was studied. A state feedback controller was designed to eliminate singular induced bifurcation. By solving the basic regeneration number and conducting sensitivity analysis, the combined influence of parameters on the basic regeneration number is studied. The asymptotic dynamical behavior around the interior equilibrium under stochastic perturbations are investigated. Numerical simulations are carried out to show consistency with theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Research on Hierarchical Active Equalization Control of Series Lithium-ion Battery Pack Based on Model
abstract: Aiming at the inconsistency of series lithium-ion battery pack, a model-based hierarchical active equalization control method is proposed by taking the state of charge (SOC) of the battery cell as the equalization object. The battery pack model is established with Modelica language, and the battery equalization topology is established based on the hierarchical active Buck-Boost circuit. The model of SOC estimation algorithm is carried out by unscented Kalman filter (UKF) with Simulink, and the equalization judgment criterion is based on the SOC deviation threshold between cells. The FMI (Functional Mock-up Interface) standard is applied to realize the co-simulation experiment between the battery pack model of Modelica and the equalization control model of Simulink. Simulation results reveal that under two different current conditions, the proposed method can effectively improve the SOC inconsistency of the series battery pack, and the maximum SOC deviation between cells is reduced from 13.2% to 0.5%.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Microgrids Based on Multi-objective African Vulture Optimization Algorithm
abstract: The exploitation and utilization of traditional energy have caused serious damage to the natural environment. New energy microgrids are a hopeful means to solve the above environmental crises. However, the scheduling problem of microgrids also faces enormous challenges. Thus, this paper develops a novel optimal scheduling method for microgrid. Firstly, the microgrid model composed of photovoltaic cells, wind turbines, diesel generators and storage batteries is established. A dual-objective optimal scheduling model including of operating cost and environmental protection cost is constructed. A multi-objective African Vulture optimization algorithm (MOAVOA) is proposed to solve the above optimization problem. Finally, simulation results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed optimal scheduling method.

articleTitle: Design of vacuum support system for manned spacecraft
abstract: One of the main tasks of manned spacecraft is to conduct space science experiments. The vacuum support system of manned spacecraft provides support for exhaust emissions and vacuum maintenance in space science experiments. The article first conducted a survey on the development and application of vacuum support technology for the International Space Station, and conducted an in-depth analysis of the demand for load vacuum extraction and exhaust emissions in China's manned spacecraft applications. On this basis, the design of the vacuum support system for China's manned spacecraft was carried out, and the ground verification test of the vacuum support system was completed. The in orbit application plan and task execution status of the vacuum support system for China's manned spacecraft were proposed.

articleTitle: Three-channel Decoupling Control for Fighter Aircraft based on Prescribed Performance Control and Super-Twisting Extended State Observer
abstract: In this paper, we propose a three-channel decoupling control method for fighter aircraft based on prescribed performance control (PPC) and super-twisting extended state observer (STESO) to solve the problem of high uncertainty and strong coupling during flight at high angle of attack. In this method, the angle of attack, the sideslip angle and bank angle around the velocity are selected as the controlled variables respectively, and three independent controllers are designed to control these variables separately, which reduces the coupling of the system and improves the control effect by decoupling the control. By taking advantage of the linear extended state observer(LESO) and the super-twisting algorithm, a STESO is used to estimate the total disturbance(including coupling terms between individual channels, modeled uncertainty, external disturbance, etc.) and compensate for them in the control law. Moreover, the control performance and robustness of STESO are verified by simulation analysis. Simulation results show that the proposed STESO achieves rapid convergence of the tracking error with less settling time compared to LESO. The controller employing the proposed observer is capable of promptly and accurately tracking control commands.

articleTitle: Abnormal Control and Trajectory Optimization in CNC System
abstract: In CNC machining, the motion controller executes in real-time to generate trajectory points. when abnormal situations occur, the controller changes its execution to deal with it, protect machine components and machining parts. In this paper, a feed rate reset method which across multiple segments is proposed and integrated in micro-line trajectory planning routine. In trajectory planning process, to make sure CNC machine not exceed its mechanical limits, look-ahead method is applied to readjust corner velocity. To optimize trajectory, two corner transition methods are chosen based on machining time and the smoothness of the velocity profile, and the controller intelligently choose one of them based on the current machining situation. These methods are tested in simulation environment and actual machining.

articleTitle: Study on automatic localization algorithm of Baliao points
abstract: In the clinical treatment of modern traditional Chinese medicine, such as reproductive system and gynecological diseases, acupuncture at Baliao points has become a primary method. An improved YOLOv7 model is proposed to train and predict the CT images of Baliao points, which will automatically detect the sacral cornu and eight acupoints, as well as calculate the required distances and angles. The experimental results show that the detection accuracy and speed are significantly improved. The mean average precision and FPS have reached 93.1% and 78.9, respectively, which are 4.6% and 25.5 higher than those before the improvement. By comparing these predicted values with the actual values provided by the hospital, the results show that the predicted values are within the safe error range, which will provide data support for subsequent research on exogenous auxiliary devices.

articleTitle: A Scheme of Digital Twin Air Combat Battlefield and Digital Twin Model Design
abstract: This paper provides a solution concept using digital twin technology for the battlefield environment for the air combat training. The scheme is divided into two aspects: digital twin battlefield and digital twin aircraft. The digital twin battlefield scheme discusses the three-dimensional modeling method of the battlefield and the update mechanism of battlefield environment data. The digital twin aircraft model scheme discusses the construction ideas of the aircraft twin model, and discusses the future application scenarios. With the advancement of technology and the iterative update of application scenarios, the digital twin air combat training battlefield will gradually realize various functions and explore more innovative application modes, realize the virtual environment interaction and digital twin function application of the entire battlefield environment.

articleTitle: Design of Urban Highway Tunnel Firefighting and Control System
abstract: This article proposes an innovative design for an urban highway tunnel firefighting and control system, addressing the serious threat of tunnel fires in cities and the limitations of traditional prevention and control methods. By incorporating advanced sensor technology, intelligent control, and real-time data monitoring, this system enables rapid detection, accurate alarm triggering, and effective response to tunnel fires.

articleTitle: Exponential stability of time-delay adaptive switched systems with two nonlinear disturbance
abstract: This paper investigates the exponential stability of adaptive switched systems with nonlinear perturbations and uncertain parameters. Firstly, the adaptive controller is designed for the subsystem, and in order to better apply to the real world, the free parameter matrix is introduced by constructing (L-K functional) considering that the state contains time delay and there are two nonlinear perturbations. Then an adaptive law which depends on switched signal is designed to avoid the coupling problem between the sub-adaptive laws caused by the shared state. The multi-Lyapunov function method is used to design the controller of the system. The purpose of using the switched rate is to ensure the exponential stability of the closed-loop system. The switched rule is obtained by means of the average residence time method. Combined with linear matrix inequality, The paper establishes the conditions for ensuring exponential stability of the system and conducts numerical calculations through the Matlab simulation. Furthermore, a practical example is provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the results obtained using the controller, applicable law, and switching rate discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Adaptive Based Fixed-time Formation Tracking Control for MASs with External Disturbance and Region Constraints
abstract: In this paper, a fixed-time time-varying formation tracking controller is proposed for second-order multi-agent systems (MASs) with region constraints based on adaptive observation. A practical finite-time disturbance observer (DO) with an adaptive update law is proposed to eliminate the negative effects of disturbance. Using the sliding mode control technique, a novel fixed-time time-varying region constraints formation tracking controller is designed and the upper bound of convergence time is given. The simulation results show that the disturbance is estimated accurately and quickly by the designed DO, the desired time-varying regular hexagonal formation is realized within the upper bound of convergence time, and all agents remain within the constraint region, which verifies the effectiveness and feasibility of the theoretical results.

articleTitle: A Multi-objective Salp Swarm Algorithm for Multi-product Two-sided Disassembly Line Balancing Problem with Special Workers
abstract: The escalating volume of discarded large-scale electronic products has triggered significant attention within the research community toward the TDLBP (Two-sided Disassembly Line Balancing Problem. In response, this study presents a biobjective optimization problem for TDLBP, incorporating the considerations of hiring special WGB (Workers with Government Benefits) workers. The objectives are two-fold: one is to maximize disassembly profit, and the other is to concurrently enhance the WGB index. The resulting problem is named a Bi-objective Multi-product Two-sided Disassembly-line-balancingproblem considering Workers-with-government-benefits. MSSA (Multi-objective Salp Swarm Algorithm) is proposed to tackle the problem. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is validated through comparison with NSGA-III and MOEA/DCRA.

Author Keywords: Bi-objective Multi-product Two-side Disassembly Line Balancing Problem

articleTitle: Modeling and Analyzing for Particulate Material of MSWI Process Based on 2D Numerical Simulation
abstract: The MSWI process offers numerous advantages, including a high reduction rate, rapid treatment speed, and onsite incineration. However, under unstable operating conditions, particularly in cases of fluctuating furnace temperatures, the concentration of discharged particulate matter may exceed the required emission standards. To better understand the characteristics of particle concentration at normal incinerator temperatures, a practical municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) process in Beijing was simulated using 2D numerical simulation. The incinerator's structure is outlined, and a two-dimensional Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) model of the incinerator is developed. Based on actual process parameters, experiments were conducted under benchmark operating conditions. The gas composition and particle concentration characteristics under normal temperature conditions are analyzed. These findings can support the optimization of control strategies for real-world MSWI processes.

articleTitle: Distributed Secure Control for Vehicular Platoon Systems Under Asynchronous DoS Attacks
abstract: This paper investigates a distributed secure control problem for vehicular platoon systems (VPSs) under consecutive asynchronous denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. During consecutive asynchronous DoS attacks period, the communication topology of VPSs are consecutively subjected to different types of DoS attacks, and the attacked communication topology may not have a directed spanning tree. Then, this paper models VPSs under consecutive asynchronous DoS attacks as a switched system based on the theory of the linear transformation method. We propose a distributed security control scheme for VPSs based on the persistent dwell time (PDT) switching rule. This scheme allows the subsystems to be unstable during the consecutive switching period. Moreover, by utilizing a piece-wise Lyapunov function and the theory of partial variable stability, a sufficient condition for ensuring the stability of the platoon is derived. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control method is confirmed through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Adaptive Learning Rate Background-Aware Correlation Filters with Feature Fusion
abstract: Under complex sea conditions, when UAVs track maritime targets, factors such as changes in illumination and seawater clutter may cause the tracker model to drift or target tracking to fail. In order to better optimize this problem, This paper presents an "Adaptive Learning Rate Background-Aware Correlation Filters with Feature Fusion". First, In the target localization stage, we propose an adaptive feature-weighted fusion strategy by combining CN features and HOG features to enhance the extraction of target appearance features. Secondly, a joint confidence discriminative strategy is adopted to adaptively update the learning rate to improve the anti-occlusion ability of the tracker. The algorithm in this paper has carried out qualitative and quantitative experiments on the OTB-50 data sets. The experiments prove that the improved tracker can outperform six advanced trackers in accuracy and robustness. Moreover, in actual maritime target tracking, under the influence of common interference factors, the improved tracker exhibits superior performance than the baseline tracker.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Innovation Identification for Norrbin Mathematical Model Via Actual Ship
abstract: In order to improve the prediction accuracy of ship maneuverability, this paper concentrates on the identification modeling problem on base of the ship trail data. Taking the Norrbin Mathematical model as an example, a nonlinear innovation identification algorithm is proposed by combine with the least squares theory and the concept of nonlinear innovation. In the algorithm, instead of using the original error information, the error innovation is derived by the nonlinear hyperbolic tangent function, which is selected to correct the related identification parameters. Based on the "Yukun" experimental ship, the trail test is carried out to obtain the data for the identification process. The comparison result has been illustrated to verify the advantages of the proposed algorithm, e.g., the high accuracy, the fast convergence speed and the clear physical meaning. It is obvious to note that the proposed algorithm can effectively solve the real-time identification problem for ship maneuverability and is with the guiding significance for the practical engineering.

articleTitle: Stability and Stabilization for CPS with Time-varying Delay and Random Deception
abstract: Stability analysis and stabilization control of cyber-physical systems (CPSs) are important and challenging problems. To this end, a novel system model based on Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional (LKF) containing certain double and triple integral terms is proposed to reflect not only the deterministic nonlinear characteristics, external disturbances and time-varying delays, but also the randomly occurring deceptions, which lead to the system mode switching. A Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional (LKF) containing certain double and triple integral terms is constructed to exploit merits of the presented single and double integral inequalities. By using stochastic analysis techniques, the addressed stability analysis and controller design problems are transformed to the convex optimization problems, which can be solved by a linear matrix inequality (LMI) approach. Illustrative examples are given to show the effectiveness of the designed controller.

articleTitle: Research on Two Kinds of Adaptive Control of Colpitts Memristor Circuit Dimension Reduction System
abstract: A kind of control problem based on the active memristor model is studied. Firstly, the dynamic behavior of the Colpitts memristor chaotic circuit system is analyzed, and the Lyapunov exponent diagram and chaotic attractor diagram of the system are given to verify the existence of complex chaotic phenomena in the system. Then, aiming at the control problem of the chaotic circuit system, two methods of adaptive feedback control and adaptive integral sliding mode control are used to design an adaptive feedback controller with known parameters and unknown parameters, and an adaptive integral sliding mode controller with unknown parameters to stabilize the chaotic system to the equilibrium point. Finally, through MATLAB numerical simulation, it is verified that the two kinds of controllers can effectively control the system to the stable point, and the two kinds of controllers are compared, which provides an important basis for the choice of controllers in practical applications.

Author Keywords: Colpitts memristor circuit dimensionality reduction system

articleTitle: Multi-agent Train Adaptive Cooperation Control Based on The Event-triggered
abstract: With the acceleration of urbanization, higher requirements are put forward for train speed coordination and resource saving. Today’s high-speed train traction and control force are distributed in each carriage, and the application of agent system in train cooperation control is becoming more and more important. To improve the performance and safety of train system, and achieve energy saving, a multi-agent train cooperative control method based on combination of event-triggered and robust adaptive control is proposed in this paper. The method combines the event triggering mechanism and the robust adaptive control algorithm to realize the cooperative control between each carriage. The effectiveness and advantages of the method are verified by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: A Novel Unsupervised Anomaly Detection Method Based on Improved Collaborative Discrepancy Optimization
abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, intelligent industrial image anomaly detection is an indispensable step in modern manufacturing and industrial production. In actual industrial scenarios, due to the lack of abnormal samples, the high cost of labeling data, and the poor representation of features when encountering anomalies, unsupervised learning methods are widely used in image anomaly detection. This paper improves the CDO (collaborative discrepancy optimization) model and proposes a novel unsupervised anomaly detection method. This paper makes innovations in the synthesis of abnormal samples, fusing three kinds of anomalies, which are Gaussian noise, mask block, and patches from randomly selected real images. The positioning effect is further improved. A new strategy to evaluate the difference between the teacher network and the student network is designed, which uses the form of simultaneous training and testing to speed up the convergence. The HRNet-type network is selected as the backbone network, which can maintain high-resolution representation during the whole process, connect convolutional streams from high-resolution to low-resolution in parallel, and exchange information repeatedly across resolutions to obtain semantically richer and spatially more accurate results. The effectiveness and superiority of the improved method are verified by comparing with the existing models. The results show that the AU-ROC and AU-PRO scores of the proposed method are improved compared with CDO and other unsupervised learning models in multiple categories.

articleTitle: Self-Learning Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm for Distributed Hybrid Flow Shop Scheduling with Preventive Maintenance
abstract: Due to advantages such as flexibility, higher production efficiency, and lower risk resilience, the distributed hybrid flow shop scheduling problem (DHFSP), as an extension of the flow shop scheduling problem, has received considerable attention from both academia and industry. However, the deterioration effects caused by wear and tear of machines and corresponding preventive maintenance (PM) strategies that can improve the deterioration effects are typically ignored in the vast majority of DHFSPs. As a consequence, a DHFSP with deteriorating effects and PM (DHFSP-DP) targeted at minimizing the makespan is first investigated in this study. To efficiently solve the DHFSP-DP, a self-learning artificial bee colony algorithm (SABC) is then designed with the following two key innovations: (1) An improved heuristic and an average random initialization are used to solve the sub-problems of job assignment and initial processing sequence; (2) The search performance of the artificial bee colony algorithm is enhanced by using a reinforcement learning method that dynamically selects the search operator. Finally, 30 test instances are used to evaluate the performance of SABC. Experimental results show that SABC outperforms other competing algorithms in solving the proposed DHFSP-DP.

articleTitle: Deformation prediction of ship plate hot working based on IGWO-SVM
abstract: Line heating is the mainstream processing method for ship plate, but it is still time-consuming and labour-intensive to get it by mechanic's experience processing. In this paper, in order to study its deformation effect, an Improved Grey Wolf Algorithm Optimized Support Vector Machine (IGWO-SVM) is proposed for the prediction of surface deformation of ship plate. On the basis of establishing the heat source model and obtaining the original data through Ansys simulation, the IGWO-SVM is used to predict the deformation of the ship plate surface, and with the processing experience of the workers as a guide, an accurate prediction model is established. It is proved by Matlab experiments that the prediction model has high prediction accuracy on the basis of ensuring the reliability of the data, which can provide guidance for actual processing.

articleTitle: Prediction model of electric vehicle driving range based on support vector regression
abstract: All status data related to electric vehicle driving generally are recorded. Making full use of those status data to predict electric vehicle driving can relax power anxiety caused by insufficient power of electric vehicles during driving to some extent. Aiming at this problem, a driving range prediction model of electric vehicles based on support vector regression is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the proposed model adopts Random forest for feature extraction, which selects influential factors that are closely related to State of charge (SOC) characteristics. Secondly, combined with the actual driving data of EVs, the driving range prediction model of EVs based on support vector regression was constructed. Simulation results show that the proposed prediction model is better than the prediction model using the original support vector progression in terms of Mean Square Error.

articleTitle: The extension of decentralized integral controllability to non-square processes
abstract: This paper studies the problem of distributed integral controllability for non-square multiple-input-output (MIMO) processes, where the number of inputs is greater than the number of outputs. Distributed or decentralized integral controllability (DIC) is a property that allows the use of stable decentralized controllers combined with integral action to achieve offset-free control and independent tuning of any subset of the control loops. Previous research has focused on DIC for linear/nonlinear square processes and nonlinear multiple-input single-output (MISO) systems, but not for non-square MIMO processes. We extend the concept of DIC to non-square MIMO processes and derive sufficient and necessary conditions for distributed integral controllability, which is a generalization of DIC for square systems. We also present a simulation study to demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Fractional-order non-singular global time-varying terminal sliding mode attitude controller for unpowered reentry vehicle
abstract: This paper proposes a fractional-order time-varying nonsingular terminal sliding mode controller for attitude control of unpowered reentry vehicles. The system is able to converge in a finite time with the proposed controller. The introduced time-varying term ensures the global robustness, and the introduced fractional-order term improves the convergence performance of the system. The stability and globality of the system have been proven, and the finite-time convergence has been demonstrated through a new method. The simulation results show that the proposed controller has better control performance compared to existing fractional-order sliding mode attitude controllers and integer-order time-varying terminal sliding mode attitude controllers.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Controller Design for Human-Assistive Piloting of an Underactuated Blimp
abstract: This paper introduces a novel solution to the manual control challenge for indoor blimps. The problem’s complexity arises from the conflicting demands of executing human commands while maintaining stability through automatic control for underactuated robots. To tackle this challenge, we introduced an assisted piloting hybrid controller with a preemptive mechanism, that seamlessly switches between executing human commands and activating automatic stabilization control. Our algorithm ensures that the automatic stabilization controller operates within the time delay between human observation and perception, providing assistance to the driver in a way that remains imperceptible.

articleTitle: A control strategy for smoothing the fluctuation of wind power grid connection based on hybrid energy storage system
abstract: The stochastic volatility of wind power generation has an impact on grid stability, and a hybrid energy storage system (HESS) based on parameter optimization with variational mode decomposition (VMD) is proposed to suppress the fluctuation of wind power on the grid. control strategy. Firstly, the VMD method optimized by the sparrow search algorithm (SSA) is used to decompose the fluctuating power of wind power that needs to be suppressed. According to the obtained spectrogram, based on the energy ratio of each sub-module and the minimum modal overlap, the high and low-frequency power is allocated to the supercapacitor and lithium battery to realize the distribution of power in the hybrid energy storage system. Secondly, to prolong the service life of the energy storage system and prevent the overcharge and over-discharge phenomenon from damaging the energy storage components, the power of the energy storage components is corrected by fuzzy control rules. Finally, the method proposed in this paper is applied to wind power data collected in a region, and the experimental results show that the strategy can effectively smooth out the fluctuation of wind power grid connection, reduce the degree of fluctuation of the charge state of the energy storage system, and realize the stable operation of the hybrid energy storage system.

articleTitle: MSFF-GAN: A Refined Method for Human Video Motion Transfer
abstract: Recently, with the advancement in Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), human video motion transfer technology has also made significant progress. However, GAN-based motion transfer algorithms generally suffer from low synthetic quality. Specifically, there are problems such as blurriness, missing parts, and misaligning key areas such as hands and feet. To achieve better motion transfer, we propose a multiscale feature fusion GAN, which can simultaneously focus on the global structure and local details of the image; in combination with global-local perceptual loss and pose consistency loss, the attention of the GAN generator to local features is enhanced. It aims to avoid problems such as limb losses and joint misplacements and effectively improve the quality and refinement of the synthesized images. We have established a video dataset containing movements such as dance and yoga for training and evaluation. In qualitative and quantitative analysis experiments, we compare our algorithm with three mainstream motion transfer models: vid2vid, EDN, and PoseWrap. Our algorithm has reached 23.9981 on the PSNR metric. The experimental results demonstrate that our algorithm outperforms mainstream motion transfer algorithms in both qualitative and quantitative evaluations.

articleTitle: Depth estimation of coded light field based on structure tensor
abstract: Depth estimation is an important task in light field. However, traditional light field has textureless regions without unique features. In addition, occlusion also destroys the photometric consistency among views in light field. As a result, depth estimation in these regions faces challenges in accuracy and robustness. In this paper, we propose a novel boundary-aware coded light field to improve the performance of depth estimation. On the one hand, phase coding structured light is introduced to enrich the features where phase values work as the codeword for every pixel. On the other hand, a structure tensor based boundary sensing method is proposed to handle the occlusion. To be specific, without calculating the depth, the proposed algorithm can predict the occlusions with the structure tensor of the phase codewords. After that, depth in the non-occluded regions is estimated based on MAE of the phase, while in occluded regions, the optimal refocus parameter is obtained with a statistic based criteria. Finally, accurate depth maps in both occluded and non-occluded regions are obtained. Experimental results show that this method can generate accurate depth maps, especially in occluded regions.

articleTitle: Design and Modeling of a Variable Stiffness Fish Tail with PCL Material
abstract: Fish in nature can adjust the stiffness of their bodies and tails to adapt to underwater swimming. Innumerable studies have been conducted on flexible robotic fish that imitate this ability. This study presents a novel elastic fishtail consisting of a peduncle and a caudal fin whose materials include silicone, a fiberglass board, and polycaprolactone (PCL) material which has temperature-dependent stiffness.
