Thermocouples and heating resistors are used to control the temperature of the PCL structure, whose strength can be controlled at different temperature, thereby adjusting the stiffness of the fishtail. To analyze the deformation characteristics of the fishtail, a kinematic model is developed based on the cantilever beam model. Finally, experimental measurements are conducted to verify the accuracy of the theoretical model. Experimental results show that the designed peduncle structure can achieve a 300% stiffness change within a specific temperature range.

articleTitle: Robust Interactive Multiple Model for Collaborative Navigation of Unmanned Surface Vessel Swarm
abstract: This paper presents a robust interactive multiple model (IMM) method to deal with the data fusion of collaborative navigation for the unmanned surface vessel (USV) swarm. Firstly, the IMM is combined with the cubature Kalman filter to handle the nonlinear characteristics involved in the collaborative navigation model based on the strategy of measuring the relative distance and azimuth. Then, a sub-filter in the IMM framework is designed as a robust filter where the Mahalanobis distance criterion is used to detect the abnormal noise statistics. Subsequently, a model selection mechanism is established to adaptively chose the proper models to cover the actual measurement noise statistics. The proposed robust IMM method has a strong adaptability and robustness to handle the varying the measurement noise statistics, it provides an effective collaborative navigation way to enhance the performance of the USV swarm. The simulation on collaborative navigation of USV swarm has been conducted to evaluate the efficacy of proposed robust IMM. The results demonstrate that it has excellent robustness compared to the traditional CKF and CKF-IMM.

articleTitle: Causes And Treatment Of AHRS Failure In Primary Training Aircraft
abstract: The primary training aircraft C172R is equipped with the GRS77 Attitude and Heading Reference System (AHRS), which is an essential instrument on the aircraft used for measuring, calculating, and providing flight attitude and heading information. It can real-time measure parameters such as the carrier's three-axis attitude angle information and magnetic field intensity, providing critical flight parameters for flight trainees. Its reliability and stability are particularly important. However, AHRS failures are common during flight training, posing challenges to the safety of flight training. The paper extensively analyzes the types and possible causes of AHRS failures in the primary training aircraft, studies the impact of AHRS failures on flight training, examines the changes in flight parameters after failure, and explores strategies for pilots to cope with failures.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Output Feedback Stabilization of Coupled Linear Parabolic PDE-ODE System
abstract: In this paper, we deal with an event-triggered output-feedback boundary control of an ODE system coupled with a heat equation. An observer-based controller for the continuous control input is designed. Motivated by it, an observer-based event-triggered controller is proposed, which is obtained by sampling the observer-based continuous-time controller. A dynamic event triggering mechanism (ETM) is introduced to determine the updating times of the actuation signal. The exponential stability in the event-based closed-loop system is proved via Lyapunov method. Moreover, a minimal dwell-time exists between any two triggering times, which means that the absence of a Zeno behavior.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Output Power Prediction Model Based On K-GCN-LSTM Neural Network
abstract: The high proportion of distributed photovoltaic integration into the distribution grid can assist the power grid peak shaving while simultaneously reducing transmission losses. However, accurately predicting photovoltaic output power is challenging due to its volatility and randomness. To address the issue of not considering the spatial characteristics among photovoltaic arrays in general photovoltaic output power prediction, this paper introduces a predictive model based on Kendall coefficient, Graph Convolutional Neural Networks and Long Short-Term Memory Neural Network(K-GCN-LSTM). First, the model sets the neighbor matrix of GCN with Kendall coefficients between the output powers of 32 photovoltaic arrays and extracts the spatial correlation between the output powers of PV arrays using GCN. Then, the model uses Long Short-Term Memory Neural Network to learn the temporal correlations of photovoltaic output power curves. Finally, the proposed prediction model is compared with the traditional prediction models, which confirms that the proposed model is more accurate in the prediction results and has a positive impact on the safe operation of the power system to cope with the high proportion of PV integrated into the distribution network.

articleTitle: Output Feedback Stabilizing Control for Uncertain Nonholonomic Systems with Input-Output Polynomial Depending Growth Rate
abstract: In this paper, the global output feedback stabilization for a class of nonholonomic systems with input-output polynomial, and unmeasurable states dependent growth is studied. Motivated by the closely related works, in order to reconstruct the unmeasurable system states and compensate the uncertainties/unknowns in the nonlinear drifts, an observer with a new dynamic high-gain is designed. Then, we adopt a nonidentifier-based adaptive controller without invoking the backstepping technique. Particularly, the complexity of the controller is reduced by combining the dynamic gain technology and universal control theory. Finally, the serious uncertainty in the chained nonholonomic systems is overcome by constructing a switching control strategy. The results show that all the signals of the closed-loop system are bounded, while the closed-loop system state converges to zero. The effectiveness of the control scheme is proved by an example.

articleTitle: Optimization of Pattern Dynamics of FitzHugh-Nagumo System Based on PD Control Strategy
abstract: The FitzHugh-Nagumo system is a chemical and biological reaction diffusion control system. At present, domestic and foreign studies are only limited to the study of the Turing-Hopf bifurcation kinetics and diffusion effects of the FitzHugh-Nagumo system. However, there are fewer reports on the effect of the control strategy on the spatiotemporal patterns. In this paper, the effect of proportional-derivative (PD) control strategy on the spatiotemporal evolution dynamics of the FitzHugh-Nagumo system is investigated. Using the linear stability analysis method, the stability conditions for the system without diffusion and the Turing instability conditions for the diffusion system are established. And using simulation we verify the feasibility of the theoretical analysis. The results show that a change in the proportional coefficient leads to a change in the Turing bifurcation threshold. In addition the PD controller can inhibit and promote the occurrence of Turing instability in the FitzHugh-Nagumo system.

articleTitle: Touch2C: A code conversion method from programming language for swarm intelligent building to C language
abstract: The Touch programming language for swarm intelligent building application (APP) development effectively reduces the development difficulty and user programming threshold, making the building more intelligent. However, the features of Touch language such as intuitive modeling of building elements, parallel programming, and the implicit specification of internode communication lead to great challenges in the compilation process of Touch language to the low-level executable object code of swarm intelligent buildings, and the APP development efficiency is not high. This paper proposes a code conversion method from Touch to C language and its supporting tools, designs code conversion algorithms for Touch language elements used to describe distributed building physical objects and parallel computing mode, which supports the automatic conversion of high-level Touch language, which is user-oriented and shielded from the details of the underlying interactions, into the C language code for underlying execution, thus realizing an integrated process from high-level APP development to low-level hardware platform execution and improving the APP development efficiency.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Stochastic Programming for Sustainable Utility Systems Optimization with Energy Storage
abstract: Utility systems consume fuels to provide steam and energy for industrial processes, resulting in significant carbon dioxide emissions. To enhance the economic and environmental efficiency of the system, a sustainable utility system integrating energy storage has been proposed. The scheduling optimization of sustainable utility systems involves multiple energy sources and various uncertainties, posing a challenging mathematical programming problem. An approach utilizing a two-stage stochastic programming method has been introduced to tackle the challenge of uncertainty. The optimal planning stage aims to minimize economic and environmental costs. In the first stage, deterministic programming is employed to solve the capacity planning problem for renewable energy and energy storage devices. In the second stage, weather scenarios are generated based on historical data, and stochastic programming methods are used to transform the uncertainty issue into a mixed-integer programming problem, addressing the operational scheduling optimization of the systems. Finally, the effectiveness of this method is validated using a real factory case study.

articleTitle: Topology optimization for blockchain networks
abstract: In order to shorten the data transmission time and improve the transmission efficiency of nodes in the blockchain, this paper proposes a method to optimize the blockchain network topology. First, the trusted value function is defined to divide the node types and construct the corresponding tree topology. According to the characteristics that nodes in the blockchain network can enter and leave at will, the changes of tree topology when trusted nodes or untrusted nodes change are considered respectively. Then, based on the tree topology, the forwarding path selection (FPS) algorithm is used to establish the forwarding table of each node, selecting a neighbor node with the maximum concurrent transmission time in the forwarding table for data forwarding. The results of the simulation experiment show that the proposed algorithm has smaller concurrent transmission time , forwarding rounds and node utilization rate than the weight first communication tree (WFT) algorithm, and the transmission efficiency of the blockchain is significantly improved.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation Approach of Dioxin Emission Concentration of MSWI Process
abstract: Municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) plays a crucial role in converting waste treatment into energy. However, the incineration process inevitably produces persistent organic poison pollutants such as Dioxin (DXN). DXN has potential risks to human health and the ecological environment. It is very important to know the boundary conditions of DXN in the process of its formation, combustion, regeneration, adsorption, and emission. This paper addresses the challenges associated with dioxin detection methods and cost by proposing a numerical simulation approach for insight DXN emission concentrations of MSWI process through multi-software coupling. Specifically, FLIC, ASPEN Plus, and ASPEN adsorption are used to couple to simulate the entire process. Simulation results show that the removal rate of DXN by bag filter is between 57.51% and 99.61%, and the emission concentration of DXN under the benchmark working condition is 0.0589 ng TEQ/Nm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. This study offers mechanistic support for controlling pollutant emission of MSWI process and serves as a valuable reference for practical engineering applications.

articleTitle: A Defect Detection Method of Differential Pulse Eddy Current for Transmission Lines
abstract: The secure and stable operation of transmission lines is crucial in achieving the reliable power supply objectives for the electric power system. Currently, there is a lack of highly accurate and interference-resistant methods for detecting defects in transmission lines. This study presents a new model for a pulse electromagnetic eddy current detection probe that could accurately detect and quantify defects in aluminium conductor steel-reinforced(ACSR) based on the differential signal. Firstly, theory of the probe is analyzed based on the magnetic field characteristics. Secondly, a finite element model of the transmission line is developed using COMSOL software, allowing for the simulation of various types of defects. Finally, by utilizing symmetrical detection coils, differential signals are obtained for defects of different types and severities, enabling defect quantification and confirming the feasibility and practicality of the proposed method. Our work provides a workable idea for practical field reuse and miniaturized sensor design.

articleTitle: An optical fiber fluorescence pH sensor based on CdTe quantum dots
abstract: The pH value is one of the essential parameters of a solution, serving as a significant indicator in the fields of chemistry, biology, environment, and others. Monitoring the pH value of liquids is often necessary in many situations. This study combines CdTe quantum dots and optical fiber for pH detection. CdTe quantum dots are a novel fluorescent material with high fluorescence intensity, which varies in fluorescence intensity in solutions with different pH values. The sensing structure is created by connecting an exposed core fiber with a multimode fiber through fusion splicing and encasing them in a glass tube. When the tested solution mixes with CdTe quantum dots and flows through the sensing structure, the excited fluorescence signal is directly coupled into the exposed core of the exposed core fiber. The fluorescence signal travels along the optical fiber and is detected. We used this sensing structure for PH detection in different solutions. Experimental results indicate a linear relationship between pH values ranging from 5.0 to 11.0 and relative fluorescence intensity. The detection limit is 0.17pH, and the response time is short. The sensor exhibits good stability and repeatability. The designed sensor structure is simple, user-friendly, and reusable, providing a powerful tool for future environmental and health monitoring.

articleTitle: XNAV/SRNS integrated navigation based on Augmented EKF
abstract: XNAV (X-ray pulsar-based navigation) is one of the effective means to realize autonomous navigation for deep space probe, which is characterized by reliability, stability and autonomy. However, the performance of XNAV is not only affected by systematic errors such as pulsar direction error and probe-borne clock error, but also facing the challenges of weak signals and prolonged observation time. In response to the above-mentioned issues, this paper proposes an XNAV/SRNS (Spectral Redshift Navigation System) integrated navigation method based on augmented EKF. Firstly, the systematic errors are augmented into the state variable for real-time estimation by EKF. Secondly, the FKF (Federated Kalman Filter) is employed to fuse the local state estimations from XNAV and SRNS subsystems, aiming to achieve the globally optimal estimation. Finally, the proposed method is validated by comprehensive simulations and comparison analysis. The simulation results show that the proposed method can overcome the defects of XNAV effectively and improve the navigation accuracy of deep space probe significantly.

articleTitle: Preliminary Design of Predictive Maintenance for Helium Screw Compressor Based on Industrial Internet Platform
abstract: The aim of this paper is to research and design a predictive maintenance scheme based on an industrial internet platform to prevent the failure of the helium screw compressor, a key cryogenic equipment, from affecting the operational efficiency of the system. The research object is the helium screw compressor, which is the core equipment of 1kW@4.5K helium refrigerator. The design relies on the equipment status data accumulated by the operation and maintenance of the cryogenic system for many years to study the potential fault types and key characteristic indexes of the equipment, so as to establish the intelligent fault prediction model. On the basis of this model, this paper plans to design a complete set of predictive maintenance processes based on the industrial internet platform, including real-time data acquisition, fault diagnosis, maintenance decision support, etc. It aims to effectively improve the level of intelligent management of the equipment, and to improve the operation reliability and efficiency of the helium screw compressor.

articleTitle: Local Heterologous Virtual-to-Real Registration of The Body
abstract: This article focuses on the registration between digital local human body models and real local human bodies, which is a fundamental task in XR digital twins, intelligent cockpits, and other fields. Our proposed method enables adaptive registration of human bodies without the need for prior parametric models and external auxiliary sensors, only requiring a binocular camera. The method consists of two steps: coarse registration and fine registration. In the coarse registration step, it relies on a deep network to extract keypoints of the human bodies in RGB images and then performs anchor point registration with pre-set keypoints on the 3D digital model. In the fine registration step, it relies on deep learning-based segmentation of human bodies which can be recovered into real human body point clouds combining the pixel depth values computed by binocular camera. The segmentation of human bodies performs fine registration with the mesh vertex point clouds of the digital model scaled and free degrees fixed. In the pipeline, techniques such as lightweight design of deep networks, optimal initial values for fine registration through coarse registration and early stopping thresholds for iterations are used to reduce computational complexity and runtime while maintaining high accuracy. Therefore our method is CPU-friendly and can achieve quasi-real-time registration at the edge devices

articleTitle: Factory Fire Detection using TRA-YOLO Network
abstract: Surveillance analysis based on deep learning is an important approach for fire prevention and control in factories. However, the detection of flames and smoke still faces problems such as false alarms due to the diverse forms of flames and smoke, as well as the background interference. To address these issues, in this paper, we propose a novel fire detection model TRA-YOLO. On the one hand, the network combines the Transformer encoder with CNN to improve the performance in extracting both the global and the local features. On the other hand, an improved ACK-Res2Net module is proposed, which uses multi-scale convolution kernels to adaptively learn features and enhances the network’s feature extraction capability in different scales, improving the detection accuracy of flames and smoke with different deformations. Additionally, the adaptive spatial feature fusion (ASFF) structure is used to suppress interference and enhance the important information, which further strengthen the anti-interference performance. Experiments show that TRA-YOLO achieves an accuracy gain of 4.1% over YOLOv5, and the average precision of flame and smoke is 2.9% higher than that of YOLOv5. Furthermore, the detection speed reaches 50fps, meeting the demand of real-time fire and flame alarming in factories.

articleTitle: Adaptive Compliance Control of Dual-arm Robot for Cooperative Handling Task
abstract: This paper proposes a position planning method based on adaptive admittance control for the collaborative handling problem of a dual-arm robot. The method involves constructing a kinematic model of the symmetrical robotic arm system using DH parameters and designing an adaptive admittance controller with the ability to dynamically adjust parameters. The controller ensures that the robot maintains a predetermined contact force with the object being operated on within an acceptable range. Simulation experiments on the Powertool system validate the effectiveness of this method.
